# Phase26 normative detail — D27–D40

This registry is an integral normative part of the formal specification. Every numbered requirement is binding within its stated scope. It preserves adopted companion detail and exact release/operating conditions; source diagnostics and interview stage metadata are not runtime requirements. Primary corrected clauses and explicit later supersession control over historical shorthand. No new product choice is introduced.

## Operative precedence

D27-C adds Internal while retaining original Public R02–R30. D29-X01 adds to the original contact requirements. D38 adds new-Note persistence to D37; D35 posted-note correction remains local. D39 current source/activation rules apply to reading; D40 source-specific unwanted handling refines prior blanket-work assumptions. User-authorized formalization supersedes earlier no-spec/no-next-question status prose. Reusable content is not new owner authority.

## Public and Internal Guidance

### REQ26-D27C-R01 — D27C-R01 Revision and bounded need

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

Internal Staff guides extend Public Guidance while preserving every unchanged Public control. Staff guides contain reusable instructions for handling Support work, not customer/case histories, member-care records, sensitive missionary identities or locations, credentials, live financial facts or a general ministry knowledge platform. A receipt-question example is a test fixture, not proof of a tenant policy or authority to perform a receipt action.

### REQ26-D27C-R02 — D27C-R02 One surface, explicit source types

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

Guidance SHALL have two equally legible tabs, **Public** and **Internal**, with no mixed All-results mode. A fresh conversation opens Public; an explicitly selected tab may be remembered within that conversation's current working session. Switching tabs preserves the entered query and return state without changing the reply/note purpose. The source discriminator is a closed owner-defined type, not a client-controlled visibility field that converts private content into public content.

### REQ26-D27C-R03 — D27C-R03 Public behavior is preserved

Applies to **US26-D27-01**, acceptance **AC26-D27-01-01–03**.

Public SHALL retain D27-R02–R30 as applicable: exact tenant/Site/Page/locale proof; selected Listed or Shared-by-link public variants; full eligible title/summary/body search; passive preview; deliberate Insert link/Link selected text; frozen wording/href and trusted provenance; same-source route continuity; withdrawal/preparation/P6 fencing; finite retention; complete authorization and compatible rollout. Shared-by-link is public, never the Internal audience. C creates no internal-to-public conversion shortcut.

### REQ26-D27C-R04 — D27C-R04 Internal source ownership

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

Support SHALL own Staff guide identity, validated structured content, draft, published revision, lifecycle and private search in operational storage through the shared API owner. It SHALL NOT use CMS drafts, private editor previews, an authenticated variation of a public Page, P17 Saved Sections, source-code agent instructions or fixture data as this authority. A qualified existing owner may be reused if subsequently proven equivalent; the current inspected contracts do not provide one. Reuse editor/search primitives and platform capabilities without copying owner state or extending the CMS public audience.

### REQ26-D27C-R05 — D27C-R05 Audience and restricted data

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

The initial internal audience SHALL be **Support staff**, meaning current active-tenant Support-read authority resolved through P12, not all tenant staff/admins, CRM readers, matching emails, inbox membership alone or a navigation alias. Staff guides are common Support instructions; no per-guide/inbox/private-person ACL builder is added. If content requires narrower financial, care, HR, security or missionary-record access, retain it in its qualified owner and use an authorized navigation path rather than copying it into common guidance. A label or author assertion cannot certify arbitrary prose is free of restricted data.

### REQ26-D27C-R06 — D27C-R06 Reader, author and publisher authority

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

Reading published guides, reading/editing candidate content, publishing to the common Support audience, withdrawing/deleting and assigning a maintainer SHALL be explicit current capabilities. Existing P12/Support content-management authority with tenant oversight supplies them; no new role enum or implicit privilege from D19 intake review, assignment, source visibility or D18 saved wording is allowed. A publisher may also be the author when authorized; no mandatory second person is invented. Any actually applicable governance requirement remains enforced. Inbox-only curation authority cannot publish to a wider tenant Support audience.

### REQ26-D27C-R07 — D27C-R07 Minimal content structure

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

A Staff guide SHALL have stable identity, a fixed canonical language, clear action-oriented title, short summary, validated structured body and accountable maintainer. One guide is one language; a translation is a deliberately authored separate guide with its own publication, not an automatic fallback or synchronized body. Start with headings, paragraphs, emphasis, bullet/numbered lists and descriptive links. No new attachment/upload/media service, executable checklist, live CRM variables, recipient tokens, embeds, scripts or automated actions is introduced. Authorized owner links may lead to relevant files or product actions without importing their protected content.

### REQ26-D27C-R08 — D27C-R08 Tiptap purpose boundary

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

Use D23's shared Tiptap architecture with a registered **Staff guide** document purpose and the restricted R07 schema. Common editor code is not shared publication or email authority. Server commands SHALL validate the complete original canonical JSON and trusted source-purpose envelope, schema/version, content bounds, links and source restrictions BEFORE generic Tiptap/ProseMirror parsing or normalization, as well as before accepting or publishing. Source purpose derives from the stored source and qualified command, never a user-supplied node attribute. Unknown protected nodes/attributes or unsupported versions SHALL fail visibly rather than be silently discarded and saved. Hiding toolbar buttons or passing generic Tiptap parsing is not sufficient validation. No new paid collaboration/AI service or editor upgrade is implied.

### REQ26-D27C-R09 — D27C-R09 Draft and publication

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

Save draft SHALL save only the authorized working candidate; it SHALL NOT publish or alter what ordinary readers see. Each guide has at most one current candidate and one current published head, with generation-based concurrency. A published guide may show **Unpublished changes** while its previous published revision remains readable. Publish to staff SHALL show the exact candidate/preview, source purpose, common audience and meaningful diff, then atomically admit an immutable published revision, trusted actor/time, current head, audit/receipt and required derived-data continuation. Publication itself includes the guide in Internal; no second Add-to-guidance switch is required.

### REQ26-D27C-R10 — D27C-R10 Edit, restore, archive and delete

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

Edits create/update a candidate against an expected generation. Discard changes leaves the published head unchanged. Archive immediately makes ordinary search/read unavailable without destroying authorized management history; a known unsafe guide can use the same immediate withdrawal boundary with an explicit reason. Restore or restore an old revision SHALL create a reviewable candidate, never silently republish. Delete archived content requires current qualified authority and explicit irreversible impact acknowledgement, removes owned body/title/summary/candidates/revisions/derived content through a durable deletion process, and retains only permitted minimal body-free audit/tombstone evidence. Unfinished deletion is visible and cannot revive content. Ordinary archive and source safety restriction are independent controls: a safety restriction persists across revisions, candidates, Restore and Publish until its authorized owner admits a current reviewed release. Ordinary publication authority, a reason label or a new revision cannot clear it. Restore must preserve an existing candidate/unsaved work unless staff explicitly review and accept its replacement; archive/delete while editing likewise require a clear save/discard and effect decision, never silent loss. Deletion SHALL re-prove applicable records retention or hold; it can stop ordinary serving while required content stays in restricted custody. Acknowledgement cannot override custody, and completion states what was actually disposed.

### REQ26-D27C-R11 — D27C-R11 Maintenance without a second workflow

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

Manage guidance SHALL distinguish Public selection management from Internal authoring/publication. Internal management exposes Draft, Published, Unpublished changes, Archived and deletion progress with clear actions; it does not create a generic review queue, social comments, progress tracker or an automatic Support ticket. Maintainer departure SHALL not delete tenant-owned guides/history; tenant oversight can assign a current eligible maintainer. Show the actual last publication and maintainer, not a fabricated review date from any edit. Content corrections use existing authorized staff-work capabilities where needed; no mandatory recurring review interval is invented.

### REQ26-D27C-R12 — D27C-R12 Find and read Internal

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

Internal SHALL search only currently authorized, currently published Staff guide titles, summaries and body text, with title/summary priority and stable tie-break. A blank query provides a paginated, predictable title list. A language filter appears when useful; there are no nested folders, mandatory tags, public Site filter or custom relevance controls. Public Site scope is preserved for return to Public but cannot silently filter Internal. No automatic query extraction from private conversations or persistent raw-query history is allowed. Empty, no-match, incomplete/updating and unavailable states are distinct.

### REQ26-D27C-R13 — D27C-R13 Consultation-only means no message insertion

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

Internal preview SHALL display **Internal — for Support staff** and readable published content, with an authorized full-page reading path when needed. It SHALL NOT offer Insert into reply, Insert into note, Copy article, automatic citation, conversion to Saved reply or a purpose switch. Existing manually authored replies/notes remain available. Known internal-purpose structured content SHALL not be accepted as externally publishable wording through client metadata stripping or a generic import path. No claim is made that Asym prevents screenshots, ordinary operating-system clipboard use or manual retyping of visible information.

### REQ26-D27C-R14 — D27C-R14 Reference navigation and action authority

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

An authenticated Staff guide link SHALL reauthorize the current actor/tenant/source on every read, never act as a bearer grant or reveal a title/body to an unauthorized recipient. Links to another guide or business owner are navigation only; the target independently authorizes its content/actions. Public/external links do not leak private guide/conversation context through referrers, tracking or auto-preview fetches. Reading a procedure, checking a conceptual step or opening a domain does not perform/approve a refund, reissue a receipt, change a contact or certify identity. Current owning-domain controls prevail over stale procedural wording.

### REQ26-D27C-R15 — D27C-R15 Support and CRM continuity

Applies to **US26-D27-07**, acceptance **AC26-D27-07-01–03**.

The same Guidance reader/finder serves Support detail and the qualified detail opened through CRM; one draft/context and current joint permissions remain. Guidance may also be consulted from the Support surface without creating a conversation. Staff author/maintain guides from its existing management area without manufacturing a ticket. Lookup/reading creates no Party, association, CRM Activity, last-contact event, note, staff-performance metric or resolution fact. Requester, participant, represented organization, actor, handler, CRM owner and guide maintainer remain distinct.

### REQ26-D27C-R16 — D27C-R16 Authoritative mutation and idempotency

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

Create/save/publish/discard/archive/restore/delete/maintainer changes SHALL use one current-authorized owner command with expected generation and durable idempotency receipt tied to the effect and payload. Head transition, actor/time, audit and required continuation SHALL be atomic. Lost response retries consult the receipt; key reuse with a different payload conflicts. Concurrent publication/withdrawal/deletion and stale saves cannot overwrite newer intent, recreate deleted content or publish an older candidate. Long-lived browser authority or an old JWT claim cannot substitute for current capability at admission.

### REQ26-D27C-R17 — D27C-R17 Database invariants

Applies to **US26-D27-06**, acceptance **AC26-D27-06-01–03**.

Operational guide/candidate/revision/head relationships SHALL be tenant-aware and constrained to the same guide identity and fixed language. Non-null tenant/source/purpose, allowed state/head combinations, at most one current candidate/head, unique revision identity, valid schema generation and protected immutable publication facts SHALL be enforced through constraints and the authoritative command. Tenant/actor/owner/approval/time/publication fields derive from trusted server context. Author deletion SHALL not cascade away tenant-owned content. CMS public references remain owner-validated soft references; Staff guides do not introduce cross-schema FKs or a shared visibility table that changes source ownership.

### REQ26-D27C-R18 — D27C-R18 Grants, RLS and privileged paths

Applies to **US26-D27-06**, acceptance **AC26-D27-06-01–03**.

Application checks plus effective grants/RLS/column privileges SHALL independently protect published reads, draft/history reads and writes. Verify existing-row USING and resulting-row WITH CHECK behavior, including Postgres's implicit reuse rules; omission of explicit syntax alone is not a vulnerability finding. A permitted write cannot move tenant, source purpose, owner or publication state into a forbidden condition. Views, RPCs/functions, storage, exported projections and service-role jobs SHALL preserve the same authorization. No public/anonymous role gets internal content or a service key; privileged execution is not permission by itself.

### REQ26-D27C-R19 — D27C-R19 Private derived data

Applies to **US26-D27-06**, acceptance **AC26-D27-06-01–03**.

Internal title, summary, snippets, counts, current/history bodies and links are protected data. Its search index and caches SHALL remain operational/private and never join the public P23 index, sitemap, public API, requester-facing knowledge source or AI corpus. Reuse shared indexing/query code only behind separate purpose/authorization contracts. Exact current tenant, membership, source/publication/safety generation and appropriate scope qualify every exposed result/count/snippet before paging. Public search SHALL expose no hidden internal-match count. Unknown current proof fails closed for that source class without substituting a wider query.

### REQ26-D27C-R20 — D27C-R20 Temporal and permission correctness

Applies to **US26-D27-06**, acceptance **AC26-D27-06-01–03**.

Publication, archive, deletion and membership revocation SHALL gate new reads immediately at the current owner boundary, independently of eventual index/cache purge. Late favorable events cannot revive a withdrawn/deleted head or broaden audience. An open reader receiving invalidation SHALL clear no-longer-authorized content and show an accurate unavailable/access state; the system cannot recall content already seen. A newly published revision is signalled without scrolling/replacing text mid-reading; reload deliberately obtains the new current version. No offline/private-body downloads or durable browser cache are added.

### REQ26-D27C-R21 — D27C-R21 Failures, completeness and recovery

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

One tab/source failure SHALL not take down the other tab, the conversation or unrelated message preparation. Search/preview requests are bounded and obsolete responses ignored. Incomplete indexing is disclosed rather than a false No matches. Current heads deny stale adverse data even if a worker is delayed. Existing durable continuation/receipt infrastructure supports replay, deletion purge and repair; normal maintenance must not require SQL surgery. Authoring shows Saved, Saving, Unsaved/conflict accurately; a failed autosave cannot claim a draft or publication exists.

### REQ26-D27C-R22 — D27C-R22 Email Studio and P6 seam

Applies to **US26-D27-07**, acceptance **AC26-D27-07-01–03**.

Public Guidance links retain D27's existing P17 source-aware wording/preparation and local P6 submission fences; no CMS/URL I/O occurs at dispatch. Staff guides are consultation sources, not a new P17 material, signature or message-reference family. Internal availability SHALL not block or re-render ordinary replies and SHALL not cause source-body copying into a preparation. D18 reusable message wording, D23 signatures, D19 held-mail review and D26 manual-origin work/CRM histories retain separate roles. All existing purpose validation, custody, actual audience authorization and source restrictions still apply to any real message.

### REQ26-D27C-R23 — D27C-R23 Retention and safe correction

Applies to **US26-D27-06**, acceptance **AC26-D27-06-01–03**.

Before activation, current published content, candidates, superseded revisions, archived/deleted bodies, derived data and body-free evidence SHALL each have a declared owner retention/disposal rule and tested final disposition, including applicable holds and restore behavior; no accidental indefinite source-history or backup exception is permitted. Reusable Staff guide source content follows its declared knowledge-source lifecycle, not D17's conversation expiry clock; this is not permission to store case/CRM data indefinitely. Published/archived revisions exist for controlled maintenance until authorized deletion or applicable owner retention removes them. Deletion/withdrawal must include derived indexes/caches and preserve restrictive tombstones through restores before serving resumes. Historical body-free evidence is not a hidden body store. Actual Support content, P17 provider-request purge and Recent sent copy URL/provenance exclusions remain unchanged. No restoration can reconstruct disposed content from backups or a projection outside its allowed recovery contract.

### REQ26-D27C-R24 — D27C-R24 Simple accessible UI

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

Use Core's base-maia/Base UI/shared tokens and existing auxiliary detail surface, not a fourth permanent pane or an app-local component system. Both tabs have clear text labels and visible focus; Internal has a persistent purpose label and no disabled send affordance pretending insertion is possible. Preserve query, filters, scroll and draft on Back/Escape/close; use a one-stack narrow-screen flow and normal full-page fallback. Qualify keyboard/screen reader, meaningful headings/link labels, non-color status, RTL/IME, zoom/reflow, reduced motion and low-bandwidth text-first use. Permissions are explained without disclosing inaccessible titles or counts.

### REQ26-D27C-R25 — D27C-R25 Performance and limits

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Use bounded indexed tenant/current-head queries, private operational full-text search and batch authorization; avoid N+1 source requests and filtering after a first-page cap. Register byte/node/depth/text/query/page-result bounds and the production-shaped capacity profile before activation. Measure body search, stale-event handling, publication and purge at each declared maximum and one beyond with safe rejection/degradation. No universal article count, arbitrary review duration or new external search vendor is frozen without evidence. Shared primitives do not require a shared public/private result corpus.

### REQ26-D27C-R26 — D27C-R26 Audit and operating ownership

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Durable guide history records trusted actor, guide/revision/generation, command/effect, publication/withdrawal/restore/deletion disposition and allowed reason without raw body snapshots in technical logs. Technical telemetry distinguishes query failure, stale head, authorization denial, save conflict and purge lag using safe IDs. A guide correction requiring follow-up may use the existing authorized shared staff-work owner with a qualified guide reference; it is not automatically a customer ticket. Tenant oversight owns orphaned/obsolete guides; platform owners own current access, propagation and deletion failures. R30's named controls must exist before monitoring is relied upon.

### REQ26-D27C-R27 — D27C-R27 Migration and replacement of the demo

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

The current `the legacy Support knowledge route` demo/read model and “attach to replies” promise SHALL be replaced or retired when the real capability activates. Fixture summaries are not source records, seeded official instructions or evidence that ACL/publication/search is ready. Legacy/demo links resolve only through explicit qualified migration mapping; otherwise show a neutral unavailable state, never an all-guides fallback or guessed title match. New staff-guide authoring/publishing and separate reader/index controls precede UI activation. No mass import of conversations, CMS drafts, Saved notes or external content into guides is authorized.

### REQ26-D27C-R28 — D27C-R28 Compatible rollout and future change

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Use additive operational schema/document versions and owner APIs; preserve independent Payload migration authority. Old readers/writers SHALL reject unsupported guide purpose/schema instead of dropping constraints. A kill switch can stop Internal publication/lookup while preserving existing Public and ordinary Support behavior, without defeating mandatory safety/deletion fences. Roll forward after new guide content is written unless rollback compatibility is proven. Restricted internal audiences, media authoring, general wiki functions and AI remain separate researched extensions, not speculative abstractions or hidden dependencies of C.

### REQ26-D27C-R29 — D27C-R29 Traceability and proof

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

The complete Internal R01–R30 and P01–P40 contracts supplement the unchanged Public clauses and proof. Trace every requirement through design, implementation, tests and release evidence. Actual runtime, DB/RLS, publication/race, browser/assistive-technology, usability and capacity groups remain required; source probes and documentary checks establish only their stated observations.

### REQ26-D27C-R30 — D27C-R30 Residual monitoring and usability acceptance

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

O01–O06 define signals, thresholds, owners and responses. Missing authorization, secret-source separation, valid publication, actual content limits or named accountability blocks release; monitoring cannot substitute. Representative staff must find the right public/internal source, distinguish shareable from staff-only, preserve their draft, perform an independently authorized owner handoff, and maintain/withdraw a guide without accidental publication, disclosure or facilitator help. Record observed issues and correct them; no mockup or vendor feature proves the experience perfect.

**P01–P40 are required and unexecuted release groups.** Unchanged D27 public-guidance proof remains required as a regression baseline. The three current-source schema observations are not implementation, DB/RLS, disclosure or usability proof.

### REQ26-D27C-PRIMARY-S0037 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Responsibility names below must map to an actual accountable team/person before activation. Missing ownership or a budget is a release blocker. These controls monitor residual operation after prevention/proof, not substitute for them.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Control | Signal and threshold                                                                                                                                            | Owner and response                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| O01     | Any unauthorized internal title/body/snippet/count/history/public-index exposure: **1 confirmed event**.                                                        | Core identity/access and Support source owners: stop affected serving/export path, contain exposure, preserve minimal incident evidence and require negative-proof repair before re-enable.                             |
| O02     | Any Save draft or unauthorized command changing the reader's published head: **1 event**.                                                                       | Support guide owner: freeze affected publication, restore qualified head through audited command, reconcile receipt/order and prove the corrected race.                                                                 |
| O03     | Any archived/deleted/revoked source served after the current owner boundary denies it, or purge exceeding the registered owner deletion deadline: **1 source**. | Support source/platform operations: stop affected serving, replay restrictive invalidation/purge and preserve tombstones; no favorable stale replay.                                                                    |
| O04     | Any published guide without an active eligible maintainer, or one confirmed obsolete/unsafe-instruction report.                                                 | Tenant Support content oversight: assign maintainer, review and correct or withdraw; use existing qualified staff work where follow-up is needed. An ordinary missing owner does not invent authority for another user. |
| O05     | Search p95 above the registered release budget for **two consecutive 5-minute windows**, or one confirmed qualifying hit lost by cap/post-filtering.            | Support/search platform owner: inspect safe query/head/plan metrics, bound load and correct completeness/performance before affected re-enable; no raw private query logging.                                           |
| O06     | One confirmed accidental public/internal action confusion, repeated save conflict causing lost work, or inaccessible critical journey.                          | Support UX owner with source owner: contain the faulty action, correct copy/focus/command behavior and rerun affected staff/AT journey before release/re-enable.                                                        |

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — Layout and access

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Use the existing Support auxiliary context area. Opening Guidance replaces the contents of that recoverable area rather than adding a fourth permanent pane. A narrow screen uses a single sheet/full-page stack. The same surface opens from the canonical Support detail in CRM. A Guidance entry in the Support surface also allows consultation without a conversation; no request is created just to read instructions.

The compact hierarchy is:

1. Guidance title, Close/Back and permission-appropriate Manage guidance action.
2. Public / Internal tabs with normal keyboard focus and selected-state semantics.
3. Search guidance; relevant visible filters on one compact row.
4. A readable result list: title, concise summary, useful language/source metadata.
5. Selected source reader with a clear purpose label and source-appropriate actions.

Avoid decorative article cards/hero images, new dashboard metrics, popularity rankings and icon-only audience badges. Let titles wrap, keep body text readable and preserve Core's shared base-maia/Base UI tokens, spacing, type scale and focus behavior. A known source restriction uses plain text and an appropriate icon, not a red warning on every ordinary staff instruction.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Public journey

Applies to **US26-D27-01**, acceptance **AC26-D27-01-01–03**.

1. Staff read the request and keep the actual reply or internal-note draft in place. Open Guidance manually; no private message is mined into a search query. Public is the first-use tab for a fresh conversation. An explicit tab choice may persist within that conversation's current session; a note/reply purpose change does not silently select a tab.
2. Search the tenant's deliberately selected public sources. Title, summary and eligible body text are covered, including selected Shared-by-link Pages. Site/language filters are shown only where useful. A blank query provides a predictable paginated list; partial indexing is disclosed instead of false No matches.
3. Preview the current owner-qualified public Page. Show title, Site/public destination, language and any meaningful Shared-by-link indication. The public projection is passive: no forms, donation widgets, scripts or embeds execute in the staff session. Consequential interactive sections are labelled with Open public page rather than silently omitted.
4. Choose **Insert link** at a valid caret or **Link selected text** to preserve ordinary selected wording. If the source/selection/draft is stale or the selection is protected, preserve the draft and request a valid source/position. Opening or previewing never inserts.
5. Return to the linked text in the same draft. Recipients, Reply/Internal note, signature and work status stay unchanged. Review/send normally under P17/Support/P6; Internal note never becomes email. Public link edits, withdrawal, same-source continuity and retention retain all D27 safeguards.

Illustration only: staff can share the tenant's published “Find your receipt” instructions when such a Page exists. That link does not generate a receipt, verify the requester or prove that a giving action completed.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Internal journey

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

1. Choose **Internal**. Preserve the query and independently run the private Staff guide search. The public Site filter no longer applies; its previous value is restored when returning to Public. Show a language filter only where it is useful, without implicit translation or fallback. Do not auto-switch the composer to Internal note.
2. Results include only current published guides available to this actor through the tenant's Support-read capability. The guide's title/summary/body are private. Drafts, history, archived guides and hidden-match counts do not appear. No results means no matches in a complete qualified query; permission or service problems have distinct safe states.
3. Open the guide in the same reader. Keep **Internal — for Support staff** visible. Show its actual publication date, language and maintainer context. Use meaningful headings and ordered steps; a derived in-page table of contents may appear when a guide has enough headings to need it, without a maintained taxonomy.
4. Read the instruction and use normal authorized product navigation if needed. For example, a general guide might explain where staff find the existing receipt workflow. The destination checks the staff member's current giving/CRM permissions and owns every action. The guide cannot grant approval, preselect a donor, auto-run a task or mark a procedure complete.
5. Close or return to the original conversation with its query, scroll, draft and context intact. The internal reader offers **Open guide** for a full-page authenticated view when a longer guide is easier to read that way. It offers no Insert into reply/note, Copy article, Quote section or automatic citation.

Internal consultation-only is intentional. D18 Saved notes already supplies reusable note wording; a Staff guide supplies maintained instructions. Adding typed internal references to messages would require additional audience, disclosure, retention and serialization work not needed to read and act on guidance. Normal text selection, operating-system copying and retyping are not claimed to be impossible. Known internal-purpose structured content must still fail an unauthorized import/publication path.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — CRM and independent consultation

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

From a CRM record, the existing permitted Support overview/Communications list opens the same canonical conversation detail. Guidance inside it has the same current permissions and state as in Support. A CRM-only reader does not gain internal-guide access; a Support reader does not gain restricted CRM data. Returning preserves the existing context. Lookup does not create a relationship, Activity, last-contact event, rating, note or financial effect.

Opening Guidance without a conversation shows the same read-only Public/Internal sources and appropriate management actions. Public link insertion is absent because there is no current editable conversation. Reading an internal instruction is not a reason to invent a ticket. This keeps Support a coherent feature within Asym rather than an organizing model for every staff action.

Shared addresses, unknown requesters, cases made for someone else, CRM merges, changed contact details and moved/reopened requests do not change guide access or grant authority. Guide maintainership is also distinct from conversation handling and CRM record ownership.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Maintainer journey: create and publish an internal guide

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

1. Open **Manage guidance → Internal**. Readers without authoring/publication authority can still consult published guides but do not receive broken editing controls. Management is a list of source records, not a second inbox: Draft, Published, Unpublished changes, Archived, and deletion progress where applicable. Search and simple state filtering are sufficient.
2. Choose **New staff guide**. Enter a clear title, short purpose summary, fixed content language and a current eligible maintainer. The audience is stated as **Support staff in this tenant** and is not an editable per-inbox or public/private toggle. A language change after source creation uses a separate deliberately authored guide; no automatic translation/synchronization is implied.
3. Author with the shared Tiptap Staff guide profile. Provide readable headings, paragraphs, emphasis, bullet/numbered lists and descriptive links. Do not show upload, embed, live recipient/CRM variable, executable checklist or AI controls. A short scope note explains that guides contain reusable instructions, not case data or secrets. It is not a guarantee of automated sensitive-data detection.
4. **Save draft** records only the candidate. Draft-only autosave can reduce loss if it reports Saving/Saved/Unsaved/conflict accurately; it never publishes. A second editor or stale autosave produces a recoverable conflict rather than last-write-wins. The candidate is available only to currently authorized tenant guide authors/publishers, not ordinary readers.
5. Preview the candidate as a staff reader and inspect the changed text against the current published version, if any. Show the real language and common audience. **Publish to staff** is a separate deliberate action that requires current tenant-scope publication authority. An authorized maintainer may both write and publish; there is no invented two-person floor or inherited D19 inbox-review permission.
6. The exact reviewed revision becomes current. Publication makes it available in Internal; no second Add-to-guidance step. If the search projection is catching up, management and affected searches show truthful updating/partial states. Failure after an ambiguous response checks the receipt rather than creating another publication.

Authors may read/edit the common tenant guide candidates through explicit authoring capability; readers see only published content. A tenant-wide publisher cannot be inferred from an inbox-specific saved-reply curator. The feature uses current P12 actions, not a new role enum or guide ACL editor.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Maintaining an existing guide

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Intent                                 | Flow                                                                                                        | Safeguard and result                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Improve instructions                   | Edit candidate → Save draft → preview/diff → Publish to staff.                                              | Current published text remains unchanged until successful publication. Open readers receive a new-version notice instead of text being replaced mid-reading.                                                         |
| Abandon changes                        | **Discard changes** after clear effect review where needed.                                                 | Current published revision remains; no reader update or source withdrawal.                                                                                                                                           |
| Restore an earlier revision            | Choose prior revision in authorized history → **Restore as draft** → inspect → publish separately.          | Existing candidate/unsaved text is preserved unless staff explicitly review and accept replacement. A safety restriction persists until its authorized owner releases it.                                            |
| Remove obsolete instructions from use  | **Archive guide**.                                                                                          | New ordinary reads/search stop; authorized management/history remain. Unsaved author work gets an explicit save/discard choice; saved candidate custody is explained. No silent public publication or body deletion. |
| Withdraw unsafe instructions           | Use the current source-safety action with reason and authorized review.                                     | Immediate serving denial uses the same source boundary, but the safety restriction is independent of ordinary Archive. A normal Publish/Restore/new revision cannot clear it.                                        |
| Return an archived guide               | **Restore as draft**, review current wording/purpose, then Publish to staff if eligible.                    | No automatic re-publication, no stale safety release. Existing candidate replacement remains explicit.                                                                                                               |
| Dispose of archived guide content      | **Delete archived content**, showing exactly the candidate, published/history and derived content affected. | Current authority/retention/holds rechecked; acknowledgement cannot override a hold. Restricted retained custody and unfinished purge are shown truthfully. No claimed completion before actual allowed disposal.    |
| Maintainer leaves or guide is obsolete | Tenant oversight assigns an eligible maintainer or withdraws/reviews.                                       | Departure does not delete tenant-owned guides/history. Existing qualified staff work may carry a guide reference; no customer ticket is auto-created.                                                                |

Public management remains different: **Add/Remove from guidance** changes the curated public selection; **Edit in Web Studio** changes source content under CMS authority. Removing a public selection does not unpublish its source. There is no Convert to Public action on an internal guide. If staff genuinely need new public wording, the CMS source must be independently authored/reviewed/published for that audience; no internal guide body is automatically transferred.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Honest states, privacy and accessibility

Applies to **US26-D27-06**, acceptance **AC26-D27-06-01–03**.

No published staff guides yet,” “No guides match these filters,” “Results are still updating,” “Internal guidance is temporarily unavailable,” “Your access changed,” and “Your changes were not saved” describe different facts. Do not expose an inaccessible title/count in an error. Do not say an email was not sent merely because a Guidance action failed; another action/tab may have submitted it. A guide read has no authority over P6 send state.

Tab/search/preview navigation must be keyboard and screen-reader usable, with visible focus, named actions and restrained result announcements. Escape closes only the current layer; Back restores query and scroll; closing returns to the trigger or insertion point. Search typing/IME does not trigger navigation. Slow previous responses cannot replace newer results. Public/internal purpose is visible text, never a color or tooltip alone.

On mobile, one stack serves list → reader → return. Controls remain reachable under zoom/reflow; long titles and RTL text wrap normally. Use existing reduced-motion and focus conventions, no hover/drag-only actions. Text-first guides avoid large downloads; there is no private offline library or new local-storage body persistence. External links do not receive the private guide/conversation URL as referrer and do not trigger automatic server fetches.

The 40 proof groups include representative staff/CRM/authoring/maintenance, keyboard/AT/mobile and failure journeys. None has been run against a new feature. This blueprint establishes what must work; it does not certify visual polish or user satisfaction before implementation and observation.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0003 — Minimal operational model

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

A guide has a stable owner-defined identifier, non-null tenant, fixed canonical language, purpose fixed to ordinary Support instructions, source lifecycle generation and maintainer reference. Its language describes its authored content; translated instructions use a separate deliberate guide identity. Titles need not be unique and never establish identity. There is no automatic locale-family synchronization, per-inbox copy or audience builder.

The working candidate is distinct from immutable published revisions. At most one current candidate and one current published head exist per guide. Publication can coexist with a candidate containing unpublished changes. A current publication is served only when ordinary source state is Published, current safety permits it and the actor has current Support-read authority. Archive denies ordinary serving even though authorized management can retain earlier revisions. A source safety restriction independently denies relevant reads/publication and survives archive/restore/new revisions until the protection owner admits a reviewed release.

Enforce tenant/guide-qualified FKs among operational candidate/revision/head records, a unique revision identity, one candidate/head per guide, valid state/head combinations, fixed language/purpose and protected publication/control fields. Actor/tenant/time/approval/control metadata comes from trusted server context. Owner references cannot be changed to a different tenant; author/maintainer departure cannot cascade-delete tenant content or erase historical attribution. The exact deletion behavior for identity references must preserve allowed body-free attribution without requiring the departed user to remain active.

Public selections continue to reference CMS by owner-validated soft identity and current public-generation/destination proof. Do not create a cross-schema FK, a polymorphic visibility switch that updates source authority, or a universal table joining internal bodies into public search. A closed source discriminator in the finder DTO tells UI which owner and actions apply; it is not a writer permission.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0004 — Current capabilities, grants and RLS

Applies to **US26-D27-06**, acceptance **AC26-D27-06-01–03**.

Common Staff guide readers are the active tenant's currently qualified Support readers. This intentionally does not expose content to every generic staff/admin role, CRM record owner, inbox participant or matching-email agent. Tenant-level Staff guide authoring capability permits the ordinary common guide candidate/history work in that tenant; tenant-level publication and source-protection/deletion actions are separately qualified. The same person may hold author and publisher capabilities; there is no obligatory new reviewer role. D19's held-mail reviewer and D18's inbox-specific wording curator do not automatically gain these actions.

The common audience is suitable only for reusable non-case-specific instructions. Restricted financial/care/HR/security/missionary records remain with their respective owning domain. A guide can explain a general path without copying a restricted record, recipient token, actual donor data, private case link or live CRM field into common content. Known classified source material is rejected on inappropriate import/copy paths. Freeform prose still requires accountable author review and a real withdrawal/correction process; the feature does not claim an infallible detector.

Application authorization and SQL grants/RLS/column controls must independently enforce the read, draft/history and mutation distinction. Both USING and effective WITH CHECK must be tested; Postgres can reuse USING if WITH CHECK is omitted, so syntax absence alone is not proof of an exploit. Test the actual new-row outcome, not just that a policy exists. Privileged workers, functions/RPCs, security-definer/invoker views, API routes and any linked-storage access need the same tenant/purpose/capability boundary. Internal/backup tables with no direct reader are revoked from exposed roles. No service credential is a client authorization shortcut.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — Authoritative command and revision transitions

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Command/event                   | Required preconditions and atomic outcome                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create guide                    | Current tenant authoring authority, validated original Staff guide document/purpose and valid fixed language; one guide/candidate/receipt. No published head.                                                                                 |
| Save candidate                  | Current authoring authority and exact expected candidate/source generation; overwrite only the acknowledged candidate, never the current published revision.                                                                                  |
| Publish to staff                | Current publication authority, no unresolved safety restriction, validated exact candidate, common audience and observed generation/diff; one immutable revision/head/audit/receipt/required continuation transaction.                        |
| Discard candidate               | Current authority and explicit intent; published head unaffected. Unsaved browser text cannot be silently claimed saved.                                                                                                                      |
| Archive                         | Current source-management authority; atomically deny new ordinary reads/search at the owner head. Existing candidate/history custody remains explicit; unsaved changes require save/discard choice.                                           |
| Restrict unsafe source          | Current protection authority/reason; immediate denial independent of ordinary Archive. Publication or a new revision cannot clear restriction.                                                                                                |
| Restore archived/prior revision | Current source/history authority; create a candidate and preserve current candidate/unsaved work unless explicitly reviewed replacement is accepted. No public/staff publication or safety release.                                           |
| Release safety restriction      | Actual authorized owner reviews current source/purpose and admits a new release generation; normal publisher permission alone is insufficient. The same actor can hold both permissions when allowed.                                         |
| Delete archived content         | Re-prove current delete authority, retention/hold and generation; deny serving, record durable purge/tombstone/receipt, dispose of allowed source/derived content. Required held content stays in restricted custody; completion is truthful. |
| Reassign maintainer             | Current tenant content oversight; choose eligible current maintainer without changing content/publication or historical author.                                                                                                               |

Each command binds idempotency to its durable business effect and payload digest. Identical retry returns the original outcome; a changed payload under the same key conflicts. Lost response requires receipt lookup, not a blind new effect. A stale autosave or restore cannot defeat archive/deletion, and a late index rebuild cannot recreate a deleted guide. Required projection/purge continuation is durable in the same authoritative commit; no distributed write into CMS/P17 is introduced.

Source safety and ordinary archive use the same immediate serving-denial infrastructure without collapsing their authorities. A restriction applies across retained candidates/revisions and recognized derivatives of that guide. Restoring an unsafe old revision and pressing Publish remains denied absent current protection-owner release. Neither this mechanism nor consultation-only UI promises to identify all manually retyped information.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — Validate before generic editor normalization

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

The original canonical input and the trusted source-purpose envelope must be checked **before** generic Tiptap/ProseMirror parsing can strip unknown attributes. Purpose derives from the stored guide and command, not `attrs.internal=true`. Validate allowed node/mark/attribute set, structural depth/node/byte bounds, fixed language/purpose, safe link destinations and known source restrictions. Unsupported input fails with recoverable author feedback and does not overwrite the last valid candidate.

The narrow profile supports structured instructional text. Do not expose media uploads/attachments, third-party embeds, raw HTML/script, recipient personalization, live CRM bindings or executable checklist nodes. Navigation links use validated HTTPS or qualified internal application destinations, never secret-bearing signed URLs, code/data URLs or arbitrary server fetches. Links to another guide or owner do not carry authorization; target reads/actions are rechecked. This shares editor/rendering primitives with D23 but not its message-publication identity or a paid collaboration service.

The actual-source experiment used the installed shared Tiptap 3.22.3 schema: synthetic unknown purpose/source attributes were normalized away; a generic image node was admitted; a strict unsupported node was rejected. No network image fetch occurred. These observations explain why profile validation must precede normalization; they do not prove a server bypass, actual clipboard handling or the new Staff guide implementation.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — Two private/public query contracts behind one UI

Applies to **US26-D27-04**, acceptance **AC26-D27-04-01–03**.

Public is unchanged D27 owner-qualified selected-Page search. Internal uses operational published Staff guide heads and private text search. Both share query UI conventions, not a result corpus. Only the active tab is queried. There is no All result mode, cross-owner score fusion, hidden internal count on a public query or automatic private query extraction from a conversation.

Internal searches title/summary/body with stable identity tie-break and complete authorized corpus before cursor paging/counts/snippets. Use indexed tenant/current-head predicates and batched current authorization. Public Site filters never apply to Internal; language is explicit. No client-side first-page filtering, N+1 source calls or stale public cache is an acceptable shortcut. Positive publication/index lag can yield a visible Updating/partial state. Archive/safety/delete/revocation must deny new results before eventual index purge. Current head checks and restrictive tombstones prevent favorable stale replay.

Private browser/server caches must bind current tenant/actor policy scope/source head and safety generation. Avoid durable browser-body/offline caching. Current revocation clears an open reader on invalidation and is rechecked on subsequent reads; already viewed text cannot be recalled. A routine new revision prompts a deliberate reader refresh without moving their scroll mid-procedure. One source/tab failure does not block the other or an unrelated Support reply.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0008 — Email Studio, public disclosure and CRM

Applies to **US26-D27-07**, acceptance **AC26-D27-07-01–03**.

Public link insertion retains D27's exact P17 source material, signature-once, immutable whole-reply preparation, Support admission and P6 current local submission/reconciliation contract. Routine public edits/removal, same-Page/Site/locale continuity, public withdrawal, restoration of safe copied links and terminal-effect non-revival remain as ratified. No post-seal CMS/URL fetch or rerender is introduced.

Internal guides do not produce an insertion, source citation, attachment, Saved reply or Internal note reference. Consequently they add no P17 guide-reference material family, no second retention graph and no guide-availability dispatch gate. Known internal-purpose document imports fail inappropriate external-purpose boundaries, while ordinary manual authoring still follows D18/D23. A guide may mention a workflow but cannot execute it or establish a business fact. No new AI ingestion is authorized.

CRM uses the same permitted Support detail. It receives no copied guide body, worker score, Activity, last-contact update or new Party merely because a staff member read guidance. The requester, participant, represented organization, actor, Support handler, CRM owner and guide maintainer stay distinct. Restricted owner actions remain independently validated/approved/audited; reading instructions or resolving Support work is not proof of their completion.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0009 — Content custody and final disposition

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Each class must have an explicit owning retention/disposal rule and tested final disposition before activation. Reusable knowledge is not transient conversation content, so no arbitrary D17 conversation timer is copied onto it. This contract deliberately uses source-purpose lifecycle; any applicable platform records policy/hold still prevails. There is no new universal legal period or promise of indefinite retention.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Class                                    | Purpose, retention/disposal rule and serving boundary                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Current published guide                  | Retained while current approved reusable instructions; ordinary serving ends immediately on Archive, safety restriction, deletion or lost reader authority. Replacement does not rewrite historical revisions.                                                            |
| Working candidate                        | One current candidate for ongoing authorized editing; replacement/discard/delete is explicit, with no unlimited hidden autosave snapshot history. Applicable source retention/hold may require restricted custody after serving ends.                                     |
| Superseded published revisions           | Only the owner's declared maintenance/history/restore retention, visible to authorized management. Restoration creates a candidate under current safety; no reader endpoint silently serves a chosen historical version. Disposed body is not reconstructible from audit. |
| Archived source/candidate/history        | Retained for explicitly declared source maintenance/records custody until qualified restore or disposal; not available to ordinary finder/readers. The implementation must declare this policy before activation rather than silently retaining every revision forever.   |
| Deleted/restricted content               | Serving stops first. Durable purge clears allowed bodies/title/summary/revisions/derived text; required held copies remain isolated under the actual records owner. Release/retry resumes permitted purge with truthful progress.                                         |
| Index/cache/preview                      | Derived, short-lived/rebuildable only from currently permitted source heads; current adverse denial precedes purge. No public corpus, independent restore authority or durable private offline cache.                                                                     |
| Audit/tombstone/receipt                  | Minimal permitted body-free identity/generation/effect/actor/disposition evidence under existing audit/records custody. Avoid storing titles or reasons that would preserve content subject to deletion.                                                                  |
| Actual Support messages and P17 material | Existing D16/D17/P17/P6 custody only. Guide use does not restart conversation clocks, extend provider-request storage, or add URLs/provenance to P17 Recent sent copy.                                                                                                    |

Backups/exports follow their actual owning recovery/custody contracts; a restored backup must apply current deletion/restriction/tenant state before becoming serveable. A retention hold racing deletion must stop unauthorized disposal, not revert the serving denial. User confirmation is not hold-release authority. P31 proves allowed disposal, restricted retention, later release/retry and no stale reappearance.

### REQ26-D27-INTERNAL_DATA_CONTRACT-S0010 — Activation and proof

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Qualify current capability/source-purpose APIs, constrained candidates/revisions/heads, private search/current denial and source custody before the UI. Register actual document/query/corpus/concurrency budgets and test at limits and one beyond. Replace/retire demo knowledge behavior and its internal-to-reply promise; do not bulk-import fixture summaries, CMS drafts or actual conversations. Any old link mapping must be explicit and tenant-qualified.

Additive compatible consumers and writer fences precede new data. Disable Internal safely without breaking Public/ordinary Support or mandatory purge/safety. Prefer roll-forward after new guide documents exist; rollback requires proof that older code preserves purpose and source state. The full 40 proof groups and unchanged public regression obligations are unexecuted. Source experiments, independent review and documentary verification are evidence about the decision, not permission to call the feature implemented or safe in production.

### REQ26-D27-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — The ordinary Support journey

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

1. **Stay in the conversation.** Staff read the request and start their normal reply or internal note. Their current inbox, recipients, purpose, signature, draft and work state remain visible. A clearly labelled Guidance action sits with related insertion tools such as Saved replies, without giving it a separate main navigation area. Opening Guidance is deliberate; Asym does not extract a search query from a sensitive message.
2. **Find a page.** Guidance opens in the existing auxiliary context surface; it replaces that surface's current content with a recoverable Back path instead of adding a fourth persistent pane. At narrow widths it becomes a single layered sheet/full-screen surface. Initial focus enters Search guidance. Blank input shows the selected, eligible corpus in a restrained paginated list. Results use a title and short source description, with Site/language only where useful for distinction. Search covers title, summary and eligible public text through the owner projection, including deliberately selected Shared-by-link Page bodies. If coverage is updating or incomplete, staff see that status; No matches is reserved for a complete qualified search. No hero images, card grid, tag cloud, popularity score or AI panel is needed.
3. **Understand the scope.** Language and Site filters appear only when there is a genuine choice. An explicitly resolved conversation language/site may initialize them; otherwise the visible scope is All languages/All sites. Staff can clear either separately. Searching Thai or Spanish never silently becomes English; zero results never silently broadens a Site. Matching title, description and snippets use safe text rendering, including right-to-left text, punctuation and international names.
4. **Preview before choosing.** Activating a row opens its preview rather than inserting immediately. Show the source title, language, public Site/domain and a public/link-only indication where it matters. Render readable source-owned public text and allowed static media. Forms, donation widgets and embeds do not execute here. A notice such as “This page includes interactive content. Open the public page to use it.” preserves meaning. Open public page uses the qualified public URL; it never opens a CMS editor preview under the guise of recipient access.
5. **Insert deliberately.** At a valid caret, the button reads Insert link and inserts the human-readable Page title. For ordinary selected text it reads Link selected text, preserving staff wording. Protected signature/content or an invalid/stale selection gives “Choose where to insert this link in your draft” and returns focus to the draft, with no loss or implicit replacement. Source eligibility is checked again; the selected Page is not assumed safe just because an earlier result was visible.
6. **Return to the same draft.** The finder closes/returns focus to the linked text using the existing editor's convention. One insertion command creates one link and one normal undo step. A succinct live announcement confirms insertion; no blocking success dialog is needed. Staff can change visible wording, Undo, continue writing or remove the link. Recipient, purpose, signature and status remain unchanged.
7. **Review and send normally.** This action does not send or resolve. P17 prepares the whole actual reply, including the Guidance dependency and current signature once; Support authorizes/adopts the reply; P6 delivers under existing invariants. An internal note stays internal. When a source is unavailable, the inline message identifies the affected link and offers an appropriate replacement/removal/retry path. It never suggests bypassing a privacy hold by stripping provenance.

Illustration only: a donor asks how to find a receipt. Staff may search “receipt,” preview the tenant's published instructions and link the words “how to find your receipt” in a personal answer. This does not issue a receipt or attest that the requester may access a specific gift. If a tenant has no such Page, staff can answer normally or use existing saved wording. The example is not a compulsory template or invented universal ministry workflow.

### REQ26-D27-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Starting from CRM

Applies to **US26-D27-07**, acceptance **AC26-D27-07-01–03**.

1. Open the CRM record under CRM permissions. Use the ratified D9/D26 Support overview or Communications view to choose an applicable conversation. The compact overview remains its existing preview, not the only source of history.
2. Open the same canonical Support detail inline where practical, with the existing full-page fallback. Joint authorization determines what can be read and done; a CRM record owner is not automatically a Support worker, and a Support handler is not automatically allowed to read restricted CRM data.
3. Use precisely the same Guidance surface, source qualifications and draft. No second CRM copy of the Page, transcript, editor or selection is created. A read-only staff member can consult public guidance but has no insertion action without the existing draft capability.
4. Return to the CRM record with its filter/scroll/selection preserved. No Activity, last-contact timestamp, donor preference, relationship, receipt/refund or case resolution is created by lookup or insertion. Actual correspondence and actual business actions retain their existing owners and histories.

Unidentified requesters, shared email addresses, represented organizations, merged/unlinked CRM records and reopened work do not change these rules. A Page's public access does not prove identity, household membership, financial access or language preference.

### REQ26-D27-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — The curator's first-use journey

Applies to **US26-D27-03**, acceptance **AC26-D27-03-01–03**.

1. An authorized curator opens **Manage guidance** from the finder or the existing Support settings area. Staff without this capability see the useful finder and an explanation if no guidance is selected; they do not get broken management links or an unrelated admin invitation.
2. The management view is one simple list: Page, Site/language, current eligibility and last selection change. Active selections and Removed history are distinguishable. Available, Unavailable and Checking are current derived conditions. These names must not be overloaded as CMS publishing states.
3. Choose **Add guidance**. The source-owner selector lists referenceable public Page variants under the curator's independent source-reference permission, with current public qualification. The curator selects an exact Site/Page/language. A public page address can identify an owner-resolvable candidate if the shared selector supports that operation; an arbitrary pasted URL is never crawled or accepted as a substitute for stable source identity.
4. Preview the Page and its public destination. For Shared by link — public, explain that recipients can view and reshare it; selection does not make it listed in public search. Review source scope, then **Add to guidance**. One command creates one selection with trusted history. Double-click/retry cannot add duplicates.
5. Return to the list with the outcome visible. During favorable search convergence the curator sees Checking/Updating, not false success about instant search availability. A new translation or another Site's similarly titled Page is not added automatically.

No custom ordering hierarchy, inbox clones, personal variants, Support keywords, per-article review workflow or mandatory multi-person approval is introduced. Existing tenant oversight can manage coverage and curator permissions. Source-reference permission is not CMS edit/publish permission.

### REQ26-D27-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — When a suitable public page does not exist

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Preserve the Support draft. A CMS-authorized person may use the existing **Open Web Studio** work path to create or improve the source under its normal editor, review and publication rules. Returning to Support requires explicit selection of the now-qualified exact public variant; a draft/editor preview is not eligible.

A Support-only worker can communicate the content gap through the tenant's existing authorized work process. This decision does not add a new generic request queue or automatically create a ticket, nor copy the private conversation into a CMS task. Any transferred context is a deliberately selected safe source reference or non-sensitive description. Ordinary Support work can continue without a new Page.

### REQ26-D27-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Maintain, remove, unpublish and restore

Applies to **US26-D27-05**, acceptance **AC26-D27-05-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Intent                                    | Clear action and review                                                                                                                           | Actual effect and recovery                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Correct wording on a Page                 | **Edit in Web Studio**, only with CMS permission; otherwise show a permission-appropriate source reference.                                       | Web Studio owns edits/versions/publication. Future previews show the current public Page. Composed/sent link wording does not change. No Support reapproval for every editorial revision.                                                                                                                                                           |
| Stop offering an unsuitable Page to staff | **Remove from guidance** with a concise statement: “This removes the page from Guidance. This does not change the public page or existing links.” | Changes the selection to Removed. A later publish event cannot re-add it. Deliberate Add to guidance creates a new generation of the same selection.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Stop public access to a Page              | **Open Web Studio** and its qualified unpublish/withdrawal path, under source-owner permission.                                                   | Source eligibility changes; Active selection becomes unavailable. New use and exact definitely-unsubmitted dependent mail are fenced under the owner/P17 contract; possible prior delivery is reconciled, not recalled.                                                                                                                             |
| Repair a missing locale/domain/proof      | Show exact unavailable condition where safe; **Retry** or navigate to the responsible source owner.                                               | Do not guess another locale, Site or URL. A network outage is Checking/temporarily unavailable, not “Page unpublished.”                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Restore a source                          | Web Studio restores/publishes under its own lifecycle; then current public/safety qualification runs.                                             | Restore-to-draft remains unavailable. Qualified publication can recover only Active selections. Removed ones remain Removed until deliberate re-add. Safe links previously copied from those selections may requalify after current owner safety/public proof without re-adding the selection; fenced/terminal prepared effects do not auto-revive. |
| Move a URL                                | Source owner publishes qualified route/domain continuity.                                                                                         | Same-Page/Site/exact-locale older links may stay valid. Different-Page replacements require deliberate Guidance reselection; no silent approval inheritance or draft rewrite.                                                                                                                                                                       |

A simple removal that is reversible uses the existing standard command/Undo pattern only if it safely preserves expected generations and audit. Destructive source publication/withdrawal uses the owning surface's actual consequences and confirmation rules. This decision does not introduce a second generic confirmation workflow.

### REQ26-D27-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — State copy and recovery

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State                                              | Staff presentation                                                                                   | Action                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No active selected Pages                           | **No guidance selected yet.** Continue writing or use Saved replies.                                 | Authorized curator sees Manage guidance.                                                                                |
| Search has no eligible matches                     | **No guidance matches these filters.** Show current scope.                                           | Clear one filter or edit search; never silently widen it.                                                               |
| Source proof cannot be checked                     | **Guidance is temporarily unavailable. Your draft is unchanged.**                                    | Retry; unaffected composition continues.                                                                                |
| One previously selected result becomes unavailable | **This page is no longer available for a new link.**                                                 | Return to results; retain query/scroll. No stale preview snippet is used as proof.                                      |
| Linked source restricts a not-yet-submitted reply  | **Review this guidance link before sending.** Show the safe specific reason and affected occurrence. | Choose qualified replacement/removal; retry only for transient failures. Existing dangerous-material rules still apply. |
| Permission changed                                 | **Your access changed. We could not insert this link.**                                              | Preserve authorized recoverable work and use normal owner authorization recovery; do not offer an elevation path.       |
| Source includes interactive sections               | **Open the public page to use its interactive content.**                                             | Explicit external navigation; no embedded staff-session execution.                                                      |

### REQ26-D27-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Accessibility, visual quality and low-bandwidth behavior

Applies to **US26-D27-08**, acceptance **AC26-D27-08-01–03**.

Use the existing base-maia/Base UI structure, type scale, spacing, borders and focus treatment. A calm text list, readable preview width, concise metadata and one clear insertion action make the feature fit Asym better than an illustrated knowledge dashboard. Source titles can wrap; Site/language context must not be reduced to inaccessible tooltip-only text. States use text and icons, not color alone.

Keyboard navigation must preserve text-editing keys and IME input, announce selected results and respect the app's existing shortcut conventions.
