Safety/privacy revocation of a specific issued link is a separate actual owner action, not a side effect of ordinary Off. Owners can still read feedback and use ordinary Support correspondence while invitations are Off.

### REQ26-D28-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Normal worker journey

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

An authorized worker handles a request through the existing conversation. They can consult Public/Internal Guidance, insert an approved public link, use a curated reply or shortcut and send through Tiptap/D4. None adds a survey to that human reply or changes its recipients/signature. When genuinely finished, the worker uses the existing ordinary completion action; there is no new mandatory survey checkbox, “ask this donor” picker or invitation confirmation for every closure.

The conversation's Feedback section is collapsed by default until relevant. It may say **Waiting until [local time]**, **Not selected**, **Not invited — contact limit**, **Invitation submission uncertain**, **Invited**, **Feedback received**, or **Unavailable**. “Invited” is tied to actual qualified submission evidence and includes uncertainty where applicable; Selected alone never renders Sent. A restricted source is omitted without exposing hidden inbox names or recipient details. Optional informational states do not compete with the main work status.

If work reopens during the quiet interval, its pending timer is cancelled and the ordinary work journey proceeds. A later genuine completion can start a new interval if no draw has occurred. After an opportunity has been sampled, reopening/merging never causes another draw. A merged group has one current selection chance; another linked original cannot retry a Not-selected result. Independently sampled pre-merge history remains visible honestly. Staff do not get a Try again or Include anyway action. They can continue appropriate care regardless of sampling or feedback.

Examples are illustrative, not evidence of current ministry practice: a donor asks how to obtain a giving statement; a staff member asks about account access; a missionary asks a general administrative question. In each case the invitation evaluates the support experience, not the correctness of a receipt, permission entitlement or success of a mission project. Actual restricted member-care/location context is excluded by its owner rules rather than copied into a generic survey.

### REQ26-D28-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Requester email and response journey

Applies to **US26-D28-04**, acceptance **AC26-D28-04-01–03**.

1. **Receive one optional email.** It uses a professional public team identity, a neutral subject such as “How was your support experience?”, brief explanation and one **Give feedback** CTA. It contains no gift amount, private case subject, missionary location, transcript, promotional appeal or personal agent performance request. Sender/reply route is qualified; a person can reply normally for continued help. The invitation explains that responding is optional and provides the protected feedback-preference action. There are no smiley-rating URLs, open tracking or reminders.
2. **Open the existing protected doorway.** The generic page explains that continuing opens an Asym action. Its selector-only GET reveals no tenant, action type or case. One deliberate **Continue** validates the fragment verifier at the exact same origin. This extra step preserves the existing P17 contract; a new direct survey URL is rejected. No login or CRM record is created. Missing fragment/unsupported browser uses the existing generic safe recovery and never moves the secret into a query string.
3. **Answer a small form.** Once authorized, show public team identity, the fixed localized question and actual link expiry. No requester name, contact details, previous comment or conversation appears. Use a fieldset with three equal-weight labelled radios: Dissatisfied; Neither satisfied nor dissatisfied; Satisfied. Nothing is preselected. The optional comment is a native textarea, not Tiptap: short plain feedback needs no rich text complexity. Show a 2000-character Unicode-aware limit and preserve text during recoverable validation failures. “Authorized staff may read this feedback. Please do not include sensitive personal or financial details. For further help, reply to the team's email.” Do not call it anonymous or promise monitoring 24/7.
4. **Review and Submit feedback.** Radio choice and comment remain editable before Submit. There is no immediate write on radio selection. An empty rating is a labelled error; negative ratings never require explanation. A valid submission atomically records one response and shows **Thank you. Your feedback has been recorded.** No extra thank-you email follows. The receipt does not imply an underlying request was solved, a complaint was reopened or a financial action completed.
5. **Retry/revisit/correction.** A lost network response checks the same receipt; identical retries cannot duplicate feedback. A used link says feedback has already been recorded without echoing the prior score/comment. Changed replays cannot overwrite another shared-mailbox person's submission. Staff also cannot change the score. A later correction or deletion follows the existing qualified Support/privacy route and is attributed honestly. Expired/revoked/unavailable states show neutral recovery without hidden case information or automatically emailing a replacement link.
6. **Stop invitations.** The invitation's distinct protected preference action leads through the same shared handoff to a clearly scoped confirmation: “Stop feedback invitations from this organization.” It requires no rating, donor login or explanation. P3 records the purpose preference idempotently. Confirmation explains that ordinary Support contact remains governed separately. Feedback participation itself changes no preferences. This action has separate purpose/state and a accepted 90-day validity from its own issuance, independent of the 14-day rating window. A used/expired rating or deleted Support content does not strand the preference action in the original email. Using one action does not consume the other. The 90 days expires only the preference credential, never the resulting recorded opt-out. The P3 preference persists under its independently authorized lifecycle; policy Off→On, CRM merges, key rotation and new invitations cannot clear it or opt anyone back in. After the preference action’s own expiry, the existing qualified contact/privacy route can handle the request; the system does not auto-send a fresh invitation.

The public form intentionally has no Attach file, user profile, knowledge search, multistep survey, chat bot, fundraising link or rich editor. It remains a narrow action inside Asym's existing protected presentation. Review official client/fragment behavior during release proof; the blueprint does not claim universal client support.

### REQ26-D28-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Staff review and CRM-first journey

Applies to **US26-D28-05**, acceptance **AC26-D28-05-01–03**.

**Support Reports → Feedback** opens a clean overview with a date-cohort selector and permitted inbox filter. A compact funnel shows Eligible → Selected → Issued → Responded, with suppression and provider-unknown detail available on demand. The response list defaults to **Needs review**; **All feedback** is a simple alternative, not a custom saved-view builder. Rows show rating text, received time, permitted inbox and permitted conversation reference. Comments appear only to a current source-authorized reader, not in tenant-wide notification bodies.

Open a row into the same conversation detail, retaining filter, position and review context. The Feedback section shows the exact submitted question version, score/comment, invitation time and “Submitted through this invitation; respondent identity is not verified.” For a neutral/positive rating with no work needed, **Mark reviewed** records reviewer/time. If further care is needed, the worker takes the existing explicit Support follow-up/reply path. Mark reviewed, reading a low rating and replying are different actions. A negative score never silently reopens work, sends an apology or creates a CRM task.

From CRM, a permitted worker opens the existing Communications → Support relation and gets the same canonical detail/Feedback section. Back returns to the same CRM record and list position; it does not duplicate comment text into a separate Activity. The Overview's up-to-three unfinished preview remains only a preview; historical resolved Support and its permitted feedback remain discoverable through the complete Support list. Revoked Support permission removes the feedback section/source, including counts and snippets, even if the CRM record remains readable. Restricting a CRM record does not delete Support source facts; links/navigation are re-evaluated separately.

### REQ26-D28-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Empty, incomplete and operational states

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

- **Off/first use:** brief explanation and Configure for qualified managers; ordinary staff see no setup burden.
- **No ratings yet:** “No feedback received for this cohort” with actual issued/unknown/eligible counts; never a 0% satisfaction score or presumed satisfaction.
- **Small sample:** counts remain usable;20 responses is only a caution threshold before a trend, not an assurance of statistical validity. No global donor/agent benchmark.
- **Paused readiness:** show the responsible owner action and expiry consequence. Do not create fresh invitations when the dependency returns after send-by.
- **Unavailable/permission loss:** safe no-content state; no stale comments, hidden totals or public recovery link into CRM.
- **Low bandwidth:** keep text readable and form minimal; recover the same command receipt, never tell the person to request another survey.
- **Duplicate/merged work:** current canonical navigation with original invitation provenance; no duplicate visible “new response” solely because a link or merge changed.

### REQ26-D28-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Visual and interaction requirements

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

Use existing Core semantic typography, spacing, Base UI components and restrained tokens. Keep the primary invitation policy card short, with details progressively exposed; no decorative KPI wall. Public form is one column with generous labelled targets and no motion required to understand state. Neutral choices are visually equal. Tables collapse into readable labelled rows on mobile. Focus returns to the triggering control when panels close; assistive technology receives error, save and receipt status once. Long international names are never forced into Western first/last assumptions because the response form does not ask for them; RTL and long translated question labels wrap without clipping.

P33/P34/P39 require actual browser, assistive-technology and staff/requester usability proof. Research identifies a strong design direction; no screenshots or user tests have been fabricated.

### REQ26-D28-EMAIL_STUDIO_INTEGRATION-S0002 — Authority and ownership

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact/effect                                                                                                                 | Authoritative owner                                                       | D28 consequence                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Candidate, eligibility, sample, one opportunity, review obligation, response                                                | Support                                                                   | Neither template publication nor P6 transport decides who should be surveyed.                                               |
| Qualified recipient and source revision                                                                                     | Existing Party/contact or explicitly qualified Support no-Party authority | Matching email never proves identity or permissions.                                                                        |
| Contactability, absolute restrictions, provider/email suppression, purpose preference                                       | P3/shared contactability with P6 gate                                     | Register a narrow feedback-only opt-out; no Support consent copy.                                                           |
| Opaque normalized endpoint control                                                                                          | Qualified shared contactability/frequency owner                           | Support declares the 30-day feedback-purpose gap; owner supplies canonical tenant-scoped key and atomic control.            |
| Question/scale semantics and response postcondition                                                                         | Support's versioned instrument                                            | P17 wording cannot secretly change the scale/meaning; no arbitrary questionnaire.                                           |
| Invitation wording, Brand Kit, compatible role, team identity, purpose profile, protected visual component, compiled output | Email Studio/P17                                                          | Purpose-specific Tiptap authoring/validation and immutable preparation; no new renderer or Layout Role solely for feedback. |
| Credential issuance, expiry/revocation and one final response                                                               | Registered Support producer behind shared D6                              | New narrow no-Party branch, not a new token/doorway system.                                                                 |
| Feedback-only preference command                                                                                            | P3 registered producer behind shared D6                                   | Separate descriptor/state from rating; never consume the rating action to unsubscribe.                                      |
| Intent, submission may have begun, accepted/failed/unknown/provider evidence and reconciliation                             | P6                                                                        | Same permanent effect and immutable provider request; no fresh retry identity or survey-specific sender.                    |
| CRM/giving/receipts/refunds/missionary care facts                                                                           | Their current owners                                                      | Feedback records no business completion, sync profile or unrestricted context.                                              |

The P6 no-Party delivery clause already allows qualified endpoint delivery without manufacturing a Party. The current P17 Protected Actions wording still requires a Party/contact authority. This is an explicit conflict to resolve by a narrow registered Support-feedback recipient branch, preserving all other action requirements. The delivery exception is not automatically an action exception.

### REQ26-D28-EMAIL_STUDIO_INTEGRATION-S0003 — Exact invitation contract

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

Register one **Support feedback invitation** meaning with optional source policy, neutral fixed instrument revision, exact locale, approved team identity/reply route, source occurrence, recipient branch, presentation dependencies, protected response action and qualified feedback-preference action. Code/catalog chooses the keys; tenant JSON cannot register a new purpose or target.

Locale uses the qualified P17 recipient/source resolver and an explicitly authorized inbox/tenant fallback only; missing approved instrument translation fails readiness instead of silently changing the question language. The public protected page uses text identity and existing CSP-compatible styling, not remote logos/resources. The invitation uses the existing compatible human-facing organization role/Brand Kit. Do not impersonate a named personal responder or append a survey inside D23's ordinary signature. One main Give feedback CTA has the fixed shared-action presentation; the preference control is a distinct appropriately labelled secondary protected purpose. The P17 catalog already describes plural actions, but its current producer API/trigger binding is singular. Explicitly qualify this closed named pair in the DTO/adapter/manifest: per-slot issuer, purpose, recipient, lifetime, revocation, Used state and immutable pins/hash. Do not assume arbitrary multi-action support is implemented or introduce a tenant multi-action builder. A saved reply, Public Guidance link or internal guide cannot masquerade as either. Do not add a general ability for arbitrary tenant links to look like protected actions.

Email Studio may let qualified authors edit professional greeting/explanation within the purpose through the shared constrained Tiptap profile; protected question meaning/CTA/purpose/preference disclosures remain contract-owned. Validate original structured JSON and source purpose before normalization. Reject unrestricted HTML, arbitrary recipient placeholders, case attachments/private Guidance, promotion, hidden tracking and tenant-owned credential URLs. Editor preview uses synthetic non-redeemable descriptors. Publishing neither creates candidates nor enables sending. No rich editor is needed for the public plain comment field.

### REQ26-D28-EMAIL_STUDIO_INTEGRATION-S0004 — Preparation and submission sequence

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

1. Support qualifies the mature sampled opportunity, recipient, current policy/source/topology and finite utility. It never assumes a known CRM email or a Resolved row is enough.
2. P3 resolves actual current feedback contactability and owner endpoint key. A missing no-Party preference/action qualification blocks readiness; a transactional label cannot bypass it.
3. Support registers the exact response issuance; its frozen expiry is issued_at +14 elapsed days or an earlier owner ceiling. Response authority is inactive until the associated effect may have submitted. Distinct P3 preference issuance has a accepted 90-elapsed-day fixed lifetime from its own issue time, bounded by its own current contact/privacy authority. Its selector/verifier/session purpose is independent. Rating Used/expiry, conversation reopen/content expiry/deletion and ordinary Off do not revoke it. It can only stop feedback contact, never read private data, restore a preference or increase contact. A used response receipt cannot reconstruct/reissue the preference URL from purged P17 material; the original email’s footer remains independently usable. This is a bounded product judgment, not a norm. The grant cannot be a raw URL or reused response authority. The 90 days expires only the preference credential, never the resulting recorded opt-out. The P3 preference persists under its independently authorized lifecycle; policy Off→On, CRM merges, key rotation and new invitations cannot clear it or opt anyone back in.
4. P17 compiles the immutable purpose-qualified message and all action/material dependencies. Its optional-feedback prepared-material ceiling is no later than source send-by and earlier source/action/privacy limits. No live CMS or recipient rerender occurs at dispatch. The governed Reply-To and D1/D25 correlation keep an ordinary reply connected to the original permitted Support context; source unavailability follows existing safe intake, never reconstructs a transcript or infers a Party by email. A human email reply is distinct from the protected response form and may legitimately reopen work under D1.
5. Immediately before P6 crosses into possible submission, current Support policy/source/inbox/topology fences and the owner endpoint reservation must still permit the exact intent. Existing source-fence-before-intent locking is preserved; the new gate must be explicit conformance, not P6 reverse-reading arbitrary Support business state.
6. Possible submission consumes the opportunity and mailbox guard, even if the provider outcome is unknown. Off after that boundary cannot recall it. P6 reconciles the same permanent effect and frozen request; no blind retry/new key. Definitely-unsubmitted work expires at send-by, with no catch-up.
7. Qualified provider outcomes trigger P17's existing finality/material disposal. The canonical source email/response has its own finite content custody. Recent sent copy excludes action targets/verifiers/remote references and cannot be a resend archive.

P6 may reconcile uncertainty beyond delivery utility; it may not start a fresh optional send after utility expires. A response through an issued link is distinct evidence and cannot rewrite provider acceptance. The 30-day contact guard treats active possible crossings conservatively; hidden ambiguity does not free a slot early. Qualify a finite P6 latest-possible-crossing bound: after no future/in-flight crossing can occur and 30 days have elapsed from that bound, different genuine work may qualify despite irreducibly unknown historical outcome. Same-effect dedupe remains; no permanent endpoint block solely because provider history is unknown.

### REQ26-D28-EMAIL_STUDIO_INTEGRATION-S0005 — Shared protected doorway and response

Applies to **US26-D28-04**, acceptance **AC26-D28-04-01–03**.

Preserve P17's exact existing doorway/session contract: selector-only inert GET/HEAD, independent 256-bit verifier in the fragment, pinned minimal script removing it from visible history and preparing—but never auto-submitting—a same-origin form. Generic GET reveals no tenant, resource, action type or terminal state. Explicit Continue POST validates and establishes the bounded non-authorizing landing session. Only subsequent deliberate Submit feedback POST can perform Support's one final response command.

The no-Party assurance is **explicit_confirmation_with_source_authorization**, limited to the exact invitation/endpoint/source/tenant/environment and response/preference purpose. It proves possession of the invitation, not a logged-in human or CRM identity. It grants no access to transcript, prior comment, Party, gift, resource or portal. Do not turn it into an exception for financial/private actions.

If the actual registered optional feedback classification requires unsubscribe headers, qualify the existing exact RFC8058 contract and adapter-owned DKIM-covered headers for that purpose; do not borrow marketing semantics or invent headers in Support. The visible browser preference action remains separately qualified. Retain exact current no-referrer/no-store/CDN no-store/CSP, trusted origin/path, CSRF/Fetch-Metadata, HMAC/digest key versions, short server-side session, revoke/expiry/used cleanup and code-owned recovery. No alternate URL, query-string token, hosted external survey or analytics script. Response form submission needs one rating, optional bounded plain comment and current expected state. Same payload reconciles one receipt; changed input cannot replay Used authority. GET/HEAD flood cannot consume a response.

The two deliberate steps are a documented cost of the existing privacy contract. Do not promise a one-click survey or weaken it silently. If later research proposes changing that shared doorway, it requires a separate owner decision; D28 is fully viable with the present one.

### REQ26-D28-EMAIL_STUDIO_INTEGRATION-S0006 — Required owner amendments before activation

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

1. **P17 catalog/presentation:** new optional Support-feedback invitation profile, instrument/locale binding, protected response and preference controls, neutral team identity and finite prepared-material class.
2. **P17/D6 recipient branch:** explicitly qualified invitation-bound no-Party Support-feedback action, with no grant to other actions or private records.
3. **P3 purpose/contactability:** shared feedback-only opt-out, no-Party endpoint authority, versioned opaque contact control and current provider restrictions, independent of marketing/service permissions.
4. **P6 producer conformance:** immutable source occurrence, immediate policy/inbox/source/topology gate, atomic endpoint reservation, finite utility and possible-submission reconciliation under existing lock/order/outbox contracts.
5. **Support privacy/CRM:** finite comment/rating/control inventory and source-authorized same-detail projection, without duplicate history or body storage.

All are small extensions of actual existing owners. None requires Phase 34's generic workflow/form builder, a new CRM, new email provider or AI. P18–P28 proof groups and the independent owner review qualify these seams before a real tenant can enable invitations.

### REQ26-D28-DATA_CONTRACT-S0003 — Minimal logical records and constraints

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Logical record                      | Required facts and constraints                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Mutation/retention authority                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Feedback policy revision            | Tenant, current enabled/sending epoch, integer percentage 1–100, qualified inbox scope, accountable owner/review coverage, expected revision, server actor/time. Unique current head, immutable revision history. Off is a sending state, not percent 0 stored as a second competing control.                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Qualified tenant policy command; finite configuration/audit owner policy.                                                                                                                                                                |
| Completion candidate                | Tenant, immutable original conversation, resolution generation, actual completion instant, frozen policy percent/revision, scope/source proof refs, due_at/send_by. Unique tenant+original+generation. No draw yet. No counterfeited old completion on enablement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Support source command and generation-safe scheduler. Terminal candidates retain minimal evidence only under qualified custody.                                                                                                          |
| Feedback opportunity                | Tenant+original conversation unique lifetime key; one candidate source, eligibility evidence, sample algorithm version, integer draw 0–9999, frozenpercent 1–100 and immutable selected outcome. For a sampled branch require selected=(draw<percent×100); for immutable linked-suppression the locally sampled percentage/draw/outcome fields are null and require no local draw and a same-tenant source-opportunity reference. Exactly one branch is allowed, and none can later change branch. | One server transaction; no user update to source/draw/scope.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Invitation effect reference         | Tenant, unique opportunity, stable P6 occurrence/intent identity, exact original/source/current fences, issued action ref, send_by and body-free status projection. No plaintext recipient, bearer token or provider request body.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Support/P6 qualified commands and source proof, no direct generic status updates.                                                                                                                                                        |
| Endpoint contact guard              | Tenant+environment+owner canonical opaque mailbox key; owning reservation/generation, current possible-submission identity/time, active crossing guard and last bounded possible-crossing instant. Atomic unique owner key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Shared contactability/frequency owner; a still-permitted/in-flight crossing stays guarded; irreducibly unknown history alone is not an indefinite suppression after qualified closure of all possible crossings and the 30 day interval. |
| Protected response issuance/session | Exact D6 descriptor, tenant/environment, source invitation/endpoint-authority revision, digest/keyversion, issued/expiry/revoke/used state and bounded server session. No raw verifier at rest in normal logs/history.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Registered producer under existing P6/P17 protocol; issuer owns finite validity and disposal.                                                                                                                                            |
| Feedback response                   | Tenant, unique invitation, fixed question revision, one closed rating, optional bounded ordinary content occurrence, server submitted_at, permanent receipt/hash of semantic input, attribution=invitation possession. Not a caller-specified Party/author.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Atomic response command; no UPDATE score. D16/D17 govern restriction/content expiry with separately attributed correction/exclusion.                                                                                                     |
| Review evidence                     | Tenant, source response, current Needs review/Reviewed projection, authoritative reviewer/time/expectedrevision, reason for any separate qualified privacy/abuse exclusion. One initial review obligation per admitted response.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Current permitted Support review command; does not mutate work status or donor score.                                                                                                                                                    |
| P3 feedback preference              | Source-owned tenant/endpoint/purpose preference and independent preference action descriptor, not a Support consent flag.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Shared contactability owner, no grant to marketing/service or CRM records.                                                                                                                                                               |

Tenant foreign keys must include or otherwise enforce the tenant component all the way through inbox, original, candidate, opportunity, effect, response and review. Nullability is explicit: a qualified no-Party delivery has null Party/contact fields and a required no-Party source reference; a Party/contact branch requires its actual refs. Neither branch may silently become the other through UPDATE. No polymorphic string pair without enforced owner validation may point anywhere in the database. Restrict deletion that would erase needed origin/authority evidence; invoke qualified privacy disposal rather than generic cascades. Historical actors may reference retained opaque actor attribution without preserving an active user login. Rating enums and integer percentage/draw checks have database constraints. No money field, floating currency value, gift amount or donor-value selector is added.

Tables exposed to authenticated roles need explicit narrow grants and RLS aligned with actual scopes; security-sensitive mutations use authoritative commands. Verify SELECT and mutations independently: a permitted old row must not be transformable into a forbidden new row. Explicit USING/WITH CHECK, column privileges and immutable-field constraints must express the intended boundary. PostgreSQL can reuse USING when WITH CHECK is omitted; omission is not automatically a hole, but relying on a broad same-tenant predicate does not constrain state/actor/ownership. Security-definer functions require qualified need, fixed search_path, schema-qualified objects and revoked ambient execution; views need correctly proven invoker/definer behavior. Service-role use is not evidence of authorization and must reprove the same owner context. Public feedback is a narrow command endpoint, never anonymous direct-table insert.

### REQ26-D28-DATA_CONTRACT-S0004 — Exact sampling population and algorithm

Applies to **US26-D28-02**, acceptance **AC26-D28-02-01–03**.

The user-facing percentage is a probability among matured eligible original-conversation opportunities. It is not a percentage of unique donors, all Support records or each worker's conversations. One donor may have multiple independent conversations; one mailbox may represent several people; one person may use aliases. Core must not invent identity resolution to convert this into a person survey.

At a genuine eligible ordinary completion while On, atomically record a candidate and frozen percentage/current source generation. Scheduler maturity at 24h checks current source state and qualification. Current absence of proof excludes safely; it is not filled from CRM or AI. A late worker may process only before due+24h and uses the frozen candidate percentage. It must not pretend it ran at due or reset the deadline. Reopened candidates before maturity are invalid; only a new genuine completion can create another candidate while no opportunity exists.

Before any draw, lock current D10 topology and examine all original opportunity dispositions. Among multiple unsampled eligible candidates, choose earliest genuine completion then stable original ID. Any current-component prior opportunity—including Not selected—prevents a second chance from another original. Record immutable linked-suppression for eligible losing originals, with no draw and a required original-opportunity reference; never key identity to a mutable root. Two independent draws committed before merge remain historical; Undo cannot revive suppressed origins. At mature admission for the chosen eligible representative, generate one unbiased cryptographic draw in 0–9999, commit the original opportunity, draw/outcome/evidence and continuation in one transaction. Example 25% selects 0–2499;2500–9999 is Not selected. At 100%, every eligible opportunity is selected but current contactability/cooldown/gates still apply. A duplicate unique-key loser retrieves the admitted decision. Repeated job IDs, policy updates, old callbacks, merge/Undo and restore never generate another draw.

After sampling, any relevant reopen/new input before submission cancels the pending invitation generation; a later completion cannot resurrect it or generate a new opportunity. Cooldown-blocked selected work is **Skipped**, not scheduled for 30 days later. A skipped/not-selected/cancelled original remains consumed. This biases the eventual sent population toward first eligible completed opportunities and away from repeat contact; report that limit, rather than claim all interactions are equally represented.

Sampling by itself does not cap burst size. P6's existing pacing and tenant/provider fairness protect required/service mail; D28 adds no competing throttle. At 25%, one mailbox with 10 independent eligible opportunities has about 94.37% chance of at least one selection before contact protection. This exact arithmetic explains why sampling and the 30 day guard are separate, not why a particular donor will receive a survey.

### REQ26-D28-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — Lifecycle and races

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State/action                        | Valid outcome                                                                                                                                   | Forbidden outcome                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy Off                          | No new candidate; current gate cancels definitely-unsubmitted work. Existing issued response windows remain as stated.                          | Hidden pending batch continues or historical candidates revive on On.                                               |
| Candidate waiting                   | Before due, no sample; source reopen invalidates generation.                                                                                    | Same-state update/label/guide use resets quiet time or creates draw.                                                |
| Candidate mature and qualified      | One opportunity and frozen draw; selected or not selected.                                                                                      | Worker-time percent, retry RNG or caller-provided source identity.                                                  |
| Selected before submission          | Current source/policy/topology/contactability/material checks; exact endpoint reservation.                                                      | Selection is treated as unconditional sending entitlement.                                                          |
| Reopen after draw                   | Cancel definitely-unsubmitted effect; retain consumed original opportunity.                                                                     | Stored selected result reused on a later close.                                                                     |
| Two endpoint contenders             | Existing owner lock/admission serializes; one wins, other skips.                                                                                | Both pass a preview-only guard and send.                                                                            |
| Merge pending work                  | Lock current topology; retain earliest completion then stableID winner; suppress rest.                                                          | Use mutable canonical root as new idempotency key.                                                                  |
| Submission may have begun           | Durable issued cohort and active endpoint guard; P6 reconciles exact effect.                                                                    | Timeout frees slot, new provider key or fake recall.                                                                |
| Known accepted/failed evidence      | P6 reduction follows exact proven outcome; history remains separate from feedback.                                                              | Rating implies delivery accepted or absence of response implies mail failed.                                        |
| Send-by reached                     | Expire definitely-unsubmitted utility; continue truthful possible-effect reconciliation.                                                        | Start a fresh optional send after cutoff or renew deadline.                                                         |
| Issued response active              | D6 deliberate authenticated-by-capability handoff; one valid response command.                                                                  | GET vote, preview redemption, transcript/CRM access or identity claim.                                              |
| Response committed                  | One Used action/receipt/review obligation; same-payload retry idempotent.                                                                       | Second score, changed replay overwrite or staff impersonation.                                                      |
| Response expiry/revocation race     | Serialize with response command; whichever authoritative transition wins determines receipt; earlier admitted response preserved under privacy. | Later write through expired/revoked authority or backdated expiry deleting accepted evidence without owner process. |
| Link/Party merge/unlink             | Recompute current authorized navigation; original response attribution stays honest.                                                            | New CRM score/person identity or invitation.                                                                        |
| Source restriction/deletion/restore | Suppress ordinary access promptly, dispose under inventory, restore fences before serve.                                                        | Reload old transcript/comment/capability from a backup or cache.                                                    |

P3’s independent stop-feedback preference issuance uses a accepted 90-elapsed-day fixed lifetime from its own issue time, shortened by its own source/contact/privacy ceiling. It remains valid across response Used/14-day expiry, Support content expiry/deletion and policy Off; it cannot read records or opt a person back in. Its grant/key/session scope is independent of the response, and both descriptors must be qualified in the closed P17 pair. The 90 days expires only the preference credential, never the resulting recorded opt-out. The P3 preference persists under its independently authorized lifecycle; policy Off→On, CRM merges, key rotation and new invitations cannot clear it or opt anyone back in. The 30 day instant is measured from source-owned submission-may-have-begun, not local UI click, template save, provider-delivery timestamp or response. Known non-submission can release an exact reservation; an actual attempted effect remains one opportunity. P6 must qualify a finite latest-possible-crossing bound and proof that no old permitted/in-flight crossing remains. Until then, hold the contact guard. After that proof and 30 days from that bound, a new genuinely independent opportunity may pass even if the old outcome remains indeterminate. Retain same-effect dedupe/history under their own finite custody; unknown historical success cannot hold a mailbox or contact-key record indefinitely. Do not release early from a timeout. A delayed definitive provider event does not renew the 30 days by its arrival time.

### REQ26-D28-DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — Response and reporting integrity

Applies to **US26-D28-04**, acceptance **AC26-D28-04-01–03**.

The fixed neutral instrument is a versioned Support fact. Invitation text may be localized/professionally edited within P17 bounds, but cannot change the rating scale. Store the one final response, not a chain of public overwrites. A changed retry conflicts; a separate privacy/correction path records its own actor and reason. No submitted comment is echoed to someone reopening a forwarded bearer link. A response can arrive while the provider outcome is still indeterminate; do not falsely mark it accepted by the provider.

Define **issued invitations** as distinct invitation effects whose submission may have begun. The displayed response fraction is **unique responded issued invitations / issued invitations in that same cohort**, with counts and inclusion dates. Accepted, rejected/failed, indeterminate and delivered evidence remain separate facts beneath that cohort. This definition cannot exceed 100% solely because a response precedes provider acceptance evidence. Excluded/redacted ratings have explicit denominator treatment; no staff mutation secretly makes the score improve. Satisfaction share, when shown, is Satisfied / all currently includable submitted ratings with that denominator visible. Current filters authorize source rows before counts/snippets/exports.

Use both explicit invitation-cohort reporting and separate received-date response browsing. A cohort becomes complete only after all its original response windows have ended or been validly terminated. Delayed receipt processing must use actual accepted response occurrence/receipt, not silently slide results into another cohort. Small samples are shown as counts; the 20 response/28 day operating caution is not a statistical guarantee. No response equals missing feedback, not neutral or satisfied. Do not weight or infer donations/agent performance from these samples.

### REQ26-D28-DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — Privacy inventory and activation gate

Applies to **US26-D28-07**, acceptance **AC26-D28-07-01–03**.

The complete release inventory must name purpose, floor, ceiling, restriction/hold behavior, deletion/restore proof and owner for: policy/audit revisions; candidates and skipped decisions; opportunity/effect tombstones; recipient control keys; response action digests/sessions; independent preference tokens/preferences; rating/comment/question version; review/correction/exclusion history; P17 sealed bytes; actual P6 communication facts; search/report caches; exports; notifications; backups and technical telemetry.

Rating/comment have their own feedback-review purpose from server submission. The old conversation’s Resolved timestamp cannot end that new purpose. Qualified Mark reviewed records its purpose end unless a genuinely continuing existing follow-up needs the source; D17’s active-purpose review safeguards and the qualified finite interval then apply, with earlier owner ceilings. Routine views, links or corrections cannot renew expired authority; an unexamined pending review cannot become an indefinite archive. Test a new response to old Resolved work under a short finite interval. They never reopen work, reset older source clocks or renew an expired transcript. Ratings/attribution/control metadata are personal or linkable, not automatically anonymous; retain only within their explicit owner purpose. Minimal tombstones can prevent replay only under their finite qualified source/control custody; when a whole original source legitimately disappears, no recreation/backfill may rebuild a new opportunity from old events. P3 suppression can outlive the comment where the actual contact-control purpose requires it, with restricted opaque references; it is not a free indefinite analytics store.

No new universal numerical retention period is invented for Support bodies. If the tenant has not qualified a finite D17 policy and actual metadata/control inventory, feedback cannot be enabled. P17 send-by/material ceilings and D6 action expiry are narrower independent limits, not content retention defaults. Holds can preserve required bytes in restricted custody while ordinary display expires. Exports/backups/derived data follow the same restriction/restore invariants rather than generic DELETE cascades.

## Contact-first requester Help

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — The experience to build

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

Opening Help or Contact takes a person directly to **Contact [tenant public name]**. They see who will receive the message, a short form, and the tenant's actual published contact methods. They can send without reading anything else. Relevant guides are available for people who prefer information, with no suggestion that they ought to try harder before asking for help.

The first screen should feel calm: a familiar Asym/app or tenant-public shell, one clear heading, short explanatory copy, a readable form, and generous space around the primary action. Use existing components and tokens. Authenticated app UI uses the approved **Base UI / base-maia** implementation and Maia/Zinc styling. Public Web Studio presentation retains its qualified tenant/theme owner; this decision does not override its theme authority or create another component library.

Illustrative composition, not a frozen breakpoint or pixel specification:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Contact [tenant public name]
> Send our team a message.
> 
> Email for our reply *               Prefer email?
> [                            ]      [published email address]
>                                     [Copy email]
> How can we help? *
> [                            ]      Phone, when actually offered
> [                            ]      [published number and hours]
> [                            ]
>                                     Helpful guides
> Name (optional)                     [Relevant guide title ↗]
> [                            ]      [Relevant guide title ↗]
> 
> [Send message]

On a wide screen, direct methods and optional guides may occupy a restrained secondary column. On a narrow screen, the reading order is heading → form → direct methods → guides. The directly reachable form remains the primary path; direct methods are plainly labelled rather than buried in footer navigation. No hero image, fixed chat bubble, introductory animation, welcome tour, large card grid or tab chooser is needed. Existing shell navigation remains consistent. The precise responsive layout is qualified against X01 rather than exposed as tenant configuration.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Content and controls

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Element              | Required behavior and purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Heading              | **Contact [tenant public name]** identifies the recipient. Use the current qualified public identity, never a guessed organization name or private staff address.                                                                                                          |
| Intro                | A brief invitation such as **Send our team a message.** Avoid invented availability, response deadlines, staffing or service guarantees.                                                                                                                                   |
| Reply email          | Visible label **Email for our reply**; required. Support the exact qualified P6 mailbox/parser profile. Do not silently correct aliases or claim that a typed address verifies identity.                                                                                   |
| Message              | Visible label **How can we help?**; required plain-text multiline control. No editor toolbar or upload prerequisite. Place concise privacy guidance beside the field only where it helps avoid sensitive credentials/payment information; do not insert a compliance wall. |
| Name                 | One optional unsplit **Name** field. No first/last-name split, required surname or forced Western ordering. Optional is explicit.                                                                                                                                          |
| Limits               | Preserve R04: 10,000 Unicode scalar message, 200 scalar optional name, newline normalization, and the separate 256 KiB raw-request ceiling. Explain an exceeded field limit beside that field; do not use a UTF-16-only HTML maxlength as the authority.                   |
| Primary action       | **Send message**. Clear pending feedback; no layout jump, timed toast-only success or repeated-submit affordance during an unresolved attempt.                                                                                                                             |
| Direct email         | Show the complete selectable published address with a normal mailto link. Copy is a helpful enhancement with brief accessible confirmation. Failure to copy leaves the address available. No private-context mailto body.                                                  |
| Phone                | Show only an actual deliberately published channel. Use international format and accurate named-zone hours if the tenant provides them. Do not imply a staffed live line or callback service.                                                                              |
| Guidance             | Zero to three ordered, relevant Listed public Page references, using current source titles and eligible destinations. No empty placeholder section when there are none. No automated recommendations, popularity feed or copied article body.                              |
| Guide link           | Plain labelled link; disclose **opens in a new tab** accessibly, with no opener/referrer. The external-link icon supplements a meaningful title. No article-reading modal or nested knowledge browser.                                                                     |
| Optional app context | One readable, removable summary of context currently authorized to be included. Never display an opaque record ID as if it explains the request.                                                                                                                           |

Only reply email and message are required. There is no required subject, topic, department, donor ID, account, phone, address, marketing consent, screenshot or attachment. Existing contextual-help and content capabilities elsewhere remain available; this contact profile is intentionally bounded.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Journey 1 — a guest wants to contact the tenant

Applies to **US26-D29-01**, acceptance **AC26-D29-01-01–03**.

1. The person selects **Contact [tenant]** from the relevant public surface. The ordinary full page and native form are immediately usable. A slow or unavailable optional guide cannot delay a separately qualified contact form.
2. They enter their reply email and message; name is optional. Field labels remain visible after input. Browser autofill is user-supplied convenience, never trusted proof or a CRM update.
3. They select **Send message**. The same authority validates both native and enhanced submission. On field errors, keep permitted text, show a concise error summary linked to each affected field, and move focus deliberately once. Avoid premature errors while someone is still entering an address.
4. The server admits one durable Contact occurrence and Support responsibility before returning **Your message has been received.** This is a persistent page/state with a meaningful heading, not a disappearing toast. It does not claim that email was delivered, staff read it, a refund was processed or the issue was solved.
5. Successful submission clears the app-managed draft. A new message requires a deliberate new intent; browser refresh or a duplicated request retrieves the same privacy-safe outcome rather than creating another request.

No guide interaction or optional confirmation email is required for this successful journey. For someone preferring their own mail client, the published email is always an ordinary alternative. Selecting email/phone opens the relevant client where supported; it does not create a Support record or prove that a message/call occurred. If a client is unavailable, the selectable address/number and the form remain understandable alternatives.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Journey 2 — a person wants information first

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

1. The person opens the same Contact page and notices a relevant **Helpful guides** link. The form and direct methods are already available.
2. They open that selected guide in its labelled new tab. The source owner renders its current public Page; Support does not copy or embed the article.
3. They return to the original tab. Under ordinary browser navigation, their draft and place remain. Opening a guide never sends, clears or reroutes the form. This is not a promise to recover a tab discarded by the browser/OS, and it introduces no localStorage or offline queue.
4. If the guide answered the question, they simply stop. Asym does not create a request, claim a resolution, update CRM last-contact, ask for ticket feedback or count a deflection from the click alone.
5. If they still want help, they submit normally. There is no **Not helpful** gate, forced search, bot handoff or second set of intake fields.

A removed, unlisted, internal, Shared-by-link, wrong-locale or unqualified guide is omitted. Do not silently replace it with another article or language. Zero guides is a complete product state. A source-wide/host/form failure is different: only a separately qualified contact route may remain available; a guide-only fallback rule cannot authorize stale or guessed contact facts.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Journey 3 — a signed-in donor, missionary or staff requester

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

These roles are possible users, not evidence that every ministry runs the same workflow.

1. **Contact [tenant]** appears consistently within the app-owned Help entry. An existing app panel may enhance the full-page form where qualified; a stable full-page route remains usable. Do not force a new panel system.
2. Prefill only the actual requester's currently authorized self data, visibly and editably. Do not substitute a related person's or represented organization's mailbox. Show a relevant authorized context summary only when available, with **Remove**.
3. The requester edits their reply address or removes context without navigating to CRM. Those actions change this submission only; they neither update contact records nor prove control of an identity or organization.
4. Recheck context and authority at admission. If only context becomes unavailable, remove forbidden source context/prefill and preserve only permitted visitor-authored text for deliberate requalification or **contact without account details**. Never silently downgrade and send.
5. A real logout, tenant or account switch clears the entire managed draft/prefill/context. Never carry it to another person or tenant. Receipt and private context are not public-cacheable content.
6. The same truthful receipt and independently qualified Support handoff apply. No additional proof of identity is demanded merely to ask an ordinary question; the owning domain may require it before a consequential action or disclosure.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Journey 4 — staff continue through Support and CRM

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

1. Authorized staff see the native **form-origin** requester message in Support, with the actual submitted response endpoint and permitted origin/context. It must not look like fabricated incoming email or a private staff note.
2. If a CRM relationship is authorized and established, **Communications → Support** and the appropriate limited CRM Overview surface show/access the same canonical Support source. Preserve list position, context and a return route when moving between surfaces. Do not copy the conversation into a second editable Activity.
3. If identity is absent or ambiguous, staff can still care for the request within their authority. A matching email, shared mailbox, forwarded message or record association does not prove identity, representation or unrestricted CRM access.
4. A first human email reply uses the qualified form-response recipient basis and real outgoing lineage. A real compatible acknowledgement thread may be continued; otherwise this is the first outgoing email. Do not synthesize incoming headers to satisfy an email-shaped adapter.
5. CRM, giving, receipts, refunds, recurring gifts, contact changes and member-care actions retain their owning permissions, validation, approval and audit history. Support may navigate to or initiate an authorized owner workflow, then reflect its actual result. Closing the request does not assert that the requested business action succeeded.
6. Existing Support reply/internal-note distinctions and recipient/attachment checks remain in force. D34 composing cues are staff-only advisory state; nothing in this public contact entry exposes a teammate's composition to the requester.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Journey 5 — interruption and recovery

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Situation                                         | User-visible result                                                 | Required behavior behind it                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Definite validation rejection                     | Specific field correction, text preserved where permitted           | No accepted primary exists; correct input before a new valid attempt.                                                                                                    |
| Lost/ambiguous submission response                | **Checking whether your message was received**                      | Reconcile the same durable intent; no blind rekey, duplicate request or alternate-email fallback.                                                                        |
| Accepted but conversation materialization delayed | Persistent **Received**                                             | Accepted work is discoverable to its authorized recovery owner and materializes once from original admission/route evidence. A queue notification alone is insufficient. |
| Optional confirmation delayed/failed              | Browser receipt remains valid                                       | Separate child outcome; do not say email was sent or ask the requester to resubmit.                                                                                      |
| JavaScript unavailable                            | Native form and full-page error/receipt                             | Same source, validation, idempotency and acceptance authority; no permissive shadow endpoint.                                                                            |
| Optional guide absent/unavailable                 | Contact remains, guide omitted                                      | Only where the required contact closure is independently qualified.                                                                                                      |
| Whole required source/route unsafe                | Clear unavailable state; actual qualified alternatives if available | No stale identity/route fallback and no success claim.                                                                                                                   |
| Rate/backpressure control applies                 | Understandable retry/recovery and retained permitted text           | Bound parsing and tenant-fair work; accessible risk-based protection, no blanket puzzle or infinite spinner.                                                             |

No offline **will send later** promise. Retrying must be tied to the actual durable result. The existing original proof groups include no-JavaScript, request races, source changes and privacy revocation; these are required implementation outcomes.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — Journey 6 — tenant maintenance without another studio

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

The tenant gets one **Requester help** entry showing the actual public/app placements, currently published contact methods, destination/readiness and optional guide selections. It is an inventory and navigation surface over real owners, not another content/template database.

1. Select the exact Help placement and see its current owner/source/release state.
2. Configure or repair contact identity/methods and the certified Contact-purpose Support route using their real Web Studio/app/Support owner actions. Display **Not ready** honestly where a required dependency is unqualified.
3. Select zero to three eligible public guides; show their current title, destination and order. Selection changes are distinct from editing or withdrawing the source Page. Provide keyboard reorder controls, not drag-only interaction.
4. Preview with synthetic content and exercise a no-write routing check. Preview must not create a form occurrence, send mail, mint requester links or write CRM history.
5. Publish/activate through the actual owner. Public and app releases have separate acknowledgements/readiness; no misleading single badge claims a distributed atomic release.
6. Enable or disable the single optional **Visitor Acknowledgement** through the existing Contact form / Route Plan **Confirmation** owner in P23; it starts Off and requires its qualified web-Contact profile. Use **Edit in Email Studio** for compatible wording, presentation and Live publication. Publishing a template alone never enables the child. Browser receipt remains independent. There is no duplicate template editor or second confirmation switch.
7. Repair withdrawn guides or a changed contact method through the owning release path. Removing the last guide is ordinary and safe. Already accepted requests retain their exact original route and recovery responsibility. A departing maintainer is replaced through qualified ownership; staff never need SQL to change public copy.

### REQ26-D29-REFRESH_UX_BLUEPRINT-S0011 — Qualification of clarity and visual quality

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

Beauty here means careful typography, hierarchy, alignment, spacing and states in the approved theme, with no decorative competition around the task. Meaning must not depend on color, hover or animation. Honor reduced motion; feedback should be calm and purposeful. Long names, addresses and translated labels wrap without concealing actions. All labels and errors are localizable; times use the relevant declared zone rather than a guessed local offset.

Add X01's separate **200% text resize**, **320 CSS-pixel reflow/400% zoom**, focus-obstruction, target-size and virtual-keyboard journey proof. Test actual initial/error/receipt screens and named browser/assistive-technology combinations, not only a narrow screenshot. See exact supplemental proof.

The existing moderated journey proof P44 must observe people choosing contact immediately, optionally reading and returning, correcting errors, changing self-prefill, handling context-only loss, coping without phone/JavaScript, and maintaining the last guide. These remain **unexecuted release tests**. This research does not prove a perfect interface, measure tenant satisfaction or authorize publishing untested screens.

### REQ26-D29-R01 — D29-R01 Purpose, priority and alternatives

Applies to **US26-D29-01**, acceptance **AC26-D29-01-01–03**.

Contact is the primary job of this Help entry; guidance is optional. Contact remains complete when no useful guide is available. Do not add a public browsable/searchable library, a public version of Internal Staff guides, AI or other channels. Guidance must reduce an avoidable round trip without gating direct contact.

### REQ26-D29-R02 — D29-R02 Direct entry and clear contact affordance

Applies to **US26-D29-01**, acceptance **AC26-D29-01-01–03**.

The existing qualified Help/Contact entry SHALL open **Contact [tenant public name]** with the form available immediately, not a search-first, department-first or channel-choice gate. Keep the entry consistent within each actual surface and preserve the user's return location. A full-page semantic route is always available; an app may enhance it with its existing accessible panel/sheet pattern without making the enhancement a prerequisite. On narrow screens contact precedes optional guides. No “Have you tried the articles?” step, forced article rating, countdown, empty bot conversation or unearned online indicator.

### REQ26-D29-R03 — D29-R03 Minimal replyable form

Applies to **US26-D29-01**, acceptance **AC26-D29-01-01–03**.

Qualify one narrow ordinary-inquiry Purpose Profile, not claimed to exist already: **Email for our reply** and **How can we help?** are required; **Name (optional)** is one unsplit field. No mandatory subject, surname, donor/account number, organization, phone, topic, department, address, screenshot, login, marketing consent or checkbox asserting articles were tried. This Help form is text-only and payment/upload-free under P23. Tenants may adjust qualified labels, explanatory copy and locale, but may not turn this standard entry into a questionnaire or change field meaning. Other P23 form purposes retain their own broader lawful customization.

### REQ26-D29-R04 — D29-R04 Validation and bounded input

Applies to **US26-D29-01**, acceptance **AC26-D29-01-01–03**.

Message is nonblank plain text, up to 10,000 Unicode scalar values after CRLF/CR normalization to LF; optional name is up to 200 scalars. Preserve international names, combining characters, punctuation and line breaks; no Western name splitting or English-only rules. Validate one reply mailbox through the current qualified P6/contactability parser and its actual supported length/encoding contract; no silent alias folding, typo “fix,” CRM replacement or claim that syntax proves ownership. Enforce a 256 KiB raw request-body ceiling before expensive parsing, plus the exact released envelope/field limits. These are accepted product bounds, not industry norms. Show visible labels, explain the optional field and keep entered answers on recoverable validation error. Client hints cannot narrow legitimate server-supported mailbox input or substitute for server validation.

### REQ26-D29-R05 — D29-R05 Public direct contact methods

Applies to **US26-D29-01**, acceptance **AC26-D29-01-01–03**.

The tenant deliberately publishes a monitored email for ordinary contact; managed Support addresses reference their qualified D25 route/public identity rather than staff/admin/login/billing email. Show selectable address text and optional Copy email enhancement alongside the mailto link. Offer phone only from deliberately published tenant contact data with a current accountable maintainer; display an international dialable number and readable formatting. Do not require a phone service or infer staffing, 24/7 availability, callback, geographic reach or live presence. A click only opens the person's external client; it proves no call/email or Support request. Published display data cannot establish P23 Verified Email Destination authority.

### REQ26-D29-R06 — D29-R06 Small contextual guide selection

Applies to **US26-D29-02**, acceptance **AC26-D29-02-01–03**.

Each qualified Help entry may select zero to three exact public Page references in a deliberate order. Use current source-owned title and optional safe summary with a canonical source-qualified destination; no copied article body or editable shadow content. Context means an explicit owner-approved page/task/entry key, not donor value, role-based public content, private records, referrer text, browsing history, URL query or AI inference. No dynamic “popular” list, mandatory search, fallback to unrelated articles or tenant-authored matching rules. Reject a fourth selection at configuration rather than silently dropping it at runtime.

### REQ26-D29-R07 — D29-R07 Public eligibility and withdrawal

Applies to **US26-D29-02**, acceptance **AC26-D29-02-01–03**.

Public discovery requires current exact Tenant/environment/Site/locale/public-generation and **Listed** source eligibility, source safety and valid canonical destination. D27's staff finder allowing Shared by link does not grant requester discovery. Internal guide titles/body/history/search and draft/preview content never enter this population. A source withdrawal/reach/locale change removes its offer without substituting another guide; restoring source eligibility may restore an unchanged active selection, but cannot recreate a deliberately removed selection. Unknown proof is unavailable, not a reason to broaden scope or use a stale cache.

### REQ26-D29-R08 — D29-R08 Source-owned presentation and optional failure containment

Applies to **US26-D29-02**, acceptance **AC26-D29-02-01–03**.

Public placements belong to P23's released Page intent. Explicitly qualify a bounded **Optional Help guides** semantic leaf over at most three Page refs, its renderer/contract version and prequalified empty/unavailable presentation. P23's initial Article dynamic-source catalog is not already a Page-help qualification. P23’s accepted Page-intent release contract still releases one complete generation; the leaf's current adverse/source admission may suppress ineligible items without rewriting saved selection, inserting replacements or changing the contact route. The contact form/direct-contact closure is a required separate dependency; a guide-only failure suppresses only the optional leaf. Unsafe whole-Page/base/renderer/form authority is not bypassed by serving a partial generation; an independent safe Contact route is usable only under its own current qualification. This is explicit P23 conformance, not arbitrary runtime template patching.

### REQ26-D29-R09 — D29-R09 Safe reading and return

Applies to **US26-D29-02**, acceptance **AC26-D29-02-01–03**.

Present guides as clear links, with a concise visible/screen-reader indication that **Open guide** opens a new tab. Use ordinary user-activated anchors with noopener/no-referrer protection; no on-load popup, miniature renderer of arbitrary CMS forms/embeds or automatic article query. The contact form stays intact in its current page. Browser-default tab/window controls remain available. A source link can explain how to use an authenticated owner action, but the guide grants no receipt, giving, identity or care authority. No guide click creates a ticket, “resolved” event, deflection claim, feedback invitation or CRM contact history.

### REQ26-D29-R10 — D29-R10 Separate public and authenticated app consumers

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

The public adapter derives scope from trusted public host/route/current P23 generation and exact released form. The app adapter derives current portal/app tenant/principal, approved entry and exact purpose/route binding through its owner. Qualify both against one common Contact purpose/occurrence/Support handoff contract; no second submissions ledger. A portal host is not a public Site; a browser-supplied Site/tenant/form ID cannot establish scope. App guidance references use qualified published public content without personalizing CMS body/list output. Public and app releases have their own receipts/readiness; do not claim a cross-owner atomic publish or silently read an unreleased mutable “latest” configuration.

### REQ26-D29-R11 — D29-R11 Prefill and shared-device safety

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

An app may visibly prefill the current actual requester's authorized self-contact information; never default to a represented organization's, linked donor's or CRM owner's address. Email remains reviewable/editable and is a submitted response endpoint, not a CRM mutation or verified identity assertion. Public anonymous content stays auth-invariant. Bind draft/prefill to current tenant, entry and local principal/session context; clear the full draft on successful receipt, deliberate logout or tenant/account change. On context-only permission/revision loss, remove unqualified context references and source-derived prefill while preserving only still-permitted visitor-authored text for deliberate requalification or reviewed contact without account details. No persistent browser storage, device-ID history, tracking identity or hidden autosave for this form. During a recoverable same-context failure preserve local answers.
