Session expiry must offer qualified reauthentication or deliberate ordinary contact without private account context; never silently retarget a private draft to another actor or submit stale record references.

### REQ26-D29-R12 — D29-R12 Optional authorized context

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

App-origin Help may present one concise **About [permitted context]** summary of its actual owner-qualified context reference, removable before submit. It is optional to ordinary contact. Server rechecks current authorization, tenant and source revision when accepting it; a plain hidden field, route parameter or matching email is insufficient. Invalid context requires a clear retry/requalification or deliberate **Send without account details** path preserving permitted visitor-authored text; never quietly attach another record. No private names, financial facts, processor IDs, screenshots or raw URLs are copied into public guide selection, search, mailto, analytics or the P23 public presentation. Linking context grants no additional staff access.

### REQ26-D29-R13 — D29-R13 One genuine form intake outcome

Applies to **US26-D29-04**, acceptance **AC26-D29-04-01–03**.

This Support Help profile requires P23's certified Support handoff as its exactly one Primary Outcome. P23's other email-only outcome remains valid elsewhere but is not a hidden fallback or a second simultaneous master. One authoritative acceptance transaction commits the immutable form occurrence, exact released route, source-owned Support work/acceptance receipt, optional child intents and required dispatch requests before **Received**, or commits none. Support acceptance responsibility is durable at that boundary. If conversation materialization is deferred, accepted pending intake is discoverable to its currently authorized Support/recovery owner and recovers the same occurrence exactly once with its original admission clocks, including after a route change. Later materialization failure is visible recovery, not lost work. An Inngest event or external email alone is not acceptance. Browser answers cannot choose recipients, inbox, actor, template, header or route.

### REQ26-D29-R14 — D29-R14 Honest form-origin source and first reply

Applies to **US26-D29-04**, acceptance **AC26-D29-04-01–03**.

Represent the submitted text as a native **form-origin requester message** with its own original source/occurrence and trusted admission time. It is not inbound RFC email, a staff-recorded D26 brief or an internal note. Do not create fake provider receipt, Message-ID, From header, inbound delivery or human actor fields to fit current email-only defaults. A replyable endpoint can exist without a Party. Staff see the actual submitted endpoint and any separately qualified context in the normal canonical conversation, with current source/recipient checks. The first human reply uses a qualified D4/P17 form-response recipient basis and actual outgoing email lineage. It may continue a real acknowledgement thread already established; otherwise it starts the first outgoing thread. Subsequent actual email uses D1/D2/D25 correlation, not subject/email guessing.

### REQ26-D29-R15 — D29-R15 Duplicate, retry and uncertain acceptance

Applies to **US26-D29-04**, acceptance **AC26-D29-04-01–03**.

Use the form owner's existing replay/idempotency mechanism, qualified end to end to permanent Support intake effect. One intent with identical semantic input returns the same privacy-safe receipt; changed input under that intent conflicts. Double clicks, refresh, lost responses and delayed dispatch cannot create another original. Received status/recovery is scoped to the exact protected browser occurrence capability/current app authority, exposes no message or CRM record and never becomes an enumerable public ticket lookup. On ambiguous network outcome show **Checking whether your message was received** and reconcile the same intent. Direct contact alternatives remain visible, but do not automatically send the draft through another channel. A person deliberately sending a separate email may create another genuine source; D10 reviewed duplicate handling applies, not silent cross-channel merge.

### REQ26-D29-R16 — D29-R16 Clear receipt and no false promises

Applies to **US26-D29-04**, acceptance **AC26-D29-04-01–03**.

After durable acceptance, show **Your message has been received** and the accurate next step: the tenant will handle it through its qualified Support process, with replies using the provided email when permitted. Display a safe reference if the existing occurrence contract qualifies it; no reference entry is required to keep conversing. Do not say delivered, read, assigned, solved, refund completed or promise a deadline from an internal target. A phone/email link click shows no Received state. A failure before acceptance clearly says it was not received; unknown remains unknown. Confirmation is persistent and accessible, not toast-only. Accepted work survives optional guide, rendering, acknowledgement, notification and executor failures.

### REQ26-D29-R17 — D29-R17 Optional visitor email confirmation

Applies to **US26-D29-05**, acceptance **AC26-D29-05-01–03**.

New standard Help forms start with visitor email confirmation **Off**. An authorized tenant may enable the existing P23 zero-or-one Visitor Acknowledgement child, subject to a newly qualified web-Contact source/recipient/P17 publication profile. Browser receipt needs no email readiness. D13 remains receiving-email-only; form admission does not invoke it as a second confirmation. The web profile may reuse neutral wording through valid authoring/copy and an explicitly compatible publication, not relabel an email-only contract. No arbitrary answer/body/context echo, CC, personal data disclosure, fundraising, workflow branch or automatic knowledge answer is added. Like D13-R17, the web confirmation’s Recent sent copy is Off-only: one body-free Automatic confirmation event with actual state, no permanent generated body/subject in support_messages, and synthetic publication preview labelled Template used rather than an actual sent copy.

### REQ26-D29-R18 — D29-R18 Confirmation timing and shared courtesy

Applies to **US26-D29-05**, acceptance **AC26-D29-05-01–03**.

If enabled, the web confirmation is eligible only for its exact accepted new form occurrence and submitted response endpoint under current form/recipient/abuse/contactability authority. Its utility ends 15 minutes after trusted form admission, with no intentional delay or clock renewal. Extend the qualified automatic-receipt courtesy control to share one tenant/mailbox 24-hour bucket across D13 receiving-email and web-form receipt families; per-source-key buckets must not permit duplicates. Human reply takes precedence when it wins the current shared gate. Preserve D13-R15’s full rule: a qualifying public human reply for the same current request and exact confirmation recipient, admitted after confirmation submission may have begun, also ends every additional confirmation provider-call/decrypt authority, including otherwise permitted indeterminate same-key follow-ups. Reconcile already in-flight outcomes without recall; a later staff send failure never revives that confirmation. Current Off/revocation/readiness/source/route fences stop definitely-unsubmitted work; possible submission follows P6 reconciliation, never blind retry/rekey. Suppression never rejects the primary request or blocks a human reply. New source and expiry semantics must be qualified across P23/P17/P6 before enabling this child.

### REQ26-D29-R19 — D29-R19 Work targets, feedback and histories

Applies to **US26-D29-05**, acceptance **AC26-D29-05-01–03**.

Explicitly qualify D14 for replyable form-origin input: a genuine owed first reply starts at trusted form acceptance/admission under the existing source/calendar policy, not a fabricated receiving-provider date or delayed worker timestamp. Human reply coverage and acceptance still govern fulfillment/First/Next; browser receipts and automated confirmations earn no human reply credit. D28 can consider genuinely completed form-origin Support only after the actual qualified human public email correspondence and all existing sampling/source/recipient guards. Mere form submission, acknowledgement or guide use is not feedback eligibility. A form occurrence is not a fake P6 inbound email; actual outgoing messages contribute once through the shared spine.

### REQ26-D29-R20 — D29-R20 CRM continuity and authorization

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

Guest requester, authenticated user, submitted mailbox, message participant, CRM Party, represented organization, worker and CRM owner remain distinct. No exact-email auto-create/link, implied identity verification or transcript permission. Qualified app context and deliberate later D9 linking may relate the actual Support source to CRM under current permissions. CRM Communications → Support opens the same canonical detail; the Overview remains its existing limited preview. Link/unlink/Party merge changes current authorized navigation, not original authorship/intake/recipient provenance. No duplicated Activity/body/last-contact/financial outcome is inferred from form or guide use. Refunds, receipts, recurring gifts, contact changes and sensitive care actions retain owner authorization and audit.

### REQ26-D29-R21 — D29-R21 Supabase grants, RLS and constraints

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

Derive tenant/environment, public/app source binding, authenticated actor when present, route, source identity, timestamps and audit from trusted server context. Guests are represented honestly without fake authenticated users. Enforce tenant-aware parent relationships, valid exclusive producer branches, one occurrence/primary effect, immutable accepted source/route/actor fields and valid state/time combinations. Preserve current owner-compatible text IDs. No direct anonymous writes/reads to Support, form-control, routing, audit or private-content tables. Qualify grants, SELECT, USING/WITH CHECK, column writes, invoker/definer views/RPCs, fixed search_path and service jobs together; a permitted row cannot be reparented or transformed into a forbidden state. Existing broad Support CRUD is not proof. Money tables/types are unchanged.

### REQ26-D29-R22 — D29-R22 Privacy, source retention and safe rendering

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

P23 occurrence is minimal delivery/recovery truth; Support owns the requester content after certified handoff, with references rather than a second readable CMS inbox. Qualify the retained envelope, replay material, selected refs, app context, request source, review/audit and every actual secondary copy under finite owner purpose/ceilings and D16/D17 restriction/disposal/restore rules. New form content has its own trusted admission; it cannot renew old transcripts through a later link/merge. Public submitted-page/error/receipt responses and app private context are no-store and no-referrer under their owner contract; static public Help content may use its qualified cache without embedding visitor answers. Escape untrusted text; no raw HTML/Tiptap/URL unfurl or automatic AI consumption. Logs/metrics/analytics/provider tags never contain answers, raw endpoints, private refs or replay secrets.

### REQ26-D29-R23 — D29-R23 Proportionate abuse protection

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

Reuse P23's trusted origin/generation/schema checks, CSRF/replay controls, bounded parser/request/field limits, tenant-fair multi-dimensional rate limits, backpressure and accessible risk-based challenges. No mandatory puzzle for every person or hidden trap that classifies assistive technology/slow typing as abuse by itself. Required retention/classification/safety floors still apply to hostile free text. If acceptance is denied, show an honest state and independently qualified published alternatives without revealing accounts or internal routes. A displayed alternate never bypasses its channel's actual safety/intake policy; anonymous emails and challenges do not grant CRM authority. No bot/spam score is called proof of a human or mission need.

### REQ26-D29-R24 — D29-R24 Maintenance without a new platform

Applies to **US26-D29-06**, acceptance **AC26-D29-06-01–03**.

Provide one understandable **Requester help** management entry showing the actual public/app placements, contact route, exact locale, selected guides, readiness, preview and current owner actions. Public Page/form/copy/phone/email publication delegates to Web Studio/P23; app-entry mappings delegate to the app's qualified presentation owner; Support routing and Email Studio editing remain at their sources. Do not claim one shared atomic release or duplicate their editors. Choose/reorder/remove at most three current public references, explain why an item is ineligible and show no-match/zero-guidance honestly. Save drafts and publish/activate are distinct; source edits do not mutate old accepted requests. No freeform URL rules, generic taxonomy, public/privacy toggle or automatic promotion from D27 staff curation.

### REQ26-D29-R25 — D29-R25 Contact readiness and failure recovery

Applies to **US26-D29-01**, acceptance **AC26-D29-01-01–03**.

Require a qualified normal contact path and published monitored email before exposing this standard Help entry; phone is optional. A guide failure cannot disable a still-qualified form/direct route. If the form cannot accept, say so, preserve safe local visitor-authored text and expose only still-current separately approved email/phone alternatives; no invented fallback address, platform inbox, another tenant or stale CMS preview. Whole-scope identity/host/locale/source ambiguity fails safely rather than displaying someone else's contact. Accepted requests remain recoverable when providers/executors fail. Managers see the exact affected owner/action and can repair without direct database changes or resetting idempotency.

### REQ26-D29-R26 — D29-R26 Accessibility and low-bandwidth behavior

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

Use existing Core semantic design tokens/Base UI ownership for app surfaces and P23's approved public presentation, with native semantic form submission and no-JavaScript path. Visible labels, optional-field text, descriptive links, proper autocomplete/input purpose, keyboard operation, error summary linked to fields, retained answers and persistent receipt are required. No placeholder-only labels, color/emoji-only status, hover-only contact or focus-stealing suggestions. Prove 200% zoom, narrow mobile, long translations, RTL/bidi, keyboard and named screen readers. A JS/network failure must not strand the ordinary form or use a weaker authority protocol. Do not promise offline submission or hide a send queue in browser storage.

### REQ26-D29-R27 — D29-R27 Performance, measurement and operating bounds

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

No new full-corpus search, behavioral analytics or article-rating subsystem. Resolve at most three selected Page refs in bounded owner queries, with contact rendered independently of optional guide latency and current authorization before content/counts. Later source-read performance must be qualified on an explicit nonproduction workload: at least 100 simultaneous Help loads and 20 competing retries of one form intent across two tenants; contact first usable p95 ≤2 seconds under a documented network/server fixture, zero duplicate primary effects and zero cross-scope disclosures. These are release targets, not measured capacity claims. Technical counts distinguish attempted/accepted/rejected/unknown/primary recovery and optional delivery; article visits are not solved/deflected/satisfied or CRM activity.

### REQ26-D29-R28 — D29-R28 Migration and rollout

Applies to **US26-D29-06**, acceptance **AC26-D29-06-01–03**.

Inventory current FAQ/contact/help routes and legacy Support writers; never publish their hard-coded organization/financial claims as tenant truth. Add compatible source/recipient/form-origin/admission/privacy contracts and narrow grants before activation; old writers cannot fake email or bypass new source semantics. Public/app consumers require their actual qualified release/readiness and stable contact recovery. No backfill submissions, fake consent, synthetic provider IDs, old-question confirmation batch or new CRM records. Feature disablement blocks new admission where necessary while preserving accepted-source recovery, receipts, privacy and P6 reconciliation. Roll forward after new data; rollback must not reinstate permissive writers or restore erased source/token data. P23/P24 open planning PRs are dependencies, not evidence of shipped readiness.

### REQ26-D29-R29 — D29-R29 Traceable proof and final qualification

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

Carry all R01–R30, category outcomes and P01–P44 into required OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets/code/tests/release evidence with exact source/owner amendments. Test user-visible outcomes and adverse races, not only helper calls or fixtures. No current source hash, model example, polished FAQ or vendor demo establishes complete intake, RLS, delivery, browser or usability safety. All real proof groups below remain required and unexecuted during grooming.

### REQ26-D29-DATA_CONTRACT-S0002 — Existing facts versus required new behavior

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

P23 ADR0170 already governs purpose-bounded forms, one Primary Outcome, atomic occurrence/primary/child/outbox acceptance, independent delivery recovery, no-JS public forms and no uploads/payments. Its Contact concept does not supply an already implemented minimal field schema or certified Support adapter. Current Support source models have email-shaped constraints/defaults and provider linkage; those are not authority to fabricate an email for a form request. D26's staff-recorded source is also distinct from a visitor's own text.

P23's released public body/list audience is invariant; portal/app ownership is separate under P24/P25. D27's public staff finder may select Shared by link Pages, while requester discovery cannot. P23 Article-list support does not automatically certify a Page-reference Help leaf. The permanent path is the explicitly bounded qualification below, not another CMS or generic form engine.

Caller fields are only the approved visitor answers plus owner-bound opaque references/replay material. A caller cannot assign approval, staff identity, inbox, publication, sensitivity, message kind or verified-Party status. ### REQ26-D29-DATA_CONTRACT-S0004 — Two producer adapters, one accepted outcome

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

**Public adapter:** use trusted public host/base/route → exact P23 Site/locale/current generation → released form/purpose/route. Reject forged form/tenant/route overrides and stale incompatible schema. Current generation and adverse owner gates remain authoritative even when a browser has old HTML.

**App adapter:** use the verified current portal/app tenant/principal → exact approved Help entry binding → same qualified Contact purpose/admission semantics. Optional current-owner context is resolved server-side and rechecked at Submit. It is never private JSON appended to the public form endpoint, a raw record ID accepted because the user is logged in, or a personalized public CMS audience. Qualify this consumer explicitly; the public endpoint cannot borrow app cookies as Site proof.

Both produce the same typed ordinary inquiry and one primary Support acceptance contract through the shared API owner. P23's canonical occurrence, outbox and recovery remain common; there is no app-specific or public-widget submission database. A management interface can coordinate setup, but public and app publication/activation do not become one distributed transaction. Compatible current source revisions must be proven; a stale schema/route cannot silently reinterpret answers.

The standard Support entry's Primary Outcome is certified Support handoff. If the tenant's broader platform currently offers only an independently qualified public email/phone contact, that contact may remain available under its owner while Support form setup is incomplete; D29 must not force-enable Support or fabricate a conversation to make the larger Asym product usable. It also must not silently switch a submitted Support form into P23 Email-only delivery. Other existing P23 forms can still deliberately choose their one Verified Email Destination before release.

### REQ26-D29-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — Input, prefill and context rules

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

Normalize message line endings to LF, require nonblank input, count Unicode scalars rather than bytes/grapheme clusters, and enforce≤10000 scalars. Optional unsplit name≤200 scalars. Preserve original meaningful text; do not rewrite names, transliterate scripts, strip punctuation or treat a subject line as a required routing field. Enforce the current qualified mailbox parser's real length/encoding support; the field remains one declared reply endpoint. Mailbox syntax and authenticated self-prefill do not prove that a new edited address is owned by the actor.

A 256 KiB raw-body guard precedes expensive decoding/parsing; the released envelope has its own field/count/byte bounds. URL-encoded four-byte Unicode can use 12 wire bytes per scalar, so a 64 KiB limit would incorrectly reject some otherwise valid 10000-scalar messages. The synthetic encoding fixture is 126677 bytes including 200 four-byte name scalars and bounded synthetic control fields; the actual released schema must prove its total envelope. HTML `maxlength` uses UTF-16 units, so do not set it blindly to the scalar limit and reject supported emoji early; client hints/counters must match server semantics or defer to the server. Invalid/oversized input returns actionable errors without logging the body or silently truncating it.

The authenticated app may prefill only the actual current requester's authorized self-contact, visibly and editably. Represented organization/linked Party data does not select the reply mailbox. Optional **About** context is a typed source-owned reference with an allowed safe display, not a data snapshot. Its admission requires current actor/source authority and same tenant. If it expires or becomes unauthorized, do not silently retarget; offer explicit ordinary contact without private details. Auth/principal/tenant switches invalidate private prefill/context and local draft state. No long-lived visitor body store/localStorage/device history is introduced to preserve optional guide navigation.

| Optional guide failure                                   | Qualified optional leaf shrinks/empties; required contact closure survives                                                       | Do not rewrite sealed Page or improvise an unsafe partial generation. Whole-scope failure uses only independently qualified recovery.                                                                                                                   |
| Acknowledgement/human reply race                         | One common current source/courtesy/P6 boundary; useful human reply can suppress unsent automatic receipt                         | No new provider ID/key, utility reset, duplicate email or human-response credit. A later qualifying human reply ends all further acknowledgement calls/decryption even after possible submission; only in-flight reconciliation remains, under D13-R15. |
| Later real email, merge, unlink or CRM permission change | Existing D1/D9/D10 source-based handling/current authorization                                                                   | No automatic sender+subject merge, Party creation, history rewrite or extra form occurrence.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Privacy restriction/expiry/restore                       | Restrict ordinary access before cleanup, preserve qualified minimal evidence and replay restore barriers                         | No recovery that rehydrates erased answers or restores revoked send/receipt authority.                                                                                                                                                                  |

The receipt path is the existing qualified form recovery capability, not D1's excluded requester conversation archive. It reveals only a privacy-safe terminal acceptance result for the exact occurrence. Rate-limit and authorize lookup; no identifier enumeration or raw answer echo. Retain dedupe/control evidence for its qualified source/replay purpose so disposal cannot allow historical event replay to recreate work; do not keep raw visitor text indefinitely as a dedupe mechanism.

### REQ26-D29-DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — Work, email and CRM effects

Applies to **US26-D29-03**, acceptance **AC26-D29-03-01–03**.

Form admission contributes a genuine external requester source/time to the certified Support adapter. Native form text is a distinct source kind; no email-only default timestamps/direction/provider fields are invented. The first actual staff reply reviews the form's response endpoint and current contactability. It freezes either the real existing acknowledgement lineage or the first actual outgoing lineage through D4/P17/P6. Subsequent actual email carries its actual provider/RFC evidence. A P6 communication event exists for actual communication at the relevant qualified owner seam, not an invented received-email record for a form.

D14's first owed response uses trusted form admission and current source/calendar semantics. It does not start late when a workflow wakes or treat browser Received as a reply. Existing acceptance uncertainty and explicit human coverage remain unchanged. D28 only considers genuinely completed work after actual accepted human public correspondence plus its established one-opportunity/sampling/courtesy/recipient rules. A guide click, form submit or automated acknowledgement creates no feedback eligibility.

The same source appears through CRM's authorized Support relation and canonical detail. Optional source references may link existing CRM context only under D9 and current owner permissions; they do not create duplicated Activity bodies, verified identities or a financial completion. A form asks for help; it cannot itself cancel a gift, issue a receipt/refund, edit a contact or access confidential care. Authorized actions stay behind their actual owners.

### REQ26-D29-DATA_CONTRACT-S0008 — RLS, storage and finite custody

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

Public anonymous clients post only to the qualified server boundary. Revoke direct unnecessary Data API grants to route/control/occurrence/private Support/audit tables and prove appropriate RLS on exposed data. Authenticated staff roles are not global read authority; check actual capabilities/current scopes and all derived views/counts. Mutations must constrain old and new state via effective USING/WITH CHECK, field privileges and command invariants. PostgreSQL may reuse USING when WITH CHECK is omitted; missing syntax alone is not proof of a hole. Security-definer RPCs need demonstrated need, fixed search_path/schema-qualified dependencies and restricted EXECUTE; service-role work re-proves the same actor/source authority. No secret/service key enters the public form.

Define custody for: public/app config revisions; selected refs/current availability; opaque app context; replay/receipt material; occurrence/recovery envelopes; actual Support text/name/response endpoint; P17 sealed bytes (web confirmation Recent sent copy is Off-only, with no permanent generated support_messages body and only a synthetic Template used preview); P6 transport facts; child work/claims; error responses; exports/search/CRM projections; technical logs and backups. The source owner specifies finite retention, purpose end, holds/restriction and physical cleanup. P23 occurrence cannot become a parallel inbox. D16/D17 cover governed Support content and all representations, with actual new source time and no old-clock renewal from a link/merge/read. Form rejection/validation errors have short purpose-bound custody, not an analytics archive of unsent questions.

Response endpoints, names and comments stay out of metrics/logs/tags/URLs. Private submitted/error/receipt/app-context responses are no-store/no-referrer; immutable public guide/title/contact publications use only their qualified public cache. Replaying a backup reestablishes source revocations and disposal fences before ordinary serve/send/retry. Unknown current authority is not permission to serve a stale positive cache.

### REQ26-D29-DATA_CONTRACT-S0009 — Qualification order and proof limits

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

First qualify the narrow purpose, exclusive public/app source ports, native form-origin Support mapping and transaction/grant constraints. Then qualify first human reply, optional guide leaf/current-contact failure containment and contextual reference handling. Add optional web acknowledgement/common courtesy and explicit D14/D28 mapping, followed by privacy/custody/restore and user-visible management/recovery. Activate only after real P01–P44 outcomes pass. Current source hashing and 24 finite synthetic examples do not prove actual PostgreSQL isolation/RLS, P6 delivery, public caching or browser usability. No live database or requester test was run during this grooming review.

### REQ26-D29-X01 — Exact corrected decision to record

Applies to **US26-D29-07**, acceptance **AC26-D29-07-01–03**.

> **D29 A — Contextual guides and direct contact:** Provide one consistent, directly reachable Contact [tenant public name] entry. Its ordinary contact form is immediately usable with required reply email and message, plus one optional unsplit name. Show the tenant's deliberately published monitored email and an actual published phone channel when offered. Provide zero to three current, explicitly selected Listed public guide references as optional secondary information; guide use never gates contact or counts as a resolved request. Use the existing approved public/app presentation and qualified source owners.
>
> Preserve all fully ratified **D29-R01–R30**, the complete source/data/CRM/P17/P6 contracts, **P01–P44** and **O01–O06**. Public P23 and authenticated app consumers retain distinct trusted scope and release boundaries while using one certified Contact-purpose occurrence and Support handoff. Exactly one durable primary acceptance precedes Received. Form-origin requester content is not fabricated incoming email or a staff note; identity, CRM associations and consequential business actions remain independently authorized. Browser receipt is independent of optional email confirmation. Email Studio owns governed wording/presentation/preparation and P6 owns delivery/reconciliation.
>
> Add **D29-X01** to R26/P40: preserve the 200% text-resize check and separately prove reflow at an effective width of 320 CSS pixels, including 400% zoom from a 1280 CSS-pixel viewport. Include the initial form, validation errors, persistent receipt, public full page, authenticated app presentation, long supported contact strings, translations and RTL content. Author-created overlays/sticky UI must not entirely obscure keyboard focus under WCAG2.2 SC2.4.11. Pointer targets meet SC2.5.8's 24-by-24 CSS-pixel minimum or its actual permitted exceptions; use 44-by-44 CSS pixels for standalone primary touch actions as the product target. Prove mobile virtual-keyboard usability separately without misclassifying the browser keyboard as author-created content. Do not claim that 200% text resizing or a narrow screenshot alone passes reflow or whole-journey accessibility.

The original complete clause text remains the governing ratified record. This supplement adds X01 and expands the explanation of how to deliver those existing requirements; it does not abbreviate or discard them. No new glossary, feature ADR number, generic form engine, contact database, public library/search, chat/telephony service, upload feature or AI component is required.

## Focused Support overview

### REQ26-D30-R01 — D30-R01 Scope, necessity and strongest alternatives

Applies to **US26-D30-06**, acceptance **AC26-D30-06-01–03**.

Provide a focused fixed Support overview using the already-required answers and their next actions. Ordinary work views and separate reports remain complete ways to work. Preserve future full configuration through qualified shared blocks; the current release includes no builder. No mandatory weekly review ritual, universal team-lead role, measured productivity improvement or whole-product dashboard role is implied.

### REQ26-D30-R02 — D30-R02 Entry, terminology and ordinary work

Applies to **US26-D30-01**, acceptance **AC26-D30-01-01–03**.

Use the existing Support **Reports → Overview** route and navigation, with **Overview** as the page title in Support context. Keep work views, search and direct conversation links available. Do not change every staff member's landing preference, create a second Support Studio destination or require opening reports before handling a request. Navigation from a report through Support and permitted CRM context preserves its explicit return location and any separately qualified safe conversation draft; opening an overview does not create a case, note or Activity.

### REQ26-D30-R03 — D30-R03 Fixed Work now composition and counting

Applies to **US26-D30-01**, acceptance **AC26-D30-01-01–03**.

Provide three concise summaries: **All unfinished**, **Unassigned**, and **Replies needing attention**, all labelled in **conversations**. All unfinished counts distinct currently permitted continuing work components whose D3 state is Open, Waiting for requester or Waiting on our side; include future-deferred Open. Show those three state counts as its breakdown without calling all unfinished work urgent. Unassigned is the D6-qualified unfinished subset with no current assignee, including waiting/deferred work and any owner-required review distinctions; it does not reset routing or mean safe to claim. Replies needing attention counts distinct continuing conversations with at least one still-owed D14 contribution. Fulfilled-but-unscored timing evidence is not outstanding reply work. Use complete source queries, not hydrated-page length.

### REQ26-D30-R04 — D30-R04 Live groups, overlap and review destinations

Applies to **US26-D30-01**, acceptance **AC26-D30-01-01–03**.

Within reply attention preserve D14's overdue, timing needs confirmation, within-target and untargeted distinctions. A conversation can have several underlying reply periods and appear in more than one such group; show the overall distinct-conversation count and label groups as overlapping, never sum them. The detail exposes all permitted underlying obligations. Unassigned is already part of unfinished, and reply attention is not another additive workload. Existing D3 due/follow-up and actionable delivery-recovery destinations remain directly discoverable alongside intake, handoff and feedback review as plain named links under **Other work and review queues — all dates**, outside the Work now filter's visual scope. Do not create a combined problems badge, copy P17 attention state or infer zero hidden reviews. These links use each existing owner's scope and do not inherit the overview date/inbox controls. A fulfilled reply or zero summary never certifies delivery recovery, due follow-up or independent review complete; no new queue is invented.

### REQ26-D30-R05 — D30-R05 Work now inbox control

Applies to **US26-D30-01**, acceptance **AC26-D30-01-01–03**.

Place **Currently handled in** inside Work now. Default to **All accessible inboxes**; allow one current authorized inbox using the existing searchable accessible selector. All accessible means the viewer's current permitted work population, not the entire tenant or every original component. Missing, forbidden or no-longer-qualified selected scope is **Selected inbox unavailable**, never empty ID interpreted as All. Require deliberate selection of another scope; preserve safe date settings. Retirement alone does not invalidate an inbox reference: retain still-owner-qualified unfinished work and selected scope, with a clear Retired label where its metadata is permitted. No retired label grants new access. Now has no Created date, historical period, donor, label or employee-performance filter. Counts/links carry the exact source predicate and current scope.

### REQ26-D30-R06 — D30-R06 Independent Results scope

Applies to **US26-D30-02**, acceptance **AC26-D30-02-01–03**.

Results has only its period and reporting-timezone controls at overview level, with persistent text: **Across the inboxes you can report on. Work now filters do not apply.** No global Inbox selector is introduced. D14 historical facts, D21 current responsible inbox and D28 original invitation inbox cannot silently be treated as one dimension. Each section aggregates only its currently authorized owner population. Do not filter historical populations through today's active-inbox catalog; retain retired source references only where their owner preserves meaningful current report access. **View full report** carries period/zone and a safe return context, not the Now predicate; the full report exposes its qualified narrower dimensions. Clicking an actual metric instead carries that metric's exact cohort/kind/evaluation context. This is the permanent simple A design; it does not require inventing a new historical inbox dimension.

### REQ26-D30-R07 — D30-R07 Period, timezone and simple controls

Applies to **US26-D30-03**, acceptance **AC26-D30-03-01–03**.

Offer Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month (month start through today) and Custom; initialize a new context to Last 30 days including today. Show actual local date endpoints, timezone and **Through [evaluation time]** for an incomplete current day/month. Resolve a qualified staff reporting timezone, then tenant reporting timezone, then visibly UTC if neither exists; allow an explicit valid IANA reporting timezone without rewriting source calendars. Date picks are inclusive local dates compiled by the owner into a half-open start-to-next-day interval, with current-period evaluation bounded at the trusted evaluation instant. Custom applies on deliberate Apply, spans 1–366 local calendar dates and ends no later than today in the selected zone. This is an overview interaction/query bound, not a new source retention period or a limit on separately qualified full reports. Explain longer-range access through the full report; do not truncate silently. Range/zone validation preserves previous results under their previous visible label until a valid replacement is applied.

### REQ26-D30-R08 — D30-R08 Reply targets section

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

Reuse D14 **Targets due in [period]**: finalized original target instances in the owned due cohort, First and Next separate. Show **On time among assessed** as on-time / assessed, alongside assessed versus finalized count, unknown evidence, exclusions and separate potential unconfirmed targets. Assessed includes confirmed unanswered-overdue misses; ordinary late cleanup/Off cannot improve the past denominator. Keep on-time, replied-late, unanswered-overdue and unavailable outcomes traceable. Do not average inbox percentages or pool candidate contributions into finalized target counts. No targets due is a complete empty result; disabled current policy is a separate configuration fact and does not blank history.

### REQ26-D30-R09 — D30-R09 Reply times section

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

Reuse D14 **Waiting periods ended by a staff reply in [period]** with separate First/Next, median, p90 and exact measured sample. The fixed overview presents **Elapsed time** explicitly; qualified service-hours analysis remains in the full report and is not silently pooled into this preview. One reply can end several waits; counts are completed waits, not messages, conversations or staff effort. Accepted-but-uncertain timestamps and uncertain cohort membership remain disclosed under D14. The median convention and nearest-rank p90 are unchanged; round display only. Genuine zero elapsed time is distinct from no data. The always-visible current-work area prevents favorable completed-response summaries from concealing unanswered work.

### REQ26-D30-R10 — D30-R10 Request labels section

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

Reuse D21's component-first cohort and current categorization, labelled **Current labels on conversations started in [period]**. First qualify current permitted components and their earliest original start; a later merged original cannot independently pull an older component into a recent period. Show N total, labelled L and unlabelled U only under complete metadata, with L+U=N when that equality is qualified. Show up to five highest-count currently permitted labels, stable-ID tie break, plus View all labels. Each count is distinct cohort conversations carrying the label; multiple labels overlap and percentages use N. No pie, Other residual or claim that the top five cover the whole cohort. Ordinary archived labels remain labelled as archived when permitted. Preserve separate Start date unconfirmed evidence rather than guessing membership or calling an incomplete population complete. Unknown metadata, missing names and privacy restrictions never become No labels or exposed raw IDs.

### REQ26-D30-R11 — D30-R11 Feedback section and Off history

Applies to **US26-D30-02**, acceptance **AC26-D30-02-01–03**.

Use D28 **Invitations issued in [period]** as the fixed preview cohort, with original source/inbox provenance and responses to that exact cohort **as of this evaluation**. Issued includes distinct effects whose submission may have begun, including indeterminate submission. Show issued/responded counts and the three rating counts/distribution with the qualified submitted-rating denominator. Never divide all responses received during the period by invitations issued during the period or only confirmed provider acceptances. Show response windows still open when relevant; no response is neither positive nor negative. Feedback Off is current configuration only: retain currently authorized historical results and all-age review navigation. With no eligible history, explain Off/not yet measured separately from error. Show no individual comments, donor names, case subjects or employee rankings on the overview; the existing authorized Feedback report/detail owns them.

### REQ26-D30-R12 — D30-R12 Conservative presentation and interpretation

Applies to **US26-D30-02**, acceptance **AC26-D30-02-01–03**.

The fixed historical composition is exactly Reply targets, Reply times, Request labels and Feedback. No automatic comparison arrows, red/green trend verdicts, overall health/satisfaction score, fundraising value, staff productivity, resolution SLA, predicted capacity or AI commentary is added. Existing genuine trends remain in detailed reports. Use short tables/definition lists and restrained horizontal comparisons only where they communicate meaning; values, units, sample/coverage and important uncertainty must be available without hover. A tiny card that cannot explain a metric uses a concise qualified summary and full-report link rather than concealing its denominator.

### REQ26-D30-R13 — D30-R13 Evaluation consistency and freshness

Applies to **US26-D30-05**, acceptance **AC26-D30-05-01–03**.

Each returned section/block has a source-qualified metric/definition revision, typed scope, period/timezone where relevant, measured unit, trusted evaluation/read-cut evidence, computed time, source-through/completeness state and exact detail descriptor. The three Work now totals and breakdowns come from one coherent authorized read cut. A displayed timestamp alone does not make separately read statements consistent. Each historical block keeps internal numerator/denominator/sample/detail coherence; do not promise one atomic snapshot across independently owned blocks. Show block-level evaluation time when it differs. Current source/privacy/permission gates still apply at serving, independently of historical evaluation time or cache TTL. Derived read models must disclose their actual supported freshness and withdrawal conformance.

### REQ26-D30-R14 — D30-R14 Refresh and interaction stability

Applies to **US26-D30-05**, acceptance **AC26-D30-05-01–03**.

Provide one explicit **Refresh** action for all visible results. Read on entry and after an applicable context change. Refresh Work now automatically no more than once each 60 elapsed seconds while visible and online; pause when hidden/offline and coalesce focus/reconnect/manual/invalidation triggers. The visible page says **Updated [time]**, never promises instantaneous live state. Period results refresh on entry, applied period/zone changes, explicit Refresh or a known relevant invalidation, not every minute merely because Now refreshes. If Now cannot obtain a current qualified read after 120 seconds, mark it **Out of date**; retain previously allowed values only under the applicable current-authority/retention contract. Unknown current authority means clear those values, not serve a stale fallback. Late responses from older context/revision cannot replace newer results. Do not move focus, re-order active controls or repeatedly announce every refreshed count.

### REQ26-D30-R15 — D30-R15 Exact detail, live change and safe return

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

A Work now count opens its exact conversation-level query; a target/wait/label/invitation metric opens its native-grain report detail and can then open canonical conversations. A number of waits need not equal a number of conversations. The descriptor binds owner/definition, scope, cohort, kind, evaluation and current tenant/principal context, never a browser-written arbitrary query. Recheck current access before opening. If the original evaluation can be replayed safely under current source rights, label it; otherwise deliberately perform a current re-evaluation with the same semantic criteria and state **Updated since overview**. Never freeze revoked access to force matching counts, silently substitute a current Created filter or construct missing historical facts from a timestamp. Back returns the prior valid control state, scroll and focus context; source restriction still wins over cached content.

### REQ26-D30-R16 — D30-R16 State model and partial failure

Applies to **US26-D30-05**, acceptance **AC26-D30-05-01–03**.

Every block distinguishes Loading, Ready with data, Ready empty, current policy Off with/without retained history, Incomplete/unknown evidence, Unavailable/failed and Stale. Missing permission does not reveal hidden names, totals or a count of forbidden inboxes. Do not initialize business values to zero or show perfect percentages while loading. Do not label an incomplete scan an exact total. Retry only the failed read where safe; one block/source failure cannot block ordinary Support navigation or overwrite unaffected results with zero. After an applied context change, old results are not displayed beneath new labels. An unavailable source must not trigger a public/client cache or broader role fallback.

### REQ26-D30-R17 — D30-R17 Shared implementation and future full configuration

Applies to **US26-D30-06**, acceptance **AC26-D30-06-01–03**.

Record future full configurability as the founder's intended direction. Implement the fixed composition as ordinary code-owned use of stable, versioned owner-qualified block/read/detail contracts. Keep presentation order and titles separate from metric identity and source meaning; avoid UI-position keys, copied formulas or one opaque mutable dashboard blob. These seams are required now because they preserve one definition and safe evolution, not to build hypothetical infrastructure. No persisted per-user/tenant layout, drag editor, generic registry administration, expression language, custom joins or hidden disabled Configure button ships under A. Future composition belongs with qualified Phase 33 shared reporting, can arrange only compatible authorized blocks and must complete its own save/share/reset/compatibility/retention UX before activation. It never gains authority over metric definitions or underlying records.

### REQ26-D30-R18 — D30-R18 Authoritative owners and no forward gate

Applies to **US26-D30-06**, acceptance **AC26-D30-06-01–03**.

Support owns source work/topology/query meaning; D14 target owners own reply facts; D21 owns labels; D28 owns feedback; P6 owns actual communication outcomes; CRM/identity/giving/care retain their authoritative facts. Phase 33 plans shared semantic/report composition and governed read models, not a shipped universal service. Qualify reusable reporting boundaries and source modules as needed without waiting for the entirety of a future reporting product or creating a competing Support semantic layer. Apps own this presentation and the shared API owner owns business reads. Browser aggregation is suitable only for permitted presentation of already-qualified aggregate values, not authoritative counts from raw conversation/message collections.

### REQ26-D30-R19 — D30-R19 Current tenant, source and field authorization

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Derive tenant/environment/actor and eligible report/work capabilities from trusted current context. Apply current source, original-component, inbox, classification, field and relevant CRM permissions before aggregates, labels, counts, breakdowns, cache, prefetch, detail, exports and audit visibility. No report/manager role automatically grants transcript, Finance or member-care access. A total over a superset is not safe merely because rows are hidden. If a source-owned aggregate policy differs from detail permission it must be explicitly qualified; A grants no new aggregate-only disclosure tier. A shared component or future shared layout never grants data. Resolve inaccessible selected scope as unavailable, not All, and discard all old tenant/principal results on context change.

### REQ26-D30-R20 — D30-R20 Supabase, grants, RLS and mutation safety

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

The overview is read-only with no new authoritative business tables or public Data API writes. Prove the actual grants and effective SELECT policies, invoker/definer views/functions, execute permissions, fixed search paths, table-owner/BYPASSRLS and service-role callers preserve R19. RLS on source tables alone does not certify a broad cached rollup or privileged RPC. Where existing projection/cache/receipt jobs write, enforce non-null same-tenant relationships, stable source/definition identity, nonnegative exact counts, legal state/completeness combinations and trusted immutable tenant/actor/source attribution. Prove effective USING and WITH CHECK on those mutations; an allowed row cannot be reparented or made publicly readable. Preserve owner-compatible IDs/delete/append-only rules. No money columns/precision or financial grants change; no speculative layout schema is introduced.

### REQ26-D30-R21 — D30-R21 Query completeness, bounds and precision

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Compute complete authorized populations and deduplication before aggregation/ranking; page detail through existing owner keyset contracts, with at most 50 rows per page in this surface. Database/API row caps and the current adapter's 2,000-row limit are not complete-report boundaries. Do not fetch every message body or publish a raw aggregate-source dump. Return only the required aggregate/coverage/detail metadata. Counts use exact nonnegative integers with checked serialization; ratios derive from exact owned numerators/denominators, remain undefined at zero denominator and round only for display. Do not average percentages or percentiles. Align indexes/query plans to actual tenant/current-home/status/source-time/original/target/feedback predicates. If an owner cannot provide a complete query within its qualified budget, show unavailable with the full report's qualified path rather than truncate.

### REQ26-D30-R22 — D30-R22 Source lifecycle and historical integrity

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Moves, merge/Undo, D12 relations, reopenings, identity/link changes, late P6 outcomes, corrections, target/feedback Off and source retirement follow their existing owners. Now reflects current component/current home; D14 keeps original target/wait/custody/actor evidence; D21 keeps its component-first current-label cohort; D28 keeps immutable issued opportunity/effect provenance. No current assignment becomes historical responder credit. D26 staff records and D29 forms keep genuine sources, including no-Party work; do not fabricate email volume, delivery, completed giving actions or a unique person from an address. A late qualified correction may change a new report evaluation with interpretation history; it does not rewrite a previously qualified export or renew expired source content.

### REQ26-D30-R23 — D30-R23 Navigation through CRM and business actions

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

Overview → exact detail → conversation → permitted CRM record and CRM → Support detail use the same canonical source with current joint authorization. Requester, mailbox, participant, authenticated user, Party, represented organization, assignee and CRM owner remain distinct. Overview itself needs no duplicated CRM names/relationship data. Source links/merges/unlinks/deletion/restrictions cannot create duplicate Activities or falsely update last contact. A count, reply status or satisfied rating cannot authorize/refund/change recurring gifts/contact details/issue receipts or close an owning-domain task. Those actions retain their source validation, approval and audit. Return context does not carry authority.

### REQ26-D30-R24 — D30-R24 Privacy, caching, logs and exports

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Read results, query/detail descriptors and any actual secondary copies have finite purpose/custody under their existing source/configuration/records owners. No new indefinite snapshot archive, browser-local report history, public share URL, persistent raw comments or screenshot export is introduced. Cached private results are principal/tenant/scope/definition/source-authority aware; a historical read-cut is not permission. Apply restriction/expiry/erase/hold/restore barriers to aggregates and indexes as required by their source. Logs contain qualified technical correlation/reason/version/time, not message bodies, comments, raw endpoints, private names or report payloads. Overview exports stay in the exact full report's current qualified export command; no browser CSV over raw sources or omnibus overview email attachment.

### REQ26-D30-R25 — D30-R25 Email Studio and side-effect freedom

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Opening Overview, refreshing, filtering or following a link sends nothing and does not mutate D3 work, D14 targets, D21 labels, D28 feedback, D29 acknowledgements, following or shared tasks. No management digest, daily report schedule, AI summary mail, confirmation or template editor is included. Source-owned consequential actions remain explicit in their existing surfaces. For any later separately authorized scheduled report, Phase 33 owns schedule/run/snapshot and per-recipient eligibility, Email Studio/P17 owns governed Tiptap-authored wording/preparation/immutable material, and P6 owns delivery/reconciliation/history. Viewing a screen or exporting a permitted report is not authority to email it to another person. Existing human reply, signature and message contracts remain unchanged.

### REQ26-D30-R26 — D30-R26 Complete maintenance without dashboard administration

Applies to **US26-D30-06**, acceptance **AC26-D30-06-01–03**.

Tenant staff can use the fixed overview immediately when its sources/capabilities are qualified; no dashboard creation or per-tenant layout setup is required. Existing inbox, target, label and feedback settings remain at their owners, with authorized Manage links only where useful. Off/not configured and historical data are separate. Product maintainers version source/read/detail contracts and release a reviewed fixed composition with compatibility checks; they do not ask tenants to rewire cards after a deployment. Retire obsolete incompatible legacy report routes/readers safely so two definitions do not compete. If a source or block is unavailable, show the exact permitted repair path without disabling unrelated Support handling or requiring direct SQL cleanup.

### REQ26-D30-R27 — D30-R27 Accessibility, mobile and visual craft

Applies to **US26-D30-05**, acceptance **AC26-D30-05-01–03**.

Use Core's exact base-maia/Base UI/shared Zinc semantic design system, existing page/navigation patterns and shared controls. Keep titles, definitions, units, small-sample/unknown context and independent section scopes readable. Desktop may use three compact Now summaries and two columns of historical sections; narrow screens preserve Now first and a single semantic column. Prefer native headings, labelled fields, tables/definition lists and named links; chart facts have keyboard/touch/text access. No hover-only numbers, color-only verdicts, animated counting, surprise reordering or auto-refresh focus movement. Prove keyboard/screen-reader flow, 200% zoom, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, long translated/RTL text, locale dates/numbers, reduced motion and low bandwidth. These are requirements, not proof of perfect UX before testing.

### REQ26-D30-R28 — D30-R28 Concurrency, retry and current-state restoration

Applies to **US26-D30-05**, acceptance **AC26-D30-05-01–03**.

Reads are effect-free and may coalesce/retry without creating business events. Bind responses and detail intents to a current request generation; aborted/late responses after filter/account/tenant changes cannot commit to the UI. Rechecking a revoked context takes precedence over returning a successful old query. Within-block totals, sample and detail descriptor share the qualified evaluation; a separate current detail explicitly acknowledges later state. Existing owner commands reached after navigation preserve their own optimistic concurrency/idempotency; the overview does not issue compensating state changes or automatic mark-read/reviewed actions. Restoration after reconnect/back/refresh preserves only currently valid control state and clears forbidden results; no offline business queue or indefinite frozen database transaction across browsing.

### REQ26-D30-R29 — D30-R29 Performance qualification and operational limits

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Avoid per-card raw-data downloads, unbounded fanout and per-conversation polling. Coalesce Work now into one bounded coherent source read; allow independent historical blocks without head-of-line blocking ordinary navigation. Reuse shared caching/read models only when current authorization and complete contribution semantics survive. Before activation, qualify an explicit nonproduction workload with at least 100,000 retained conversations, 1,000,000 relevant message/target source events, 100,000 feedback opportunities, 100 simultaneous overview viewers and skew across at least two tenants. Require p95 Work now data ≤2 seconds and historical sections ≤4 seconds under recorded server/network/query conditions, zero cross-scope disclosures and zero incomplete populations labelled complete. These are accepted release fixtures/targets, not measured capacity claims. Enforce tighter owner budgets if applicable and document exact supported range/limits before release.

### REQ26-D30-R30 — D30-R30 Rollout, migration and rollback

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Inventory current Overview, Agents/Teams/Inbox/Labels routes, raw reports API, serializer/adapter caps, business-hours shortcuts and cached/fixture consumers. Add qualified source projections/readers and parity proof before activating the fixed view; old readers cannot remain an access/meaning bypass. Preserve IDs, original times and unavailable legacy evidence; no backfill of fabricated target/response/feedback history. Use compatible versions and a feature kill switch that removes the faulty overview reader while leaving safe work/report paths intact. A data-preserving rollback must not revive broad readers, stale private caches or erased sources; prefer guarded roll-forward. New source facts and future shared composition must remain readable through qualified stable contracts without maintaining parallel truth.

### REQ26-D30-R31 — D30-R31 Observability, audit and proof

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Technical diagnostics record safe request/definition/source versions, scope category, completeness, evaluated/source-through times, latency, rows examined/returned where safe, failure and refresh/revocation reasons. Ordinary viewing does not append a fake business communication or audit every displayed value. Source corrections and real configuration changes retain the owning durable business/security audit. Carry the exact R01–R32, category findings, P01–P48 and O01–O06 through required glossary/ADR/OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets/implementation/tests/release evidence. Source/hash checks and extracted helper observations prove only their stated scope. No actual database/provider/browser/usability/performance qualification is claimed in grooming.
