### REQ26-D30-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — A useful starting place

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

A staff member reaches **Support → Reports → Overview**. Their ordinary work view remains directly accessible and their default landing is not changed. The page is available under actual current Support/report capabilities; no special “team lead” identity automatically grants data.

The fixed visual hierarchy is:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Support / Reports
> Overview                                             Refresh
> 
> WORK NOW                         Updated [time]
> Currently handled in [All accessible inboxes v]
> 
> All unfinished       Unassigned          Replies needing attention
> [N] conversations    [U] conversations    [R] conversations
> Open / Waiting...    Part of unfinished  Overdue / Timing... / Untargeted...
> View unfinished      View unassigned     View reply attention
> 
> Other work and review queues — all dates
> Follow-ups · Delivery recovery · Intake review · Handoff review · Feedback review
> [Only currently permitted owner destinations; independent of filters]
> 
> RESULTS FOR [Last 30 days v]   [actual dates]   Timezone [zone v]
> Across the inboxes you can report on. Work now filters do not apply.
> 
> Reply targets                         Reply times
> Targets due in [period]                Waits ended by staff reply in [period]
> First / Next, assessed + uncertainty   First / Next, elapsed median/p90 + sample
> View target report                    View reply-time report
> 
> Request labels                        Feedback
> Current labels on conversations       Invitations issued in [period]
> started in [period]                    Responses to that cohort as of [time]
> Coverage + up to five labels           Rating counts + open-window context
> View label report                     View feedback report

This is structural, not a frozen pixel grid. The bracketed permission explanation is a design annotation, not mandatory product copy. The actual review links are visually outside the Work now selector container and lead to independent owner queues. If a link is not authorized, omit it without hinting at hidden records. Do not add a union badge or make its data obey the nearby controls.

Desktop can use three restrained current summaries and two columns of historical panels. Mobile becomes one column in the same semantic order. The page uses existing Maia/Zinc tokens, spacing, typography and Base UI controls. Names and units carry meaning; colored tiles, decorative gauges, animated counters and a large “Support health” score do not.

### REQ26-D30-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Morning work review

Applies to **US26-D30-01**, acceptance **AC26-D30-01-01–03**.

Illustrative scenario: Maya helps oversee donor care at a tenant supporting missionaries and projects. She is concerned that an older inquiry was missed. This tests the design; it is not an asserted universal ministry workflow.

1. **Open Overview.** Work now uses All accessible inboxes and the latest qualified result. It makes no claim about inboxes Maya cannot access. Loading values are placeholders with an accessible busy state, not zero.
2. **Narrow current work if useful.** Maya chooses Donor care under Currently handled in. Only Work now changes. The Results caption remains visible and unchanged. A missing, forbidden or no-longer-qualified selected inbox asks for a deliberate replacement rather than switching to All or returning an empty healthy count.
3. **Understand the summaries.** All unfinished includes Open and both Waiting states, including future-deferred Open. Its state breakdown explains that not every unfinished request needs immediate action. Unassigned is a subset, not additional volume. Reply attention deduplicates conversations with still-owed replies, with explicit overlapping source groups. An inbox marked Retired can still show owner-qualified retained work; retirement alone neither removes that work nor grants access.
4. **Open the concern.** View reply attention opens that exact current conversation-level predicate, not a “created recently” list. The older inquiry remains discoverable regardless of the Results period. Each conversation opens its actual permitted underlying periods and normal detail.
5. **Handle the real work.** Normal assignment, reply, assistance, reminder and ending actions remain in their owners. The overview does not claim a request, mark a review read, send a message or resolve a task by being opened.
6. **Return without reconstructing context.** Back restores safe controls, scroll and focus; a new evaluation is labelled if the data changed. A preserved report context never preserves revoked transcript/CRM authority.

Existing source-owned due follow-up and actionable delivery recovery remain directly discoverable through those named destinations; they are not new queues or a union badge. A fulfilled reply can leave reply attention while a later actionable delivery failure needs recovery. Zero current reply-attention never certifies that these other obligations are complete.

Feedback, intake and handoff review can be relevant even when a period preview has no data or feedback is Off. The separate all-date links preserve those existing journeys without introducing another queue or a new combined alert concept.

### REQ26-D30-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Reviewing a period

Applies to **US26-D30-03**, acceptance **AC26-D30-03-01–03**.

Maya selects Last 30 days, sees the actual date range and timezone, and understands that today's interval is still in progress. Presets apply once. Custom allows 1–366 local calendar dates with a deliberate Apply and rejects future-ending/invalid ranges inline; the prior valid results keep their prior label until a valid request starts. For a longer analysis, the relevant full report supplies its own qualified range support.

The four sections cover each report's authorized population, including retired-source references where the owner preserves meaningful current report access. Today's active-inbox catalog must not erase historical populations. They intentionally do not pretend the Now inbox is an equivalent historical dimension. This costs one extra step when Maya needs a specialized inbox-specific historical review: **View full report**, then use its source-appropriate filter. It avoids multiple competing selectors and misleading numbers on the common starting page.

**Reply targets** separates First and Next and shows the accepted due cohort, assessed ratio, finalized coverage, unknown/potential cases and exclusions. A small summary cannot hide those facts behind a tooltip. If there are no due targets, say so; a policy currently Off does not erase old results.

**Reply times** labels elapsed time and completed waiting periods. For each First/Next sample, show median, p90 and measured count, with the existing timing/cohort exclusion summary. One reply can end several waits. Service-hours detail remains available in the full report. Do not call the number effort, resolution speed or recipient satisfaction.

**Request labels** explicitly reports current labels on the component-first conversation-start cohort. Show total/labelled/unlabelled coverage and up to five leading labels with counts and N-based percentages. A small horizontal table/bar comparison is suitable; a pie is not, because memberships overlap. Archived applied terms remain labelled where permitted. Show Start date unconfirmed and unavailable metadata according to the existing owner instead of quietly dropping them into complete totals.

**Feedback** shows invitations issued in the period and responses to those same invitations as of evaluation. A reply arriving this week to an older invitation does not enter this week's issued-cohort numerator. Include current open response-window context and rating sample/coverage. Comments, personal names and case details stay in the authorized full report/detail. Feedback Off leaves historical data visible; it simply stops new policy work under D28.

Clicking a number opens its exact native-grain detail. Clicking **View full report** navigates more generally with period/zone only. This distinction prevents a target count from pretending to be a conversation count or silently applying the current-work inbox.

### REQ26-D30-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — CRM continuity

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

From a result, the staff member opens the same canonical Support conversation available from CRM Communications → Support. Current Support/source and relevant CRM/field permissions govern context in both directions. No duplicated contact/customer record, raw email-to-Party identity claim, copied activity or new last-contact timestamp is created.

If the staff member cannot view the linked giving/care record, the report does not reveal it through a count, subject, hidden-row badge or preview. A refund, receipt, recurring-gift or contact change remains the owning domain's actual command, with its validation, approvals and audit. Returning preserves safe navigation, not an authorization grant.

### REQ26-D30-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — States and recovery

Applies to **US26-D30-05**, acceptance **AC26-D30-05-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State                           | What the person sees and can do                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Loading                         | Stable section structure and named busy state; no fabricated zero/100% or focus movement.                                                                                     |
| Complete zero/no sample         | Accurate empty wording with the selected dates/scope; no percentage where the denominator is zero.                                                                            |
| Current policy Off with history | Retained qualified historical numbers plus a quiet current-setting indicator; normal report/review access remains.                                                            |
| Off with no history             | Explain that there are no measured records for the cohort and the relevant policy is Off; Manage appears only when authorized.                                                |
| Unknown/incomplete evidence     | Show the qualified unknown/coverage meaning, or block an exact total when its owner cannot supply one. Do not score unknowns or call partial data complete.                   |
| One source failed               | That section offers Retry and an honest unavailable state; other sections and ordinary work remain usable.                                                                    |
| Now refresh delayed             | Updated time remains visible; after 120 seconds without a current qualified read, show Out of date. Cached values require continuing authority; otherwise clear them.         |
| Offline/hidden tab              | Automatic refresh pauses. Retain only qualified local information under existing policy; do not issue offline actions or catch-up polling storms.                             |
| Context changed/revoked         | Discard late old results; clear forbidden data; keep only safe controls/return paths. A removed selected inbox is not silently All.                                           |
| Detail differs after click      | Show the exact original safe evaluation if supported, or explicitly Updated since overview after current reevaluation. Do not use an old timestamp as fake historical replay. |

Refresh re-reads the current contexts. Now may update once per minute while visible/online; historical results are not recalculated on every Now poll. Updates do not steal focus, animate through values or announce every number. Meaningful user-triggered completion/error announcements remain available.

### REQ26-D30-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Maintenance and future configurability

Applies to **US26-D30-06**, acceptance **AC26-D30-06-01–03**.

There is no Create dashboard, compulsory setup wizard, layout save or inactive Configure button. Authorized Manage links go to the actual inbox/target/label/feedback owner. They do not create another editor or settings copy. Product maintainers own the fixed composition's reviewed release and keep old deep links either qualified or clearly unavailable rather than exposing a second version of the truth.

The future direction is fully configurable composition through shared reporting. Prepare by keeping stable owner-qualified block/read/detail contracts, metric definitions and presentation separate. Do not create layout tables, a registry UI, widget scripting, custom formulas or a general builder now. Later configuration must have a complete ownership/save/share/reset/migration/permission journey and may bind only compatible source scopes. This avoids repainting the current UI around an unnecessary unfinished platform.

### REQ26-D30-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Accessibility and proof

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Use native semantics and existing Base UI controls, visible focus, labelled dates/timezone/scope, predictable heading and keyboard order, tables with correct headers and text alternatives for every plotted value. Preserve full meaningful long names via accessible wrapping/details, not hover-only truncation. Test named screen readers, keyboard, 200% zoom, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, touch, long translations, RTL/bidi, locale formatting, reduced motion and low bandwidth. Preserve the established shared motion/touch tokens rather than adding another design system.

The main P01–P48 defines the release outcomes. Moderated tests must establish that staff understand the two independent scopes, find an older owed request, interpret samples/Off correctly and return from detail/CRM without repeated entry. No rendered prototype, automated accessibility result or actual Asym usability study has been performed in this grooming stage.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0002 — Owners and exact result grains

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fixed block                      | Authoritative facts                                      | Grain / cohort                                                                                                                                          | Required outcome                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `support.work.unfinished`        | D3 work, D10 current topology, D20 qualified query       | Distinct current continuing conversations in Open/both Waiting, including future-deferred Open; current selected home                                   | Complete N with source-qualified status breakdown. No urgency or completion inference.                                                                       |
| `support.work.unassigned`        | D6/D8 handling, same work/query owners                   | Unfinished conversations with no current assignee and retained owner review distinctions                                                                | U is a subset of N under the same read cut. No fresh-intake routing or permission to claim is created.                                                       |
| `support.work.reply-attention`   | D14 still-owed contributions and current work            | Distinct continuing conversations with at least one still-owed qualified contribution                                                                   | Overall distinct count plus D14 groups that can overlap. Fulfilled-but-unscored evidence is not owed work. Detail retains every permitted underlying period. |
| `support.report.target-results`  | D14 finalized target/policy/evidence                     | Targets due in the selected half-open interval; First/Next separate, potential uncertain sources outside finalized denominator                          | On-time/assessed with finalized coverage, misses/unknown/exclusions and potential unconfirmed cases.                                                         |
| `support.report.reply-times`     | D14 qualified accepted-response coverage/time            | Waiting periods completed by staff reply in interval; exact measured elapsed durations, First/Next separate                                             | Median/p90/sample and excluded or uncertain timing/cohort counts; no message/conversation/effort substitution.                                               |
| `support.report.current-labels`  | D21 origin memberships and catalog, D10 current topology | Whole permitted current component first; earliest original start in interval; current labels/current report responsibility                              | N/L/U where complete, Start date unconfirmed/metadata uncertainty, distinct overlapping label counts and stable top-five presentation.                       |
| `support.report.feedback-issued` | D28 opportunity/effect/issued/response/custody facts     | Distinct invitations whose source-qualified first submission-may-have-begun occurrence is in interval, plus their includable responses as of evaluation | Issued/responded and rating distribution with separate owned denominators, including indeterminate submissions; no received-date numerator.                  |

These are conceptual stable block identifiers to register in code-owned source contracts; exact package/type names remain implementation design. They identify the questions, not table names or new sources. One label rename or UI reorder cannot change a block's identity or definition.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0003 — Scope and periods

Applies to **US26-D30-03**, acceptance **AC26-D30-03-01–03**.

Now scope is explicitly All accessible inboxes or one exact current inbox under current source rights. Missing, forbidden or no-longer-qualified selected ID is invalid, never All. Retirement alone is not invalidity: preserve still-owner-qualified retained work and references without creating an archive-access grant. Its three blocks have one compatible scope and coherent evaluation cut; U≤N when complete, and the three status counts partition N. Reply attention is separately deduplicated; its groups and the three summaries are not additive.

Results has no overview-level inbox or CRM filter. Do not filter historical populations through today's active-inbox catalog; a retired source remains included only where its owner preserves meaningful current report access. It covers each report's current authorized population with its own accepted historical/current dimensions. Period/zone is common input, not common cohort meaning. Full-report navigation passes period/zone only; source-specific narrower filters belong there. Metric drilldown preserves the exact native cohort and kind, which differs from generic report navigation.

A report zone determines the half-open UTC interval derived from inclusive local calendar dates. It never changes a stored source/target calendar or evidence time. Current day results are evaluated only through the trusted read/evaluation time, visibly partial. The fixed overview's 1–366-date range and four presets bound interaction; a source owner's tighter execution constraint must surface explicitly, not silently narrow population. Full reports retain their own qualified capabilities. Resolve skipped/ambiguous local calendar boundaries using the qualified shared timezone/date owner; no browser-duration arithmetic assuming every date is 24 hours.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0004 — Server read boundary and evaluation evidence

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Use the shared API owner report readers returning only required aggregates, coverage and safe navigation descriptors. Thin app routes authenticate, validate and delegate. Do not download conversations/messages then calculate authoritative results in React. Current broad report snapshot APIs are inventory to converge, not a capability to reuse for convenience.

A result logically carries:

- Stable owner/block/definition version and measured grain/unit.
- Trusted tenant/environment/principal context and effective typed scope, without treating caller IDs as authority.
- Exact period/zone/time basis for the applicable block.
- Qualified evaluation/read cut, computed time, source-through/completeness and source/privacy authorization revisions needed by the owner.
- Counts/numerators/denominators/coverage with unambiguous empty/unknown/excluded meaning.
- A validated detail descriptor tying exact cohort/kind/definition/evaluation to its source reader.

No particular wire schema, central DSL or persistent evaluation table is implied. Reuse current owner machinery. A timestamp is not an MVCC snapshot or durable replay facility. Single-statement or qualified read-transaction consistency must prove a block's value/detail semantics; independently owned blocks need not pretend to share a distributed snapshot. Never hold a database transaction open while a person browses. A derived read model can serve only if it preserves required authorization granularity, complete contribution evidence and current restriction/withdrawal semantics; an all-tenant cached total cannot be fixed by filtering its final label.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — Detail, pagination and re-evaluation

Applies to **US26-D30-04**, acceptance **AC26-D30-04-01–03**.

Detail descriptors are source-issued/validated bounded query context, not a browser-supplied SQL filter or access capability. Derive current tenant/actor at use. Reuse exact definition/cohort/kind and current source rights. If the owner supports safe replay of the original read cut, disclose that evaluation. Otherwise rerun current source facts under the same semantic criteria and show Updated since overview with new As of evidence. Source erasure/access loss wins over count equality.

Targets are target instances; response durations are completed waits; invitation metrics are invitation effects. Their detail may link multiple rows to one conversation. Conversation-level Now detail is distinct current continuing IDs. Never translate a report predicate to D20's ordinary Created filter, duplicate a merged root per label, or claim a page of 50 rows is a complete aggregate.

Use owner keyset detail paging capped at 50 records here, stable tie-breaks and current authorization for every page. If data changes between pages, follow the existing owner's coherent snapshot/re-evaluation behavior; do not silently create missing/frozen historical rows. The overview displays only five leading labels but computes rank/count across the complete qualified population.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — Lifecycle and timing table

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Event                                    | Required behavior                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Work moves A→B                           | Now moves with current home; old target/wait/feedback provenance does not become B's historical action. Results uses existing owner dimensions, not Now selection.                           |
| Merge/Undo                               | Current component deduplication updates Now and D21 cohort atomically under source topology; originals/periods/invitations retain immutable identity. D12 relations do not merge membership. |
| New form/staff-recorded source           | D29/D26 genuine provenance/time enters only eligible source contracts. No fabricated RFC/P6 receipt or Party is added for reporting.                                                         |
| A reply fulfils work with uncertain time | Remove its fulfilled contribution from owed attention; keep uncertain scoring/cohort evidence in the historical owner report.                                                                |
| Target/feedback policy Off               | Stops the owner's applicable future effects; retained qualified history remains reportable. All-age feedback review is a separate destination.                                               |
| Late response/provider/correction        | Apply owned event/finality/correction rules in a new evaluation. Never set historical occurrence time from callback arrival or revise an exported snapshot in place.                         |
| Filter/account/tenant change             | Increment/fence request context; clear disallowed values and drop old late responses. Invalid selected scope never broadens.                                                                 |
| Link click while data changed            | Reauthorize and safely replay or explicitly re-evaluate. Return location carries no permission.                                                                                              |
| Privacy expiry/restriction/restore       | Deny current source-derived serving first, then perform qualified physical cleanup/restore suppression; overview refresh never renews source life.                                           |

Reads are idempotent in business effect: none create a communication, mark review done, change assignment, draw feedback, publish content or start an email. They may return newer current facts on a later evaluation. Existing owner mutations after navigation keep their own command identity/version and durable outcome; the overview adds no compensating workflow.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — Authorization and database proof

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Authorization precedes grouping, percentages, top labels, result counts and details. Current Support/original source/classification/field rights are checked even where the UI only shows numbers. Relevant CRM context requires its own permissions. A broad staff or report role, historical assignment, shared layout or email match grants nothing beyond the actual capability model. If an owner has not qualified a complete authorized total, respond with an honest unavailable/incomplete state; do not reveal a withheld count or silently invent a smaller cohort under the old caption.

Inventory actual table/view/function/RPC/Data API/service paths. Verify grants plus effective RLS predicates, invoker/definer execution role, PUBLIC execute, safe search_path and any BYPASSRLS job checks. An omitted WITH CHECK is not automatically a defect: PostgreSQL can reuse USING in applicable policies. The required proof is the effective old/new-row boundary and immutable attribution, not syntax alone.

No new authoritative business/layout table is required by A. If an actual existing or necessary projection/cache/receipt writer is used, its source-owner contract must enforce same-tenant endpoints, stable keys/definition/source revision, complete/noncomplete states, trusted actor/time, safe exact counts, unique effect/update generation and authorized lifecycle/delete behavior. Untrusted mutation cannot reparent tenant/source, change visibility or rewrite append-only business evidence. Financial data types/grants and money operations remain untouched.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0008 — Privacy, caching and performance

Applies to **US26-D30-07**, acceptance **AC26-D30-07-01–03**.

Cache only the permitted source-qualified projection under exact tenant/principal/effective scope/definition/source-control context. Revalidation of current authority is independent of data freshness. The 60-second foreground refresh and 120-second stale UI threshold are not permission leases or retention grants. A context revocation must discard forbidden values through current policy; unknown authorization has no stale-serving fallback.

No message bodies, response comments, personal names, raw endpoints or full CRM context are required by this overview. Do not send them to analytics, logs, provider tags, local storage or performance traces. Detail descriptors/result caches have finite owner-qualified query purposes and existing disposal/hold/restore rules; no eternal snapshots or new standalone archive. Full-report export remains its own permission-aware command, not a browser serialization of source collections.

Indexes and query plans must match actual source predicates and current authorization. Reuse qualified rollups only where their granularity permits current revocation and correct component/cohort changes. The default plan is bounded server aggregation with seven known fixed blocks, Now coalesced; do not install another BI vendor or build a warehouse. D30-R29/P44 define prospective workload/p95 proof and tighter owner budgets. No production measurement is claimed.

### REQ26-D30-DATA_CONTRACT-S0009 — Required source corrections and rollout

Applies to **US26-D30-06**, acceptance **AC26-D30-06-01–03**.

The independent five-observation source probe confirms specific old helper behavior: created-range waiting/current-open disagreement, empty specific scope broadening, current-home changes affecting historical-looking results, empty/genuine-zero collapse and raw missing-label fallback. It ran extracted pinned functions with synthetic inputs, not actual DB/RLS/API/browser behavior. The underlying source and runner provenance is in the source registry.

Do not merely repaint those outputs. Qualify the authoritative aggregate/read/detail path and legacy migration first; verify all grants/old routes/caches, then activate a compatible fixed composition. A kill switch removes only unsafe overview/report readers while safe work continues. Rollback cannot restore broad source dumps or erased caches. Future configuration can consume the same truthful blocks only after its separate full ownership/lifecycle/UX qualification. All D30-P01–P48 remain required and unexecuted release proof.

## Follow-up time choices

### REQ26-D31-R01 — D31-R01 — One purpose and one shared reminder

Applies to **US26-D31-03**, acceptance **AC26-D31-03-01–03**.

Follow up schedules the existing shared Support conversation reminder. It is optional, visible to currently authorized staff and independent of the conversation's work status, assignment, read state, CRM task, reply target and business outcome. Scheduling/replacing preserves D3 work meaning. It creates no personal alarm, new work domain or generic scheduling framework.

### REQ26-D31-R02 — D31-R02 — A small fixed menu

Applies to **US26-D31-01**, acceptance **AC26-D31-01-01–03**.

Every permitted entry point offers the same four quick meanings: In 1 hour; In 4 hours; Tomorrow at the displayed current local minute; In 1 week at that minute on local date plus seven. Show actual weekday, unambiguous date including year, time and relevant zone before commitment. Choose date and time remains visible after the four choices. No preset is automatically applied, remembered as a new default, or required before another action.

### REQ26-D31-R03 — D31-R03 — Two explicit kinds of time arithmetic

Applies to **US26-D31-01**, acceptance **AC26-D31-01-01–03**.

Use a trusted server reference instant. Elapsed choices add exactly 3,600 or 14,400 seconds, then round the resulting future instant upward to a whole minute; this adds less than sixty seconds and the displayed result is the value committed. Calendar choices take the actual reference local date plus one or seven and its displayed HH:mm with seconds zero. Never round the reference across midnight before choosing the calendar date. Calendar days need not equal 86,400 elapsed seconds. No business-day, Monday, holiday or D14 service-calendar adjustment occurs.

### REQ26-D31-R04 — D31-R04 — Explicit timezone context

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

For a new chooser, use valid `the tenant-owned default timezone` from the owning tenant context. If missing/invalid, visibly use UTC, expose a nonblocking configuration issue to the authorized maintainer and allow a valid per-use zone override. The picker always displays its zone, with the offset applicable at the target date when needed to disambiguate it. Changing this picker zone does not change tenant settings, a missionary profile, CRM data or any existing reminder. Do not derive zone from requester identity, location, IP address, a reporting filter or service-hours calendar.

The per-use zone control is available for quick and Custom choices and supports validated IANA identifiers, including UTC. New reminders do not require a new profile preference or a browser-zone authority. On edit, begin with the recorded zone and exact accepted instant. Within Custom, deliberately changing the input zone retains the entered date/time fields and resolves a new candidate; show the changed result and require Set/Update before commitment. This is distinct from changing a read-only display zone, which preserves the instant. A legacy reminder without original zone provenance keeps its instant and clearly uses a current display zone; do not invent historical provenance.

### REQ26-D31-R05 — D31-R05 — Stable preview without artificial expiry

Applies to **US26-D31-01**, acceptance **AC26-D31-01-01–03**.

Resolve quick offers once on deliberate open or Refresh choices, using one reference and selected zone. Keep the shown instant stable while a person reads, points or types. When relative wording ages, qualify it with its reference time or use its exact calendar label; expose Refresh choices without moving existing targets. A valid explicitly reviewed future candidate has no arbitrary preview timeout. Explicit refresh, new choice or zone edit may produce a new preview, never an automatic new write. Commit validates the exact candidate rather than recomputing a delay from send time or retry time.

The server validates local date/time/zone/offset against the submitted instant and returns a reviewable discrepancy if they disagree. A preview is not a security grant or proof someone read a screen. No preview token table, job, cryptographic viewing attestation or separate workflow is required.

### REQ26-D31-R06 — D31-R06 — Custom with direct entry

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

Choose date and time opens one focused form with labelled date, time and timezone; direct entry and calendar selection coexist. A fresh Custom form starts on today's date in the displayed zone with time unset, unless continuing a deliberately selected candidate or editing an existing reminder. Date selection alone does not save. Time is minute-granular for newly chosen values. Show one exact combined preview and one Set follow-up or Update follow-up action. Cancel/Escape before submission has no effects; preserve values on validation/network errors.

Use explicit locale-format hints and a calendar representation that maps unambiguously to an ISO date, while displaying familiar localized month/day names and 12/24-hour time. Do not silently interpret ambiguous free-form dates or add a natural-language parser. Invalid dates are errors, not normalized rollovers. Date/year navigation must not require hundreds of month clicks.

### REQ26-D31-R07 — D31-R07 — DST, political changes and precision

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

If a chosen wall time does not exist, keep the requested values, explain the clock change and offer valid nearby choices or another time. If it occurs twice, show the two actual offsets/instants and require a choice. No default earlier/later selection or silent gap adjustment is permitted. A quick calendar offer with such ambiguity opens that focused review instead of committing. A valid elapsed-duration instant is already unambiguous; show its actual target offset.

Persist the accepted UTC instant and enough original local input, IANA zone and resolved offset provenance to explain it. Later timezone preference, tzdb, travel or inbox changes do not rewrite an accepted instant. Existing seconds/microseconds are not rounded by opening, viewing or cancelling edit. Deliberately changing a Custom date, time or input zone creates a new minute-granular candidate; show old/new exact values before Update, including any original seconds. Preserve accepted original evidence even if later zone rules render that instant differently.

### REQ26-D31-R08 — D31-R08 — Validation and due boundaries

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

For a genuinely new admission, require a finite supported instant strictly later than trusted server time at the serialized mutation boundary. Custom supports the representable ISO civil-year range 0001–9999 intersected with valid future UTC instants; it imposes no arbitrary seven-day or one-year business limit. Reject overflow, infinity, impossible dates, missing zone, contradictory offset and past/equal-now input without losing the form. Do not use `due_at > now()` as a persistent database constraint: valid reminders must become due.

Due execution uses now greater than or equal to the accepted instant. Existing overdue work remains due, never silently moved forward. A long date uses existing durable product scheduling/recovery within the qualified provider horizon; it does not become one unbounded provider sleep. Stored support for a year is not a promise that timezones or staff plans remain unchanged until then.

### REQ26-D31-R09 — D31-R09 — Existing lifecycle and simple correction

Applies to **US26-D31-03**, acceptance **AC26-D31-03-01–03**.

At most one current reminder exists for a conversation. Change time conditionally replaces its generation. Remove reminder cancels that generation and deferral while preserving work meaning. Work now is the existing explicit Open action and clears deferral. Resolve cancels; an incoming qualifying event follows D3. On resolved work, use an explicit reopen followed by scheduling, or an already-qualified reviewed Reopen-and-remind action under D3; opening the picker cannot reopen work. This decision adds no new compound command. Waiting-side-only changes preserve the reminder. A current due generation clears deferral and creates Open Follow-up due review with the prior reason preserved. Due processing does not directly select an assignee, but D7's applicable active-coverage evaluation still runs and may reassign work under its own rules, including when the original scheduling staff member has left.

A Support conversation merge or Undo retains D10's reviewed resulting reminder plan and qualified generation. Do not silently choose earliest/latest or resurrect an old job. A related/new conversation does not inherit a reminder merely through source linking.

### REQ26-D31-R10 — D31-R10 — Trusted mutation and database safety

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

All menu, keyboard, bulk and authorized embedded-detail mutations use the same D3 command in the shared API owner. Derive tenant and actual human profile/system attribution from trusted context, not caller fields or assumed auth-user/profile-ID equality. Recheck current conversation/inbox/resource access and reviewed versions. Enforce same-tenant parent relationships, unique current reminder/generation, finite due data, allowed state combinations and immutable ownership in the authoritative transaction.

Use least-privilege grants and RLS. Evaluate both old-row USING and resulting-row WITH CHECK for allowed client mutations, and revoke bypassing direct lifecycle/timer/history writes. A permissive additional policy cannot leave the old bypass open. Check view invoker policy, function EXECUTE grants, fixed search path and service-role authorization separately. Existing tenant FKs/RLS are not alleged absent. Do not add money fields, copy CRM identifiers without tenant-aware relationships, or cascade-delete required history.

### REQ26-D31-R11 — D31-R11 — Concurrency and replay

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

Atomically admit state revision, current reminder/generation, immutable before/after command evidence and required durable dispatch/recovery intent. Concurrent schedule/replace/remove/Resolve/new-input actions serialize or conflict against reviewed versions; no lost update or revived cancelled generation is permitted. Before fresh future-time/stale-state validation, reconcile an identical previously admitted command after checking current access. Return its original receipt and separately current authorized state. Changed input under one identity conflicts. A new deliberate change uses a new identity. Late receipts cannot overwrite newer state.

### REQ26-D31-R12 — D31-R12 — Dependable execution and honest recovery

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

The product reminder remains authoritative; the shared workflow ledger, claims and identifier-only envelopes execute it. A callback checks current tenant/conversation/generation/due/eligible state atomically. Required D7 coverage-evaluation intent commits with due-created Open work; any resulting qualified transfer uses the guarded assignment path. Early attempts remain pending with a durable future attempt. Old, cancelled, applied or superseded attempts are no-ops even after a claim lease expires. Recovery scans bridge commit-before-dispatch crashes and finite provider run horizons. Failed/unknown saves reconcile; reopening the picker does not assume failure. Display intended due and actual processing time separately.

### REQ26-D31-R13 — D31-R13 — Complete access journey

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

Expose a labelled Follow up control beside status and assignment, with existing reminder date visible. Quick activation commits the displayed time; Custom alone opens the richer form. Preserve selected conversation, list position, filters, return destination, scroll/focus and unsent rich-text draft. Keep a successfully deferred conversation open in detail if it leaves the current queue, with truthful membership feedback. Existing follow-up views and D30 recovery navigation remain discoverable; no new overview metric is introduced.

### REQ26-D31-R14 — D31-R14 — Bulk and alternate entry points

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

Keyboard/palette opens the same chooser; typing in TipTap or another input cannot accidentally invoke it. Qualified exact-ID bulk operations show the selected count and one exact shared instant/zone, then report authorized per-item success/conflict/failure using D3/D7's existing contract. Server evaluation occurs per item, including dates that become past during a batch. Never silently recalculate later items to new instants. Retry only the same unresolved intents; don't expand selection to newly matching rows or leak inaccessible records.

### REQ26-D31-R15 — D31-R15 — CRM and owner-domain continuity

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

CRM shows the same canonical Support conversation and current reminder only when both its relationship context and Support data are currently authorized. Entering from CRM preserves the record return path and supported detail context. Support record access does not grant CRM, finance, missionary or care access, and CRM access alone does not expose restricted Support metadata. A requester, participant, authenticated user, CRM person, represented organization, assignee and CRM owner remain distinct. Email matching, labels and reminder assignment confer no identity or authority.

Links, merges, unlinking, archive and permission changes use their owning domain's authoritative relationships. A reminder references the conversation, never a copied CRM due field. It neither creates a duplicate person/task nor rewrites contact data. Genuine D11 delegated tasks remain separate linked work. Scheduling, expiry or resolving Support cannot mark a refund, receipt, contact change, recurring gift or delegated business task complete.

### REQ26-D31-R16 — D31-R16 — Email Studio and TipTap seam

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Opening, previewing, setting, changing, removing and expiring this reminder perform no email content preparation, dispatch, scheduled send or new catalog-notification action. Support owns work/reminder facts; P17/Email Studio owns governed email content/preparation; P6 owns delivery/reconciliation. D4 send review remains a separate deliberately selected operation; plain Send preserves a valid reminder. This choice does not add a combined-send action or weaken an existing one.

D24 curated shortcuts cannot store/apply reminder presets. TipTap remains the rich-text editor for qualified replies, notes, signatures and shortcut wording; ordinary date/time fields are shared form controls. Never mount a second rich-text composer in the picker or change recipients, attachments, notes/reply mode, signatures or prepared message material. Existing independently qualified platform failure escalation remains governed by its owner; it is not a new reminder email.

### REQ26-D31-R17 — D31-R17 — Privacy and minimization

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Reminder APIs, caches, realtime events, history, searches and CRM projections use current tenant/resource authorization. Retained UI state is cleared on logout/tenant switch/revocation as appropriate. Technical timing telemetry excludes message bodies, recipients, donor identifiers and exact location data; trusted business history records permitted actor/cause/operation references. The selected timezone is scheduling provenance, not a missionary location claim. Donor/public surfaces do not expose staff reminder internals. Existing owner-governed retention, redaction, export and backup rules apply.

### REQ26-D31-R18 — D31-R18 — Visual and accessible interaction

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

Compose existing shared `base-maia`/Base UI primitives, semantic Zinc-family tokens and Core typography, spacing, focus and motion. Use readable sentence case, one compact surface, exact secondary timing text, generous hit areas and a distinct but restrained focus/selection treatment. No all-caps microtext, ornamental clocks, new palette, primitive library or app-local calendar fork. Mobile uses a responsive single-column dialog/sheet with visible action and keyboard-safe scrolling.

Provide keyboard operation, input labels/format hints, announced validation and save outcomes, focus return, contrast, zoom/reflow, reduced motion, high-contrast support and touch targets. Meet WCAG 2.2 AA; use at least 44-CSS-pixel primary action rows as a product touch target, distinguishing that from the AA 24-pixel minimum and exceptions. Calendar cells may use the shared compact geometry when AA/spacing and real touch tests pass. Reuse does not establish accessibility without testing.

### REQ26-D31-R19 — D31-R19 — Performance and operational bounds

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

The four quick options are constant-sized, calendar rendering is bounded and timezone lookup is searchable without rendering every result at once. No per-conversation scheduler is created on picker open. Batch validation/reads and use indexed tenant/current-due/generation access paths, with separate bounded shared recovery admission for provider horizons. Do not scan all messages or send one preview request per row/keystroke. Preserve tenant fairness and accepted-work recovery when new scheduling is disabled.

### REQ26-D31-R20 — D31-R20 — Maintenance and future evolution

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Product and shared-UI owners maintain one versioned definition of the four quick meanings, one renderer/resolver contract and common conformance tests. Tenant staff maintain no preset list. Changing future menu labels or zone defaults cannot reinterpret saved instants or receipts. Support operations own stale/failed due work through normal recovery controls; direct database repair is not the routine process. Personal presets or AI suggestions require later researched decisions and must remain inputs to the same human-authorized command.

### REQ26-D31-R21 — D31-R21 — Migration and release sequencing

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Qualify D3's command, constraints, history, worker and read-model contract before enabling the new chooser. Fence legacy writers, then backfill known instants without reinterpreting them from old labels. Mark missing provenance as unknown. Ambiguous old work follows D3's migration-review rule. Deploy compatible readers before writers, verify mixed versions, activate by controlled tenant scope, and preserve due recovery/history if new scheduling is disabled. Roll-forward fixes must not shift existing due dates; rollback must not restore bypassing old writers.

### REQ26-D31-R22 — D31-R22 — Traceable proof

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Trace D31-R01–R24 through the glossary/ADR, required OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets, implementation and release evidence. Keep D3/D4/D7/D14/D24/D26/D30 semantics consistent. Execute all P01–P32 release groups in the proof ledger before claiming readiness. Reference arithmetic and documentation checks are not SQL/RLS/worker/browser/provider or participant proof. Unknowns in throughput and usability become explicit release gates and operating signals, not confident scalability or perfection claims.

### REQ26-D31-R23 — D31-R23 — Failure states and low-bandwidth use

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

While preview resolution is loading, keep the compact surface and usable explicit inputs; do not show a false exact time. Saving shows a single pending operation. A definitely rejected save retains input and gives an actionable cause; an unknown outcome keeps its identity and offers Check status. Cancel before submission is different from closing an admitted operation. Reconnect reconciles before new actions. Custom remains usable for entry during a transient outage, but scheduling is only confirmed after authorized server admission. No offline delayed auto-send or browser alarm is promised.

### REQ26-D31-R24 — D31-R24 — Independent clocks and responsible promises

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

A follow-up time is an internal review commitment, not a customer-visible appointment, service target or guaranteed execution second. It does not alter D14 calendars/targets, D30 historical cohorts, D5 explicit ending, CRM/giving/task deadlines or notification consent. No mandatory chaser, automatic resolution, SLA pause, recurrence or future configuration requirement is inferred from time selection. Any deliberately written customer promise remains governed by the existing Support work and owner-action rules.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — Job and entry

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Maya is handling an inquiry for a tenant's donor-care team. She needs to check it again after receiving information. This is an illustrative task to test the experience, not a claim about all ministries' work hours or donor processes. She already has the conversation open, possibly from its CRM record, and may have an unsent reply.

Use the visible **Follow up** control alongside existing status/assignment. A clock icon can support the label, never replace it. With an accepted reminder, show **Follow up · Mon, 14 Sep, 14:30** and its timezone detail in the opened control. Use the same component and command from CRM-entered Support detail; viewing the CRM record does not itself grant access. The label is an internal work reminder, not a promise to send an email.

One compact popover is appropriate on a desktop. The title is **Set follow-up** or **Change follow-up**. Display the timezone once above the list, with **Change** available; display an offset per row where the target offset differs or is needed for clarity. Each row's accessible name includes its full actual date/time/zone. The shared layout wraps long text rather than truncating essential timing.

An example at Sunday, 13 September 2026, 14:30 in Bangkok:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Choice                | Actual result shown before activation |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| In 1 hour             | Sun, 13 Sep 2026 · 15:30              |
| In 4 hours            | Sun, 13 Sep 2026 · 18:30              |
| Tomorrow at 14:30     | Mon, 14 Sep 2026 · 14:30              |
| In 1 week at 14:30    | Sun, 20 Sep 2026 · 14:30              |
| Choose date and time… | Opens Custom                          |

The common zone line reads **Bangkok · UTC+07:00**, mapped to `Asia/Bangkok`; the IANA identifier is available without hover in the zone control. The example intentionally includes Sunday: a week is seven local dates, not the next presumed business week. Exact formatting follows the active locale; dates never rely on ambiguous slash notation alone. The operational noun remains Support Hub; this does not create a new Support Studio domain.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Quick journey, step by step

Applies to **US26-D31-01**, acceptance **AC26-D31-01-01–03**.

1. **Open.** Load the authorized current reminder and trusted reference needed for exact offers. Keep the conversation, recipients, draft, filters and return path intact. If a save is still of unknown outcome, show reconciliation instead of treating the record as unscheduled.
2. **Read.** Show four resolved choices and Custom. The visible zone initially uses the tenant's valid default. Staff can deliberately change it for this use. No hidden browser/requester/location inference occurs.
3. **Choose.** Click or keyboard-activate a row once. Its exact displayed instant is the intended mutation; no second modal or separate Save button appears for a normal quick choice. Hover/focus performs no write. If the row needs DST disambiguation, its action says **Review time** and opens the focused Custom state instead.
4. **Save.** Show one pending action with appropriate accessible status and prevent duplicate local intention. Actual duplicate protection is the command receipt, not the disabled button. Keep the old accepted reminder authoritative until the server admits replacement.
5. **Return.** Show **Follow-up set for Mon, 14 Sep at 14:30 · Bangkok**. Keep the accepted value persistently accessible in detail. If the conversation no longer belongs to the current queue, say so without unexpectedly closing the detail or jumping to another record.

The common path is two deliberate activations from detail: open, select. This is a designed interaction count, not measured completion time. A placeholder, loading row or unverified browser calculation must not pretend to be the exact server-qualified result.

Quick offers remain bound to their original reference. Do not recalculate under the pointer or while a screen reader is reading. When wording ages, show **1 hour from 14:30**, or an actual weekday/date after rollover; offer **Refresh choices**. An explicitly reviewed future Custom/absolute candidate does not expire after an arbitrary minute. Past or contradictory values are corrected in place. Refresh makes new offers; retry preserves the original candidate.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Custom journey, step by step

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

1. **Open the same focused surface.** Choose date and time replaces the list with the form, with Back returning to the list without mutation. It does not create stacked modals or another composer.
2. **Date.** Use the existing shared calendar and a labelled directly editable date field. A new Custom value begins on today's date in the chosen zone; month/year navigation and text entry avoid endless calendar paging. An explicit candidate or existing reminder takes precedence over this initial date.
3. **Time.** Start empty for a fresh Custom value. A clearly labelled time input supports typing and the locale's 12/24-hour convention. The person supplies the intended minute. Do not default to midnight, nine or an unselected hidden hour. The field's selected value, not mere focus, controls the candidate.
4. **Timezone.** Keep the named zone visible beside/below these fields. Change is available through searchable zone selection; search by a supported city/name, and display the IANA identity when names could be confused. Result offsets are computed for the chosen date, not today's date. Within Custom, changing the zone keeps the entered date/time and resolves a new candidate in that zone. Show the changed result, including old/new values when editing. Nothing changes until Set/Update. A read-only display-zone change outside this form merely converts the same instant.
5. **Review in place.** Show the full combined result immediately below valid inputs: **Follow up Monday, 14 September 2026 at 09:15 · New York (UTC−04:00)**. No internal implementation details are shown. If the time has two possible offsets, require the explicit occurrence choice here. If it does not exist, retain it and offer valid nearby times or manual correction; none is pre-committed.
6. **Set follow-up.** The one primary action saves that exact candidate through the shared command. Selecting a calendar day, changing a month or choosing a zone never saves. Cancel/Escape returns without changes before submission. Errors preserve values and focus; accepted-but-unknown outcomes reconcile the command identity.

New values are minute-granular. Existing reminders may have seconds: merely opening the form never rewrites them. While an old value remains unchanged, display its exact seconds in the existing-value detail and keep Update inactive. Deliberately changing its date, time or input zone creates a new minute-granular replacement; show old/new exact values before Update, including the original seconds. Cancel preserves the accepted original. Saved provenance distinguishes original input from present-day display.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Edit, remove and work now

Applies to **US26-D31-03**, acceptance **AC26-D31-03-01–03**.

Open the accepted reminder to inspect **Current follow-up**, its actual time, zone and permitted author/history. The same surface offers quick replacement choices, **Change date and time**, and **Remove reminder**. Editing starts from the original instant/recorded zone; a later tenant-zone change does not shift it.

Remove reminder conditionally cancels the current generation and removes deferral. It preserves the work status and does not cancel a CRM task, send an email or remove due review already admitted. A stale remove cannot delete a newer replacement. Staff use the existing **Open / Work now** action when they mean to return to active review now. Those two intentions have distinct labels and effects.

No destructive-style full-screen confirmation is needed for this reversible reminder cancellation. Show the admitted result and retain the normal correction path. Do not provide a fake Undo that restores an old generation after intervening input, expiry or another staff member's edit.

Resolved work requires explicit reopening. The control explains **Reopen this conversation to set a follow-up** and links to the existing authorized status action; an already-qualified, explicitly reviewed **Reopen and remind** action remains permitted under D3. The chooser never hides a timer on resolved work and adds no new compound command or Reopen-and-send operation.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Returning through CRM and working with another person

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

Maya can enter the same Support detail from an authorized CRM Support list, review the reminder, make an authorized change and return to the originating CRM record. There is one due instant and one Support history. No copied CRM task or Activity event is generated merely by this action.

Another authorized worker sees the same reminder; its creator does not acquire exclusive ownership. If that worker changes it while Maya edits, Maya receives a focused conflict showing the currently authorized value. Her proposed input is retained for an explicit new decision; it does not automatically overwrite the newer value. Replayed older receipts remain receipts, not current state.

A CRM person merge does not move a reminder onto a new person record or create a second one. A Support conversation merge must retain D10's explicit resulting reminder plan; competing reminders are not silently reduced to earliest/latest. Unlinking a CRM association does not cancel Support work, and access revocation removes unauthorized context immediately on subsequent authorized reads/actions.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Other accepted entry points

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

The existing keyboard or command-palette action opens this chooser on the explicit target, rather than applying an invisible twenty-four-hour value. Global shortcuts respect text-input focus, especially TipTap. Datepicker arrow keys remain local to the calendar and cannot navigate or modify the conversation accidentally.

Existing qualified bulk actions use exact selected IDs, a visible count and one exact candidate in one visible zone. They retain D3/D7's per-item results. No silent per-inbox timezone recalculation occurs. If a batch takes long enough that the candidate becomes past before a new item's admission, that item requires correction; successful items stay saved. A batch recap may stay available while rows leave a filter, so disappearance is not mistaken for failure.

Choosing a reminder while composing is a separate D3/D4 work action. It does not send, prepare, schedule, rewrite or discard the email. D24 shortcut contents cannot store reminder choices. The ordinary TipTap editor and its recipient/attachment/signature review remain untouched.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Due and failure journey

Applies to **US26-D31-03**, acceptance **AC26-D31-03-01–03**.

At or after the accepted instant, the current qualified reminder returns the conversation to **Open** with **Follow-up due**, retaining the previous reason for waiting. The timer does not directly choose an assignee; D7's applicable coverage evaluation still runs and may reassign work under its own rules, including after the original scheduling worker leaves. Underlying CRM/giving/task outcomes do not change. The selected time is a review time, not evidence an awaited answer arrived. Staff can find due work through existing follow-up/recovery views and D30's independent navigation.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State                   | What the person sees and can do                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Preview loading         | Stable small surface and loading feedback; no fabricated exact result. Custom entry can remain available.                                 |
| Validation error        | Inline error attached to the field and values preserved. Correct an invalid date, missing time or past value.                             |
| Ambiguous local time    | Two explicitly labelled offsets/occurrences; no default selection.                                                                        |
| Nonexistent local time  | Explanation of the clock change, original input retained and valid alternatives offered for explicit choice.                              |
| Save pending            | One pending operation; closing the surface does not falsely cancel an admitted request.                                                   |
| Definitely not admitted | Keep input and show the actionable error. Retrying follows the command's known outcome.                                                   |
| Outcome unknown         | “We’re checking whether your follow-up was saved.” Check status reconciles the same identity.                                             |
| Conflict                | Show current authorized state and preserve the proposed value for deliberate review.                                                      |
| Offline                 | Preserve permitted in-memory input, show connectivity state and confirm nothing until server admission. No browser alarm or silent queue. |
| Due processing delayed  | Display original due time, pending/failed recovery honestly and the actual eventual processing time. Never slide the due time forward.    |
| Permission revoked      | Stop reading/writing the restricted detail; give a nonsensitive explanation and safe return navigation.                                   |

The copy is accepted product wording. There is no routine extra reason field, required internal note, assignment wizard or calendar settings trip. A real Support promise can already be documented through the existing authorized conversation tools.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — Visual and accessibility specification

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Use the exact Core `base-maia` geometry and shared Base UI primitives. Reuse semantic background, foreground, muted text, border, focus and accent tokens in both themes. Use sentence case and normal readable text. Main choices align consistently; the actual date/time is supporting text with enough contrast to be read, not a low-contrast tooltip. One subtle divider separates Custom; another separates existing-reminder removal. Focus and selected state are clear without relying on color alone.

On narrow screens, use the shared responsive dialog/sheet pattern with one column, the same four choices and a compact Custom form. Keep the primary action visible above the virtual keyboard or reachable by normal scrolling. No horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS pixels; long translations and zone names wrap. Primary action rows target at least 44 CSS pixels. Shared compact calendar cells must meet WCAG 2.2 AA target/spacing requirements and pass real touch testing; the AA standard is not falsely described as requiring 44 everywhere.

Use the primitives' correct button/list or dialog/form semantics. A composite form must not be embedded as if it were a single menu item. Focus moves into the appropriate form field, returns to the trigger on dismissal and stays recoverable after errors. Keyboard calendar navigation, direct text entry, visible format hints, full accessible date names and associated error messages are required. Announce meaningful resolved/saved/error changes politely, not a ticking countdown. Respect reduced motion and high-contrast settings.

W3C's datepicker example supports the focus/input principles but warns that production and mobile assistive-technology testing are necessary. GOV.UK date guidance distinguishes choosing a future date from recalling a known date; use both calendar and direct entry here, not a copied birth-date form. No vendor screenshot is treated as proof that the final Maia composition works.

### REQ26-D31-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0010 — Maintenance journey and proof

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

There is no tenant preset editor, publication workflow or personal preset list. Product/shared-UI maintainers change one definition and run conformance checks across detail, keyboard, bulk and CRM entry. Existing reminders never change when a menu label or default changes. A tenant administrator can correct the existing tenant timezone through its authorized settings owner; the picker does not quietly edit it. Previously saved instants remain fixed.

Use the P01–P32 proof and six operating controls. Real staff tests must establish that workers can pick the intended time, identify its zone, correct it and explain its shared work/no-email effect. Until those tests and real browser/accessibility checks run, this is a complete reviewed design, not a proven perfect UI.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004-O01 — Operational controls for residual risk

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Any currently eligible reminder more than 5 min overdue without an admitted due result, measured from product due data; sample recovery at least each minute under healthy operation.

**Response:** Alert, inspect shared dispatch/claim/backlog, recover through product-owned conditional path and preserve original due time. Escalate sustained platform outage; never mass-reschedule into the future.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004-O02 — Operational controls for residual risk

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Any confirmed unauthorized reminder/receipt disclosure or cross-tenant mutation; threshold 1.

**Response:** Disable affected exposure/new mutation path, preserve authorized due recovery where possible, invoke incident response and require repaired authorization proof before reactivation. This does not replace a release-blocking authorization suite.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004-O03 — Operational controls for residual risk

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Any duplicate applied effect for one current generation or accepted command whose required history/intent is missing; threshold 1.

**Response:** Stop affected new writer/worker path safely, preserve evidence, reconcile canonical state and repair permanent atomic/idempotency boundary before re-enabling.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004-O04 — Operational controls for residual risk

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** At least 3 confirmed wrong-time/zone misunderstandings in a rolling 30-day period, or any reproducible timezone/format mapping defect.

**Response:** Investigate with minimized metadata and consenting task observation; fix labels/resolution/accessibility. Do not add personal settings merely to suppress reports. Re-run affected conformance/UX tests.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004-O05 — Operational controls for residual risk

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** p95 server preview/admission latency>2 s for 15 min with at least 100 measured operations, or repeated recovery batches failing P27's healthy-load goal.

**Response:** Inspect plans, indexes, tenant skew and shared capacity; bound/throttle fair new work if needed while preserving due recovery. Repeat load qualification after the relevant fix.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004-O06 — Operational controls for residual risk

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Any read of invalid/missing tenant default zone causes a visible UTC fallback; threshold 1 per distinct configuration revision.

**Response:** Staff may deliberately choose another valid zone; show one deduplicated configuration issue to the authorized administrator, repair through tenant settings and clear the issue on validation. Existing accepted instants remain unchanged.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004 — Operational controls for residual risk

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Named owners below are operational responsibilities. Assign actual on-call/role coverage before activation; no unverified person is named as current owner. A signal without collection and response is not a completed control.

Signals are content-minimized. Do not collect message bodies, donor addresses or precise missionary location to debug a timing chooser. Business history, security records and operational traces have separate purpose, access and retention. Observe each reminder's intended and actual processing time without treating a missed transport heartbeat as proof of a missed business effect.

### REQ26-D31-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0005 — Ordered delivery and rollback

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

2. Carry the exact temporal/authority/UX boundaries into appropriately owned requirements and map P01–P32. Do not create a parallel Support scheduler or CRM due field.
3. Qualify canonical D3 state/history/command/worker recovery and fence every direct/legacy writer, including outgoing-message reminder clearing. Make schema/readers compatible before enabling new writes.
4. Implement shared date/time resolver and Maia controls, then all qualified entry points, source history and CRM return journey. Do not ship the interface with an unqualified Custom/backend seam.
5. Test migration and mixed versions, then real authorization/concurrency/worker, browser/accessibility/staff and representative-load gates. Record actual provider plan/run horizon and dependency versions. Activate for bounded tenant scope with the six controls and proper support ownership.
6. New-scheduling disablement stops new work safely while preserving reads, accepted-message reconciliation, existing due recovery and history. Reverting the UI cannot revive an old browser/direct-write bypass. Prefer roll-forward repair after new data exists; any rollback must prove semantic compatibility and preserve immutable admitted instants.

No outstanding product design issue is delegated to monitoring. Remaining runtime evidence is the normal implementation/release obligation, clearly distinguished from the completed grooming artifact.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0005 — O31-01 — Preserve one shared conversation reminder

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; plausible.** A visually familiar picker can accidentally introduce personal alarm state, multiple reminders, recurring definitions or a new task per scheduled conversation. That fragments custody and can hide the team's real follow-up.

**Exact language:** “Quick choices and Custom resolve input for the existing single current D3 shared conversation reminder. Scheduling replaces or creates that source-owned plan under its current identity/generation rules; it creates no private alarm, repeating series, CRM task, second due-state model or automatic assignment. A reminder's creator is attribution, not exclusive ownership or authority. Actual delegated tasks continue through D11's shared Mission Control owner.

**Proof:** two authorized workers see the same accepted reminder and original author/time; a later replacement is one new qualified generation, not an additional private timer; ordinary scheduling creates no task or CRM activity.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0006 — O31-02 — Resolve visible calendar intent through a trusted server boundary

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; likely if the current fixed-hour browser expression is reused.** A calendar label can produce a different day/time than staff saw, particularly across midnight, DST, slow connections or a stale picker. A caller-supplied due timestamp is not proof of the reviewed input or actor.

**Exact language:** “Each choice has explicit duration or calendar meaning. Before its committing action, show the server-qualified actual date, time and relevant zone, including any needed unambiguous calendar adjustment. The canonical command verifies the exact reviewed meaning/result and current source/work/reminder authority; it does not silently recompute a different time at commit or trust browser now. A changed or now-invalid result requires current correction/review while preserving safe input. Store the accepted UTC instant and sufficient input/zone/resolution provenance; later viewer or source-default changes alter display or future choices, never that scheduled instant.

This is a consistency requirement, not a mandate for another confirmation modal, persistent preview database or new timezone platform. Use qualified shared controls and date/time owner facilities. Do not infer the zone or workday from a requester's email, CRM address, missionary location, presumed US week or hidden personal settings.

**Proof:** picker crosses midnight; chosen calendar time is repeated/nonexistent; actor/device zone changes after acceptance; delayed commit becomes past; duration and calendar choice with superficially similar labels remain distinguishable. Validate future time at command admission, not through a database constraint that becomes false when a legitimate reminder reaches due.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0007 — O31-03 — Idempotency belongs to the accepted reminder effect

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; plausible.** Retrying “Tomorrow” or “In one hour” as a newly evaluated expression can postpone a successfully admitted reminder after a lost response. A stale due callback can revive canceled work or overwrite a replacement.

**Exact language:** “A retry reconciles the same immutable accepted command/intent and due instant under current disclosure authority. It cannot renew relative time, create another generation or reapply an old success over newer work. Changed semantic input under the same identity conflicts. A genuinely new correction/reschedule is explicit and receives a fresh qualified generation. Due execution rechecks current tenant, source, topology, generation, state and due instant; canceled, superseded, applied or completed-cycle work cannot execute again.

**Proof:** lost response then next-day retry; successful reschedule followed by old command replay; duplicate/early worker call; source event cancels pending work; partial bulk retry preserves successful item outcomes and original reviewed time rather than applying again to all selected rows. Retain D3's exact-ID/per-item bulk rules; no new all-matches operation.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0008 — O31-04 — Shared infrastructure executes, but never decides, due work

Applies to **US26-D31-03**, acceptance **AC26-D31-03-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; plausible.** A second worker queue or browser timer can lose reminders during an outage; using workflow-run status as business truth can reopen work incorrectly. Conversely, treating no new reminder notification as a reason to suppress legitimate existing failure escalation loses operational recovery.

**Exact language:** “The product-owned reminder/history and required shared dispatch/recovery intent commit atomically at the existing command boundary.
