Shared workflow infrastructure consumes identifier-only tenant/source/generation envelopes and re-proves the product claim. The due instant and actual processing instant stay distinct. Ordinary Follow-up due is source-owned work/UI history, not a new catalog notification. Existing independently qualified workflow/owner failure escalation retains its own scope and message policy; this choice neither introduces a per-reminder alert nor disables required recovery.

**Proof:** crash before/after intent commit; shared executor disabled; early callback retains recoverable due work; late recovery shows the original overdue instant; re-enable never treats a canceled generation as eligible. A source state remains discoverable without requiring a Resend connection or publishing a template.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0009 — O31-05 — Keep compose/send and reusable shortcuts separate

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; plausible and directly exposed by vendor Send & snooze patterns.** A reminder click can unexpectedly send the draft, or extending a D24 saved shortcut can bypass the already closed patch and review contract.

**Exact language:** “D31 adds no Send-and-remind operation. A reminder chosen while a reply is composed is a separate deliberate use of the existing qualified D3/D4 control. D24 shortcuts cannot store or apply reminder presets. Plain Send reply preserves a valid reminder; explicit Open/Resolve or another admitted work choice retains its existing D3 consequence and may make an older reminder review stale. No keystroke, preset insertion, template save or picker dismissal sends email or applies the saved shortcut.

**Proof:** unsent/edited reply survives scheduling/cancel; plain send preserves the accepted time; concurrent Send-and-resolve versus scheduling has one honest current-state outcome; a D24 export/import/activation cannot add reminder fields; keyboard Enter in date input commits only its focused permitted operation and not the external composer send shortcut.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0010 — O31-06 — CRM access is a shared source journey, not copied timing authority

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

**Concern: critical severity; plausible.** Creating a reminder from a CRM record can silently grant Support access, force a Party, copy a task deadline or expose a restricted work item through its date/label/count.

**Exact language:** “Support-first and CRM-first use the same authorized conversation detail and same D3 reminder command. Derive tenant, actor/profile, source and current permission from trusted context; a URL/association/current CRM owner is not authority. Expose due time, provenance and controls only under current Support/source and relevant CRM disclosure rights. Preserve safe return/draft context, not stale permission. Unknown/no-Party staff/form-origin work remains serviceable through its qualified source without fabricated mail or CRM identity.

**Proof:** CRM record is readable but Support source is not; source becomes restricted while picker is open; same-user tenant switch discards in-flight prior values; unlinked manual-ready conversation schedules without email readiness; a linked donor/task change neither rewrites due time nor duplicates an Activity.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0011 — O31-07 — Do not couple reminder time to task, money or reply-target deadlines

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; plausible.** A reschedule can look like an extension of a promised response, Finance task or donor action, and “due” can be mistaken for completion of the awaited work. Shared controls do not mean shared facts.

**Exact language:** “The Support reminder is when Support reviews the conversation. A D11 task deadline, D14 internal reply target, owner-domain completion requirement and any actual staff promise retain independent meaning and authority. Scheduling or rescheduling does not pause, fulfill, reset or synchronize them. At due, current D3 work becomes Open for follow-up with truthful cause; no reply, delivery, refund, receipt, recurring-gift change or care action is inferred.

**Proof:** a valid future reminder coexists with an overdue D14 target and an incomplete Finance task; target due review retains its separately valid future reminder according to D14; changing a task due date leaves the Support reminder unchanged; a fulfilled reply can still have independent actionable delivery recovery.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0012 — O31-08 — Topology and status transitions retain their accepted plan reviews

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; plausible.** A menu acting on an old original can silently target a newly merged component, duplicate reminder promises during Undo or restore canceled reminders when a related conversation is created.

**Exact language:** “Bind scheduling and replacement to the reviewed current source/component and reminder/work revisions. D10 merge/Undo and D12 continuation keep their explicit resulting-plan review, source attribution and fresh-generation rules. Equal due times do not prove two promises equivalent; no min/max shortcut resolves incompatible plans. Waiting-side-only changes preserve the valid reminder; explicit Open clears deferral and Resolve cancels it as already accepted. Resolved work requires an explicit qualified reopen plan before a new reminder; no hidden timer survives completion.

**Proof:** merge while picker open; two reminders with equal time but different purposes; Undo requiring Keep for both versus separate plans; late canceled callback; new related request receives no inherited timer by default. No new promise graph or reminder-owner system is needed.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0013 — O31-09 — Preserve complete follow-up discovery and current privacy

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Concern: high severity; plausible.** A reminder can disappear from standard views because it is deferred/unassigned/old, or after processing clears its timer column even though review remains owed. A retained cache can disclose the due state after source access is revoked.

**Exact language:** “D3/D20/D30's all-age follow-up and recovery discovery remains authoritative. A quick choice does not create private hiding or a second reminder-only list. Current due review remains discoverable from source work/cause after timer processing; no query equates an empty old timer field with completed follow-up. Owner-qualified retired inbox work remains available without a new access grant. Current source privacy, finite metadata custody and restore suppression apply to picker state, reads, history, queries and cached due cues.

**Proof:** due processing clears the deferral but review remains; waiting/unassigned/deferred work remains in its qualified views; old source outside an Overview period is still findable; retained retired source is permitted only under current owner qualification; revocation prevents old cached metadata reappearing.

### REQ26-D31-OWNER_REVIEW-S0014 — O31-10 — Native date/time controls and a bounded common menu

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

**Concern: medium severity; likely under implementation shortcut or customization pressure.** Rich-text date entry, hidden natural-language parsing, app-local picker forks or a settings hierarchy can make the narrow choice harder to understand and maintain.

**Exact language:** “Use the existing qualified shared native/date/time controls and Core's Base UI/Maia/Zinc system. Tiptap remains for qualified rich-text content, not date/time inputs. The common quick menu is code-owned and small; Custom remains a complete accessible escape path. Labels expose precise resolved meaning rather than hidden parser syntax. Fixing a menu definition changes future selections only. A adds no personal saved preset store, tenant/inbox override hierarchy, registry editor, recurring schedule language or automated inference.

**Proof:** keyboard, touch, long/RTL locale text, 12/24-hour presentation and screen-reader resolution; the same accepted choice has the same meaning across permitted entry points; a later product preset revision cannot rebase an existing accepted reminder. Actual menu, morning-hour, zone-resolution and bounds must be settled in the root's full selected-answer synthesis; this owner report does not invent them independently.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0002 — Permanent contract recommended to the synthesis

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

Use four common choices — **In 1 hour**, **In 4 hours**, **Tomorrow at this time**, and **In 1 week at this time** — plus **Custom**. These values are a accepted product choice, not a discovered universal ministry schedule. No universal morning hour, next-business-day rule, holiday skipping, recurrence, saved personal menu or automatic reminder on waiting is needed.

The picker starts in the current tenant's validated `default_timezone`, an actual owned field. Missing/invalid configuration produces a visible UTC fallback and an appropriate configuration issue; it does not block all work. An explicit per-use IANA zone override is available for every choice. A browser zone may help a person locate their zone but does not silently replace the chosen zone, establish identity/location or become the time authority. Editing an existing reminder initially preserves its recorded instant and zone; absent legacy zone provenance is shown honestly rather than inferred from today's settings.

Quick choices derive from one actual trusted server reference instant. Elapsed and calendar arithmetic are different:

1. **In 1/4 hours:** add exactly 3,600/14,400 elapsed seconds, then round the resulting target upward to the next whole minute, with an already exact minute unchanged. Display that resulting date/time/zone. The rounding adds less than 60 seconds and never schedules earlier than the named duration.
2. **Tomorrow / In 1 week at this time:** take the reference's actual local calendar date and displayed HH:mm in the selected zone, add one/seven local dates, and resolve that wall time in the same zone. Seconds are zero. Do not round the reference into the next day first. Calendar choices can differ from 24/168 elapsed hours across offset transitions.
3. **Custom:** choose an explicit local date, time and zone, then resolve it to one unambiguous instant. A new Custom form may show today's selected-zone date with time blank; do not secretly select an hour. An explicit carried candidate or existing reminder retains its value.

After selecting a choice, the candidate is an exact displayed instant. Preserve it while the person reviews and on retries. Do not rerun the relative recipe at commit, on focus, on reconnect or after tenant settings change. No 60-second hard expiry, durable preview table, preview job, reservation lock or viewing-attestation protocol is justified. A valid future absolute candidate is still useful after a minute. A stale relative caption can use anchored wording or the absolute date; offer deliberate **Refresh choices**. New current authorization/state checks still run at admission. A time that has become past must be corrected, never silently postponed.

The representational range may be ISO calendar years 0001–9999, with both selected local values and serialized instants supported by the qualified stack. This is a finite interchange/UI bound, not a promise of an uninterrupted multi-millennial provider run, a 365-day business limit or a retention exception. Newly selected time precision is whole minutes; existing accepted legacy seconds are not rounded merely by opening/editing/displaying a reminder.

The current D3 reminder remains the sole authority. Scheduling/replacement/cancellation admits the exact current component, expected material work/reminder/topology scope, trusted actor, semantic operation identity, intended instant and required history/dispatch intent atomically. Worker execution uses the exact admitted generation and trusted due comparison. No menu interaction creates requester email, a second CRM task or a new target/feedback policy.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0005 — DC01 — Calendar words and elapsed durations cannot share one arithmetic recipe

Applies to **US26-D31-01**, acceptance **AC26-D31-01-01–03**.

“Resolve duration choices by adding their exact elapsed seconds to the trusted reference and then ceiling the resulting instant to minute precision. Resolve calendar choices from the actual reference-local date and displayed HH:mm before rounding, add the declared one/seven calendar dates, and explicitly disambiguate that local result. At 23:59:59 on 13 September, Tomorrow at this time is 14 September at 23:59 in the selected zone, not 15 September at midnight. Show the exact result before admission.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0006 — DC02 — Timezone is scheduling context, not identity, calendar policy or a live binding

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

“Initialize from the current tenant's server-qualified default timezone, with visible UTC fallback if absent/invalid and an owned configuration diagnostic. Permit deliberate one-use IANA override. Never infer a person or permission from the zone, import a restricted missionary location, or substitute an SLA/report zone. The chosen zone and input provenance explain the accepted instant; subsequent tenant/device/viewer zone changes do not reschedule it. Opening an existing reminder preserves its accepted instant and recorded zone; unknown old zone remains unknown.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0007 — DC03 — DST ambiguity must be surfaced before the instant becomes authoritative

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

“Require one unambiguous local-to-instant result. For a nonexistent time, preserve the user's input and show the exact proposed valid alternative for explicit acceptance or editing; do not silently normalize it. For repeated time, expose the two offsets/instances with understandable labels and require a choice. If a zone's rules change before new admission so the reviewed mapping no longer agrees, show the changed result and require review. Existing accepted reminders retain their instant unless explicitly rescheduled.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0008 — DC04 — A selected instant should not drift while the person reviews or retries

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

“Obtain a trusted reference without trusting the browser clock. Unselected offers display their reference-derived result; once selected, preserve one exact absolute candidate until explicit editing/refresh. Do not auto-change choices under hover/focus or recompute the selected due time at save/retry. An aged relative caption uses its anchored or absolute meaning. Revalidate current authority, scope, supported mapping and future time at admission. A now-past candidate requires correction with input retained; no silent move to tomorrow or plus-one-hour. No preview reservation, persistent preview record or viewing-attestation system is required.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0009 — DC05 — Finite canonical time validation belongs in the server command

Applies to **US26-D31-02**, acceptance **AC26-D31-02-01–03**.

“Use a closed input contract for actual ISO local date, minute time, validated IANA zone and explicit resolution, yielding one finite canonical instant. Reject ambiguous numeric date strings, offset-less instant claims, infinity, nonfinite numbers, invalid dates, unsupported years/offsets and coercion-dependent values. New custom/quick choices support the declared 0001–9999 interchange range with both local and UTC representations valid; reject an offset conversion that exits it. Newly selected time is minute-precision. Do not round already-accepted legacy instants on read or unchanged edit. New admission requires due_at greater than trusted current time sampled at the serialized mutation boundary; existing due work naturally has due_at less than or equal to now.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0010 — DC06 — The reminder is a versioned D3 command, not a status field patch

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

“Use the existing canonical conditional work/reminder command to set, replace or cancel one current shared reminder. Bind the current continuing component and expected material work/reminder/control/topology versions. Derive tenant/profile actor/cause on the server. Commit the exact resulting reminder state, fresh supersession generation where needed, before/after evidence and durable dispatch/recovery intent atomically. No separately successful status/timer/history requests or caller-chosen author constitute admission. Network/provider work occurs after the local transaction.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0011 — DC07 — Retry reconciliation must precede new-admission future-time checks

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

“Reconcile an existing semantic command identity before interpreting past time or advanced generation as a new Schedule failure. An identical retry returns the original durable outcome and separately current authorized state; it never reschedules, restores an old generation or claims the original action failed. Changed semantic input with the same identity conflicts. Only a genuinely new admission applies current future-time validation. Cancellation retries similarly return their existing result without cancelling a later reminder. A workflow dispatch-key match does not replace semantic-payload equality.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0012 — DC08 — Durable execution must survive executor limits and stale workers

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

“Product reminder identity/generation/due instant remain authoritative beyond any workflow run or log lifetime. Admit durable recovery with the schedule; dispatch only through the shared qualified ledger/executor. A bounded indexed product scan must discover current reminders whose due execution or handoff is missing, including already-dispatched runs that later fail. Far-future due values remain product-owned and enter finite supported executor horizons through qualified recovery; do not keep an endless chain of steps in one run or clamp the user's date to the provider limit. At execution, re-resolve current tenant/component/generation/state and compare due <= trusted now atomically. Early attempts remain pending; cancelled/superseded/applied generations do nothing. A work-claim timeout alone never authorizes an old effect.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0013 — DC09 — The picker must preserve ratified work, merge, coverage and email semantics

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

“The new picker changes only the explicitly reviewed D3 reminder intent. Waiting-side changes preserve it; explicit Open/Resolve and qualified input/cancel/replace retain their accepted effects. Plain Send reply preserves valid reminders. Due processing creates Open/Follow-up due and applicable D7 coverage evaluation without depending on the original scheduler still being employed or online. D10 merge/Undo retains its complete reminder reconciliation and fresh generations; no min/max time automatically substitutes for independent promises. D24 shortcuts do not gain reminder actions. D26 creation uses the same optional reminder and real source; D30 remains an effect-free view.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0014 — DC10 — Database grants, RLS, constraints and service paths must enforce the same command

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

“Inventory and fence all public/direct/status/snooze/macro/bulk/worker writers. Server-only compound reminder mutation is the default. Any approved direct read/write, view or RPC must preserve current source/record/field authorization, immutable tenant/profile/cause/ownership and effective old/new-row constraints. Prove grants, SELECT, USING and WITH CHECK behavior, PUBLIC execute, invoker/definer/search_path and service-role/BYPASSRLS checks. Keep same-tenant relationships and stable existing conversation TEXT IDs; enforce at most one current reminder, unique command/effect generations, finite due values and valid active/terminal combinations. No new money fields or financial grants are required.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0015 — DC11 — Selection, bulk, cache and outcome presentation cannot retarget work

Applies to **US26-D31-04**, acceptance **AC26-D31-04-01–03**.

“Single, keyboard, CRM-context and already-authorized selected-item entry points use the same qualified choice/command semantics. Bulk freezes reviewed exact IDs and explicit scope; one reviewed common due instant does not become separately recomputed plus-one-hour per delayed item. Reauthorize each current item and retain durable correlated outcomes; Stop leaves committed results intact, retry reconciles only unresolved effects. Account/tenant/context changes fence old picker/results and late mutations. No broad all-matches action, hidden mass-email audience or success toast over unknown items is added.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0016 — DC12 — Metadata custody and migration must not create indefinite holds or fake history

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

“Keep only the minimal owner-qualified due/zone/input-kind/generation/cause/receipt facts needed for current work and finite history. Identifier-only workflow envelopes carry no transcript, sensitive explanation or arbitrary timezone-derived personal profile. A far-future reminder is not a D17 content-retention override; existing active-purpose controls and actual records policy remain mandatory. Migrate qualified legacy due instants without rewriting them from current zone/defaults or fabricating original intent/actor. Unknown/invalid legacy state receives explicit owned repair; overdue valid work is recovered, not moved forward. Fence old writers before activation; rollback must not restore status-coupled clearing, broad grants or erased content.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0017 — Logical data and admission shape

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

This does not freeze a physical table or API field spelling. Reuse D3's current reminder plus transition/command evidence and the existing shared workflow ledger.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact                                | Owner and invariant                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Current component/reminder identity | Support current topology and D3; one current shared reminder per continuing component, same-tenant references.                                                                                                |
| Intended due instant                | Finite canonical timestamptz-compatible instant. Current work generation determines applicability; being past does not make an admitted active row invalid.                                                   |
| Chosen zone and input provenance    | Minimal explanatory data: validated zone, quick-choice kind or Custom, actual local date/minute/offset choice when necessary. Not identity, permission, a recurring expression or a live settings dependency. |
| Human scheduling/cancelling actor   | Trusted authenticated profile/current capability at admission; not assignee, email match or supplied actor ID.                                                                                                |
| Due execution actor                 | Explicit qualified system cause and source generation, not a fabricated human or a nil UUID copied into a profile FK. Original human loss of access does not erase genuine work.                              |
| Expected versions                   | Material work/reminder/component/authority control, sufficient to reject conflicting overwrite without using incidental `updated_at` as a universal mutex.                                                    |
| Durable command outcome             | Semantic operation identity, exact normalized payload/result and current-state response separated. Same payload retry reconciles; changed payload conflicts.                                                  |
| Dispatch/recovery intent            | Same local admission, tenant/source/generation-bound identifier-only handoff; executor acknowledgement is not proof due work was applied.                                                                     |
| Historical time evidence            | Original scheduled due, admitted time and actual applied time distinct. Zone/display change or retry cannot rewrite occurrence/history.                                                                       |

For **new admission**, acquire/recheck the required current source guards, sample trusted time after relevant lock waits, validate the reviewed candidate and atomically write the accepted effects. PostgreSQL `now()` reflects transaction start, so it must not silently become a fresh post-wait validation time. For **an already admitted retry**, first recover the compatible original receipt under current disclosure rules; do not run a new schedule validation against the old due time.

The common quick-choice list is code-owned configuration with stable semantic keys. A localized label is not the key, and changing a label/order cannot change accepted times. No user/tenant preset persistence is needed for A. A future personal menu would require its own owner/lifecycle and would still select a shared reminder, but it is not part of D31 A.

### REQ26-D31-DATA_REVIEW-S0018 — Reference examples for required tests — not executed results

Applies to **US26-D31-05**, acceptance **AC26-D31-05-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Case                                                     | Expected outcome                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reference `2026-09-13 14:30:00`, fixed-offset zone, +1h  | `15:30:00`; exact-minute targets are not moved to `15:31`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Reference `2026-09-13 14:30:01`, +1h                     | Target ceilings to `15:31:00`, a 59-second upward precision adjustment visibly shown.                                                                                                                          |
| Reference `2026-09-13 23:59:59`, Tomorrow at this time   | Next local date at `23:59:00`; never add another date because a rounded anchor crossed midnight.                                                                                                               |
| Local day crosses a +1h DST change                       | Tomorrow at the same HH:mm can be 23 elapsed hours; +24 elapsed hours is a different intent.                                                                                                                   |
| Local day crosses a -1h DST change                       | Tomorrow at the same HH:mm can be 25 elapsed hours; repeated wall-time choice requires explicit offset/instance.                                                                                               |
| Picker remains open across midnight                      | The selected absolute candidate remains unchanged. Relative offer captions become anchored/absolute or deliberately refreshed.                                                                                 |
| Save accepted, browser response lost, due then processed | Retry returns the original accepted outcome and current due-review state; no fresh future reminder.                                                                                                            |
| Due becomes past while new request waits for a row lock  | New admission rejects it with values retained; it does not use transaction-start now as permission to hide already-due work.                                                                                   |
| Tenant timezone edited after acceptance                  | Stored instant remains identical. Display may change only under visible selected context; no rescheduling event.                                                                                               |
| Reminder far beyond executor run horizon                 | Product record remains authoritative; bounded shared scheduling/recovery eventually hands off the same current generation within a supported window. No giant sleeping run or unlimited step chain is assumed. |
| Same reminder instant with legacy seconds                | Read/unchanged edit preserves seconds. Only a deliberate new time choice adopts minute precision.                                                                                                              |

## Private attachment previews

### REQ26-D32-R01 — D32-R01 — Bounded broader scope

Applies to **US26-D32-02**, acceptance **AC26-D32-02-01–03**.

Provide all declared initial preview lanes: PNG/JPEG/WebP, still GIF, static ordinary unencrypted PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, TXT and CSV. A format name is not eligibility: source permission, actual byte/type/structure, hygiene, supported features and resource limits must pass. Publish the profile's supported and excluded features with the product. Do not call a filename chip, thumbnail-only display or image/PDF-only implementation completion of C.

### REQ26-D32-R02 — D32-R02 — One source, separate derivative

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Support owns each original attachment occurrence and its parent-message context. The file owner holds immutable original byte identity/digest and qualified storage/hygiene facts. Preview records identify the exact tenant, source occurrence, byte version, renderer/profile build, projection inputs and source restriction generation. A ready result cannot point to a different source/version or serve a newer file under an old name. File names are presentation, never keys or storage paths. Derivatives are not P18 Generated Documents, current official PDFs, CRM attachments or Email Studio assets.

### REQ26-D32-R03 — D32-R03 — Metadata-first, explicit actions

Applies to **US26-D32-01**, acceptance **AC26-D32-01-01–03**.

Show a compact card at its message with currently permitted name, type, actual size, source and availability. Do not disclose a forbidden name merely because metadata exists. Preview and Download original are separately labelled actions. Do not auto-open, eagerly convert every file, or automatically download when preview fails. Existing already-qualified inline message images/authoring remain governed and are not removed or broadened by this control. Same-name files retain distinct occurrence identities.

### REQ26-D32-R04 — D32-R04 — Complete in-context reader

Applies to **US26-D32-01**, acceptance **AC26-D32-01-01–03**.

Preview opens one shared responsive reader, with readable source/file identity, current format-specific controls, persistent close and Download original when allowed. Preserve conversation, draft, recipients, scroll, focus, list/search and CRM return context. A viewer is not a new routed work record, mark-read/review action or status mutation. Close restores the invoking context. Switching files within the selected message must reauthorize each file and preserve identity; do not build a global file browser.

### REQ26-D32-R05 — D32-R05 — Current source authorization

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Derive tenant and actor from trusted server context. Before metadata, conversion admission, source reads, ready promotion and every protected rendition/full/range retrieval, check the relevant current source/file purpose, membership/inbox/CRM scope, classification, hygiene and restriction/expiry state. A viewer/assignee/requester/CRM association is not an access grant. A worker acts through a narrow product claim, not a copied UI permission or raw service-role bypass. Reusing cached bytes does not reuse an authorization decision.

### REQ26-D32-R06 — D32-R06 — Isolated parsing and rendering

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Use one shared owner-qualified preview pipeline with deterministic per-format profiles. Original untrusted binary parsing, image decoding, Office conversion and workbook extraction run outside ordinary web/API request workers in bounded isolated jobs. The parser has no network egress, credentials, tenant storage access, host mounts or ability to resolve document-supplied paths. A trusted supervisor supplies only the authorized input and receives bounded output. Disable macros, external references, linked resources, DTD/entity expansion and executable/embedded content; configuration allow-lists alone do not replace process/network isolation.

Do not pass private source URLs to public Office/Google/demo viewers, external conversion sites or a generic fetch proxy. Use the shared existing durable workflow envelope/claim/recovery pattern; no tenant workflow builder or second scheduler is introduced. A specific maintained tool such as a LibreOffice-based converter is a candidate implementation, not evidence of safe or faithful behavior until its exact profile passes.

### REQ26-D32-R07 — D32-R07 — Admission, lifecycle and publication

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Separate source/hygiene eligibility, technical generation and user-visible availability. A preview request atomically records the exact requested profile/input and durable generation intent. Coalesce identical currently eligible work for the same tenant/source/version/profile/projection inputs; concurrent opens cannot create competing ready outputs. Queued → processing → ready is a technical lifecycle, not proof of source access. Unsupported/over-budget/invalid input is terminal for that exact profile; transient failure may retry within the declared budget. Restriction/expiry invalidates ordinary use in every technical state.

Outputs upload into private tentative custody with a known attempt identity and cleanup deadline. Storage success is not Ready. Ready promotion atomically rechecks source generation, byte/profile identity, eligibility and required manifests/audit; late/superseded results stay cleanup-only. Partial object success, lost responses and duplicate callbacks reconcile the same intent. A revoked requesting viewer cannot read a result; an independently eligible later viewer may reuse it only under current source-purpose authorization.

Successful promotion atomically transfers the accepted output's custody to the Ready/source-bounded deadline; the 15-minute tentative sweeper retains authority only over scratch and unpromoted outputs. Cleanup must claim the same immutable object's current unpromoted custody conditionally; once deletion is claimed, promotion is forbidden. A stale cleanup claim cannot delete a promoted output. Ready expiry uses its own guarded disposal path. No object key is reused for another generation.

### REQ26-D32-R08 — D32-R08 — Private delivery and browser isolation

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Serve original and rendition data through the currently source-authorized private capability with no-store treatment, bounded full/range requests and no reusable public/signed-provider URL escape. Range and conditional requests require the same authority as a full read. Renderer workers/browser contexts receive only narrowly permitted data; PDF/binary rendering is isolated from application credentials, DOM and unrestricted navigation/network. Cross-context messages are typed, source-bound and origin-checked, never arbitrary fetch/HTML/command instructions. Disable scripting, embedded-file launching, form submission, external resource fetching and automatic link activation.

A browser reader is still executable software processing untrusted bytes; use a maintained patched build, restrictive CSP/embedding policy and actual isolation tests. Already-delivered DOM, memory, clipboard, screenshots or downloaded originals cannot be recalled. Revocation blocks future retrieval and invalidates current clients without claiming remote erasure.

### REQ26-D32-R09 — D32-R09 — Truthful coverage and fidelity

Applies to **US26-D32-02**, acceptance **AC26-D32-02-01–03**.

A successful parser/converter response does not prove complete content. Bind a coverage/limitations manifest to the result: representation type, included pages/slides/sheets or text scope, detected omitted features, missing resources/fonts/cached values, profile/build and output digest. Show a short persistent summary with expandable details. Mark a result Limited when material features are omitted. If coverage cannot be established under the profile, report Preview unavailable rather than Ready complete. Never infer that formatting, a signature image or a calculated-looking value validates a document or financial fact.

### REQ26-D32-R10 — D32-R10 — DOCX reading profile

Applies to **US26-D32-02**, acceptance **AC26-D32-02-01–03**.

Render the visible main document, headers/footers and supported embedded images into static pages. Use a defined no-markup reading view that shows the final-text presentation of revisions without accepting or changing those revisions. Detect comments, tracked changes, hidden text, embedded objects and external links; disclose omitted material. Do not export comments/revision history/hidden text accidentally or run linked content. A document with unsupported layout, fields or missing fonts/resources must carry exact limitations or become unavailable when meaningful legibility/coverage cannot be established. Preserve the immutable original.

### REQ26-D32-R11 — D32-R11 — PPTX reading profile

Applies to **US26-D32-02**, acceptance **AC26-D32-02-01–03**.

Show visible slides in original order as static pages. Preserve original slide numbering when hidden slides are omitted. Disclose hidden slides, speaker notes, transitions/animation, linked media and embedded objects that are not represented. Do not autoplay media, execute actions or present a missing animation state as proof of the complete presentation. Unsupported/fidelity-losing content gets a Limited indication or unavailable result under the declared profile, never silently substituted blank slides.

### REQ26-D32-R12 — D32-R12 — XLSX saved-value profile

Applies to **US26-D32-03**, acceptance **AC26-D32-03-01–03**.

Provide a read-only grid of visible worksheets, rows and columns using saved cell values and original sheet/cell coordinates. Never recalculate formulas, refresh external data, execute macros or use a print-area PDF as a complete workbook. Show a formula's saved cached result with its provenance; missing results are Unknown, not blank/zero or newly computed. Preserve cell types, raw decimal/text values and leading zeros. Format only supported date/number/currency/percent styles faithfully; otherwise expose the raw saved value with a clear unsupported-format indication. Excel dates retain their workbook date-system meaning and are not silently converted into timezone instants.

Retain sparse structure and original indices without allocating a whole rectangular sheet from an untrusted dimension. Hidden/filtered rows, columns, sheets, comments, charts/drawings and unsupported features are omitted and disclosed; hidden content is not a separate authorization boundary. Pivot definitions, refresh and interactivity are omitted, but visible saved pivot-result cells remain ordinary saved cells in the grid; no cache is refreshed. No unhide, formula editing, sorting that rewrites source meaning, data import, total calculation or export/re-serialization is added. A selected-cell detail can show saved/raw value and formula as escaped text, never evaluate it. All-hidden/empty/missing-cache cases are explicit states.

### REQ26-D32-R13 — D32-R13 — Literal text and CSV

Applies to **US26-D32-03**, acceptance **AC26-D32-03-01–03**.

TXT uses strict UTF-8 with optional BOM, or UTF-16 with a required BOM. Unsupported/malformed encoding is reported without silent replacement-character loss. CSV has explicit Comma default plus per-view Semicolon or Tab choices and View as text. Parse choice belongs to projection identity and affects no tenant preference. Preserve quoting, embedded newlines, empty fields, leading zeros and formula-looking text literally; never infer numbers/dates/booleans, execute formulas or dereference links. Ragged or malformed records produce a truthful text fallback or unavailable table, not guessed alignment.

Escape all text and control display safely, with bidi/isolation handling where needed. File extension does not authorize HTML/SVG/script rendering. No active syntax, shell, HTML or URI interpretation is introduced. Viewing text is not publishing it into D22 search.

### REQ26-D32-R14 — D32-R14 — Images and PDFs

Applies to **US26-D32-02**, acceptance **AC26-D32-02-01–03**.

Images preserve aspect ratio, orientation and readable zoom using a qualified inert rendition with unnecessary metadata stripped; the original remains unchanged. GIF, animated PNG and animated WebP previews show the first composited still frame and explicitly say animation is not shown. They must not imply the first frame represents the complete animation. If the qualified decoder cannot establish that representation within bounds, preview is unavailable. PNG/JPEG/WebP decoding respects both pixel and decoded-memory bounds.

PDF preview displays qualified static pages and their available text/navigation layer without document scripting, external fetching, embedded-file launch, executable actions or form submission. Existing form appearances, annotations and layers must follow a declared static profile; missing appearances, dynamic XFA/encryption, unsupported layers/attachments or other omissions are disclosed or rejected. No password entry, signature verification or document repair is added. Search within the currently authorized preview may use its existing text; image-only sources state that searchable text is unavailable. No OCR or cross-file indexing is implied.

### REQ26-D32-R15 — D32-R15 — Explicit resource ceilings

Applies to **US26-D32-05**, acceptance **AC26-D32-05-01–03**.

Preview eligibility is bounded by the smallest applicable existing source/provider policy and this preview profile. Initial engineering ceilings are: 20 MiB original input; 200 MiB cumulative expanded package bytes; 10,000 package entries; XML depth 128 with no external entities/DTD; 200 output pages or visible slides; 40,000,000 pixels per image; 256 MiB cumulative decoded-image working data; 50 total workbook sheets; 100,000 populated cells; 1,000,000 decoded Unicode scalar values for text/CSV; and 50 MiB total generated output. Exact-boundary tests must count actual streamed/decoded data, not trust metadata or ZIP declarations.

Each parser attempt has maximum 60 elapsed seconds, 30 aggregate process-tree CPU seconds, 2 GiB process-tree memory and 512 MiB temporary disk. Permit at most two attempts for the same generation and only after a classified transient failure; deterministic unsupported/corrupt/oversized inputs never retry automatically. No output is silently truncated and labelled complete. These are accepted engineering limits to qualify, not vendor capacities or changes to accepted intake/send limits. An otherwise eligible original can remain downloadable when preview exceeds its narrower limits.

### REQ26-D32-R16 — D32-R16 — Failure and low-bandwidth behavior

Applies to **US26-D32-01**, acceptance **AC26-D32-01-01–03**.

Distinguish Checking file, Preparing preview, Ready, Limited, Unsupported, Too large, Unavailable due to source restrictions, and Failed to prepare using source-safe copy. Do not reveal protected filenames or internal malware detail through an error. Keep conversation and draft usable while generation runs. Closing the viewer is not cancellation of admitted shared work; returning may reuse the same eligible result. Never report provider/storage acceptance as a finished preview or treat unknown outcome as permission for a blind new conversion.

Load a bounded first page/sheet and fetch additional authorized content deliberately/within a bounded reader window; do not download all attachments on thread open. Offer Retry only where the prior intent's result and remaining allowance permit it. Download original is separate and independently eligible in every failure state. Network failure, failed hygiene and unavailable source are not interchangeable.

### REQ26-D32-R17 — D32-R17 — Derivative retention and source revocation

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Derivatives are dispensable working copies with a fixed maximum 24 elapsed hours from first Ready admission, further bounded by the source's current restriction/expiry and owner obligations. Reads do not extend this deadline. Distinguish the stable source/version/profile/projection input key from each technical generation identity: expiry retires the generation, and a new deliberate eligible admission may create a new generation under that unchanged input key, with concurrent opens coalescing one live generation. Never renew the old deadline or change an old command receipt. Original source retention is never extended. Temporary/tentative attempt material has a fixed maximum 15 elapsed minutes from attempt start and is registered for cleanup before byte I/O. Required cleanup recovers crashes/orphans using the same identity.

D16/D17 source restriction immediately fences future access/promotion across originals, thumbnails, extracted grids/text and page renditions. Reconnect/visibility-return/current updates invalidate stale client representations. Retention changes, merge/Undo, object restore or delayed worker completion cannot resurrect restricted content. A legitimate hold preserves only owner-required custody; it does not grant ordinary preview access or manufacture a Support archive.

### REQ26-D32-R18 — D32-R18 — Database, grants and trusted attribution

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Represent lineage with same-tenant primary/foreign keys from source occurrence to immutable byte version and preview generation. Require valid finite byte sizes/digests/profile identity, explicit lifecycle and generation, valid timestamps and uniqueness for one semantic generation. Generated outputs are immutable once Ready; a new profile/input produces a new generation. Reference counts and owner-governed deletion must not cascade-delete another domain's original or required audit. Keep source eligibility separate from technically ready bytes.

Business reads/commands live in the shared API owner and the approved authorized read collections. Derive tenant/actor/owner/audit fields from trusted context. Revoke direct client mutations of lifecycle/lineage/result fields; inspect actual grants, USING and WITH CHECK, overlapping permissive policies, views, RPC EXECUTE/search_path and storage policies. Privileged services independently enforce product claims. Current broad CRUD, a public bucket or a filename/type/URL record is not this contract; existing tenant FKs/RLS are acknowledged, not alleged absent.

### REQ26-D32-R19 — D32-R19 — CRM and whole-product continuity

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

CRM opens the same currently authorized Support original and viewer with preserved return context. A person/household/organization association, message participant, requester, authenticated user, assignee or CRM owner does not become an attachment access grant. Linking/unlinking/person merges change authorized source relationships through their owner, not copied file ownership. Support conversation merge/Undo preserves original attachment lineage and restrictions; no earlier source becomes visible solely through grouping.

A requester-supplied receipt, bank-like spreadsheet or missionary document is evidence attached to a conversation, not a verified financial/CRM/care record. Viewing, downloading or closing the preview cannot change contact details, grant care access, issue receipts, refund gifts, modify recurring gifts, complete tasks or resolve Support. Existing deliberate owning-domain workflows retain validation, approvals and history. Preview creates no duplicate CRM task or interaction.

### REQ26-D32-R20 — D32-R20 — Email Studio, Document Studio and TipTap

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

Preview/read/download does not prepare, send, forward, attach to a reply, publish a reusable asset or alter sender/recipients/signature. P17/Email Studio governs later qualified outbound content/preparation; P6 owns transport and communication evidence. Preview derivatives cannot be silently used as message originals or promoted into the public email-assets bucket. Explicit later reuse follows D18/D23/D24 source/asset controls and rechecks current authority.

P18 Document Studio owns official generated-document identity/currentness and its own qualified renderer profile. D32's conversion output is a preview only, with no issuance, signed authenticity, canonical accessible PDF or archival-validity claim. TipTap remains the rich-text editor for messages/notes/signatures/wording; binary/document viewing uses the shared reader, not an imported editable document in TipTap. Existing source/operational failure attention remains with its owner; no per-preview email notification family is introduced.

### REQ26-D32-R21 — D32-R21 — Search, AI and cross-representation disclosure

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

D22 conversation/filename search remains unchanged. Preview text/grid extraction serves this exact authorized reader only; it is not a new search corpus, AI retrieval source or reusable knowledge article. Find within this preview covers the entire declared represented authorized content, including not-yet-displayed pages/sheets, through bounded current-authorized reads. No matches requires completed coverage of that scope; incomplete search reports incomplete coverage and offers retry, never a false zero. Image-only content is labelled nonsearchable. Untrusted document text/instructions never authorize a tool, data mutation, external fetch or message. No automatic OCR, summarization, classification expansion or financial extraction occurs.

### REQ26-D32-R22 — D32-R22 — Privacy and access evidence

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Log technical operation/profile/status/size/budget/latency identifiers without source bodies, cell values, filenames, storage URLs or tokens. Record durable source/byte access audit under the file owner's existing meaning; generation logs and access events are not communication/CRM interactions. Only currently authorized users inspect safe history. Retention/redaction/export/backups follow their source and platform owners. No cross-tenant content-digest cache or raw-byte deduplication grants another tenant access or leaks existence through counts/timing/lookup.

### REQ26-D32-R23 — D32-R23 — Accessibility and visual craft

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

Use the existing `base-maia`/Base UI shared components, semantic tokens and Core typography. One restrained reader shell adapts its content controls; do not build separate applications for formats. Primary controls have readable labels, visible focus, adequate contrast, touch targets and keyboard equivalents. Mobile uses a full-height responsive reader, predictable close/back, retained file identity and reachable actions. Pan/zoom/rotate/page/sheet navigation has non-drag and keyboard alternatives.

Support direct page/cell navigation and a semantically usable text/grid reading mode for represented content without silently replacing the visual source or inventing missing alt text. Preserve logical focus and source coordinates in virtualized grids, provide accessible paging/text fallback for the same represented values, and disclose source text/image-only limitations. Meet WCAG2.2 AA for product controls, reflow and input; test actual supported assistive technology. An untagged/scanned original is not made accessible by a canvas or an unverified automatic transcript; source limitations cannot excuse inaccessible product chrome.

### REQ26-D32-R24 — D32-R24 — Concurrency and idempotency

Applies to **US26-D32-04**, acceptance **AC26-D32-04-01–03**.

Conversion intent, source/profile generation and required dispatch/audit/cleanup intent have an atomic admission boundary. Identical requests reconcile the same semantic generation; changed input under the same identity conflicts. Old responses cannot replace newer authorized state. A cancellation/restriction/new profile races promotion under one current generation fence; stale outputs never become Ready. Duplicate range requests may reread authorized bytes but cannot duplicate generation or mutate source work. Export/download is an independent deliberate read effect, not a reusable authorization token.

### REQ26-D32-R25 — D32-R25 — Dependencies, performance and maintenance

Applies to **US26-D32-05**, acceptance **AC26-D32-05-01–03**.

Own one maintained format-profile registry in the shared preview capability, not tenant custom plugins or Support-specific replicas. Pin the qualified parser/converter/viewer build, fonts, locale behavior, security settings, supported features and output contract. Patches/profile changes create explicit new lineage and revoke unsafe ready renditions where required. Do not switch engines silently after admission or reuse a transitive dependency as an undeclared contract. Use finite tenant-fair queues and bounded worker pools; no parser runs for every list row or keystroke.

The actual engine selection and deployment sizing must pass the declared safety/fidelity/accessibility/resource corpus before activation. This is implementation qualification of the decided capability, not permission to defer its product meaning or to import P18's official-renderer role. A dependency outage leaves source work and qualified originals available; it cannot weaken policy or route files into a public service.

### REQ26-D32-R26 — D32-R26 — Migration and rollout

Applies to **US26-D32-05**, acceptance **AC26-D32-05-01–03**.

Qualify immutable source/byte custody, hygiene, private delivery and source-revocation enforcement before the new viewer. Inventory legacy URL/local/metadata-only records; do not declare them Ready from extension/count alone or invent a digest for missing bytes. Migrate only trusted retained bytes through their owning connection and current policy; unavailable legacy records keep truthful repair state. Do not fetch arbitrary stored URLs. Deploy compatible readers/contracts, fence legacy bypasses, then activate by qualified tenant/profile scope.

A kill switch can stop a renderer, new generation or serving an unsafe profile while preserving source restrictions, cleanup, history and unrelated Support work. A code rollback cannot restore public/raw-URL access or removed bytes. Post-write correction is an explicit new rendition/profile or safe roll-forward; preserve source identity and original evidence.

### REQ26-D32-R27 — D32-R27 — Required proof and monitored risk

Applies to **US26-D32-05**, acceptance **AC26-D32-05-01–03**.

Trace this decision through the glossary/ADR and required OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets to real release evidence. Execute all P01–P40 in the proof ledger, including malformed/hostile input, tenant isolation, revocation, actual sandbox/network denial, content fidelity, accessibility, concurrency, migration and representative load. Reference probes and document review do not establish production conformance. Block activation of any claimed format lane that fails; keep policy-safe diagnostics and existing original access without calling the narrowed rollout full C.

### REQ26-D32-R28 — D32-R28 — No unnecessary expansion

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

This is a staff inspection feature within Asym. It creates no editor, annotation/redaction canvas, external sharing links, bulk ZIP export, public file library, personal document store, requester portal archive or D29 form upload. No new broad mandatory CRM/missionary workflow or AI assistant is required. The supported set can evolve only through explicit shared-profile qualification and product scope decisions, not automatic package support or competitor parity.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — Supported initial reading experiences

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Source format   | Staff view                                                                                                 | Deliberate limitations                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PNG, JPEG, WebP | Fit-to-space image, readable zoom, pan and reset; original orientation/aspect retained.                    | Animated PNG/WebP use the first composited still with an animation-not-shown notice. No edit/crop/annotation or metadata/location inspection; original bytes unchanged.                                                         |
| GIF             | First composited still frame with a small **Still image** notice.                                          | Animation is not played or claimed fully represented.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| PDF             | Static pages, page count/navigation, fit/zoom and available text reading/find.                             | No scripting, form submission, password entry, embedded-file opening or signature validation. Unsupported dynamic/encrypted/appearance cases are explicitly limited/unavailable.                                                |
| DOCX            | Static paged reading rendition with supported embedded content and no-markup final-text presentation.      | No editing or acceptance of revisions. Detected comments/revision history/hidden text/linked content and other omissions are stated.                                                                                            |
| PPTX            | Static visible slides in original order, with source slide numbers and fit/zoom.                           | Hidden slides, speaker notes, animation/media/actions and unsupported objects are omitted and disclosed.                                                                                                                        |
| XLSX            | Read-only visible-sheet grid with original row/column coordinates, saved values and selected-cell details. | No recalculation, editing, external-data refresh, unhide, charts or pivot interaction/refresh. Visible saved pivot-result cells remain. No full workbook fidelity claim; missing formula cache is **Saved result unavailable**. |
| TXT             | Escaped, selectable literal text with wrapping and bounded navigation.                                     | UTF-8, optional BOM; UTF-16 only with BOM. Unsupported encoding is stated, not guessed.                                                                                                                                         |
| CSV             | Read-only literal-value table, explicit delimiter and View as text.                                        | Comma default; per-view Semicolon/Tab choices. No type/date/formula inference, import or export rewriting.                                                                                                                      |

These lanes must all be qualified to claim completion of C. “Supported” means a declared structure/feature profile within resource limits, not every file bearing that extension. Legacy DOC/XLS/PPT, macro-enabled/encrypted formats, ODF, archives, audio/video, SVG/HTML and unlisted formats are unsupported for preview in this release. This does not itself classify them as malicious or authorize downloading them. Download original is decided independently by the existing source/hygiene policy.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Entry and ordinary journey

Applies to **US26-D32-01**, acceptance **AC26-D32-01-01–03**.

Maya is responding to a donor-care inquiry with a screenshot, Word document and spreadsheet attached. The example tests the journey; it does not establish the prevalence of those files or access to restricted financial/care records.

1. **Find the attachment on its message.** Show a compact card with permitted name, actual type/size and availability. Keep source/message identity available so two `details.xlsx` files are not confused. A label such as **Checking file** reflects real hygiene state; metadata count alone cannot say it is ready.
2. **Choose Preview.** Use an explicit labelled action when eligible. No file is converted or opened solely because Maya opened the conversation or searched its filename. A separate **Download original** action is available only when authorized. Unsupported preview does not automatically invoke it.
3. **Keep working while it prepares.** Open the reader shell immediately with filename/source identity and a calm status. Generation can continue in the background while she closes the shell and works on her reply. Do not freeze the conversation, erase a draft, display fake percentages or send completion mail.
4. **Read the qualified result.** Display one content area with the appropriate small toolbar. A thin **Preview** context label distinguishes it from the original. A short limitation strip appears only when material known omissions exist, with **Details** for the coverage manifest. Technical parser/library names stay out of ordinary UI.
5. **Use the original when needed.** Download original retains original bytes; it never downloads a converted substitute under the original name. No extra automatic file reuse/forward/share action is introduced. The OS/browser may handle a deliberate download according to user settings; Asym does not promise control over that external copy.
6. **Close and continue.** Escape or Close returns to the exact attachment card and conversation position, with the unsent TipTap draft, recipients, chosen work intent and CRM return path intact. Closing does not mark the file reviewed, change status or complete the underlying request.

The desktop reader is one generous modal/dialog using the existing shared pattern, not a tiny tooltip or a permanent multi-pane document workspace. Its persistent header contains close/back, filename and source context; its footer/header provides Download original only where permitted. Format-specific navigation remains consistent in placement. The conversation stays mounted behind it; no independent copy of work or draft is made.

On mobile, the same reader becomes a full-height surface with stable close/back and reachable controls. It is usable with portrait layout and the virtual keyboard. Essential information wraps rather than truncating file identity into indistinguishable names. An optional next/previous attachment control stays limited to the invoking message and rechecks every file's current access; no cross-conversation gallery or File Manager is created.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Documents and slides

Applies to **US26-D32-02**, acceptance **AC26-D32-02-01–03**.

Show the first ready page/slide at a readable fit and provide page/slide count, previous/next, direct navigation, zoom and reset. Bound neighboring-page loading. Source numbering remains visible when slides are omitted; slide3 must not be silently relabelled slide2. Text reading mode represents the same qualified content and coverage, not an independent summary or canonical accessible-document export.

DOCX wording should say **Reading preview** and, when relevant, **Revision markup and comments are not shown**, with **Pending revisions remain in the original** in details. No-markup presentation displays the resulting final-text reading view; it does not accept edits in the source or mean that pending revisions are absent. PPTX can say **Static slides · animation and speaker notes are not shown**. A detected missing linked image or font substitution can materially alter meaning and must appear in the limitations, or block the preview if the profile cannot keep it useful and legible.

The renderer must not quietly fetch a linked image from the internet to improve appearance. It must not insert missing data, recalculate document fields or make an absent chart look like a valid blank. The original remains the source for inspection outside the bounded preview when authorized.

For a PDF, no **Verified**, **Official** or signature-valid indicator is inferred from visual appearance. Some documents have no useful text layer; the reader says **No searchable text in this preview** and does not silently enable OCR. Dynamic forms or encrypted files outside the profile do not prompt for a password or fall through to an external viewer service.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Spreadsheet journey

Applies to **US26-D32-03**, acceptance **AC26-D32-03-01–03**.

The XLSX view is deliberately a sheet/value reader rather than a print preview:

1. Open on the first visible sheet in original order. Show a compact sheet selector and preserve its source name. All-hidden and empty workbooks have distinct states. Hidden sheet names need not be listed; a permitted count/notice explains omitted content.
2. Show original row and column coordinates. Hidden/filtered rows and columns remain omitted; visible coordinates retain gaps instead of renumbering data. Sparse worksheets are rendered in bounded windows, not a dense rectangle allocated from a huge declared dimension.
3. Use saved typed cell data. When a formula has a cached result, display that saved result with a persistent **Saved values · not recalculated** context. A formula with no cached result shows **Saved result unavailable**, not a false zero. A genuinely empty cell is still empty.
4. Selecting a cell opens a small detail area with coordinate, displayed/saved raw value and optional escaped formula text. Leading zeros, large integer strings, decimal precision, source workbook date system and unsupported formatting remain distinguishable. This is not an editable formula bar.
5. Unsupported chart/image/comment/formatting features are disclosed. Pivot definitions, refresh and interactivity are omitted, but visible saved pivot-result cells stay in the grid as saved values; no cache is refreshed. Do not substitute a PDF print range or claim the grid represents every hidden/formatted aspect of the workbook. No sorting/filtering/recalculation/import/task completion is added. The existing visible/hidden source state remains the basis.

Provide an accessible paged/table or cell-detail reading path over the **same represented values**, with proper headers/coordinates, rather than hiding them behind mouse-only virtualization. Paging maintains source coordinates and does not become a second data export. The raw workbook's financial-looking values are unverified attachment data; no giving or CRM write is derived from them.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Text and CSV journey

Applies to **US26-D32-03**, acceptance **AC26-D32-03-01–03**.

TXT is readable selectable text with a wrap control, line references where useful and Find in this preview. Filenames, XML-like text, HTML tags, formulas and links remain escaped/inert. Do not let text content alter the app DOM or create navigation.

CSV opens with visible **Delimiter: Comma**. Staff may select Semicolon or Tab for this view, see the newly parsed result, or choose **View as text**. This handles international files without a preference hierarchy, import wizard or ambiguous automatic inference. The selection is a new projection input and cannot accidentally reuse a comma-parsed cached grid.

Do not assume the first record is a header and remove it; display row1 unless a later separately justified feature explicitly chooses headers. Preserve quoted embedded line breaks, trailing empty fields, leading zeros and every formula-looking cell literally. Malformed or inconsistent quoting/rows makes the table unavailable with original text available when its independent encoding/size checks pass. Never shift values into a guessed column layout.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Find, links and copying

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

**Find in this preview** searches the entire declared currently authorized represented content of this one file, including pages/sheets not yet displayed; it does not search hidden/comment content, other attachments or all conversations. Results state coverage limits and retain coordinates/pages. **No matches** is shown only after that represented scope is completely searched; incomplete retrieval says **Search incomplete** and offers retry. Image-only content is labelled nonsearchable. A saved spreadsheet value is searched as represented; no formula calculation or AI extraction is involved. Query telemetry does not retain private terms.

Links inside documents remain inert until a separately qualified existing link-handling path permits a deliberate action; no parser or viewer automatically navigates or loads a URL. No new external-link inspector or authenticated URL broker is added solely for C. Ordinary selectable text/copy behavior follows current content policy; the product cannot promise that readable content is impossible to copy or screenshot. It adds no bulk extraction/export button.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Failure and state language

Applies to **US26-D32-01**, acceptance **AC26-D32-01-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Condition                                    | Staff-facing behavior                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Safe metadata only; bytes/scan not qualified | **Checking file** or source-specific unavailable state. No Preview/Download bypass.                                                                   |
| Eligible generation queued/running           | **Preparing preview**; keep the surrounding work usable. Close/return does not create a new job.                                                      |
| Supported qualified complete profile result  | Show the reader with ordinary Preview identity; no claim that the original is authoritative business truth.                                           |
| Known material omissions                     | **Limited preview** plus concise cause and expandable coverage details; original remains distinct.                                                    |
| Unsupported format or features               | **Preview isn’t available for this file**; Download original only if independently allowed.                                                           |
| Resource ceiling exceeded                    | **This file exceeds the preview limit** with relevant user-safe size/page explanation; no silent partial result labelled complete.                    |
| Deterministic corrupt/unparseable input      | Explain unavailable preview without pretending the source bytes are missing. No automatic retry loop.                                                 |
| Transient generation failure                 | Safe **Couldn’t prepare preview** status and a qualified retry path within the existing intent allowance. No blind new request after unknown success. |
| Source removed/expired/reclassified          | Invalidate future reads and the current viewer; show a nonsensitive source state. No old preview/download URL remains an escape.                      |
| Access revoked/tenant switched               | Close or replace restricted content, clear inappropriate retained state and provide safe return navigation. No hidden filename/count leak.            |
| Download not permitted                       | Do not suggest Download as the repair for a renderer or safety failure.                                                                               |

No error messages expose raw storage keys, service credentials, source URLs or parser stack traces. Same-source rechecks also apply during page/range loads and to a result that was generated earlier by another worker.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — CRM and authoring continuity

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

Entering from a CRM Support row opens the same currently permitted original message/file. Return closes the viewer, restores the Support detail, and then returns to the originating CRM record. No file is copied onto every person/organization related to the conversation. CRM access alone never grants Support bytes; a Support assignee does not gain restricted CRM, finance or missionary context.

A draft's newly selected local file and an admitted message attachment are different states. Existing D18/D23 upload and source/asset qualification must finish before a reusable preview/download exists; the metadata-only current `local:` staging stub is not an implementation. This decision does not waive real upload/send qualification. Viewing an attachment never inserts its original or preview into TipTap. Deliberate future Attach/Reuse actions retain their existing identity, permission and audience review.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0010 — Visual craft and accessibility

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

Use Maia geometry, shared semantic tokens, clear typography and a single consistent reader shell. Use restrained borders, readable source identity and a short toolbar; do not crowd ordinary inspection with engine versions, full retention policies or a dashboard of file metadata. Coverage and actual failure information must remain easy to find, not hidden in a tooltip. Distinguish literal file type from verified eligibility.

Meet WCAG2.2 AA for app controls and content presentation that the product owns. Test visible keyboard focus, logical reading order, labels, current-page/sheet announcements, Escape/Close return, 200% text zoom,320-CSS-pixel reflow of chrome, high contrast, both themes and reduced motion. Provide buttons for pan/zoom/rotate navigation where gestures exist. Preserve legitimate image aspect and permit two-dimensional content scrolling without making the surrounding controls require horizontal scrolling. Touch targets use the shared accessible geometry; no color-only status or hover-only information.

Source accessibility limits are reported honestly: scanned pages may have no text; a source image may have no description; reading-order extraction may be insufficient. No fabricated alternative text or unverified automatic transcript is inserted. That does not excuse unusable controls or a grid with no equivalent accessible way to inspect its represented values. W3C grid guidance informs interactive navigation; a read-only table should use simpler semantic table behavior when sufficient.

### REQ26-D32-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0011 — Maintenance journey

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

Staff manage no renderer settings or converter account. The shared file/preview owner maintains one versioned format profile, qualified test corpus and dependency/security/cleanup controls. Changes affect new renditions, never the original file or a completed business record. An unsafe profile can be disabled centrally without disabling all Support work or weakening file restrictions. Tenants retain their existing file/content policy owner; C adds no admin extension editor.

All actual format, sandbox, private-range access, mobile/assistive-technology and staff-task tests in P01–P40 remain required. This blueprint is complete design documentation, not evidence of a tested perfect UI.

### REQ26-D32-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P01 — Forty falsifiable release groups

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

**Required outcome / positive, negative or boundary case:** Every included lane—PNG/JPEG/WebP/still GIF/PDF/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/TXT/CSV—has a real successful supported-file journey and supported-feature manifest. Metadata chips, first-page-only thumbnails or image/PDF-only rollout cannot count as C complete.

### REQ26-D32-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P02 — Forty falsifiable release groups

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

**Required outcome / positive, negative or boundary case:** Card shows current permitted metadata, actual size/type/readiness and distinct Preview/Download original actions; opening a conversation or finding a filename performs no eager conversion/download. Same filenames keep distinct original occurrences.

### REQ26-D32-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P03 — Forty falsifiable release groups

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

**Required outcome / positive, negative or boundary case:** Image orientation/aspect/color/zoom remain useful; GIF and animated PNG/WebP are explicitly first-composited-still, not full-animation proof. Unsupported decoding/coverage becomes unavailable. Pixel and decoded-memory boundaries apply before uncontrolled allocation.

### REQ26-D32-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P04 — Forty falsifiable release groups

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.

**Required outcome / positive, negative or boundary case:** PDF static pages/text/navigation work; no scripting, XFA execution, form submit, embedded-file launch or automatic external resource/link activation. Unsupported encryption/dynamic appearance/layer cases disclose limits or fail truthfully.

### REQ26-D32-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P05 — Forty falsifiable release groups

Applies to **US26-D32-06**, acceptance **AC26-D32-06-01–03**.
