### REQ26-D33-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — One control where reading happens

Applies to **US26-D33-04**, acceptance **AC26-D33-04-01–03**.

Place **Reading: Compact ▾** in the conversation reader utility header beside **Find**. On a narrow screen it remains a labelled control in the conversation header's utility row, not an unlabelled icon squeezed between destructive actions. Retain the existing Support shell/list/detail hierarchy; the label remains available in an empty reader pane so an authorized staff member can choose a default before opening a conversation. No tenant-settings detour, new profile-settings route or administration permission is required.

The menu is short and single level:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Your Support reading default
> Only for you in River Mission. Changes save automatically.
> 
> ● Compact
>   Fold repeated quoted history and signatures
> ○ Full
>   Show complete message content
> 
> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
> This conversation
> Expand repeated content

River Mission is an illustrative tenant label, not production data. Show the real currently authorized tenant name. Compact remains the initial choice; it does not make type smaller or change folder/list density. The menu offers one permanent choice group and one clearly separated temporary action, not two competing sets of Compact/Full radios. Add **Use my default (Compact)** to the temporary group when overrides exist; show the actual confirmed default in parentheses. With no active conversation, temporary actions are absent; saving the personal default still works.

Use the existing shared Base UI DropdownMenu radio components. Exactly one effective mode exists; there is no nullable mode or Both state. A radio's proposed/checked selection must be accompanied by accurate Saving/confirmation/failure status, not called a saved value before acknowledgement. Unknown preference state is visibly distinct and cannot fabricate a confirmed saved checkmark. Underlying copy clearly distinguishes the current local choice from the last confirmed default where they differ.

### REQ26-D33-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — What Compact actually does

Applies to **US26-D33-02**, acceptance **AC26-D33-02-01–03**.

Each message keeps its author, audience/recipients, time, delivery state and attachment controls. Normal body text has the same Maia typography, spacing and line height as Full. Only whole regions meeting the conservative repetition contract fold. Use **Show quoted history** or **Show repeated signature**, with a small directional icon, descriptive accessible name tied to its message, and visible focus. Labels explain the region; they do not imply it is irrelevant, removed, private or safe to ignore.

The first unique closing/contact detail remains readable. An unmarked or uncertain signature stays visible. A changed link, image, number, table cell, emphasis or inline answer keeps the whole affected quote open. A quote-only or signature-only message must not become a blank-looking response: keep its content visible when it is the only substantive body region. Nested quotations are folded as the largest wholly eligible region rather than creating many nested controls. If a parent is changed/uncertain, leave that parent open; do not pursue inner word-level folds that make an inline answer hard to follow.

Do not hide current drafts, signatures in the composer, prepared/send review material, internal notes or work history. D33 does not change what the requester receives. Full in this feature refers to email-body reading, not raw transport source, source history restoration or a staff's unrestricted access to all linked records.

### REQ26-D33-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Ordinary Compact journey

Applies to **US26-D33-02**, acceptance **AC26-D33-02-01–03**.

1. Maya enters Support in River Mission. A successful absent-preference read resolves to Compact without creating a row. If the preference is not yet known, the reader can start temporary Compact without blocking authorized messages.
2. She opens a conversation from the inbox. Normal content appears immediately; repeated eligible history has labelled disclosures. New inline content, first forwarded context and uncertain material remain visible.
3. She opens **Show quoted history**. It expands in place. Focus stays on the disclosure or intentionally navigates to the result, and no preference write occurs. She can open another region without closing the first.
4. She chooses **Expand repeated content** in the Reading menu. The reader policy becomes temporary Full for this conversation, shown as **Reading: Full · this conversation**. The saved-default radio remains Compact. Progressive loading continues; Full does not download the whole archive or its files.
5. She chooses **Use my default (Compact)** when finished. This clears temporary expansion rules for this conversation, except an active Find target/focused region that must remain reachable. Restoring Compact preserves the visible message anchor and does not move Send beneath the pointer.
6. She opens another conversation. The saved Compact default applies. Returning through the same qualified navigation session restores her earlier safe anchor/disclosures; a fresh visit/reload uses the saved default. No per-conversation expansion rows are stored.

An individual section expansion does not calculate or save a new global mode even if it happens to be the last collapsed section. The header mode describes the current default/temporary presentation rule. Only the conversation-wide temporary action sets **Full · this conversation**; this avoids a moving label based on how many regions have loaded.

### REQ26-D33-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Choosing and saving Full

Applies to **US26-D33-04**, acceptance **AC26-D33-04-01–03**.

1. Maya opens **Reading: Compact** and selects **Full** in **Your Support reading default**. The visible copy makes the persistent effect explicit before selection. No second confirmation or Save dialog is added.
2. The current reader shows Full immediately and preserves draft/focus/message position. Display **Saving…** beside the utility control or in its status region; announce it politely without repeated spoken updates.
3. On confirmed success show **Default saved** quietly. The control is **Reading: Full**. Future Support conversations in this tenant and the same authorized Support reader through CRM use Full on other devices after normal preference retrieval.
4. Another staff member and Maya's other tenant remain unchanged. Existing open readers on other tabs/devices learn the changed default for their next entry; they do not abruptly collapse, expand or jump while someone reads.
5. Choosing Compact later is the reset. It is an explicit conditional Compact save that retains a revision fence, not a delete or reset-all-preferences command. Both choices remain available even when the current email has no foldable content; a small explanatory line can say that this message has no repeated sections, without disabling the personal setting.

Full displays all current safe body content through the same reader. It retains quotation indentation, links, alternative text and tables within qualified rendering, with safe overflow where inherently needed. It does not grant remote-image fetch, execute arbitrary HTML, recalculate attachments or expose raw email source. It does not automatically collapse old whole messages; source-window navigation is a separate existing control.

### REQ26-D33-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Save, loading and connection failures

Applies to **US26-D33-01**, acceptance **AC26-D33-01-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Situation                                  | Reader behaviour                                                               | Visible recovery                                                                  | Persistence rule                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Confirmed no saved value                   | Compact.                                                                       | Menu identifies initial Compact.                                                  | No write on read.                                                                      |
| Preference loading                         | Correctly scoped confirmed cache where available; otherwise temporary Compact. | Neutral loading status; messages remain usable.                                   | No assumed revision/value write.                                                       |
| Preference unavailable/invalid/unsupported | Current local mode remains; initially temporary Compact.                       | **Could not load your default. This view only.** Retry.                           | Never overwrite saved Full with fallback Compact. Retry reads before saving.           |
| Save definitely rejected                   | Chosen local mode stays for this visit.                                        | **Could not save your default. This view only.** Retry after cause resolution.    | Last confirmed server value remains authoritative.                                     |
| Save response lost/ambiguous               | Chosen local mode stays.                                                       | **Could not confirm your default was saved.** Retry/reconcile.                    | Do not assert failure or success; read/retry cannot overwrite a newer different value. |
| Another device changed value               | Current reading/disclosures stay; known default updates.                       | **Default updated elsewhere.** Deliberate apply/retry is available when relevant. | Current revision wins; no automatic conflict rebase.                                   |
| Source comparison unavailable              | Full qualified content for affected message.                                   | Normal readable content; no alarm for conservative fallback.                      | No preference change, no source rewrite.                                               |
| Source renderer unavailable                | Qualified safe text if available, otherwise truthful content error/Retry.      | **Message content could not be displayed.** Existing owner recovery.              | Never raw HTML, blank success or unqualified cached content.                           |
| Actual source permission lost              | Remove/block affected source and its display state.                            | Existing source-authorized unavailable state.                                     | Reading preference cannot bypass loss of access.                                       |

A mode choice during unresolved persistence applies locally with **This view only**. A successful later lookup does not silently persist an earlier local choice; deliberate Retry/save confirms the current intended value. Serialize rapid local saves and preserve the latest local intent; old responses or rollbacks cannot override it. After an external conflict, stop automatic queued writes and ask for an explicit reapply of the current desired mode through the same small menu. This is ordinary conflict recovery, not a modal approval workflow.

### REQ26-D33-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Search, CRM and attachment journeys

Applies to **US26-D33-03**, acceptance **AC26-D33-03-01–03**.

**Search:** Maya finds a phrase in an older quote. D22 loads the exact permitted original region, reveals it and highlights the match even beyond mounted history. Her saved Compact setting stays Compact. Clearing Find leaves the inspected region open; a later explicit reset can compact it when no active focus/match depends on it. No inaccessible match count or placeholder reveals hidden sources. Browser Find is supplementary, not a replacement for this journey.

**CRM:** she opens a linked conversation from an authorized Party record. The same reader resolves her current tenant/profile preference and keeps CRM return context. A Support link does not reveal restricted giving/member-care context. After inspecting the conversation she returns to the same CRM record/position. No second preference, interaction record, source copy or background CRM mutation exists.

**Attachment:** she deliberately previews a qualified D32 attachment and returns. Mode, open regions, source message anchor and draft are preserved while current access is rechecked. Full reading never eagerly opens files. A source restriction that occurs while the preview is open wins over restored reading state. Download original remains separate; this control does not attach a file to the reply.

**New arrival and merge:** a newly received message is readable under the current reader policy but does not steal focus or rewind scroll. Existing new-message behaviour remains; no new mark-read rule is introduced. Merge/Undo changes context and invalidates dependent repetition proofs without changing original content or personal preference. Original message IDs and current scope govern return anchors; if an anchor is no longer eligible, return to the nearest permitted stable context with an honest notice, not substituted text.

### REQ26-D33-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Visual and accessibility discipline

Applies to **US26-D33-04**, acceptance **AC26-D33-04-01–03**.

Use a quiet, text-led utility control, not a theme/density dashboard. Keep body text the visual priority. Maia's existing compact utility variants may keep the header tidy; they must not shrink the email body. Use semantic background/foreground/muted/border/ring tokens and existing radius/spacing/type. Do not copy ReUI's icon rails, coloured tag assortment, 440px fixed list or v3 mail's Radix primitives merely to resemble the screenshot.

The shared menu must support arrow navigation, Enter/Space selection, Escape dismissal and predictable focus return, with programmatic grouping/check state. Disclosure controls expose aria-expanded and control the corresponding permitted region; collapsed descendants are not tabbable. Text descriptions wrap at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom; no page-wide two-dimensional scrolling is introduced. Essential touch controls have 44 CSS px targets and no hover dependency. Test screen reader announcements, RTL/LTR mixed quotations, Thai/CJK, long names, literal dates/timezones and large font settings. Opening history is immediate; do not animate height or auto-scroll long distances. Existing reduced-motion and Base UI motion tokens govern any menu animation.

No screenshot or primitive documentation establishes these outcomes. The browser-reference review records what was actually observed. P01–P36 require actual qualified implementation and participant evidence. This is the complete accepted journey, not a promise that the current scaffold already behaves this way.

### REQ26-D33-DATA_CONTRACT-S0002 — One small authoritative preference

Applies to **US26-D33-01**, acceptance **AC26-D33-01-01–03**.

D20-R01/R12 already generalizes the shared preference machinery and distinguishes personal display state from shared view definitions. Extend that owner with a closed Support-reading subject. The existing CRM gift-history route, patch helper and table settings are not a generic implementation of it. The independent data review pins actual schema/API/cache findings and a two-case real helper probe.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact                      | Owner / authoritative key                                                                                                  | Constraint                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Personal default          | Shared personal-preference owner; current tenant + real authenticated profile/member + closed Support-reading key          | At most one row; only Compact/Full; initial virtual Compact revision0 on confirmed absence.                                                              |
| Concurrency revision      | Same preference record                                                                                                     | Persisted positive monotonically increasing revision, separate from schema_version and wall-clock timestamp. Serialize without unsafe numeric precision. |
| Update attribution/time   | Trusted current server context                                                                                             | Caller cannot choose tenant, custodian, actor, owner, role or timestamp. Current membership/Support reader capability required.                          |
| Current reading policy    | Qualified reader visit                                                                                                     | Compact/Full derived from confirmed preference or deliberate local choice. Temporary only; no per-conversation row.                                      |
| Region disclosures/anchor | Current reader + exact permitted original/source generation                                                                | Transient identifiers/positions, not persisted body excerpts; source restriction invalidates them.                                                       |
| Segment map               | Qualified safe current message representation + source/restriction/render/segment versions + authorized comparison context | Expendable derivative; never the canonical body or a write authority. No cross-tenant/global-digest index.                                               |

The API exposes an explicit status: confirmed value/revision; confirmed absence; unavailable; invalid/unsupported. Do not convert query errors to absence. Browser credentials/profile IDs are resolved through the actual authenticated profile mapping, not support-agent email fallback. Current read eligibility authorizes personalizing the reader; CRM gift-history permissions and Support administration are unrelated gates.

No initial backfill or write-on-read is required. An explicit Compact save persists a revision fence even if the UI was already showing initial Compact. Reset means Compact through the same command. Tenant/account deletion uses the shared personal-data owner's cleanup; the preference has no legal/business-history retention purpose. Offboarding blocks access immediately; role changes do not silently copy the setting to a replacement person with the same email.

### REQ26-D33-DATA_CONTRACT-S0003 — Conditional desired-state command

Applies to **US26-D33-04**, acceptance **AC26-D33-04-01–03**.

Input contains only the closed desired mode and expected preference revision (plus the existing trusted request envelope). The server resolves the scope/key itself. Execute one atomic conditional operation:

1. Resolve current authenticated profile, tenant membership and permission for the reader/personal preference. Reject unsupported mode/unknown mutable fields; do not silently drop them.
2. Read/lock or conditionally address the unique preference row. Confirmed missing is virtual revision0. A concurrent first insert is protected by the unique constraint and reconciled as a race, not a duplicate row.
3. If expected revision equals current revision, persist the deliberately chosen mode and advance revision once, including an explicit same-value confirmation. This prevents an old request at revision0 or an old pre-reset revision from becoming valid again.
4. If revision differs and desired mode equals current mode, return **Already current** with the current revision. This confirms current desired state, not that the earlier transport request definitely committed. It produces no new write.
5. If revision differs and desired mode differs, return conflict with currently authorized value/revision. The stale request never overwrites it. A new deliberate reapply uses the freshly presented revision; do not automatically rebase queued writes.

This is desired-state idempotency, not exactly-once transport or business history. It needs no durable outbox, retry workflow or receipt journal. A browser AbortController/timeout cannot establish that a server write was cancelled. Reconcile a lost response against current state; distinguish confirmed rejection, unconfirmed commit and superseded value.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Race / retry                                                       | Required result                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Two first Full saves at revision0                                  | One insert at revision1; other returns Already current1. No duplicate or extra revision.                                           |
| First Full versus first Compact at revision0                       | One admitted revision1; other conflicts if different. UI keeps its own desired local view without calling it saved.                |
| Save Full at0, response lost, retry Full at0                       | Current Full1 returns Already current1; no extra write.                                                                            |
| Full1 then deliberate Compact at1→2, old Full-at0 retry            | Conflict/current Compact2. Never reset to Full.                                                                                    |
| Confirm Compact from absent0→1, delayed Full-at0 arrives           | Conflict/current Compact1. An explicit reset/confirmation fences older absent-state writes.                                        |
| Same-value deliberate save Full at current1                        | Advance to2, confirming that fresh intent; a retry at1 returns Already current2.                                                   |
| Another device changes while a local write is queued               | Preserve newest local view, reconcile current revision, stop automatic queued rebasing; explicit retry decides whether to reapply. |
| Old mutation error/response arrives after a newer confirmed result | Ignore it for current view/cache rollback. Do not restore a whole stale response.                                                  |
| Tenant/profile switch during read/save                             | Result remains bound to original scope; it cannot populate the new scope's reader or preference.                                   |

Serialize client writes and maintain a current local-intent generation. Newer desired local view is never reverted by older responses. A queued request may proceed using the exact acknowledged successor of this client's preceding accepted command only while no intervening external revision/conflict is known; otherwise stop and reconcile for explicit reapply. Choosing a temporary mode while a preference request is unresolved remains available and has no save effect. No offline autosave queue later surprises the person after switching tenants or signing out.

### REQ26-D33-DATA_CONTRACT-S0004 — Grants, RLS and service-role path

Applies to **US26-D33-04**, acceptance **AC26-D33-04-01–03**.

The current preference implementation revokes direct browser grants and uses a service command. Retain least privilege and qualify the additive command instead of broadening clients to write a generic settings JSON object. RLS is defence in depth for granted row access; it does not protect a service role that bypasses it. Actual tenant/profile/key checks and immutable-scope transition constraints remain necessary in the server/RPC path.

Require unique/non-null scope, closed enum/checks, tenant-aware membership integrity, valid revision range and owner-qualified delete behaviour. A profile FK and tenant FK separately do not prove their pair belongs to a current membership. Index the actual point lookup/unique scope; do not create a full-text or content index for the preference. Domain money precision, public storage buckets and append-only business events are not part of this schema.

Verify table grants, policies, SELECT eligibility and UPDATE old-row/new-row checks, views/functions and execution grants. PostgreSQL may reuse USING as WITH CHECK when no separate expression is supplied; do not claim every omitted WITH CHECK automatically opens reassignment. Nevertheless make the intended old/new invariants explicit and prove allowed writes cannot retarget tenant/profile/key or accept arbitrary revision/attribution. Functions that run with elevated rights need fixed trusted resolution, least execution grants and current caller checks; SECURITY DEFINER is not an authorization repair by itself. Supabase RLS, PostgreSQL CREATE POLICY.

### REQ26-D33-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — Source maps and safe reading

Applies to **US26-D33-04**, acceptance **AC26-D33-04-01–03**.

Compact/Full both start from the D23 qualified safe source. Segment typed safe nodes or an equivalently qualified representation, not arbitrary HTML string offsets. A quote/signature marker is a candidate boundary only. Establish complete meaning-aware repetition within currently eligible original context; altered inline content, hrefs, assets, formatting, first/unique context or unsupported structure stays visible. Compare historical admitted content, never live P17/profile data. A quote-only/signature-only body remains meaningful and visible.

Maps bind exact current source version, restriction generation, renderer/segment profile and comparison eligibility. They reference the current message's own permitted content; they never replace it with another message or permit reconstructing a removed source from a surviving quotation. Restriction/expiry/move/merge/Undo and permission changes invalidate stale maps and requests. An earlier comparison source losing access yields no hidden-source hint; the current source can simply display full permitted content. Material already delivered cannot be remotely recalled.

D22 full Find/search remains over its authorized retained population, not current DOM/fold state. Match targets use current source identities and correctly mapped text/structure boundaries; stale matches cannot jump to substitute content. Only required source windows load. Full/disclosure never authorizes attachment fetch, active HTML, remote tracking images or raw-source export.

### REQ26-D33-DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — Cache and lifecycle

Applies to **US26-D33-04**, acceptance **AC26-D33-04-01–03**.

Keep confirmed preference, local mode and transient disclosure state separate. Preference keys include tenant/profile/key, segment keys include current source lineage, and asynchronous cache results carry scope/version. No content in durable browser storage is required to remember a two-value default. Existing approved server read-model hooks/TanStack Query can cache preference state with correct scoping; they cannot reuse the current table-only key or indiscriminate rollback unchanged.

Passive refresh updates the known default for the next untouched reader entry. It never reshapes active reading without deliberate application. Access revocation is different: it immediately fences affected content and clears stale client state on the existing source-change/reconnect/visibility contract. Fresh reload uses the confirmed default; same navigation-session back from CRM/preview can restore authorized IDs/anchors/disclosures. Missing or changed targets have truthful recovery.

Activate only after the full safe reader, typed preference command and bounded segment profile pass actual proof. Schema compatibility must preserve existing D20/CRM settings. Unknown future versions remain explicit and read-only rather than being coerced into Compact and overwritten. Rollback retains preference rows/revisions and source restrictions. A segmentation kill switch serves qualified Full for the affected profile without writing the person's saved mode.

See P01–P36 and O01–O06. The actual-source helper probe establishes two current limitations; required CAS, RLS, cache, browser and source-map behaviours remain unexecuted release obligations.

## Composing awareness

### REQ26-D34-R01 — R01 — Meaning and scope

Applies to **US26-D34-01**, acceptance **AC26-D34-01-01–03**.

Support SHALL show recent deliberate composition by currently eligible authenticated staff in the current authorized Support reader. It SHALL NOT show passive viewers, last-seen times, draft previews, cursor positions, work duration or typing statistics. The cue is advisory; absence is never an all-clear or evidence that nobody else is working. It grants no assignment, ownership, coverage, Follow, read receipt, permission, lock or completion meaning.

### REQ26-D34-R02 — R02 — Small, discoverable presentation

Applies to **US26-D34-01**, acceptance **AC26-D34-01-01–03**.

Use one stable utility line immediately above the active Reply/Note composer, also visible at that location before composition starts. Preserve D33 Reading/Find and the current reader shell. Show “Maya Chen is composing”; both Reply and Note use the same neutral wording. Show at most two qualified names inline, then an additional qualified count; narrow layouts may show “3 teammates composing” with an accessible current-name disclosure. Two is a layout limit, not a query limit. No passive roster, takeover, modal, sound, toast per event, red alarm styling or pulsing typing dots is added.

### REQ26-D34-R03 — R03 — Identity and complete projection

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

Names come from Core's authorized internal staff identity owner, not a browser payload, email address, requester, CRM contact, assignee or public email signature. Omit the current authenticated profile and deduplicate eligible sessions by real profile only after source and identity qualification. One tab stopping does not clear another eligible active tab. Use existing authorized same-name disambiguation, international names and bidi isolation. A hidden person's existence SHALL NOT leak through a generic label, count or overflow. If a bounded query cannot establish the complete permitted set, show unavailable rather than a partial exact count.

### REQ26-D34-R04 — R04 — Genuine input, private content

Applies to **US26-D34-01**, acceptance **AC26-D34-01-01–03**.

Qualifying activity includes actual input/deletion, paste, dictation, IME composition and deliberate composer operations such as formatting, link edits, recipient changes, saved-wording/signature insertion, attachment selection/removal and undo/redo. Focus, selection, reading, opening, draft restoration, prefetch, autosave, remote/programmatic updates and background AI generation alone do not qualify. Detect intent through the existing editor/controls without serializing or transmitting text, keys, preedit candidates, recipients, attachment identities, body length or Reply/Note mode for awareness.

### REQ26-D34-R05 — R05 — Eligibility and endings

Applies to **US26-D34-01**, acceptance **AC26-D34-01-01–03**.

Publishing requires the current visible, active document, a qualified mounted composer and current compose authority for its exact source. Moving focus within composer controls does not stop it. Stop promptly on idle, explicit discard/cancel, successful reply/note admission, source/tenant/session exit, access loss, hidden document or inactive application window. Opening a modal file preview suspends composition while preserving the draft. Stop is best effort; server expiry is mandatory. Return, reconnect, focus restoration or a restored draft alone SHALL NOT resume composing; a fresh deliberate composition action is required.

### REQ26-D34-R06 — R06 — One explicit initial timing profile

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

Send a leading start or explicit stop promptly, without a trailing typing debounce. Ordinary combined control/snapshot refresh runs every **5 seconds** while locally composing or displaying a current peer cue, otherwise every **10 seconds** while the reader is eligible. Use a **15-second** composing liveness bound, a **30-second** observer lease and a **30-second** local inactivity cutoff. A renewal cannot refresh the fresh-input frontier unless new qualifying input occurred. Server expiry is the minimum of liveness, last accepted fresh input plus 30 seconds, session/observer expiry and source fences. Controls carry a fixed **15-second** server-issued freshness window; snapshots have at most **12 seconds** of display trust from request start. These are initial Asym engineering choices, not vendor standards. The detailed clock and ambiguity semantics in the data contract govern boundary cases.

### REQ26-D34-R07 — R07 — Trusted session and source

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

Core SHALL derive tenant, authenticated profile, actual auth-session binding and current source authority on the server. A profile or client-provided session ID is not an auth-session proof. The current auth owner must expose a qualified real-session binding; legacy Support email-to-agent matching is insufficient. Each server-issued reader instance binds its exact tab/context, original-source affinity and current topology/restriction generation. Reader permission and composition permission are distinct checks. Source changes cannot silently retarget an existing instance.

### REQ26-D34-R08 — R08 — Narrow database boundary

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

Use one regular application-schema technical session record per issued reader instance with separate observer and composition deadlines. Keep trusted scope immutable; use actual Core key types, same-tenant relationships, finite time/sequence constraints, unique opaque instance/topic identity, indexed current-source/expiry lookup and bounded cleanup. No custom object is added to Supabase's managed `realtime` schema. Revoke direct client lease DML/read and raw-row change publication; only closed authorized commands and projections may access it. Verify actual grants, effective RLS USING/WITH CHECK, function execution/search path, storage non-use and every privileged service path. No caller may set actor, tenant, deadline, approval, authority or audit attribution.

### REQ26-D34-R09 — R09 — Ordering and freshness

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

All instance controls use one monotonic sequence and server-issued generation with fixed not-after time. Accepted updates atomically compare current instance, scope, sequence, generation and deadline. Already-issued windows cannot be extended by a different heartbeat. Lower/duplicate controls do not renew state. Expired, closed or unknown instances cannot be recreated by update/upsert, even after cleanup. A new qualified instance receives a new ID. Coalesce desired state; never queue or replay offline typing. An old Start, Renew or Stop cannot revive or clear a newer episode.

### REQ26-D34-R10 — R10 — Ambiguous control outcomes

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

Use one serialized control stream per reader instance. A transport timeout is not proof the server rejected the last command. On ambiguous mutation outcome, stop writes and perform a current-authorized reconciliation read of that instance's last accepted sequence, window and state; this read renews no deadline and never rotates the window. Do not replay/relabel the old body or invent the next generation. A still-live episode may renew within its original input deadline; expired/stopped state requires new qualifying input. An expired control window or unknown/closed instance requires fresh registration, without reviving the old instance. Flush a pending current Stop promptly after reconciliation. No permanent command receipt journal or new signing infrastructure is required for this expendable signal.

### REQ26-D34-R11 — R11 — Current authorization through every surface

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

Qualify both producer and observer against exact current source affinity, membership, identity visibility and source topology at control, snapshot and fanout admission. A continuing merged root, CRM link, shared inbox, assignment or matching email is not sufficient. Do not expose composition on inaccessible constituent B to someone permitted only constituent A. Known context/access changes invalidate local state; new reads and newly admitted wakes deny obsolete audiences. An already authorized in-flight hint or already seen screen cannot be recalled; do not claim instant erasure across disconnected devices.

### REQ26-D34-R12 — R12 — Private hints, not client Presence authority

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

Only the server may publish a versioned, content-free `refresh` hint to each current eligible observer's opaque private topic. The hint contains no name, actor/source ID, count, mode or activity reason. Clients cannot publish Broadcast or Presence on these topics. Verify topic ownership and private receive policies. Supabase's cached join authorization is defense in depth, not current per-event authorization. No shared conversation-room wake is used as a shortcut around current recipient selection.

### REQ26-D34-R13 — R13 — Fresh snapshots and conservative expiry

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

Names and deadlines come only from an authenticated current snapshot with trusted server as-of, absolute expiry and matching instance/context/request generation. Subscribe then reconcile to close the missed-event race; coalesce wakes with single-flight reads and one dirty follow-up when needed. Expiry SHALL be anchored conservatively to monotonic request start, not response arrival or mutable browser wall time. Reject late/mismatched responses and clear expired claims locally without waiting for another event. Resume from hidden/sleep/bfcache/reconnect requires fresh authorization before reuse.

### REQ26-D34-R14 — R14 — Honest availability

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

A current, complete empty snapshot renders no composer cue; it does not say nobody is working. While the broker is unavailable but current HTTP snapshots remain healthy, keep valid cues with quiet “Live updates delayed” text. After snapshot trust expires or current state cannot be qualified, remove names and show “Live composing cues unavailable.” Do not show transient startup warnings on every mount. These states never prevent independently qualified reading, draft editing or sending. Permission denial removes the inaccessible surface under its owning contract, not as a mere transport error.

### REQ26-D34-R15 — R15 — React and editor lifecycle

Applies to **US26-D34-04**, acceptance **AC26-D34-04-01–03**.

Use a small Support client island, stable human-intent listeners, non-render refs for counters/timers and the existing qualified browser Supabase client through the shared database adapter. Own/refcount exact channels; never remove all application channels or disconnect another feature. Topic/private configuration is immutable per generation. Strict Mode, remount and account changes must clean up only owned resources. Awareness SHALL NOT add draft serialization, replace the editor, use every Tiptap transaction as input, force full-thread renders or call router refresh per heartbeat. Preserve selection, IME, undo, autosave and D33 local reading state.

### REQ26-D34-R16 — R16 — Core Next/Vercel boundary

Applies to **US26-D34-04**, acceptance **AC26-D34-04-01–03**.

Business handlers belong in the shared API owner, transport adapters in the shared database/infrastructure adapter layer, presentation in the shared supported UI path and app routes remain thin. Snapshots and control responses are private/no-store current request results, excluded from shared Next/CDN/persisted query caches and prefetch state. Follow Core's actual Cache Components and runtime-map rules; do not add prohibited route-segment exports. Qualify supported deployed runtime, actual Vercel/Supabase regions and installed versions. Supabase is chosen to reuse the current stack; current Vercel WebSocket support is not falsely declared impossible.

### REQ26-D34-R17 — R17 — CRM continuity

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

CRM opens the same authorized Support reader and composing capability, preserving the current source and return context. Staff working there and in Support can see each other's eligible cue without a duplicate ticket, person, draft or CRM Activity. Requester, participant, authenticated staff, contact, represented organization, assignee and record owner remain distinct. Composition performs no CRM/financial/member-care mutation. Access and consequences of contact, receipt, refund, recurring-gift or other business actions stay with their owning domains; resolution does not prove those actions completed.

### REQ26-D34-R18 — R18 — Email Studio and delivery seam

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

P17 Email Studio owns governed reusable wording, signature/authoring policy and immutable outbound preparation; P6 owns actual dispatch, retry, provider outcome and communication evidence. D34 owns only expiring composition metadata. Deliberate use of existing wording/signature tools may count as local activity, but D34 never reads or creates their content/preparation, shares drafts, alters recipients/quotes/signatures/attachments or emits mail. Ending a cue on reply admission is not a Sent claim. Notes keep their internal audience; no public or donor-visible typing event is introduced.

### REQ26-D34-R19 — R19 — Real collision protection remains mandatory

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Two colleagues may compose at once. The existing D1/D4 current-source/reviewed-version admission check must still independently handle simultaneous sends and newly committed work, preserve both private drafts and require the appropriate updated review. Presence, absence, availability failure or a forged self-report SHALL NOT bypass or block this authority. Durable send idempotency is tied to the actual business effect and is not replaced by D34's ephemeral sequence.

### REQ26-D34-R20 — R20 — Privacy and future AI

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Retain no viewing/composition history, per-person productivity metric or content-bearing awareness log. Technical observer rows are not publicly browsable viewing records. Future AI may not retrieve D34 as donor/CRM evidence, receive private draft text through it, impersonate a human composer or take actions based on it. Existing explicit AI/authoring permissions remain separate. Minimize technical logs, exports, traces and backups under actual platform retention; short row expiry does not promise deletion from every backup.

### REQ26-D34-R21 — R21 — Bounded work and capacity

Applies to **US26-D34-04**, acceptance **AC26-D34-04-01–03**.

Apply the exact initial per-instance, source-context and response budgets in the runtime contract. Coalesce unchanged renewals and transition wakes; no wake per keystroke or ordinary unchanged keepalive. Do not fan out to hidden/unqualified readers, preload every conversation or silently truncate a permitted set. Above a declared limit, degrade awareness honestly and preserve source work. Measure database writes, authorization, fanout, snapshot round trips and UI paint; provider message quotas and a local benchmark do not establish Core capacity.

### REQ26-D34-R22 — R22 — Expendable transport and repair

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Commit each accepted lease transition atomically, then attempt bounded awaited hint dispatch. Catch HTTP rejection/timeout; a broker 202 is admission, not delivery or display. Hint failure cannot roll back the lease, fail a draft save or block a reply. Bounded snapshot reconciliation and expiry repair lost/duplicate/out-of-order hints. No durable outbox, notification engine, workflow retry backlog, database trigger on each heartbeat or new WebSocket host is added solely for this cue.

### REQ26-D34-R23 — R23 — Maintenance and cleanup

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

The Support capability owner maintains cue behavior; the shared identity/database owners qualify security and session handling; platform operations owns broker/runtime health. Use the existing scheduler for bounded expiry cleanup, targeting physical removal within **15 minutes after observer expiry/closure**, without a history table or cascading business deletion. Expired rows never appear even if cleanup is late. Restore, mixed versions and disablement must honor absolute expiry and current authorization, and force fresh instances rather than revive activity.

### REQ26-D34-R24 — R24 — Rollout and recovery

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Deploy additive app-schema/command/policy support before the guarded client. Explicitly enable only qualified tenants after real proof. Keep new-client/old-server and old-client/new-server failure benign and cue-only. A versioned protocol rejects unsupported envelopes. A server-side kill switch stops registration, publication and snapshots; notify connected qualified clients where possible and otherwise expire visible state. Roll back code with harmless finite rows retained; do not destructively remove schema while live versions use it. Never compensate by weakening access or widening room topics.

### REQ26-D34-R25 — R25 — Accessible stable UI

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Use actual shared Base UI/base-maia and semantic Zinc/theme tokens, readable contrast and typography. Names/status are text, not color/hover-only signals. The current-name disclosure works with keyboard, touch, zoom and RTL/LTR content. Use polite coalesced aggregate announcements for meaningful changes; never announce renewals or keystrokes. Preserve composer/send position, focus, scroll and reduced-motion behavior. Test mobile/IME/assistive technology and low-bandwidth conditions; visual polish is not assumed from a component library.

### REQ26-D34-R26 — R26 — Observation without surveillance

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Record content-free request outcomes, timing, stale-control rejection, broker failure, freshness loss, admission-limit rejection and cleanup lag under existing restricted operational telemetry. Do not log names, draft fields, raw topic tokens or a timeline of specific staff activity. Business and security audit records retain their own meaning; D34 creates no fake communication audit. Each monitored risk SHALL have the named signal, threshold, owner and response in the proof/operations ledger; privacy/authorization failure is a release blocker, not a metric tolerated until enough incidents accumulate.

### REQ26-D34-R27 — R27 — Falsifiable release evidence

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

The proof ledger's positive/negative/source/tenant/RLS/session/concurrency/input/lifecycle/failure/load/migration/accessibility and Support-to-CRM groups are required before activation. The healthy connected start and explicit-stop target is **p95 at most 1,000 milliseconds**, measured input-to-peer-paint in the declared region/network/load fixture. Report cold/reconnect/degraded results separately. Source inspections, mocked SDK calls and the reference model do not pass actual database, browser or deployment proof. Trace each clause through the feature ADR, glossary and required OpenSpec/tasks/tickets/tests/release evidence; no artifacts are prematurely called implemented.

### REQ26-D34-R28 — R28 — Evidence and proportionality

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

This decision uses verified current source/docs, documented vendor behavior and clearly labelled product judgments. No Asym tenant study or live deployment latency/permission test was performed. The need for an advisory cue follows the founder's selected workflow and credible collision patterns, not a measured duplicate-reply rate in ministries. Do not invent missionary workflows, copy commercial customer identities or build unrelated help-desk capabilities for parity. The numeric envelope is complete and testable now; changes after measurement must update the one versioned profile and affected evidence, not silently drift.

### REQ26-D34-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — What staff see

Applies to **US26-D34-01**, acceptance **AC26-D34-01-01–03**.

The ordinary current conversation remains the focus. Immediately above its Reply/Note composer, the utility line can say **Maya Chen is composing**. The same location is visible while reading before opening a draft; it sits apart from the selected audience control and the Send button. D33 Reading/Find stays where it is. A reserved flexible utility row prevents a cue arriving from moving the Send action under a pointer or disrupting the current reading anchor.

Use readable existing secondary-text sizing/contrast, a small neutral composition icon if useful and the existing profile presentation treatment. Text carries meaning. No tiny hover-only avatar, red alarm, animated dots, sound or toast. Do not reduce body type or touch targets to fit several names. Initial render without a known transport problem remains calm; a short startup connection phase is not a warning on every ticket.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Current qualified state                         | Visible treatment                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One other profile                               | “Maya Chen is composing”                                                                                                      |
| Two profiles                                    | “Maya Chen and Arun Rao are composing”                                                                                        |
| More profiles                                   | First two names plus an accessible “and3more” disclosure; exact count comes only from the complete permitted snapshot.        |
| Narrow layout                                   | “5 teammates composing”; open a small current-name disclosure with keyboard/touch.                                            |
| Complete current empty set                      | No composer line. Never “Nobody is working,” “All clear” or “You have this ticket.”                                           |
| Broker unavailable, HTTP snapshot still current | Valid cue if any, plus quiet “Live updates delayed.”                                                                          |
| Snapshot unknown/expired/unqualified            | Names disappear; “Live composing cues unavailable.” No stale roster is left behind.                                           |
| Known source access loss                        | Source owner's restricted/unavailable treatment takes priority; do not reveal identities/counts through an error explanation. |

The disclosure contains only the currently permitted composers, in stable order while the set is unchanged. It has no search, history, visit duration or last-seen. Optional explanatory text reads **“Shows recent drafting activity. Drafts stay private.”** Existing same-name disambiguation may show a permitted identity attribute; never expose a hidden email/role merely because two names match. Do not split international names into an assumed first/last pattern. Isolate mixed-direction names so punctuation remains correct.

### REQ26-D34-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Journey1 — Staff begins in Support

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

1. Maya opens a permitted request from the existing Support list. Loading and reading do not advertise her as composing. Her existing Compact/Full default and temporary expansions remain stable.
2. Arun has the same qualified source open. He is not shown as a viewer. Both receive only currently permitted peer composition metadata.
3. Maya deliberately begins a reply, dictates text, pastes wording, edits recipients or performs another qualifying composition action. The client sends a leading content-free intent independently of editor rendering. Arun sees “Maya Chen is composing” under the healthy measured latency target.
4. Arun may avoid duplicate effort, continue reading or work on a separate authorized note/draft. No automatic wait/takeover/lock appears; the cue does not decide who owns the work.
5. Maya pauses briefly or moves between formatting/link/attachment controls. The cue does not flicker on each key or toolbar blur. After30seconds without local qualifying work it stops; a lost connection may cause the server's15second liveness bound to remove it sooner. Her private draft remains saved under D2.
6. Maya submits her reply. On actual reply admission the cue stops promptly. Queued/sent/failed/provider-unknown state is separately presented by D4/P6; cue disappearance never claims Sent. On validation rejection the draft and still-eligible episode remain; if inactive/expired she starts a new episode on another edit.
7. If Arun also submits, D1/D4's actual source/version collision review independently governs. Neither a cue nor missing cue bypasses that check or discards either draft.

### REQ26-D34-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Journey2 — Staff begins in CRM

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

1. A staff member opens the permitted Support item from its CRM-linked history/context. This uses the same canonical Support source, not a CRM copy or a new conversation.
2. CRM contact access alone grants no extra Support, finance, missionary or member-care visibility. The reader and identity projection establish exactly what may be shown. A staff member limited to originalA cannot learn someone is composing on inaccessible originalB just because both appear under a continuing merged component.
3. The same utility line and composer behavior appear. Eligible composition started in Support is visible through this reader and vice versa. It requires no duplicate person, Activity, draft, task or “sync” record.
4. Moving to an authorized CRM task preserves the return context/draft but stops Support composition eligibility when its active composer is left. Making a contact/giving/receipt action is owned and audited by that domain; this cue neither initiates nor verifies it.
5. Returning restores current authorized reader state, D33 mode and private draft. It clears stale remote cues and fetches current state. Only a fresh deliberate composition action announces work again.

These are two entry journeys into one capability, not two feature implementations. Illustrative names and donor-care situations are examples, not claimed observed ministry workflows.

### REQ26-D34-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Input and transition matrix

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Action                                                                                                      | Announce or renew composition?                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text input/deletion/paste/drop/dictation, IME composition updates/commit                                    | Yes, coalesced human intent; never send contents/candidates or publish every key.                        |
| Deliberate formatting, link edit, recipient/attachment change, saved-wording/signature insertion, undo/redo | Yes; same neutral cue, no action/mode details.                                                           |
| Focus/autofocus, opening Reply, nonempty restored draft, selecting text, Find, scrolling                    | No.                                                                                                      |
| Autosave, editor hydration, remote signature/template update, background AI generation                      | No. A later deliberate insertion/edit may qualify under existing authoring permission.                   |
| Focus moves inside toolbar/popover owned by composer                                                        | Preserve the current episode within idle/liveness bounds.                                                |
| App/window becomes inactive; document hidden; file preview modal takes over; leave source                   | Stop promptly and preserve the draft. Browser events are best effort; server expiry covers missed stops. |
| 30s without input                                                                                           | Stop episode, no Away/Paused label.                                                                      |
| Successful Reply/Note admission, explicit discard/cancel                                                    | Stop. Do not wait for email provider delivery.                                                           |
| Access/tenant/auth-session/source changes                                                                   | Invalidate and clear old context; source owner decides available work.                                   |
| Reconnect/return/restore                                                                                    | Reauthorize/read current state; no automatic old typing replay.                                          |

Browser window blur is not identical to hidden document. This product deliberately suspends _publishing composition_ while its application window is inactive. The visible observer can still receive current peer information as long as its reader remains qualified; hidden readers stop ordinary interest renewal. Native picker/permission interruptions must preserve drafts and restart only on deliberate return interaction, not create an Away roster. IME focus transitions must be tested before treating blur as a universal event rule.

### REQ26-D34-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Failure and recovery journey

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

A slow/missing cue must not make the editor slow. Typing, autosave and source reading have their own qualified paths. If a wake is lost, the combined5s/10s snapshot loop repairs normal awareness. If snapshots also fail, known peer claims expire from request-start deadlines and the quiet unavailable state explains that live awareness is not current.

On a lost control acknowledgement, freeze only cue publication, reconcile the exact issued state without renewing it, and either continue a still-valid episode or require fresh input in a fresh instance. Never resubmit captured old input as new. There is no error dialog demanding the staff member solve a broker issue, and no per-keystroke retry toast. Pending stop is flushed promptly when control state is known. User-facing send failure/conflict remains separate and actionable under its own contract.

If the current-name disclosure is open when an actor disappears, update its contents without jumping focus; if it becomes empty, close safely and restore the triggering control's logical location. Do not announce that work is certainly finished. New names do not reorder unchanged entries on each renewal. No count from an incomplete/over-limit response is shown.

### REQ26-D34-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Mobile, accessibility and visual quality

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Use the same small cue in a narrow single-column reader. Do not pin a floating badge over the keyboard, obscure reply recipients or squeeze the Send button. Preserve D33's400% zoom,320CSS-pixel reflow and44CSS-pixel primary touch targets; meaningful names/controls remain reachable without a horizontal-only interaction. Existing Base UI disclosure semantics should expose label, expanded state, focus return and Escape behavior. Tooltip text alone is insufficient on touch.

Use a polite aggregate live region only for meaningful actor-set/availability changes. Coalesce rapid changes for speech without delaying visual freshness; ordinary renewals are silent. An ending can be announced as “Composing cue ended,” not “Nobody is composing.” Never move keyboard focus for presence. Reduced-motion mode remains static; this feature needs no continuous animation in either mode. Test screen readers, IME, dictation, keyboard-only, touch, same-name and long/RTL names against the actual composed interface.

### REQ26-D34-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Maintenance journey

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Tenant staff do not configure heartbeats, collision locks or an activity dashboard. The default cue works in qualified readers. Support administrators retain existing staff permissions/assignment/coverage controls; membership changes apply through those owners, not a parallel presence list. No new customer/donor preference is introduced.

The Support owner sees aggregated cue-health signals and can disable only awareness for an affected tenant/context. Platform operations checks broker/runtime/region/quota failures; database/identity owners investigate authorization or cleanup failures. A content-free diagnostic correlation is sufficient; do not request private drafts or record a staff activity timeline. Test/version/rollout procedures are in proof and operations.
