### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002 — Acceptance groups

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

An assertion about actual authorization/privacy is zero-tolerance at release. The source/identity/currentness prerequisites must be real before activation. A component-only happy-path test or generic provider demo does not pass them.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O01 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Healthy connected input-to-peer-paint p95>1,000ms over two consecutive5min windows with≥100 samples/window, or>5% samples fail to reach a current display within that target. Low samples show insufficient evidence, not green health.

**Required response:** Inspect stage latency/region/fanout; reduce feature admission or disable affected cue scope if persistent15min; preserve source/send work. Requalify before restoring broader capacity.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O02 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Broker dispatch/join failures>2% over5min with≥100 attempts, or30consecutive failures at lower traffic.

**Required response:** Mark broker path degraded through real client connection state, inspect provider status/quotas, retain current HTTP fallback. Disable wake attempts under shared circuit policy if needed; no durable retry storm.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O03 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** >2% of eligible reader-minutes with expired/unavailable snapshot trust over15min, or three consecutive snapshot failures for one current reader.

**Required response:** Quiet unavailable UI, diagnose API/auth/overload path with content-free outcomes. Rate-limit repair and preserve editor; fix before increasing activation. Do not treat every authorization denial as network failure.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O04 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** **Any** confirmed unauthorized identity/source/tenant disclosure, spoofed other-actor cue or prohibited draft payload in awareness.

**Required response:** Immediately disable affected awareness (global if scope uncertain), retain minimal authorized incident evidence, follow existing incident/privacy process and fix/requalify. Never wait for a percentage threshold.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O05 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Admission-limit rejection>1% over15min with≥100 eligible attempts; sustained>70% of configured provider capacity or measured sustainable service capacity for5min; any incomplete snapshot labelled complete.

**Required response:** Preserve generic unavailable, inspect noisy tenant and current query/fanout costs; adjust capacity only with proof. Incomplete-as-complete is a correctness defect requiring disable/fix, not ordinary scaling.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O06 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Oldest closed/observer-expired technical row remains>15min beyond its expiry/closure at any scheduled sweep; or cleanup fails three consecutive5min sweeps.

**Required response:** Repair existing scheduled cleanup/index/batch path; expired rows remain ineligible. Do not preserve an activity history or manually delete business data. Investigate backlog and restore normal purge.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O07 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** >1% protocol/version/window rejects over15min with≥100 controls excluding deliberate negative tests; any growing owned-channel/listener count after100 settled mount/send cycles in release smoke; any cue-correlated editor draft loss or global-channel teardown.

**Required response:** Inspect stale client/mixed-version/ACK fences and SDK ownership; roll back/disable cue if it affects work, then fix and repeat relevant proof. Draft loss/other-feature disruption is immediate disable, not tolerated at1%.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003 — Monitorable operating risks

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Owners are explicit accountable **roles**, not invented named employees. Assign the actual on-call/release person to each role in deployment evidence. These controls do not authorize per-person staff tracking. Use short-lived content-free correlation/aggregate telemetry and existing protected security audit only when needed.

Clock/network outages and a provider issue are monitored; unauthorized exposure, wrong source attribution, draft loss, unsafe send or resurrection are blockers that monitoring must help discover, never accept.

### REQ26-D34-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004 — Deployment sequence and rollback

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

1. Complete owner source/session predicates and additive schema/closed commands. Validate actual grants/RLS/service paths in isolated test tenants, with no real mail.
2. Qualify SDK/REST adapter and client island; exercise missed-hint/current-snapshot behavior and the full input/source matrix.
3. Execute P01–P36 and name actual deployment roles/versions/regions/quotas/ceilings. Existing D1/D4/D2/source/privacy prerequisites must pass independently.
4. Enable a bounded consenting pilot under current product release policy, then expand within the measured envelope. No new commissioning process for every ordinary staff member or user-configurable heartbeat is introduced.
5. Kill/rollback affects only awareness. Current clients clear on known disabled response and otherwise at trust expiry; server ignores/rejects old controls. Leave finite compatible rows/policies until old consumers are drained; roll forward repair and issue fresh instances. Do not drop schema or widen access to make rollback appear healthy.

### REQ26-D34-RUNTIME_CONTRACT-S0002 — Request path

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

`current visible reader → qualified Core API control → app-schema ephemeral lease → private server-originated refresh hint → current-authorized HTTP snapshot → isolated peer cue`.

Typing and the existing private draft editor never wait for this path. A cue reports recent authenticated intent, not the draft. Supabase carries the private wake; actual names are obtained only through Core's current read boundary. This avoids trusting raw client Presence and cached room membership without creating a second message/CRM authority.

Use existing browser Supabase ownership through the approved authorized read-projection boundary; one qualified browser client per actual browser auth context, and owned/refcounted channels. Different tabs have separate browser runtimes—no new cross-tab coordination service is introduced. Same-topic requests in installed realtime-js2.103.0 reuse the existing channel even if configuration differs, so every issued topic has immutable private configuration. Remove only the component's owned channel when its last consumer leaves. Never call global removeAllChannels/disconnect as one reader's cleanup.

The server uses the qualified adapter's bounded REST send without keeping one RealtimeChannel object per observer forever. If SDK `channel().httpSend()` is used, dispose the ephemeral owned channel after the send; the lack of an actual socket does not prevent a warm client's in-memory channel registry from growing. Server credentials remain in the existing server-only credential boundary. No package install/upgrade is required by this decision.

### REQ26-D34-RUNTIME_CONTRACT-S0003 — Endpoint and render ownership

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Business logic remains in the shared API owner; thin app route reexports and the shared database client matrix remain authoritative. Core uses Cache Components and its current runtime map prohibits route-segment `dynamic`, `runtime`, `preferredRegion` and `maxDuration` exports. Do not paste a generic force-dynamic example. Current cue responses use private/no-store HTTP handling and current authenticated request context; neither Next shared cache nor CDN/persisted TanStack cache may store names/active state. Follow Core's TanStack convention for the narrow read model rather than installing SWR because a generic skill suggests it.

Keep volatile timers, sequence/window, latest input/eligibility and in-flight desired state in the feature controller, outside React render state where they do not affect presentation. The view changes for an actual permitted actor-set or availability change. A renewed deadline can update an internal timer without rerendering the full conversation/editor. Never route-refresh per wake, move the editor between parents on a cue change, serialize extra draft content or subscribe the entire page to every activity tick.

The installed Tiptap3.22.3 `useEditor` branch does not force transaction rerenders when `shouldRerenderOnTransaction` is absent/false, despite generic older commentary. Existing parent/draft onUpdate costs still need profiling. Preserve `immediatelyRender:false`, draft serialization and qualified input adapters; do not silently replace current draft behavior or add a collaboration extension. Subscribe to actual intentional composition, including IME/paste/toolbar actions; not every transaction or keydown is user input.

### REQ26-D34-RUNTIME_CONTRACT-S0004 — Subscription, refresh and control orchestration

Applies to **US26-D34-04**, acceptance **AC26-D34-04-01–03**.

Register only a current visible eligible client reader, not SSR, prefetch or an offscreen list. Obtain its private topic, subscribe, then reconcile after subscription to close a snapshot-before-subscribe gap. An initial snapshot may run in parallel for responsiveness, but does not replace post-join reconciliation. A failed join does not prevent current HTTP snapshots.

There is one serialized control stream and one coalesced snapshot path per instance. A combined accepted control can carry its current snapshot. Periodic refresh, hints and post-join reconciliation share single-flight/backpressure; a wake during a request sets one dirty follow-up instead of creating concurrent snapshot-only reads. Snapshot-only reads do not advance the control generation. A just-completed combined response may satisfy a pending periodic read. Process a valid control ACK separately from its peer projection: a later snapshot can supersede old peer data without losing the ACK's accepted sequence/window; an ACK cannot overwrite a newer displayed projection. A pending current start/stop flushes after a known control result or read-only reconciliation, rather than waiting another5seconds.

Ordinary combined refresh is5s while locally composing **or** displaying at least one still-trusted peer, otherwise10s. Count the union once. Use bounded timer jitter only for background scheduled renewals, while maintaining the hard deadlines and declared maximum interval; do not delay leading starts/stops. Hidden/inactive instances cease composition; hidden readers stop renewals and requalify on return. Token/session/source changes fence old results. Logout clears volatile state. Strict Mode, repeated mount, hot reload and async teardown must never stop a newer generation.

Only meaningful transitions wake eligible observers; unchanged liveness renewal never fans out. Natural expiry is locally timed and reconciled, not a job/event per expiration. Wakes are hints: duplicates/out-of-order delivery coalesce into current reads. No missing hint needs a durable replay queue. A server lease transaction is authoritative for the ephemeral state; the subsequent REST wake is bounded best effort. Catch non202 rejection/timeouts;202 never proves the recipient saw a cue.

### REQ26-D34-RUNTIME_CONTRACT-S0005 — Initial bounded profile

Applies to **US26-D34-04**, acceptance **AC26-D34-04-01–03**.

These are deliberately explicit **Asym engineering limits/qualification fixtures**, not measured production capacity, vendor entitlements or ministry-usage evidence. Keep them in one versioned owner configuration, with no tenant-facing tuning UI. Changing a hard safety/UX bound requires updating the contract/proof; increasing a capacity ceiling requires measured authorization/load/quotas and operational review.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Limit                      | Initial contract and behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Ready leading dispatch     | Start/Stop request begins within150ms of actual eligible transition when no earlier control/recovery blocks it. Pending transition flush is leading after settlement.                                                                                                                                              |
| Fast/quiet periodic work   | One combined request per5s/10s respectively; no redundant composer and observer loops.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Client in-flight bounds    | One control mutation and at most one snapshot-only read; combined responses coalesce pending reads. All transport requests timeout locally after3s. Timeout cannot cancel an already admitted server effect; reconcile before another control.                                                                     |
| Cue control flood          | At most120 admitted controls per instance per rolling60s with a burst ceiling of10 within1s; ordinary5s cadence uses12/min. Excess intent coalesces; repeated abuse rejects cue controls without blocking other product endpoints.                                                                                 |
| Snapshot flood             | At most120 snapshot requests per instance per rolling60s with burst10 within1s, counting combined snapshot responses; wake storms coalesce. Shared rate limiting must be current across server instances.                                                                                                          |
| Live instances             | At most10 eligible reader instances per real tenant/profile and2,000 per tenant, plus a deployment-level ceiling tied to actual provider capacity. Unknown/expired instances do not count; visible overflow receives generic unavailable, not a roster/hidden-person count.                                        |
| Complete source projection | At most100 currently eligible observer instances/contributions for a qualified source context in one result/fanout selection. Fetch/check N+1 to detect overflow; never label a partial set/count complete. Overflow disables awareness for that qualifying context with generic unavailable; source work remains. |
| Snapshot wire size         | At most64KiB uncompressed JSON, inclusive of complete eligible names/deadlines/metadata; above bound return unavailable without partial names/counts. No message/draft/attachment content.                                                                                                                         |
| Hint coalescing            | At most one transition hint per observer per250ms; newer changes collapse to refresh-needed. Per-dispatch work bounded by100 eligible observers. Use a qualified REST envelope/batch within the actual provider limit; do not assume an undocumented batch size.                                                   |
| Hint budget                | Explicit400ms dispatch timeout after lease commit. Exhausted budget drops the hint and records its status; periodic snapshot repairs it. API latency/cue path remains independent of draft/save/send.                                                                                                              |
| Ephemeral cleanup          | Existing scheduler checks at least every5min; physical removal target within15min after observer closure/expiry. Use bounded indexed batches, never table scans or deletion of business records.                                                                                                                   |

Do not build a generic custom rate-limiting platform for this feature. Reuse the actual qualified shared limiter/admission boundary; if it cannot enforce current cross-instance budgets, this prerequisite must be qualified before activation. There is no assumption that a process-local map limits a distributed deployment. A deployment ceiling is configured below verified real quotas with headroom and enforced centrally; no tenant can consume an unbounded share. Numerical provider plan settings are operational evidence, not invented from a public pricing table.

The high fanout case is intentionally bounded. At a limit, return an honest unavailable cue rather than removing RLS, sending broad account broadcasts, fabricating totals or hard-locking normal work. The100-instance ceiling concerns underlying live contributions, not the two-name visual limit. Authorized same-profile display dedupe does not erase its multiple browser requests.

### REQ26-D34-RUNTIME_CONTRACT-S0006 — Latency and cost proof

Applies to **US26-D34-04**, acceptance **AC26-D34-04-01–03**.

Let N be live reader instances, F the union of instances locally composing or displaying a current peer cue. Ordinary combined traffic is `(N−F)/10 + F/5` requests per second. Each may require one lease update and an authorized snapshot. With N500/F300 that is80requests/s; with N1,000/F1,000 it is200requests/s. These are arithmetic examples, not measured capacity. State transitions, wake-triggered snapshots, joins, auth queries and cleanup add cost. Wakes scale with transitions×eligible observers. REST batching reduces HTTP envelopes, not necessarily delivered-message quota counts.

Healthy connected release target: p95≤1,000ms from qualifying start/explicit stop to the other eligible reader's rendered cue/removal. Instrument input, control admission, dispatch, wake receipt, snapshot completion and paint without content. Report p50/p95/p99 and loss/unknown rates, not just average websocket latency. Count transitions delayed by ordinary in-flight controls; do not cherry-pick only an idle transport. Separately report cold registration, reconnect, broker failure and constrained networks.

The minimum repeatable release fixture uses1,000 total active instances across20tenants,500 fast instances, one100-instance eligible source context and at least10,000 start/explicit-stop samples after warm-up. Include the deployment's supported representative near/far staff regions, actual Supabase primary/Vercel region/Node/runtime/SDK versions, and measured network RTT/loss. Synthetic mock clocks do not establish regional behavior. Also run one noisy tenant, simultaneous reconnect, overflow N+1, two-device staff and mixed-version cases. The one-second healthy target is assessed only for declared supported connected-network conditions; degraded-network results must meet truthful expiry/no-lost-work behavior, not a universal zero-lag promise.

Before enabling real tenants, record actual plan quotas and confirm the declared deployment ceiling at ≤70% of measured sustainable requests and provider configured message/connection/join capacity under the tested mix. “70%” is an operating headroom rule, not proof a vendor guarantees it. A failed target requires latency-path optimization or a reviewed smaller activation envelope; do not silently weaken authorization or claim the target passed.

### REQ26-D34-DATA_CONTRACT-S0002 — Facts and identity ownership

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

Current Core `getAuthContext` resolves authenticated user/profile/tenant but does not return a qualified actual auth-session ID. Current Support helper agent/email matching does not prove the publisher's real internal identity or exact original-source access. These are verified source gaps, not allegations of an exercised exploit. The identity owner must supply the real-session predicate before activation. Token refresh preserves an actually continuing session; logout/revocation or a changed real session cannot reuse its old cue instance.

Do not introduce a second staff/contact table. A requester can be unidentified, use a shared email, represent an organization or write on another person's behalf; none of those facts identifies the authenticated composing staff member. A staff profile is not its public reply signature, CRM record owner or support assignee. The same real staff identity may hold different roles across tenants. All current source/role/identity visibility checks remain explicit.

### REQ26-D34-DATA_CONTRACT-S0003 — Minimal logical data shape

Applies to **US26-D34-05**, acceptance **AC26-D34-05-01–03**.

Names here are conceptual field roles. Final column names must follow actual Core migrations/types. Current Support identifiers include text IDs; do not silently impose UUID FKs on them. No money, currency, giving total or recipient/contact copy is introduced.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact                                       | Required invariant                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Opaque instance ID and protocol version    | Server-issued primary identity, globally collision-resistant; non-null. Unknown IDs are never created by control/snapshot. Protocol version is closed and explicit.                                                              |
| Tenant, profile and real-session reference | Non-null trusted immutable scope; same-tenant member/profile relationships and current membership/session checks. The platform identity owner resolves a real session without copying credentials.                               |
| Reader/source context                      | Non-null canonical source reference plus original-affinity/topology/restriction generation. Same-tenant source integrity; immutable for the instance. Registration of a different context closes/replaces rather than retargets. |
| Observer topic                             | Opaque unique non-source-bearing server value, scoped to this instance/session; immutable private configuration. Not a secret authorization substitute.                                                                          |
| Sequence and window generation             | Non-negative bounded bigint/integer with checked overflow behavior; increment server generation atomically on accepted controls. Never wrap. Exhaustion closes/reissues. API encoding cannot lose JS integer precision.          |
| Window issued/not-after                    | Trusted timestamptz with not-after at most issued+15s. Fixed for already-issued controls.                                                                                                                                        |
| Observer expiry                            | Trusted timestamptz at most accepted observer control+30s, shortened by known session/source fences.                                                                                                                             |
| Optional composing episode                 | Either inactive with no active expiry, or current episode identity/frontier/expiry with coherent non-null active fields. No combination can claim active without a qualified input frontier.                                     |
| Fresh-input frontier                       | Last server acceptance of authenticated fresh-input intent, not receipt of an ordinary renewal/read. No actual content or keystroke timestamp is recorded.                                                                       |
| Closed/cleanup state                       | A closed instance is terminal. Deadline expiry makes it unusable immediately, even before physical deletion. Cleanup no later than15min after closure/observer expiry under O06.                                                 |

Use regular logged application rows. Do not add an append-only activity history, custom managed-realtime objects or raw-row subscription publication. Index tenant/context plus observer expiry and cleanup expiry to support bounded active selection; use the actual source owner predicates/indexes. Avoid a fresh index per UI condition. Unique instance/topic and same-tenant relationships are database constraints, not only conventions.

Deadline arithmetic/state-combination CHECK constraints can compare stored columns; do not pretend a CHECK using current time expires a row automatically. Active selection and commands compare current authoritative server time. Freeze trusted attribution, source and topic after insert. An allowed UPDATE must not transform a row into another tenant/profile/source or extend a deadline without a fresh qualified command.

Deletion of ephemeral technical rows has no cascading business effect. Source/member deletion must invalidate/remove or safely orphan-ineligible these rows according to the actual owning domain contract; prefer same-tenant FK restriction and ordered technical cleanup where physical deletion exists. No cascade from a lease to conversation, profile, CRM record, message, audit or file is permitted. Archived/restricted/merged sources lose eligibility by current policy even if the FK still exists. Cleanup failure can leave only expired unreadable technical state, never live authority.

### REQ26-D34-DATA_CONTRACT-S0004 — Closed commands and SQL security

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

The browser submits an issued instance, expected sequence/window and a closed intent (`observe`, `input`, `renew`, `stop`, `close`); exact transport names are design detail. It does not submit trusted actor/tenant/source changes, names, roles, deadlines, arbitrary JSON state or session attribution. Initial registration accepts a source locator as an untrusted requested target, then resolves current owner authority before binding it. Caller-controlled source IDs are never authority by themselves.

Use the qualified the shared API owner boundary plus database adapter/transaction; app route files remain thin. In one transaction, authenticate actual identity/session, qualify current source and command permission, compare instance/sequence/window/state, update deadlines and return accepted current control state. Coordinate with source-owner revisions/locks so a racing source mutation cannot admit a control under a source state that was already invalidated at the command's linearization point. Do not assume a frontend permission badge does this.

Clients have no direct SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants for lease rows and no raw-row Realtime publication. Inspect actual exposed schema grants, policies, views/RPCs, function execute grants and search paths. Prefer invoker semantics where appropriate; a necessary privileged/definer path needs explicit trusted current authorization and bounded operations. Service-role bypass is not caller authorization. Test both old-row admission and new-row validity. PostgreSQL may reuse USING when WITH CHECK is omitted; missing explicit syntax alone is not proof of a vulnerability. No Storage policy is added because D34 stores no files or attachments.

`realtime.messages` policies only authorize the correct authenticated real session's issued active private observer topic and allowed receive extension. Browser Broadcast/Presence publishing and unrelated topic joins are denied. Cached join policy cannot replace the application fanout/snapshot check. A privileged REST publisher uses a qualified server-only credential path that never reaches the client, source or logs.

### REQ26-D34-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — Ordered control protocol

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

1. A visible qualified reader registers: new opaque instance/topic, sequence0, generation0, fixed window expiring15s later, observer deadline30s later, inactive composing state. Registration is not composition and is not performed by SSR/prefetch.
2. The client sends one control at a time with the issued generation, a strictly advancing sequence and current intent. Intervening input is a coalesced dirty flag, not an event queue. A ready first input/stop dispatches in the leading edge; a pending transition flushes after the in-flight control settles, not after another timer interval.
3. The server requires current time strictly before both the window and observer expiry, exact current generation, sequence greater than last accepted, current real session/source rights and supported protocol. Duplicate/lower sequence is a no-effect rejection, not a renewal. Accept atomically updates last sequence, rotates generation and issues its new15s window. Snapshot-only/read-reconciliation does not rotate it.
4. `input` means new human intent since the last accepted/known report. It may start a new composition episode or extend an existing one. It updates the fresh-input frontier to server acceptance time. `renew` extends only a still-active episode's liveness and cannot restart an inactive/expired/stopped episode or change its input frontier. `observe` renews observer interest only. Every accepted eligible control can return the fresh authorized peer snapshot, avoiding redundant refresh.
5. `stop` ends only this instance's current episode; the observer may remain live. A later actual input in a valid window may start a new episode. `close` ends the entire instance. A lower older Start/Renew/Stop cannot affect the newer sequence/episode. Any unknown, closed, expired-window or expired-observer update is rejected; it never upserts.
6. On ambiguous ACK, freeze writes and reconcile through a fresh authorized read of that exact instance. It returns last accepted sequence/generation/window/state but extends nothing. If its current window and episode remain live, a fresh eligible renewal may continue within the unchanged input deadline. Do not replay an old input or claim it became fresh by reading. If the window/instance is dead, close where possible and register a new inactive instance. New human input after recovery is required to announce again.
7. Stop/close remains best effort at page exit. Server expiry removes stale claims even when the browser never sends another packet. Logout/current-source denial never causes re-registration until legitimate current authority exists.

One generation plus one last sequence is enough. No permanent receipt journal, message queue, cryptographic-token service or per-keystroke events are required. A control received close to its not-after time may represent older self-reported activity; the fixed window bounds this but cannot prove what a human was actually doing. An authorized malicious client can claim its own composition. It cannot claim another identity or gain/deny business authority.

### REQ26-D34-DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — Exact timing and snapshot interpretation

Applies to **US26-D34-02**, acceptance **AC26-D34-02-01–03**.

All server duration arithmetic uses trusted elapsed-time semantics and timezone-independent stored instants. Do not use business-hours/D14 calendars. The accepted profile:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Parameter              | Exact meaning                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Leading dispatch       | Begin a ready start/stop request within150ms of qualifying local transition; this is an implementation target, not the remote visibility claim or a guarantee during an in-flight request/recovery. |
| 5s fast loop           | One combined control/snapshot loop while local composition or a current displayed peer cue exists. Ordinary keepalives, not an extra loop per purpose.                                              |
| 10s quiet loop         | One combined observer/snapshot loop otherwise, only while eligible. Transition/wake reads may occur sooner.                                                                                         |
| 15s control window     | Fixed not-after for each issued generation; later changes do not retroactively freshen an old report. At equality it is expired.                                                                    |
| 15s composing liveness | Upper bound after accepted eligible input/renewal, shortened below.                                                                                                                                 |
| 30s local idle         | Stop after30 elapsed seconds since last qualifying local input; focus/renew/autosave do not reset. Server also enforces its independent input frontier.                                             |
| 30s observer lease     | Upper bound after accepted observer-control activity; read-only reconciliation cannot extend.                                                                                                       |
| 12s snapshot trust     | Maximum local age measured from request start; a response does not get12 fresh seconds upon arrival.                                                                                                |

For an active episode:

`composingUntil = min(serverNow + 15s, lastAcceptedFreshInput + 30s, observerUntil, applicable session/source deadline)`.

Without fresh input, ordinary renewals cannot move the30s frontier. Publisher liveness can disappear earlier than the30s idle grace under network loss. The ideal connected grace is30s; it is not a claim that a lost client's actual last keystroke is known to server precision. A late fresh-input report can add up to the15s control-window age before the server frontier; this is bounded self-report uncertainty, not literal live typing. Under compliant client behavior Stop is leading edge; the worst case remains expiry. A stale valid report never becomes unbounded because of repeated keepalives.

Snapshot returns trusted `asOf`, absolute per-contribution expiry and context/generation. At client request start `m0`, derive `mappedExpiry = m0 + max(0, expiry - asOf)`. This subtracts the entire request transit/processing time conservatively rather than trusting browser wall-clock synchronization. Display a peer only before `min(mappedExpiry, m0+12s)` and only in the matching current context. If a response arrives beyond that bound, discard it. Same-profile aggregation uses the latest still-qualified contribution expiry; it cannot inherit an inaccessible contribution's lifetime.

The snapshot itself becomes unknown after `m0+12s`, including an empty result. Expiring the last peer locally does not prove a fresh empty set; schedule a current read and use unavailable if trust is lost. Response order is fenced by request/context generation. **Control acknowledgements and peer projections have separate gates:** a newer snapshot request may supersede an older combined response's peer projection without discarding its valid accepted control sequence/window. Conversely a valid control ACK cannot overwrite a newer peer projection. Both remain bound to the same current instance/context. Browser clocks may not progress consistently through sleep on every platform: clear on visibility/pageshow/focus/reconnect before reuse and refresh. Never persist these clocks/names in local storage, SSR globals or query dehydration.

### REQ26-D34-DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — Source changes, fanout and the unavoidable network boundary

Applies to **US26-D34-03**, acceptance **AC26-D34-03-01–03**.

The server snapshots and dispatch admission evaluate current producer/observer real session, original source, membership, identity display and relevant topology. Keep candidate selection and authorization bounded, complete and indexed. A CRM reader limited to one original may see only composition actually qualified on that source; a shared continuing component is not a room-wide authorization key. A target change needs fresh binding, preserving the private draft under its owner.

A valid current fanout decision followed by a later revocation may leave a content-free hint in flight. That is not a claim of perfectly atomic database-plus-network revocation. No new dispatch is admitted on an already revoked basis; the hint provides no authority and its snapshot rechecks. Already delivered names may remain until a known invalidation/fresh read or their conservative12s trust expires. This finite disclosure-after-prior-authorized-read is explicit; instantaneous erasure from a disconnected screen is impossible. Never keep names visible indefinitely in an offline cache.

Same-profile tabs/devices use separate issued instances. Aggregate after filtering; hide the viewer's own profile. In a controlled context change, clear old local cues immediately and asynchronously close the old instance. A stopped/expired row cannot be repurposed by source merge, unlink, Undo or physical cleanup. Registration/snapshot denies inaccessible links without saying whether another hidden source/person exists.

## Own-note corrections and history

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — The ordinary experience

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

Maya notices that her posted internal note says Tuesday when she meant Thursday. She opens that note's actions, chooses **Edit note**, fixes the word and selects **Save changes**. The note stays exactly where it was, with its original author/time and a quiet **Edited** link. There is no additional confirmation, required explanation, timer or notification to the donor. This illustrative correction is distinct from a donor later changing their plans, which belongs in a new note.

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Maya Chen   Internal note                  Original posting time   ⋯
> 
> The donor requested a callback Thursday.
> 
> Edited · [View history]

While editing, keep the same header and location:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Maya Chen   Editing internal note          Original posting time
> 
> [Existing compact formatting controls]
> [Editable note text                                      ]
> 
> Existing files                 (only when files exist)
> [Current permitted file name]   [Open / Preview]
> 
> Earlier versions remain in history while available.
> [Save changes] [Cancel]

Use the existing Base UI/base-maia components, Maia/Zinc semantic tokens, Internal note editor and safe static renderer. Keep readable body typography, clear hierarchy, modest borders and stable spacing. Existing shell tokens—not the current component's hardcoded amber styling—control the appearance. Do not add an elaborate toolbar, large history cards, extra navigation rail, animation around every save or a second design system.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Enter, correct and save

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

1. **Find the action.** The note has an accessible actions menu on pointer, keyboard and touch. Eligible authors see **Edit note**; other readers may see **View history** when available. Neither author matching nor authority is inferred from the visible name. Do not advertise a disabled Edit action to everyone merely to explain permission architecture.
2. **Start editing in place.** Keep the Internal note identity explicit. Load and validate the current permitted canonical body before writable initialization. Focus the editor predictably; avoid selecting/replacing the entire note automatically. The separate Reply/Note draft and its selected recipients remain untouched.
3. **Make an ordinary correction.** Text, supported formatting and ordinary links work as expected. Paste and keyboard editing follow the qualified note profile. Normal paragraph/select-all deletion may remove existing mention tokens or inline pictures, without adding new mention targets or sending anything. No hidden protected-token rule should make a normal correction fail only at Save.
4. **Keep files understandable.** The original source's currently permitted files stay in a read-only **Existing files** section. There are no Add, Remove or Replace file controls in this correction flow. When relevant, explain: **Removing an image from the text does not remove the file from this note or its history.** Existing preview opens through D32 and restores the draft/position on return. Use a fresh ordinary note for new supporting files or notifying a teammate.
5. **Save deliberately.** **Save changes** shows an in-place saving state. Disable repeat submission while its outcome is unresolved. Confirm only the authoritative result. On success, restore the readable note, update Edited/history and return focus without moving the timeline. A brief polite status can announce **Changes saved**; it is not the only evidence of success.
6. **Handle no change quietly.** Save can be disabled when the client knows nothing changed, but the server still checks canonical equality. A true no-op creates no revision, Edited time, notification or activity. Cancel simply exits an unchanged edit.

This is a correction editor, not a new message composer. It has no Reply/Note audience switch, sender field, signature insertion, new notifying-mention picker, file upload or Save-and-send option. Plain @name text remains ordinary text. The client must not reuse the current creation composer's insertion-time activity callback.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Cancel and leave without surprises

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

**Cancel** before submission discards only this private edit and restores the current permitted note. A dirty navigation or move to another note uses one small **Keep editing / Discard changes** guard; this is appropriate for leaving, not an extra step on every Save. Escape dismisses the innermost menu/history overlay and returns focus; it must not silently erase a dirty editor.

There is one active posted-note editor in a reader. A second request to edit first resolves the existing local candidate. No persistent multi-note draft manager or server autosave is created. Ordinary list refresh does not replace the candidate. Browser/OS tab eviction cannot be promised recoverable.

After Save has been submitted, Cancel cannot claim to undo it. A person may close the view, but returning reconciles that original operation. A lost response shows **Checking whether your changes were saved**, not **Save failed** or a fresh-send invitation. The data contract gives the exact unknown/retry path.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Read history without a document-management interface

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

Select **Edited** or **View history** to open one read-only shared disclosure. Its title identifies **Note history** and the original note/author where currently permitted. Show the selected version's complete safe body; mark **Current** and **Original** when their facts are available. Earlier versions have their own edit time/attribution. Keep the original posting time distinct from later edits.

Show up to20 permitted metadata entries at a time and load one body on selection. More history uses ordinary **Load more** with a stable cursor; no giant body list or eager total count. New edits do not reshuffle what the user is reading: explain that a newer version is available and let them refresh deliberately. Return to the note at the same position.

History does not offer Restore, comparison markup, export, branch, revision comments, mention replay or attachment re-acquisition. It uses the safe static renderer, not an editor mounted for every version. A person can read permitted earlier text; a new correction must still start from the current note and current authority. Do not promise that Original or every earlier body is retained forever.

If an earlier representation is expired/restricted, show an appropriate body-free state only when the user may know that history fact. Never expose hidden version counts, timestamps, filenames or actors through gaps. Current text redaction cannot safely locate the same sensitive words in all old versions; affected older bodies remain restricted unless the source owner qualifies a safe representation. History is not a **View original** escape from privacy controls.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Conflict: keep the person's work and require deliberate review

Applies to **US26-D35-04**, acceptance **AC26-D35-04-01–03**.

Two sessions belonging to Maya may edit the same note. If another save wins first, the second cannot overwrite it silently. Display **This note changed** with two clear labels: **Currently saved note** and **Your unsaved changes**. Only show currently permitted content.

The author reviews the current note and deliberately starts a correction from that current base, reapplying the intended change. Their old local text can remain available for this review while permitted. There is no **Overwrite anyway**, automatic rebase, automatic merge or generic diff platform. The server still checks the new base when saving. Repeating the old request cannot create another revision.

If the conflict is actually redaction, expiry, lost permission, tenant/account switch or an incompatible original-source change, withhold/clear forbidden content. Do not preserve an unsafe candidate merely because an ordinary concurrency error would preserve it. Explain the resulting state plainly—**This note is no longer available to edit**—without revealing a hidden source or actor.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Support and CRM continuity

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

The same note can be reached from Support or through the CRM's canonical Support reader. Edit and history apply the same current Support source permissions in both places. The successful current version is shared because it is one source, not because two copies synchronize.

Keep the CRM record/list, Support reader selection and return route. If a Party/relationship is merged, unlinked or becomes restricted, requalify the note's actual original source. Viewing a merged conversation or a CRM record does not grant every constituent's history. Authoring a note about a refund/contact update does not perform the action; its owning domain still authorizes and records it.

D22 ordinary search/Find follows the current permitted version. It must not return a removed phrase from an older revision as if it were current, nor silently add all revision bodies to its corpus. D33 Compact/Full preferences do not edit or restore content.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Awareness and attention remain separate

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

An explicitly qualified use of D34 may show the existing neutral composing cue during deliberate note editing. It uses the edited note's actual original source and real edit authority, even within a merged reader. No history-viewing cue, note/reply-mode disclosure, draft text, cursor or lock is added. Moving back to Reply stops/rebinds that context while preserving the other private draft. D34 failure does not block Edit or Save.

Routine edits do not send a new follower alert, @mention or donor email. If a correction needs someone's attention, use the existing deliberate staff-attention/new-note path. Already delivered messages cannot be recalled. P17/P6 retain immutable preparation/delivery evidence and their current adverse source fences; exact changes may suppress unsafe outstanding source-dependent material without falsely erasing valid historical delivery facts.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — Legacy and maintenance

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

An old note may lack provable human authorship or a losslessly editable canonical body. Explain **Editing isn't available for this older note** where the note itself is visible, and preserve ordinary new-note clarification and authorized privacy controls. Do not invent a historical author from today's matching email or label generated activity as human because it shares the note endpoint.

Activation qualifies the actual author/source model, parser/editor cohort, history/custody and all writers first. Maintainers use existing owner migration/repair tools; users are not asked to understand SQL, profiles or deployment versions. A history retrieval outage does not erase the note. An unknown Save result is reconciled from its original operation, not repaired by manually recreating the note.

### REQ26-D35-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0010 — Accessibility, mobile and proof of quality

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Use accessible names and selected/expanded/busy states from shared primitives; no hover-only timestamp or color-only Edited badge. Keep DOM and visual order coherent. Preserve the existing shell's focus management and reduced-motion behavior. Opening/closing history, saving, errors and inner menus each have deliberate focus return; do not announce every typing/render change.

Test actual editing, validation, conflict, unknown outcome, history and return at200% text resizing and320CSS-pixel reflow/400% zoom, including long translated labels/names and RTL. Test keyboard/screen readers, contrast, author-created sticky focus obstruction,24CSS-pixel targets or actual WCAG exceptions and44CSS-pixel standalone-primary touch targets. A mobile virtual keyboard must leave text and reachable Save/Cancel usable; history should use the existing responsive full-width disclosure rather than nested desktop overlays.

The primary UX research documents actual helpdesk alternatives and their limitations. The proof ledger requires moderated author/reader/CRM/maintenance journeys and actual browser/AT outcomes. No number of polished drawings, source hashes or synthetic model assertions proves that users enjoy the result. Those observable task outcomes remain release requirements.

### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002 — Forty falsifiable release groups

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Use real qualified source, database, actor/session and browser paths in authorized nonproduction fixtures. Verify user-visible and domain outcomes, including the negative paths. Do not replace these with tests that merely repeat an implementation helper.

The20-row page bound and200-revision fixture are different units. The20 competing attempts do not authorize20 successful saves from one base.
