### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O01 — Six operating controls

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** **One** cross-tenant/other-author/hidden-version disclosure or unauthorized edit; one known redacted/expired representation served after its current source fence.

**Owner:** Core security and exact Support/source privacy owner

**Response:** Disable affected edit/history path, preserve minimal evidence, apply current source containment, correct the writer/read/cache/restore boundary and re-run negative proof before reactivation. Never export the exposed body into diagnostics.

### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O02 — Six operating controls

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** **One** forked current head, duplicate accepted operation effect, no-op creating a revision, Saved without durable required source/result obligations, or operation-key reuse after pruning.

**Owner:** Support API/data owner

**Response:** Fence affected mutation path, reconcile the original operation/head using trusted control facts, repair the atomic/identity boundary and prove the triggering race. Do not fabricate another note or silently delete a valid revision.

### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O03 — Six operating controls

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** **One** routine edit causing a new note/alert/donor send, author/source/audience change, financial/CRM fact mutation, or native human/retention clock renewal.

**Owner:** Support source owner with P17/P6 or affected domain owner

**Response:** Stop that producer/callback, reconcile actual in-flight effects without claiming recall, restore correct owner mapping and prove both negative edit and positive independently authorized new-note paths.

### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O04 — Six operating controls

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Required edit invalidation/safety-continuation oldest unresolved age **over60seconds for5minutes**. Current read/safety gates must already withhold stale forbidden results.

**Owner:** Support projection/search owner and Core operations

**Response:** Inspect identifier-only failed work, retry/reconcile the original source effect, diagnose blocked dependency/capacity, expose truthful currentness and repair without replaying Save. Unsafe disclosure escalates immediately to O01 regardless of age.

### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O05 — Six operating controls

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Save or selected-history-body p95 **over2seconds for15minutes with at least100 observations**, or unexpected operation errors **over1% for15minutes with at least100 attempts**, excluding expected validation/authorization/conflict/backpressure outcomes from that error numerator.

**Owner:** Support API/UI performance owner and Core operations

**Response:** Check exact source/query/profile/network conditions, repair plans/worker/consumer regressions and apply fair backpressure. Keep unknown results truthful; never reduce authorization/history retention to hit a metric. Report excluded backpressure separately.

### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O06 — Six operating controls

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** **One** saved silent node/attribute loss, renderer-empty-as-success, new/retargeted prohibited reference or unintended actual file-membership change.

**Owner:** Shared editor/Support source owner

**Response:** Disable affected profile/writer, preserve the lawful original source for repair, correct validation/adapter/cohort and prove faithful supported deletion versus accidental loss. No lossy auto-migration or hidden restoration.

### REQ26-D35-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003 — Six operating controls

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

These controls handle residual operation after mandatory proof. Severity failures are not accepted as a way to avoid fixing the design. Owners are accountable Core role owners; tenant staff do not need access to private operations payloads or SQL.

All six signals use minimized identifiers/outcome classes, not note text, private references or per-person productivity reports. Historical operation identity/material and metrics retention remain governed by their own finite purposes. These accepted timing thresholds are explicit operational choices, not claimed measured current performance.

### REQ26-D35-EDITOR_EMAIL_STUDIO_CONTRACT-S0002 — Ownership and event meanings

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Operation or fact                                            | Owner and outcome                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Original human note and its revisions                        | Support owns source identity, human origin, author/publication provenance, current head and correction history. Ordinary correction has its own minimal edit event, not another note publication.                                                                    |
| Canonical content schema and purpose validation              | Existing D23/P17-qualified Internal note vocabulary/compiler, consumed through its source-owner command. Original JSON validation precedes editor parsing. A schema/profile reference does not make P17 the owner of the note or its revisions.                      |
| Local editor UI                                              | Existing shared Tiptap/Internal note profile and Base UI/base-maia components. Private candidate; no creation callback, autosave or note/message publication on mount/input/Cancel.                                                                                  |
| Sender/signature/Reply and system-message authoring          | Existing D23/P17 Email Studio owners, unaffected by a routine internal-note correction. No signature insertion, sender/recipient change or new outbound content preparation.                                                                                         |
| Optional following and separately qualified direct attention | D15 owns optional following; direct-mention/required attention retain their existing qualified producer/source/audience contracts. Routine edits create neither; a separately published new note or deliberate authorized attention retains its normal consequences. |
| Prepared/delivered communication                             | P17 owns immutable preparation; P6 owns submission, retries, provider outcomes and reconciliation. A note edit cannot rewrite delivered bytes or delivery evidence.                                                                                                  |
| Privacy and expiry                                           | D16/D17 source owners govern current/history material, derivatives, candidates and source-dependent prepared copies. These fences remain stronger than ordinary editing/history.                                                                                     |
| Existing files                                               | D32/source occurrence owners authorize preview/download and safety state. D35 does not acquire/remove/replace a file; an inline appearance is not its custody record.                                                                                                |
| Current search/read preferences                              | D22 uses current permitted head; D33 stays a reading preference. History does not become an additional general search/AI corpus.                                                                                                                                     |
| Composing awareness                                          | Explicitly qualified reuse of D34's existing neutral controller with the edited note's actual source and author-edit authority. Advisory, content-free and independent of Save correctness.                                                                          |
| CRM                                                          | Same canonical current-authorized Support source and return context. CRM identities/relationships and financial/care mutations retain their owners.                                                                                                                  |

### REQ26-D35-EDITOR_EMAIL_STUDIO_CONTRACT-S0003 — Canonical profile and installed-source truth

Applies to **US26-D35-03**, acceptance **AC26-D35-03-01–03**.

D23 already requires purpose-specific code-owned profiles, exact original JSON validation, deterministic safe derivation and qualified editor/render dependency cohorts. D35 reuses that requirement for **correction of an existing Internal note**, with an edit-time allowed-reference inventory from its loaded current base. This is a bounded command/profile context, not a second canonical schema or reusable workflow engine.

Current inspection finds core/react/static-renderer3.22.3 alongside mention/suggestion/html and some extensions3.23.1. Public npm reports core/react3.31.3 as stable on14September2026. These are evidence-date facts, not versions installed by this work or a permanent upgrade instruction. D23's compatible cohort/parser/render qualification remains a prerequisite; do not claim the mixed current consumer is proven safe because packages are present.

Tiptap's documented Pro snapshot history belongs to its collaboration/Document Server system and brings private-registry/Yjs/server dependencies. It is unnecessary for a source-owned note revision and static history reader. Reuse the ordinary editor and store revisions under Support; do not add Pro history, tracked changes, document restore, co-editing or an external snapshot service. Tiptap snapshots, content checking, React performance, Next.js integration.

### REQ26-D35-EDITOR_EMAIL_STUDIO_CONTRACT-S0004 — Editing without reference or notification surprises

Applies to **US26-D35-03**, acceptance **AC26-D35-03-01–03**.

Allow prose, supported formatting and ordinary safe links. Existing mention or inline-image appearances may be deliberately moved/deleted, including normal paragraph deletion and local undo. The server validates a subset of permitted base references and unchanged retained target/source/purpose attributes. This prevents new notifying targets, foreign assets and retargeting without freezing paragraphs or rejecting normal editing through a hidden immutable-node rule.

The actual file list/occurrences/bytes remain unchanged and visible under **Existing files**, with D16/D32 checks on every access. Removing an image from text is not removal from the note/history. No new upload, file replacement/removal or notifying mention picker is presented in this edit. New supporting material or deliberate attention uses an ordinary new note; actual sensitive removal uses D16. Editing does not copy attachments into a new occurrence or renew their deadline.

Do not reuse the current creation composer's mention-insertion callback: it calls `logSupportActivity`, whose generated sentence is posted through the ordinary note endpoint. That path must be absent from mount, candidate parsing, input, paste, undo, reference deletion, history, Save and Cancel. Programmatic initialization and literal @name text create no publication/attention. Unknown saved semantic nodes cannot disappear merely because a permissive parser accepts the result.

### REQ26-D35-EDITOR_EMAIL_STUDIO_CONTRACT-S0005 — Quiet edits and source-dependent notification safety

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Routine edit success creates no new D15 follower notice, notifying mention, donor email, P17 preparation or P6 send/retry. Editing is not republishing; it neither calls addPrivateNote nor increments native-human publication/message/unread/response/retention clocks.

Source-dependent previews, attention entries and pending communication must still follow current D15/D16/D17 fences. Separate these cases:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Case                                                                               | Required outcome                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ordinary currently valid source preview                                            | Show only its current permitted representation through the owner. A stale excerpt is not a second source of truth.                                                                                   |
| Prepared but not safely submit-authorized source-dependent content becomes invalid | Stop or correct it through the existing owner safety-continuation/material contract before further render/decrypt/send. No ad hoc rewrite of immutable prepared content or silent replacement email. |
| Provider submission may already have occurred                                      | Reconcile actual in-flight results and preserve factual evidence. Do not claim recall or repeat a provider call because the note was edited.                                                         |
| Delivered notification                                                             | Its bytes/facts remain historical under their custody contract; editing cannot unsend it. Current links still reauthorize and must not reveal old forbidden payload.                                 |
| Valid body-free historical event                                                   | May remain while its facts and purpose are permitted. Do not erase or falsify every previous notice merely because the body changed.                                                                 |
| New ordinary note or separate deliberate staff attention                           | Has its own actual current-source/admission/audience rules and normal P17/P6 consequences. It is not falsely claimed to have no possible notification effect.                                        |

New or removed mention appearances do not change Follow membership or grant conversation access. The contrast in vendor behavior is material: Front documents access consequences for a mention into some individual-inbox conversations, while Freshdesk's current restricted-ticket behavior preserves access restrictions. Core's existing current audience/source intersection governs, regardless of a token or link in text. Front comments, Freshdesk ticket actions.

D29's web acknowledgement source/profile, P23 Confirmation toggle,15-minute utility/24-hour courtesy and first-form-reply contract are unchanged. Note editing neither triggers nor configures it. Likewise a saved note correction does not mutate governed outgoing signature/wording, recipients, receipts, giving actions or public guidance.

### REQ26-D35-EDITOR_EMAIL_STUDIO_CONTRACT-S0006 — History, redaction and source truth

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

Store ordinary editorial revisions as Support-owned content, with minimal ordered edit metadata distinct from purgeable JSON/HTML/text. **View history** is read-only and reauthorizes the exact source and representation. It has no Restore, historical mention replay, file acquisition, external export, automatic summary or AI authority. Ordinary current search uses the current head; older permitted versions remain reachable only through explicit history.

Redacting a span in today's note cannot establish where its meaning exists in earlier versions. When the source owner cannot qualify a safe earlier representation, restrict that affected older body and known derivatives as a whole, retaining only permitted body-free evidence. No fuzzy matching or new semantic redaction service is needed. D16's qualified safe representation/removal is distinct from an ordinary author revision. D17 deadlines remain anchored to the original content generation; neither edit/history nor new preparation renews them.

Metadata can also be sensitive. Do not expose hidden authors, files, timestamps, counts or gaps from inaccessible revisions or merged constituents. Source removal/unlink/merge/Undo and restored backups preserve current restrictions. A source-dependent receipt or history link is not authority to retrieve a disposed body.

### REQ26-D35-EDITOR_EMAIL_STUDIO_CONTRACT-S0007 — D34 reuse and UI isolation

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

A posted-note edit is deliberate note composition, but the existing D34 producer must explicitly qualify this context. Bind the real principal/session, original note/source and edit authority. An A-source note inside a merged reader cannot reuse a Reply instance targeting B. The neutral cue does not reveal note mode, note ID, candidate text, recipients, assets or selected historical version. Reading history, focus and hydration do not start it.

Retain D34's existing timers, snapshot/currentness rules and stop-on-save/cancel/source/session loss behavior. One qualified controller context follows the active editing activity; switching to Reply/Note preserves separate private drafts and stops/rebinds correctly. There is no second schema, service or presence history. A missing cue is never an edit lock, permission grant or guarantee that another device will not save; the conditional source-head save is always required. D34 outage does not block editing.

### REQ26-D35-EDITOR_EMAIL_STUDIO_CONTRACT-S0008 — Required qualification

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Before activation, prove the exact Internal note profile/cohort and strict parser/static-render behavior; absence of insertion-time side effects; actual original human/author provenance; current and earlier version privacy; edited-source safety continuation before/after possible mail submission; canonical CRM/D22 access; D34 original-source binding; and all keyboard/mobile/history/conflict/unknown-save states. The proof ledger enumerates these outcomes.

The independent editor/owner report includes exact current source/reference pins and the resolved natural-removal tradeoff. No upgrade, provider message, live channel, editor implementation, rendered UI, browser/AT test or production conformance is claimed by this document.

### REQ26-D35-DATA_CONTRACT-S0002 — Minimum model and ownership

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Use the existing Support source owner. Logical names below describe invariants, not a new generic schema, table-name mandate or event-sourcing platform.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact                     | Authority and constraints                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Note identity            | Existing tenant plus stable original Support note/message and original conversation/source IDs. Actual note/conversation IDs are TEXT; use actual owner types rather than a UUID conversion.                                                              |
| Native human publication | Positive trusted source kind, original authenticated principal and original publication evidence. Current type=note, display JSON, email, importer or agent ID is insufficient.                                                                           |
| Current head             | Exactly one currently available editorial revision of that same tenant/note. Source restriction, topology and retention facts stay with their existing owners. An expired or unknown source is never upserted into a new note.                            |
| Revision metadata        | Stable identity/order, exact predecessor/base, trusted editor/time, canonical profile version and minimal operation provenance. Ordinary edits append; they do not revise original authorship/time or reuse a previous head ID.                           |
| Revision material        | One qualified canonical structured body and derived safe HTML/text. Source-bound reference appearances are content; file membership/bytes retain their independent occurrence owner. Material can be restricted, safely represented or purged by D16/D17. |
| Save operation/result    | One semantic business operation scoped to trusted actor/tenant/note/base/fences and desired canonical content. Minimal body-free outcome/resulting-revision evidence; no second saved candidate body in a receipt or audit.                               |
| Derived views            | Current timeline/CRM/search/compatibility body and history pages reference authoritative head/source state. They cannot write a second truth, retain extra copies beyond purpose or grant access.                                                         |

Use same-tenant/note foreign keys, unique revision sequence/identity and unique operation occurrence, valid available/restricted/disposed state combinations, immutable original provenance and deliberate delete behavior. The current pointer must resolve within its note. A migration actor cannot become the original author. Preserve required source restrictions and replay control when removing content; do not cascade through independent CRM/financial identities or retain body JSON in an undeletable audit table.

A compatible old current-body column may remain during mixed deployment only as a derived projection. Neither generic collection mutation nor a service job may overwrite canonical material/head/provenance. Business database logic remains in the shared API owner; approved collection/adapter boundaries stay in the approved authorized read-projection boundary. Thin routes do not become another database or authorization boundary.

### REQ26-D35-DATA_CONTRACT-S0003 — Admission and replay, in order

Applies to **US26-D35-04**, acceptance **AC26-D35-04-01–03**.

1. **Qualify the edit read.** Resolve the actual principal and tenant from trusted context; prove current original-source read/edit permission, native-human origin and original author equality. Fetch one current canonical version and its head/source/privacy/topology fences. Opening changes no data and creates no edit event.
2. **Prepare locally.** Validate before writable initialization; keep a private candidate separate from Reply/Note drafts. Submit one absolute desired canonical document, exact note/base/fences and operation identity. Server derivation controls actor/source and generated representations.
3. **Check an existing operation under current rights.** If its immutable semantic meaning matches, return its prior minimal outcome without another mutation. Do this before treating its old expected head as a new stale save. Changed meaning conflicts. Separately retrieve whatever current head remains permitted; a past Saved result must never overwrite a later revision or privacy change in the UI.
4. **Serialize a new operation.** Coordinate the original source, note/current head, operation and relevant privacy/retention/topology controls under the existing owner's transaction/lock discipline. Acquire locks in a consistent order and refresh trusted eligibility time after waiting. At `now >= applicable deadline`, content is unavailable even if the disposal worker has not run. No transaction waits for a human or provider I/O; no blanket global serializable mode or edit lock is needed.
5. **Recheck exact base and authority.** Current author/source eligibility, expected head and source-control fences must all agree. A stale base is a conflict even if text happens to equal current content after an A→B→A sequence. Lost rights/restriction is not an ordinary content conflict and does not disclose current forbidden bodies.
6. **Validate the complete candidate.** Enforce the exact qualified Internal note schema/profile, original-source references and canonical budgets before normalization/compilation. Compute equality under that qualified canonical contract, not a lossy parser or raw body-string shortcut.
7. **No-op or atomic correction.** A current-base equivalent candidate records a minimal immutable no-change operation binding/result and creates no new revision/Edited event/counters. A genuine change appends one revision, advances the one head, records minimal edit/result history and required identifier-only source invalidation/safety-continuation obligations atomically, or none. Existing source/send-review fences advance where their actual owner requires it; this is not a new human publication, last-contact or retention event.
8. **Return and reconcile.** Known rejection preserves only still-permitted local text. Success returns the authoritative current representation separately from the immutable operation outcome. Lost response enters Checking and read-only lookup of the original operation; no blind new operation, body reapplication or fake Cancel. Deadlock/serialization/retry treatment retains the same business identity and correct requalification.

Current rights also govern replay/outcome lookup. If minimal result facts remain independently permitted after payload disposal, they can be returned without a body; otherwise return a generic unavailable/denied state without leaking source existence. A lookup never renews a receipt, content, session lease or retention clock. Every admitted Save, including No changes, binds its operation identity. Retain that minimal binding or an equivalent durable rejection fence until the note is irreversibly non-editable and restore/replay cannot re-enable its identity. Response caches and content material may be pruned independently, but their expiry never releases an operation key; this retains no extra body/diff and creates no unlimited history exemption. Candidate digests, tokens and content-derived fingerprints remain protected/minimized and cannot become a permanent low-entropy privacy oracle.

### REQ26-D35-DATA_CONTRACT-S0004 — Valid and invalid transitions

Applies to **US26-D35-04**, acceptance **AC26-D35-04-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Transition                                             | Rule                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Readable current note → private Editing                | Current human-author/edit/source proof and qualified canonical source; no mutation.                         |
| Editing → Cancelled                                    | Before submission, discard only the local edit and return to current permitted reading. No revision.        |
| Editing → Saved next revision                          | Exact current base/fences, valid changed candidate, one atomic operation.                                   |
| Editing → No changes                                   | Exact current base and equivalent canonical content; no new revision.                                       |
| Editing → Conflict                                     | Base/source/topology changed; no overwrite or automatic rebase. Deliberate new review is required.          |
| Submitted → Checking                                   | Outcome unknown. Read-only original-result recovery; closing is not cancellation of a committed effect.     |
| Any state → Restricted/unavailable                     | Current privacy/permission/expiry dominates; clear forbidden local/rendered bodies and deny further writes. |
| Saved revision → ordinary mutated old body             | Forbidden. Corrections create a new head; privacy-safe representation/disposal is a separate owner action.  |
| Past revision → Restore or automatic new head          | Not offered. A new correction starts from the current base under current authority.                         |
| Note → new email/public audience/new author/new source | Forbidden through Edit.                                                                                     |
| History read → new alert/activity/AI index             | Forbidden.                                                                                                  |

### REQ26-D35-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — References, mentions and files

Applies to **US26-D35-03**, acceptance **AC26-D35-03-01–03**.

The source's attachment occurrence membership, identifiers and bytes remain unchanged by D35. The candidate may deliberately remove or move supported existing mention/inline-image appearances; its retained typed refs/target attributes must be a valid subset of those in the loaded current base. Do not create a new notifying target, retarget a node, acquire a foreign/remote asset or flatten a typed node into an authority-bearing string. Undo inside an unsaved candidate may restore only still-allowed references from that base. A later edit cannot use an old history view as a token-restoration authority.

Removing an inline picture leaves the actual existing file list; it is not privacy deletion. Every current/history preview/download rechecks D16/D32 and the exact source occurrence, including scan/restriction changes. A shared physical blob does not transfer source access. Ordinary href edits follow safe-link rules and do not fetch remote content. New supporting files or notifying mentions use an actual new note and its existing admission/attention rules.

The current creation composer immediately calls `logSupportActivity` from mention insertion; that helper posts generated text through ordinary note creation. The correction profile must not call that path during mount, editing, undo, Save, Cancel or history. New native publications must themselves acquire truthful human/generated provenance; otherwise future Edit eligibility remains unprovable. This is an existing-source qualification fix required by D35, not permission to infer source kind from message text.

### REQ26-D35-DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — Privacy and retention across history

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

Current note and all revisions belong to the same original D17 content generation/deadline. Editing, history reads, CRM links, merges, late jobs or receipt lookups do not renew it. Metadata/control facts and bodies have distinct qualified purposes/retention; “immutable revision” never means permanent private bytes. No arbitrary last-N deletion substitutes for D17, and no infinite-history product promise overrides its finite custody.

Apply D16 restrictions to every current/history representation and known derivative: canonical JSON, HTML/text, indexes, snippets, previews, exports, browser buffers, source-dependent prepared notification material and restores. A current selected-span redaction cannot be presumed to map onto differently worded earlier versions. When no safe earlier representation is qualified, restrict that affected revision body and derivatives as a whole, preserving only permitted body-free facts. No fuzzy matching, first-occurrence removal or semantic redaction engine is invented.

Coordinate save versus redaction/expiry/move/merge with authoritative source controls, not independent before/after UI checks. An old candidate cannot restore restricted material after its base was withdrawn. Restored backups must apply current withdrawal/expiry fences before serving or retrying. Redaction may produce a source-qualified safe representation; it does not rewrite original authorship or claim an ordinary user edit occurred.

### REQ26-D35-DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — Reads, history, search and CRM

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

Authorize exact note/source and each representation before returning bodies, metadata, counts, names or files. Same-tenant staff membership and CRM access are insufficient. A current merged root is handling/navigation context; the edited note stays with its original constituent source. Merge/Undo, unlink, move and permission changes invalidate stale reviewed context without reparenting history or authorship.

History returns at most20 permitted metadata rows, one selected body and an opaque cursor bound to the current authorized note/source plus a stable viewed frontier. A new edit can be signalled without reordering the open list; the user refreshes deliberately. Revalidate between pages and bodies, and never expose hidden revision gaps/counts. All retained permitted versions remain reachable; the page bound is not a data-retention cap. **Original** requires proven original content. An observed legacy body is **Recorded baseline**, not invented original text.

D22 current search/Find/snippets/rank/counts follow the current permitted head and its own currentness rules. Revalidate stale index matches; older versions belong only to explicit history. Identifier-only projection/safety work is durable with the edit and repaired idempotently from that edit. A failed search update does not roll back the saved note or justify showing an old positive as current. CRM uses the same source with preserved navigation and no duplicate Activity, copy or independent overwrite path. The edit changes no giving, receipt, refund, recurring, care or contact fact.

### REQ26-D35-DATA_CONTRACT-S0008 — Grants, RLS and deployment

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Verify actual deployed table/column grants and exposed schemas together with SELECT, effective old-row USING/new-row WITH CHECK, function/view invoker/definer context, execute grants/search path, storage and privileged/nonhuman paths. Current migrations' broad authenticated CRUD and explicit tenant/staff UPDATE checks do not establish author-only editing. PostgreSQL can inherit USING for omitted UPDATE/ALL WITH CHECK; use actual effective semantics. Do not use service role to avoid these boundaries or trust user-editable JWT metadata. PostgreSQL17 policies, locking, Supabase RLS.

Qualify native creation provenance and close old writers before enabling revision-aware edits. Backfill only independently provable original actor/source facts and one honest observed baseline. Ambiguous/generated/imported/unsupported legacy rows remain non-editable with permitted reading, ordinary new-note clarification and D16 paths. Do not manufacture previous versions, re-author as migration worker or renew old retention.

Add compatible schema/constraints/readers first, fence old writers, then enable gated editing and history. Disable edits while preserving accepted result/revision recovery and privacy/current reads. After new data exists, a rollback cannot discard history, restore broad writers or resurrect erased bodies; use a compatible roll-forward. No package upgrade, live SQL or migration is executed by this grooming record.

### REQ26-D35-R01 — D35-R01 — Scope and strongest alternative

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

Allow the original human author to edit their own ordinary posted internal Support note while that exact note/source and actor remain eligible. There is no arbitrary grace period. Incoming mail, outgoing email, system/AI events, other people’s statements, CRM-owned notes and D26 staff-recorded request briefs retain their own contracts. New events belong in new notes; ordinary new-note creation remains available for clarification or new material. Do not add a tenant correction-policy mode.

### REQ26-D35-R02 — D35-R02 — Local, discoverable editing

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

Offer **Edit note** in the note's accessible actions menu to its eligible author. Preserve the Internal note label and replace only that note's readable body with the qualified editor. Use **Save changes** and **Cancel**, in that order of importance. No hover-only action, forced modal stack, required edit reason, autosave, new setting or timer. Keep the original note position, separate Reply/Note draft, reader scroll and return focus. Only one posted-note editor is active in the current reader at a time; ordinary switching preserves intent through R08 rather than silently dropping changes.

### REQ26-D35-R03 — D35-R03 — Readable history

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

After a real successful change, retain original author/posting time and show **Edited** with an accessible edit time and **View history** action. History is a single read-only disclosure over this exact note: current version, Original only when true original-content provenance is qualified, a clearly labelled Recorded baseline for an observed legacy baseline, and earlier permitted saved versions with attribution/times. Initially fetch at most20 permitted metadata rows and one selected version body; use keyset pagination for more. No eager full-body archive, diff editor, Restore button, revision branching, new history export or per-revision comments. A reader sees only currently permitted versions and metadata; forbidden existence/counts are not leaked by gaps or placeholders. Display an unavailable/expired state only when its control facts themselves are permitted.

### REQ26-D35-R04 — D35-R04 — Correction versus new work

Applies to **US26-D35-03**, acceptance **AC26-D35-03-01–03**.

Correcting a typo, transcription or phrasing keeps the note in place. A changed circumstance, new action or new supporting material belongs in a fresh ordinary note. Explain this briefly near the editing affordance/help; do not require a reason code, classifier, AI judgment or universal confirmation before Save. A material correction that someone must act on can use existing deliberate staff attention through its qualified owner. An Edited marker does not claim that previous readers or recipients saw the correction.

### REQ26-D35-R05 — D35-R05 — Real authorship and current authority

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

The server derives the real authenticated principal, tenant and current staff/source authority; immutable original authorship and positive native-human publication provenance must be independently trustworthy. A row labelled note may actually be generated/system activity. Require current read and edit eligibility plus original-human-author equality at the atomic mutation. A matching email, current agent display JSON, role, assignment, CRM record link, API key or D34 cue is not authorship proof. No routine administrator override, service-worker impersonation or reassignment of note authorship. A disabled/revoked actor cannot save using a formerly valid editor session. History viewers require current note/source and version disclosure authority, not edit permission or mere CRM access.

### REQ26-D35-R06 — D35-R06 — Qualified canonical content

Applies to **US26-D35-03**, acceptance **AC26-D35-03-01–03**.

Reuse D23's Internal note canonical Tiptap profile and safe static renderer. Validate original persisted JSON and incoming full candidate against the exact code-owned schema/purpose, allowed attributes/nodes/marks, source references and depth/size/count limits **before** parser normalization. Derive HTML/text through the owner compiler; caller renderings are not write authority. Missing or incompatible original structure is a visible read-only migration/repair state, not successful blank content or permission to strip unknown fields. The exact profile and limits must be qualified before activation; D35 creates no separate numeric content allowance. Do not accept raw arbitrary HTML, fetch pasted external assets or execute content. A valid no-change candidate is handled under R09.

### REQ26-D35-R07 — D35-R07 — Practical correction profile, files and mentions

Applies to **US26-D35-03**, acceptance **AC26-D35-03-01–03**.

Edit prose, supported formatting and ordinary safe links. Deliberate deletion or movement may remove an existing typed mention or inline image appearance, including by deleting its paragraph; this is different from a parser silently losing unknown content. Submitted typed references must be a validated subset of the loaded current base's allowed references; retained target/source/purpose attributes cannot be changed. Undo within the unsaved editor may restore a still-allowed base reference. No new or retargeted notifying mention, asset acquisition, file removal/replacement or file-membership change is part of this correction command. Existing file occurrences/bytes remain unchanged and visible under **Existing files**. Explain that removing an image from the text does not remove the file from the note/history. Use the existing new-note action for new files/attention; D16 handles actual sensitive-content removal. Plain @name text is not a mention or permission grant. Mount, typing, paste, reference changes, history, Save and Cancel must never invoke an insertion-time activity callback or the ordinary addPrivateNote path.

### REQ26-D35-R08 — D35-R08 — Private draft, cancellation and navigation

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

Edits remain private local working state until Save. Cancel before submission discards only this edit and restores the current permitted note; unchanged Cancel needs no prompt. Dirty navigation, opening another edit or deliberately leaving the reader uses the existing small discard/keep-editing guard; do not create persistent multi-note draft storage or an offline queue. Background refresh must not overwrite the local candidate. Privacy/source access loss, real logout/account/tenant change or incompatible topology invalidates and clears forbidden local bodies regardless of a dirty-navigation prompt. Browser/OS tab loss is not promised recoverable. Browser close warnings are best-effort, not data guarantees.

### REQ26-D35-R09 — D35-R09 — Truthful save and no-op

Applies to **US26-D35-04**, acceptance **AC26-D35-04-01–03**.

Save deliberately shows an in-place saving state; do not replace the readable note with an unconfirmed candidate, falsely mark Edited or drop the candidate on a known failure. On success, show the authoritative current result and return focus without jumping chronology. Canonically unchanged content creates no revision, edit timestamp, activity or invalidation event. Every admitted Save, including No changes, records a minimal immutable operation binding/result with no body or diff. Do not use raw string equality alone when the qualified canonical representation treats content as equivalent. Empty or invalid content follows the existing qualified note profile; do not silently delete the note or add a new required field.

### REQ26-D35-R10 — D35-R10 — Conditional save and real concurrency

Applies to **US26-D35-04**, acceptance **AC26-D35-04-01–03**.

Save binds the exact original note/source, current base revision and relevant permission/privacy/content-generation/topology fences. Recheck them atomically. At most one competing candidate against the same base can advance the head; stale saves cannot silently win, rebase or restore superseded content. On conflict, show **This note changed** with the currently permitted saved version and **Your unsaved changes**. Let the author review the current version, deliberately continue from that new base and reapply their correction; there is no one-click overwrite, automatic merge or generic diff platform. A privacy/authorization conflict instead clears or withholds forbidden content. Multiple devices and D34 awareness do not weaken this guard.

### REQ26-D35-R11 — D35-R11 — Durable effect identity and unknown results

Applies to **US26-D35-04**, acceptance **AC26-D35-04-01–03**.

Bind one opaque operation identity to trusted tenant/actor/note, base/fences and canonical desired content. Same operation and same meaning produce the same minimal durable result; changed meaning conflicts. Do not rely on transport retries, short TTLs or a per-tab boolean. After a lost response, show **Checking whether your changes were saved** and use a read-only current-authorized outcome lookup. Unknown is not failed, cancelled or permission to mint another operation. Close during a possibly accepted save may stop waiting but cannot claim rollback; returning reconciles rather than resending. Current source/privacy rules govern even a replay response. Outcome evidence is content-free/minimized and follows its owner retention; old-body equality hashes/tokens cannot become a permanent private archive. Retain the minimal operation binding or equivalent durable rejection fence until the note is irreversibly non-editable and restore/replay cannot re-enable that identity. Response-cache or material expiry never releases the operation key. Accepted effect identity cannot be reused to create a second effect after cache expiry.

### REQ26-D35-R12 — D35-R12 — One source-owned revision model

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

Retain one stable Support note identity, immutable original tenant/source/human-author/publication provenance, a source-owned chain of content revisions and exactly one current revision pointer while content is available. Each admitted edit adds one next revision, updates that pointer, records truthful minimal edit attribution and any required source-invalidation obligations in one authoritative transaction, or none. Use actual owner-compatible TEXT IDs and tenant-aware relationships; do not assume UUIDs because a UI emits one. Revision identity/order/provenance do not allow arbitrary body overwrite. Retained content is separately purgeable under D16/D17; immutable history is not undeletable sensitive bytes. A compatibility current-body projection is derived, never a second write authority or second CRM note. Note edits do not bump conversation last-human activity, unread/new-note signals, reply clocks, status, assignment or retention anchors.

### REQ26-D35-R13 — D35-R13 — Database, grants and privileged paths

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Constrain same-tenant note/revision/current-head/operation references, unique revision order and unique business operation, required original provenance, valid lifecycle combinations and deliberate delete behavior. The current pointer must belong to its own note; a permitted update cannot reparent it or change actor/source ownership. Index actual tenant/note/order/source predicates and prove plans. Qualify effective SELECT/USING/WITH CHECK, column privileges, views/RPCs, invoker/definer functions with fixed safe search path, storage and service-role paths together. No generic browser CRUD or worker can bypass the command. An omitted UPDATE/ALL WITH CHECK may inherit USING in PostgreSQL; the issue is effective enforcement, not syntax absence. Minimized audit/receipt facts and content bodies have explicit separate access/retention. No money schema or external CRM synchronization is added.

### REQ26-D35-R14 — D35-R14 — Privacy dominates every version

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

D16's actual source restrictions/redaction apply to current body, old revisions, edit drafts, history reads, typed references, file appearances, previews, search, exports, prepared source-dependent notices and restored backups. A body-only edit is not a sensitive-data-removal tool. A redacted span in the current body does not prove a safe mapping to earlier revisions. Where the owner cannot qualify a safe earlier representation, restrict the affected prior revision body and known derivatives as a whole, retaining only permitted body-free evidence. Do not fuzzy-match across versions, remove only the first matching span or build a new semantic redaction engine. Do not offer history as a way to recover removed content, or silently expand a current redaction to another person's unrelated source. A history row may show only a permitted body-free unavailable fact; neither old text, forbidden author metadata, counts nor filenames leak. Source-aware corrective disposal uses existing owners and does not require routine manual SQL. Authorization loss is not merely a network-error fallback to cached content.

### REQ26-D35-R15 — D35-R15 — Retention and temporal truth

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

All revisions remain bound to the note's original source/content generation and existing D17 deadline. Saving, looking at history, linking through CRM or reapplying text never resets the anchor or renews an old source. Expired content is unavailable even if deletion workers lag. No last-N eviction substitutes for the accepted finite retention policy, and no unlimited-history promise bypasses it. Body-free edit/control history and operation receipts retain only their qualified minimal purposes and ceilings. Policy change, paused disposal, merge/Undo, archive and restored backups retain original source ordering and current adverse fences. A truly new ordinary note retains its genuine admission semantics; it cannot recreate forbidden old material.

### REQ26-D35-R16 — D35-R16 — Email Studio, attention and external copies

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

A routine note edit is not a new note publication, @mention dispatch, follower alert, donor email, P17 preparation or P6 resend. Preserve D15's quiet correction behavior and current-source-safe previews. Already prepared/sent communication material and actual delivery facts are not overwritten by editing a source. Where changed/redacted content invalidates outstanding source-dependent notification material, enforce the existing adverse fence/correction/disposal rules before further rendering/decrypt/send; do not blanket-delete valid body-free historical events or falsely claim recall. Independently qualified new-note or deliberate staff attention uses existing P17/P6 owners and can have its normal effects. D29 confirmation, D23 outbound signature/wording, recipients and financial messages are unaffected.

### REQ26-D35-R17 — D35-R17 — CRM continuity without inherited rights

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

CRM displays/opens the same current-authorized canonical Support note; one successful edit is visible through that source without duplicate Activity, copied body, two-way sync, CRM last-contact mutation or duplicate notifications. Preserve the selected record/list and return context. Linking/unlinking, merged constituent sources, Party merges, reassignment and permission changes must requalify the original note/source rather than inherit access from the visible CRM record or merged root. CRM people/organizations/relationships and giving/receipts/refunds/recurring/contact/member-care actions remain owned and authorized elsewhere. A changed note sentence does not perform, approve or establish completion of those actions.

### REQ26-D35-R18 — D35-R18 — Current reading and search

Applies to **US26-D35-02**, acceptance **AC26-D35-02-01–03**.

Ordinary timeline, D22 search/Find and snippets use the current permitted note head. Historical content is accessed only through deliberate qualified note history, not silently added to global/search/AI corpora. Revalidate stale indexed matches and counts before disclosure; a removed term cannot surface from an old revision as a current hit. Required projection invalidation/recovery is durably tied to the source change; repair does not mint a new edit. While an index is not current, apply D22's truthful currentness behavior rather than false completeness. D33 reading preference remains presentation only and does not save, restore or alter a revision.

### REQ26-D35-R19 — D35-R19 — Existing D34 awareness, explicitly qualified

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Deliberate editing of a posted human note may use the existing D34 neutral composing controller only after this producer's exact note/original-source and edit-authority binding is qualified. It cannot reuse a Reply composer instance for another constituent source. Switching between edit and Reply/Note preserves private drafts and stops/replaces the technical context under D34. Retain the same label, privacy, timing, expiry and stop-on-save/cancel rules; no new presence service/schema, edit-mode disclosure, draft sharing, history viewing signal or lock. D34 outage never prevents an independently qualified save. Read/history/focus alone is not composing.

### REQ26-D35-R20 — D35-R20 — Accessible and polished presentation

Applies to **US26-D35-01**, acceptance **AC26-D35-01-01–03**.

Use exact shared Base UI/base-maia, Maia/Zinc semantic tokens and the qualified Internal note editor/static renderer. Keep a calm note card, readable body and stable action placement; do not copy hardcoded legacy amber styling as authority. Visible labels and text states, accessible menu/history controls, deliberate focus return, linked validation errors and coalesced status announcements are required. Test200% text resizing,320CSS-pixel reflow/400% zoom, long international names/RTL, contrast, keyboard/screen readers and mobile virtual keyboards. Apply WCAG2.4.11 author-created focus-obstruction and2.5.8 target-size/exception requirements, with44CSS-pixel standalone-primary touch targets as a product goal. No hover-only timestamps, color-only Edited signal, destructive Escape surprise or unnecessary motion. Use existing motion/reduced-motion behavior.

### REQ26-D35-R21 — D35-R21 — Bounded performance and fair work

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Load one active editor and one selected historical body, never one editor per revision. History pages are capped at20 permitted metadata rows with stable keyset cursors bound to current source/authorization and a stable viewed frontier; newer edits do not silently reorder the open history list. Make currentness visible and let the reader refresh deliberately. No full-history count or body preload is required. In qualification, use two tenants, a200-revision retained note, bodies at the exact profile's ordinary and allowed maxima,100 concurrent authorized readers and20 same-base competing saves/retries. Require zero duplicate heads/effects/cross-scope disclosure and healthy-fixture p95≤2seconds for confirmed Save and selected-history-body readiness. Record hardware/data/profile/network conditions; these are accepted acceptance targets, not measured capacity. Existing actor/tenant-fair admission limits/backpressure apply, with bounded failure preserving permitted drafts and never deleting history to control load.

### REQ26-D35-R22 — D35-R22 — Legacy and safe activation

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Current note creation/rendering does not establish trustworthy authorship or a revision capability. Inventory actual writers/author provenance/content shapes first. Current generated activity can share the ordinary note endpoint; note type or a text prefix cannot establish native-human provenance. Only qualified legacy authorship may be migrated to editable provenance; never infer it from today's email or display JSON. Preserve one honest observed baseline version without inventing prior revisions or original creation evidence; label it Recorded baseline unless true original-content provenance is independently qualified. Unqualified old content stays readable where permitted with a clear editing-unavailable explanation and ordinary new-note/D16 paths under their own rights. Qualify the canonical editor cohort, parser/renderers, source model, constraints/grants and old-writer fences before activating Edit. Mixed readers use only a derived compatible current body; old writers cannot overwrite heads. Disable new edits without losing accepted revision/outcome recovery or privacy enforcement. Rollback after new revisions cannot restore permissive writers, discard accepted history or resurrect erased bytes; use a compatible roll-forward path.

### REQ26-D35-R23 — D35-R23 — Truthful audit and repair

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Record trusted actor, note/source, operation, predecessor/successor identities, actual time and minimal outcome in a typed business edit event; do not store body diffs, free-form reasons, endpoints, private filenames or candidate JSON in audit/log/metric tags. Technical traces diagnose save/read/invalidation failures separately from durable business history. Privacy-safe operators can reconcile the original operation and source projections without impersonating the author, fabricating a note or direct SQL. D16 disposal/restore controls govern affected payloads; a successful edit does not erase previously valid communication evidence.

### REQ26-D35-R24 — D35-R24 — Simple defaults and explicit exclusions

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

Ship one author-edit policy, not a tenant policy builder. No grace timer, required reason, restore/compare suite, branching/real-time co-editing, Pro document-history service, persistent multi-note drafts, history export, new AI retrieval/action path, general CRM note platform or bulk edit is justified by this need. New attachment/mention acquisition remains ordinary new-note work; supported current text/reference removal remains natural under R07. This is simplification at the right boundary, not permission to omit source/version/privacy checks.

### REQ26-D35-R25 — D35-R25 — Proof and operating gates

Applies to **US26-D35-05**, acceptance **AC26-D35-05-01–03**.

The proof and operations ledger supplies precise positive/negative/boundary/source/concurrency/CRM/migration/accessibility/user-journey outcomes and named operating controls. They are required before activation, not optional monitoring substitutes. Source inspection, synthetic examples and document review are not actual SQL/RLS, provider, browser/AT, performance or participant proof. Reconcile every finding into these clauses and the final data/editor/UX contracts before recording the answer.

## Deliberate reply quotations

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — The ordinary reply remains ordinary

Applies to **US26-D36-01**, acceptance **AC26-D36-01-01–03**.

Maya, a hypothetical tenant support worker, opens a donor's email asking which period a receipt covers. She writes a self-contained answer. The composition area shows the existing From/To/Cc and reply-target context, her answer, managed signature/footer and Send. No quoted history is present; no setting, checkbox or prompt asks her to decide every time. Opening the same conversation through its authorized CRM context provides the same composition experience and preserves the CRM return path. The example demonstrates communication only: neither sending nor quoting proves a receipt was changed.

The optional action belongs beside the current reply context because it refers to that email. It should not compete with Send or be hidden in global preferences. **Add quote** is quiet secondary text with an optional quote icon; its description identifies the email by permitted sender/date. Use **Quote message** in an individual message's actions. That distinction lets an earlier email provide context without changing who receives the reply.

Illustrative information hierarchy, not a pixel-perfect component implementation:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Reply to Alex · 14 Sep, 09:42                         Add quote
> To: Alex                           [existing recipient controls]
> 
> Your reply…
> 
> │ Excerpt from Alex · 14 Sep 2026, 09:42 ICT       Remove quote
> │ Which period does this receipt cover?
> 
> Continue your answer…
> 
> [Managed signature — existing controls]
> [Required footer — governed content]
> 
> [Send]                                         [existing actions]

The border uses logical start so RTL layouts work. The quote body uses ordinary readable text, not a wall of muted italics. Metadata is secondary but legible. Existing Maia spacing/radii, semantic tokens, focus ring and touch targets define visual geometry; no custom palette, deep card nesting or new toolbar system. A recipient's actual email uses the qualified email renderer, not interactive composer controls.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — Add context in one action

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Maya invokes Add quote. That one action requests the exact currently identified email's safe body. The action shows a small loading state if qualification takes time; the rest of the answer remains editable. With a valid remembered caret, the quote lands at a safe block boundary there. Otherwise it lands after authored content and before the managed signature. It never replaces highlighted answer text or enters the signature block. The new block starts expanded, and a normal paragraph after it supports continuing the answer.

The insertion is one undoable edit. Double activation during the same pending action creates one block; a later deliberate action may create another. No global history picker, new draft, second editor, mandatory preview or “Are you sure?” screen intervenes. One source is read per action; quote processing does not recursively retrieve a thread. Any existing authored answer, ordinary files and other quotes remain intact.

Focus must follow the user's action, not a late network response. If Maya stayed in the same editing context, reveal the new block and place the caret after it. If she continued typing elsewhere, do not steal focus or move her scroll; announce Quote added and provide a deliberate way to locate it. A stale/incompatible insertion anchor never overwrites work. If she switched conversations, canceled or removed the pending action, its result cannot insert later.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Quote only the useful passage

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

If Maya selects one sentence within an eligible email, the same message action can become Quote selected text. It captures the selection before a menu changes focus and verifies the exact canonical source range. Only that excerpt is inserted. This is an accelerator; keyboard, screen-reader and touch users can quote the message and trim when it fits, or use Choose excerpt without precision text selection.

Selection across two emails, a stale representation or unqualified DOM mapping produces a concise message, **That selection couldn't be added. Choose an excerpt from the message.** No hidden full email appears as the result of a selected-text action. Repeated identical passages require exact positions; Thai combining marks, emoji and RTL are not split. Meaningful tables cannot be flattened into misleading text. If a safe excerpt cannot be represented, preserve the existing answer and allow reading the source without pretending a quote was added.

**Choose excerpt** is the exceptional accessible path when the whole message is too long or browser text selection is unsuitable. It stays in the existing source reader. **Start here** beside a permitted paragraph selects that paragraph, ready to add; **Extend through here** on a later block extends the contiguous selection. The selected range/count is visible above **Add excerpt** and **Cancel**. The controls have ordinary keyboard/touch/screen-reader operation; Shift-drag or precision selection is never required. One small paragraph from a long email can be quoted even when the whole email would exceed the draft budget. The source/revision/block mapping remains authoritative and the normal Add quote still has no picker. A list/table that would lose meaning is indivisible; an individually oversized or unsupported block gets an honest limitation rather than automatic truncation. Cancel leaves the draft untouched.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Edit without a specialist workflow

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Maya removes irrelevant lines directly in the normal editor and writes her explanation below. The source identity stays fixed; because the quotation's meaning-bearing content changed, the visible and outgoing attribution becomes **Edited excerpt from Alex …**. This rule applies to changes in text, ordered content, meaningful list/table structure and link destinations, including trimming. Qualified presentation-only formatting is exempt. Changing a link destination while keeping its visible words is an edit and must be labelled. The comparison uses a canonical semantic projection, not an AI judgment about what the author meant. It avoids a deletion-versus-rewriting classifier and avoids attributing Maya's changed words verbatim to Alex. A freshly source-selected excerpt starts unchanged and does not need the Edited label.

She can format text with the qualified Reply tools, use safe links, move a quotation, remove it or undo. Each known transformation retains its source dependency. The source-bound block is not a new reply type or an internal note. Ordinary handwritten blockquote formatting is still available, but it cannot fabricate a verified source attribution. The quotation is editable content; its source metadata is the narrow protected semantic unit. Source-attribute tokens, editor-purpose IDs and admin links never become public markup.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Long messages and media stay honest

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

A source email may already contain nested history, a previous signature or addresses embedded in its body. The action shows the actual qualified representation. It does not pretend a visual fold reliably identifies the newest authored paragraph. Maya can remove unwanted parts. After inspecting a quote she may collapse its display if that existing editor behavior is qualified; the visible label remains **Quoted text — included in email**. Collapse is never removal, and the product does not need a new collapsed-history preference.

Text quotation does not add files or load remote images. A concise **Images and attachments aren't included** notice appears when relevant and safe to disclose. For an image-only source with no useful permitted text, no empty “success” block is inserted. Staff can attach a file separately only through the existing file-use authority. Private links, expiring action URLs and signed object URLs cannot sneak through as harmless text hyperlinks. Required governed signature images are unaffected.

If the exact shared document limit would be exceeded, the quote is not partially inserted. Explain the applicable limit with its real units and offer a smaller selected excerpt. The answer remains usable. No folklore Gmail clipping threshold or competitor attachment cap is adopted as an Asym limit.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Change recipients or target without surprises

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Quoting an earlier email never changes To/Cc, Reply-all or the selected reply target. If Maya deliberately adds a new recipient afterward, the application rechecks whether this quote may be disclosed to that audience. Eligible content gets one inline **Recipients changed — review quoted text** notice, with the quote expanded. Any D2 review already covering this exact quote/audience satisfies the same requirement; no duplicate modal. Ineligible material must be removed or the audience corrected. Acknowledgment is not permission override.

Merely removing a recipient rechecks eligibility but does not normally need another acknowledgment. If Maya explicitly retargets the reply, keep the authored answer and existing source-labelled quotes; use D2's target/context review. Do not replace a quote with the newest incoming message. If merge/unmerge/source restrictions remove eligibility, withhold only affected content when separable. Current source access determines which explanation can be shown.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Remove, undo, leave and return

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Remove quote deletes only that block. There is no confirmation dialog because ordinary current-authorized Undo can reverse it. It does not delete the incoming email or its files, edit history, change recipients or send a notification. A pending add is canceled without a late resurrection. Known retained copies keep their dependency; a source dependency can disappear only when no derived material remains.

D4 owns private draft persistence and conflict recovery. The same draft, version and source manifest are saved together; opening history/CRM and returning must not invent another draft. Browser tab loss or offline delivery is not newly promised by this feature. Unsaved/saving/saved/unknown remain honest. Logout, tenant/account change or privacy loss clears forbidden editor/cache/undo material, even if a dirty-navigation prompt would otherwise preserve it. An older saved quote does not restore an expired source.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — Send, receipt and reply continuity

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Maya sends through the existing action. A routine valid quote adds no extra Send confirmation. The visible reviewed answer, quotations, honest attribution, signature/footer and independently authorized attachments form one canonical message. Support validates source and audience, P17 compiles/prepares the complete message, and P6 seals/dispatches it with its existing identity. No later template adds the thread, no provider expands “original message,” and literal brace tokens remain literal.

If a quote is still loading, the user must finish or cancel that pending inclusion before Send; an optional quote cannot silently vanish during sending. If extraction alone is down, a new reply without a quote still works when its own prerequisites pass. If current source permission/privacy changed, targeted repair preserves independently safe answer text. If the provider outcome is unknown, the already accepted send follows P6 reconciliation; removing a quote cannot turn it into a fresh resend. Delivered email remains historical fact.

The recipient sees the new answer and only deliberately included context. Their client may group or collapse messages differently; Asym cannot guarantee that presentation. A donor replying from a normal email client does not need a Core/CRM account. Support keeps its canonical conversation; CRM shows only authorized communication context and the existing actual-send outcome. Neither quote nor send updates giving records or confirms an underlying business action.

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0010 — State and recovery inventory

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

These are UI states over existing source/draft/send owners, not a second persisted workflow state machine.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State                  | Visible behavior                                                              | Valid exit / forbidden transition                                             |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No quote               | Ordinary answer; Add quote when exact eligible source exists                  | Deliberate Add; no auto-inclusion                                             |
| Choosing excerpt       | Existing source reader with labelled start/extend controls and selected range | Add qualified excerpt or Cancel; no source edit or forced full quote          |
| Adding                 | Local action busy; answer remains editable; cancel available                  | Qualified insert, cancel or useful failure; no late cross-draft insertion     |
| Included               | Expanded source-attributed editable quote                                     | Edit, remove, optional collapse, normal Send                                  |
| Edited excerpt         | Same block with honest semantic-change attribution                            | More edits, Undo, remove, valid Send; no falsified original-author words      |
| Collapsed              | Included-in-email label remains                                               | Expand/remove; collapse never removes transmitted text                        |
| Audience review        | Current eligible quotes expanded and targeted notice                          | Single qualified review, audience correction or remove; no access override    |
| Unavailable/restricted | Only permitted control facts; safe answer preserved                           | Remove/reapply current permitted source; no stale preview/Undo recovery       |
| Draft conflict/unknown | Existing D4 conflict/result recovery                                          | Exact operation reconciliation; no blind overwrite                            |
| Prepared/unsubmitted   | Frozen complete message and current owner fences                              | Identical eligible execution or owner-qualified repair; no in-place body edit |
| Submission possible    | P6 actual accepted/rejected/unknown state                                     | Exact reconciliation; no new key/rerender or claimed recall                   |

### REQ26-D36-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0011 — Accessibility and usability proof

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Test the normal send, add/trim/remove, earlier-message quote, invalid selection, changed recipient and source-expiry journeys using mouse, keyboard, screen reader, touch and a narrow viewport. Include IME input while an extraction response arrives, browser zoom, long international names, Thai/RTL/mixed scripts, large nested messages and a visible mobile keyboard. Source/quote/answer ordering must agree between DOM, focus, visual display and sent plain text. Menu dismissal restores focus; no quote body is automatically spoken as a status announcement. Maintain at least the existing compliant contrast and focus tokens.

Release proof must demonstrate source-selected quotation without a mandatory modal, ordinary removal without a confirmation, no answer loss or unintended recipient/file changes, and discovery without coaching. A small purposive usability study identifies task failures; it is not population evidence that all ministries prefer A. The exact research protocol, failures, fixes and retest evidence belong to P28 in the proof record.

Five is a accepted small-study floor, not statistical proof or a claimed standard. Record task completion, obstacles and fixes, not satisfaction claims alone.

Publish measured p50/p95 and environment/network assumptions against the accepted D23 budget. No universal instant/scale claim or new per-keystroke compile/quote job.

**Decision clauses:** R12/R22/R26

### REQ26-D36-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P30 — Thirty release groups

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

**Independent observable outcome:** Exercise operating alerts, quote-only disablement, schema/canonical repair and source-owner handling.
