**Decision clauses:** R23–R26

### REQ26-D36-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O01 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** Any confirmed cross-tenant/source disclosure, unexpected active quote token/resource, or prepared-versus-reviewed material mismatch: **one event**.

**Accountable owner:** Support engineering on-call with security/privacy owner

**Response:** Immediately stop affected new quotation/preparation, preserve body-free evidence, apply source/provider owner containment and correct/verify before re-enable; do not replay possibly submitted mail.

### REQ26-D36-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O02 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** Eligible quote extraction technical-failure rate **over 2%** in a rolling **15 minutes** with **at least 100 eligible attempts**. User cancel, explicit policy denial and over-limit validation are excluded and separately typed.

**Accountable owner:** Support engineering on-call

**Response:** Diagnose source/compiler/storage/timeout root cause; scope-disable quote insertion if persistent, preserve plain replies and fix/retest. Low-volume tenants are not claimed covered by this aggregate alert; direct failures stay visible and reportable.

### REQ26-D36-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O03 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** Extraction p95 exceeds the release-qualified shared budget in **two consecutive 15-minute windows**, each with **at least 100 completed eligible operations**.

**Accountable owner:** Support performance owner

**Response:** Inspect payload/concurrency/region evidence; bound work or repair regression. Do not relax authorization or silently truncate. The actual budget must be published by P09/P29 before activation.

### REQ26-D36-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O04 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** Any confirmed stale result resurrecting a removed quote, lost authored text, duplicate durable insertion from one operation, or duplicate send: **one event**.

**Accountable owner:** Support draft owner; P6 delivery owner for actual sends

**Response:** Contain affected action, reconcile the original operation, repair and add regression evidence before re-enable. Keep independently valid draft text.

### REQ26-D36-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O05 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** **Three independently reported occurrences of the same quoting task obstacle within 30 days**, or **one reproduced accessibility blocker**.

**Accountable owner:** Support product/design owner with accessibility lead

**Response:** Reproduce in the actual journey, prioritize corrective design and retest affected tasks. Do not turn failure into a new setting/approval step by default. Record resolution in existing work tracking when authorized.

### REQ26-D36-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Accountability refers to release-assigned roles; deployment must name an actual on-call/team for each. These are accepted initial response thresholds, not measured baselines or vendor limits. Correctness is a release gate as well as an incident trigger. Use the existing observability/repair system rather than a new quote dashboard.

### REQ26-D36-R01 — D36-R01 — Default, scope and alternative

Applies to **US26-D36-01**, acceptance **AC26-D36-01-01–03**.

New human external replies, including entry through CRM, start with the new reply only. Do not append history on editor mount, draft restore, retarget, Reply-all, signature change, preparation, retry or provider submission. Already saved deliberate content remains visible under its own current authority; this default does not silently strip legacy drafts. Automatic exact-message or whole-history quoting is not added as a tenant/personal setting. Staff remain responsible for an understandable answer; recipient-client grouping is not guaranteed.

### REQ26-D36-R02 — D36-R02 — Discoverable entry with no extra ceremony

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Place a text-labelled **Add quote** action beside the existing reply-target/context row, with a concise accessible description identifying the selected email. It directly quotes that exact eligible email without an intermediate picker or confirmation. Each eligible email in the current original email thread also offers **Quote message** through its keyboard/touch-accessible actions. This uses the same insertion command and never means Reply, Reply-all, Forward or Change target. Avoid the ambiguous label original: it could mean first email or reply target. A missing source in a form/phone-origin first reply produces no fake email and no dead history control. A source already displayed but temporarily unavailable may expose a permitted neutral explanation and retry.

### REQ26-D36-R03 — D36-R03 — Selection is an accelerator, not a requirement

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

When a contiguous text selection belongs to one currently authorized source message, offer **Quote selected text** in that message's existing action path. Capture the selection before focus moves. The server verifies the exact source, representation/revision and selection against canonical content; DOM offsets, first substring match or clipboard HTML alone are insufficient. Preserve Unicode graphemes, repeated passages and paragraph boundaries. A cross-message, stale, hidden/unloaded or unmappable selection is not silently widened to the whole email. Explain the selection could not be used. Quote message plus ordinary trimming is an accessible fallback only when the whole insertion fits and is representable. Do not fetch hidden source text merely because the reader is Compact.

Provide a non-destructive **Choose excerpt** action in the existing source reader for users who need a smaller excerpt without browser text selection. In this exceptional mode, **Start here** on a permitted semantic block selects that one block; optional **Extend through here** on a later block selects a contiguous range. Show the selected range/count and **Add excerpt / Cancel**. Controls work with keyboard, touch and assistive technology. Bind exact source/revision and canonical block endpoints; reuse qualified source-selection mechanics without granting privacy/edit authority. Safe list/table structures remain indivisible where splitting would lose meaning. Load only the bounded current source page under the reader contract; no thread-wide picker, second editor or default wizard. A single indivisible block may still be unsupported/over-budget: explain that limit and preserve the answer rather than claiming every source can be quoted.

### REQ26-D36-R04 — D36-R04 — One insertion in the current editor

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Reuse D18's stable insertion grammar: remember the current draft and caret, insert at a valid block boundary without replacing a selection, or fall back to the end of authored body before the managed signature when no valid caret exists. Never insert into the signature/protected footer or overwrite an answer. An outstanding insertion is bound to its original draft, operation and source, not whichever ticket opens next. If the draft's insertion anchor changed incompatibly, retain the permitted result for an explicit reapply or ask the user to invoke again; never jump into another draft. One action creates one undoable insertion, even after double-click or repeated network result. A separate deliberate action may insert another quotation: no arbitrary one-quote cap or multi-message bulk inclusion feature.

### REQ26-D36-R05 — D36-R05 — Natural editing with honest attribution

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Insert the quote expanded with a restrained block border and readable ordinary type. Reuse the normal Reply editor for trimming, supported formatting and safe links. Source identity/date metadata is server-derived and cannot be edited into another speaker or source. Initially show a qualified **Excerpt from [sender], [date/time]** attribution; if meaning-bearing canonical content changes, including text/ordered content, meaningful list/table structure or link destinations, use **Edited excerpt from …** in both the composer and outgoing HTML/plain text. Only qualified presentation-only changes are exempt; qualified Undo to the exact inserted semantic excerpt may restore the original label. Compare the source-qualified canonical semantic projection, not a semantic-AI guess or plain-text-only equality. A changed hyperlink destination with identical anchor text must be marked Edited. The label is truthful provenance, not a claim that the source author approved a rewrite. Staff can write their interpretation outside the quote. Do not add a trim-only editor, change-reason form, diff viewer or approval dialog.

### REQ26-D36-R06 — D36-R06 — Visible inclusion, simple removal

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Show the actual inserted content on first addition. Offer **Remove quote** on its labelled block and ordinary editor Undo; neither requires confirmation. Preserve the surrounding answer, recipients, signature and other quotations. Later collapse is optional reading convenience with the explicit label **Quoted text — included in email** and an accessible Expand control, not a tiny unexplained ellipsis. Collapsing never excludes bytes. Do not auto-collapse immediately after insertion, silently expand all older history, or move focus because a background result arrived. Expanding/collapsing is local display state, separate from D33 Compact/Full. Undo cannot restore content made unavailable by source privacy or permission changes.

### REQ26-D36-R07 — D36-R07 — Exact reviewed representation, no hidden extraction promise

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Quote the eligible source's qualified safe email-body representation or verified selection, preserving meaning, block order, locale and direction. It can already contain nested quotes or signature/address text; show that actual content and let staff trim it. D33 visual folding and heuristic reply/signature detection are not extraction authority. Do not silently invent a fresh-message-only parser, remove negation/table relationships, append concealed headers, or reconstruct extra signature/recipient blocks. Nonessential unsupported styling may be normalized with a concise loss indication. If safe meaning-preserving conversion cannot be established, do not return a successful empty or truncated quote: offer the permitted readable source and the ordinary answer path. Sanitized quote projection is derived, never a new authoritative incoming message.

### REQ26-D36-R08 — D36-R08 — Text quotation does not acquire files

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Initial deliberate quotation carries safe text/structure/links, not historical attachments, inline images, tracking pixels, remote resources, embedded documents, provider objects or signed storage URLs. If the selected visible content had omitted media, say **Images and attachments aren't included**; use neutral placeholders only when their metadata is permitted. Do not silently collapse an image-only source into a meaningful text quote. Staff can use the existing independently authorized attachment path. Ordinary permitted web links remain inert clickable links, validated without fetching; tokenized action/private-storage links follow their owner and are not rebroadcast as ordinary URLs. D32 preview grants no attachment/send authority. The shared required signature/logo remains separate.

### REQ26-D36-R09 — D36-R09 — Current source and disclosure eligibility

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

At extraction and material admission, require current authenticated staff identity, tenant membership, exact original source read authority and the existing Support authority to disclose the included content to the actual outgoing audience. Only eligible external email messages from the current selected original email thread are offered. A merged staff handling timeline is not one email transcript. Internal notes/D35 history, internal guidance, D26 private briefs and unrelated CRM/financial/care material are outside this quote action. A nonstaff email recipient does not need staff RLS access; disclosure eligibility is the existing communication boundary, not a requirement that every recipient be a Core user. Matching email, assignment, participation, Party link or possession of a source ID never grants permission.

### REQ26-D36-R10 — D36-R10 — Recipient changes get proportional review

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Adding a quote never adds recipients. Later audience expansion or a material recipient identity change revalidates each quote's disclosure and invalidates prior audience review. Put **Recipients changed — review quoted text** beside the quote/recipient context, expand affected quotations and provide a single clear inline acknowledgment for the now-eligible complete audience. Reuse any D2 review covering those exact quotes/audience instead of adding a second confirmation. Pure recipient removal revalidates without a gratuitous acknowledgment unless another material source rule changed. Server denial cannot be overridden by acknowledgment. New recipients must not see source-recipient/Bcc metadata merely because it was in an email header; do not reconstruct header lists. The final audience is sealed by the existing send contract.

### REQ26-D36-R11 — D36-R11 — Reply target and topology stay stable

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Quote message from an earlier eligible email adds context only. It does not retarget Reply. If staff explicitly change the D2 reply target, retain the answer and show existing quote source attribution; revalidate the quotes and invoke the existing single target/context review. Never swap their bodies for the new target. New incoming mail, assignment changes, CRM merges, Support merges/Undo, reopening or sorting cannot silently switch source, target or audience. Source identity remains the original message. If a topology change removes eligibility, withhold affected content and explain only permitted facts; do not turn a formerly valid source into a new send authority.

### REQ26-D36-R12 — D36-R12 — Fast local interaction and honest loading

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Adding/removing/collapsing a quote does not publish work, create an activity or send anything. Show action feedback promptly while source qualification runs; cancelable extraction failure leaves the answer untouched. A late result after Remove, Cancel, navigation, tenant switch or newer source selection is ignored. Keep typing responsive while fetching. An in-progress quote cannot silently miss the click on Send: show **Finish adding the quote or cancel it to send**, with Cancel add available. If a quote is unavailable, Send remains blocked only for a draft that still intends to include it; explicitly remove it to send the independently valid answer. Do not make optional extraction service failure disable unrelated plain replies.

### REQ26-D36-R13 — D36-R13 — Private drafts, restore and multiple tabs

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Use the accepted D4 private draft/version/save/recovery contract; create no second quote-draft table, long-lived browser body cache or offline queue. Preserve user input and quote dependencies together. Ordinary failures keep permitted unsaved text with the current save status; known saved and unknown outcomes remain distinct. Concurrent draft writes or quote results cannot silently replace a newer document. Real account/tenant changes and permission/privacy loss clear forbidden data, including editor undo buffers and pending results. Draft restoration never automatically acquires a fresher source body, missing images or new recipients. Material changes require the ordinary review; a quote source snapshot is not a live content subscription.

This action belongs to external Reply. Switching to Internal note preserves the existing separate purpose-specific draft; it does not convert a note/history into an external quote or let a pending Reply insertion land in the Note editor. Existing explicit purpose-qualified content movement retains D23/D16 source rules.

### REQ26-D36-R14 — D36-R14 — One canonical message, inert source text

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Use ADR0030/D23's versioned document and code-owned Reply profile with a typed source-bound quotation or equivalent qualified schema representation. Validate untrusted original/candidate nodes, marks, attributes, positions and bounds before lossy parser normalization. Derive HTML/plain text in the shared server compiler. Source text, `{{braces}}`, @names, copied signatures and links never become executable variables, mentions, commands, protected actions or resource fetches. Source attribution identifiers are internal metadata and must not leak into public HTML attributes/URLs. Keep ordinary user-created blockquote formatting distinct; it cannot claim source provenance from a caller-written label. The current global brace-substitution serializer is not an acceptable permanent quote compiler.

### REQ26-D36-R15 — D36-R15 — Provenance survives known transformations

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Bind each insertion to immutable original source identity, qualified content/representation revision, selected range or whole-body projection, sanitized snapshot identity and deriving operation. Keep source-owned restriction/expiry dependencies across the draft, canonical document, prepared material and known editor copy/cut/move/unwrap/Undo transformations. Exact internal selection/edit operations may carry lineage; arbitrary clipboard claims do not establish it. Drop a dependency only when all retained derived material from that source is proven absent. If mapping is unqualified, conservatively withhold affected dependent material under D16 rather than infer clean state from text similarity. Do not build global clipboard surveillance, substring matching or AI provenance. Independently retyped/external text cannot be guaranteed traceable; retain the honest D16 limitation rather than promising universal recall.

### REQ26-D36-R16 — D36-R16 — Database and mutation boundaries

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Support/API owns the qualified extraction and draft-admission command; browser data follows the approved authorized read collections or qualified server read models. Reuse source/draft/preparation records and their dependency manifest, not a second CRM or reusable quote library. Persist tenant-aware source/draft references with composite tenant keys or equivalent enforced same-tenant relationships, non-null original source identity for a managed quote, immutable source/actor fields, valid schema/revision checks and indexed reverse dependencies for restriction lookup. Server context derives tenant, real actor and validated owner/source references; caller JSON cannot assert authorship, approval or provenance. Current IDs/body evidence are not silently backfilled from email strings.

Where rows are exposed, qualify grants plus RLS for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and both pre-state USING and post-state WITH CHECK on allowed updates. Post-state validity alone does not make tenant/owner/source columns immutable; restrict those columns/commands explicitly. SELECT-policy prerequisites, policy combination, views, RPC EXECUTE grants, definer search_path and service-role bypass must be tested. Use invoker views where appropriate; privileged paths must repeat equivalent tenant/current-authority checks. No source body/history grants are added to recipients. Delete/cascade behavior must preserve required restriction/effect evidence without orphaning derived content; body/key disposal follows D16/D17. No new money column/type or giving mutation is introduced.

### REQ26-D36-R17 — D36-R17 — Privacy and retention outrank stale convenience

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Apply D16/D17 to source and every controlled quotation representation before serving, materializing, decrypting, exporting or sending it. A current redaction/expiry/restriction makes old source material ineligible even when a draft, preview, cache, undo or saved quote predates the change. Preserve independently safe authored answer text when reliably separable; otherwise withhold the affected larger representation and give a truthful recovery path. Removal and Undo are not privacy restoration. Retention deadlines do not restart at quote insertion; the earliest applicable source/intent/prepared deadline continues to govern execution material. Already delivered mail and independent downloads cannot be recalled or rewritten. Body-free send/audit facts remain truthful; no claim of erasure from every external copy.

Classify each governed materialization in the finite D16 representation inventory. Tracked source-derived draft/prepared/display copies retain their restrictions; independently authored or received quoted emails are separate evidence requiring their qualified owner correction. Do not run a global matching-text erase cascade, automatically renew a linked original on native reply admission, or drop all lineage at send. Actual native admission retains D17's own clock; merely copying old text is not a new lifetime for the old source.

### REQ26-D36-R18 — D36-R18 — Atomic preparation and immutable delivery

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

At Send, bind the reviewed draft revision, exact target/audience and qualified source/privacy/topology generations to the existing semantic intent. Recheck them at the authoritative preparation boundary and current P6 dispatch eligibility; a stale cached capability or a Realtime hint is insufficient. The source-fence/preparation transition and source restriction/expiry ordering must serialize so two individually valid operations cannot permit unsafe material. P17 prepares the complete reviewed message, including edited-quote labels and signature/footer, and freezes its hashes/schema/presentation dependencies. P6 seals and dispatches those bytes. If material has definitely not been submitted and must change, return to qualified preparation/review under the owner contract; do not mutate frozen material. Once submission may have begun, reconcile the same intent/envelope and apply ADR0032's bounded recovery; no new key, re-render or blind second send.

### REQ26-D36-R19 — D36-R19 — CRM continuity without duplicate truth

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Support reached from a CRM person/organization/relationship view uses the same original-source reader, current draft and quote command. Preserve return context and scroll without duplicating note/message bodies into CRM. A quote action creates no Party/contact, association, CRM Activity, follow-up task, ownership change or giving operation. Requester, email participant, authenticated principal, CRM person, represented organization, assignee and CRM owner stay distinct. Source quotation or a sentence about a receipt/refund is not evidence that its owning business action succeeded. Linking/unlinking/merging CRM entities changes navigation/projection only under its owner; all source and business permissions still apply. CRM remains usable without Support enabled.

### REQ26-D36-R20 — D36-R20 — Email Studio's exact role

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Support chooses and authorizes the source content, target, audience and deliberate quotation action. Email Studio/P17 owns compatible structured authoring/schema, governed signature/presentation, full-message compilation and immutable preparation. P6 owns sender/connection qualification, delivery identity, provider submission/retry/reconciliation and communication evidence. They must not independently fetch a Support transcript, auto-add history, re-evaluate source text as a template, attach historical files or inject unseen source headers after review. Quoting is not Email Studio template publication, Saved Section publication, a new signature default or a campaign feature. D29 optional Contact confirmation, D15 staff attention, D34 composing awareness and D35 note editing remain unchanged.

### REQ26-D36-R21 — D36-R21 — Accessible, coherent Maia interface

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

Use exact base-maia, Base UI shared primitives and semantic tokens. Keep quote text as readable as the answer; use a subtle border rather than tiny pale type or a visually dominant nested card. All add/remove/expand actions have visible or accessible text and work without hover, selection gestures or keyboard shortcuts. Maintain source-to-composer focus and stable reading position; concise status announcements do not read entire quotes automatically. Preserve IME composition, screen-reader editing, bidi names/Thai/RTL text, local date formatting with accessible absolute time/timezone, keyboard/virtual-keyboard access and reduced motion. Prove WCAG2.2AA relevant criteria, including 320CSS-pixel reflow, 200% text resize and unobscured focus. Apply existing touch tokens; 44CSS-pixel touch hit areas are a product target, distinct from WCAG2.5.8's 24CSS-pixel minimum and exceptions.

### REQ26-D36-R22 — D36-R22 — Bounded work without a new platform

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Extract only the selected source on demand; do not load/compile an entire thread or tenant to add one quote. Reuse the existing editor, static renderer, async read model and current source cache discipline. Publish the D23 shared Reply limits before activation: raw/normalized input bytes, nodes/depth, selection and source-reference counts, complete HTML/text/MIME bytes, compile/extraction timeout and tested concurrency. The stricter owning/provider limits win. Test zero, maximum and maximum-plus-one, using explicit units and representative Unicode/nested/table-heavy sources. No silent truncation; offer a smaller selected excerpt or remove quote while preserving the answer. No new quote-specific arbitrary cap, worker platform, vector index, live collaboration, automatic summarization or promise of unlimited/instant performance.

### REQ26-D36-R23 — D36-R23 — Compatible rollout and repair

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Qualify the shared schema/compiler, source provenance/disclosure, draft persistence, restrictions and P6 fences before exposing Add quote. Additive schema deployment and server readers precede new writes. Mixed-version readers cannot drop unknown quote nodes or re-save a blank/stripped draft; provide a safe read-only incompatible state. Classify existing authored blockquotes and raw drafts truthfully; do not invent source IDs, sender attribution or proof from matching text. Unqualified drafts need a reviewed migration path, not destructive automatic cleanup. A feature kill switch can stop new insertion/preparation while keeping authorized reading and accepted-intent reconciliation. Rollback cannot re-enable restricted old material or replay sent messages; after new format writes, compatible roll-forward is the safe path.

### REQ26-D36-R24 — D36-R24 — Useful evidence without body surveillance

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Record body-free technical extraction/admission/failure timings and typed reason codes, with protected correlation to source/draft version/intent only as authorized. Durable communication history records the actual prepared/sent result through existing owners, not every click or keystroke. Source dependency evidence and authorization/adverse decisions must be diagnosable without copying quoted content, recipient addresses, filenames, raw errors, signed links or editor documents into logs/analytics. Ordinary quote addition/removal creates no attention event or notification. No staff productivity score, contact-deflection metric or new dashboard. Named residual controls and thresholds are in the proof record; security and content correctness are release gates, not monitor-only risks.

### REQ26-D36-R25 — D36-R25 — Prove full user and owner outcomes

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

The required release groups in the proof record must pass on qualified nonproduction browser, API, actual RLS/grants, editor, compiler, privacy, migration and dispatch paths before activation. Include Support-to-CRM journeys, recipient changes, duplicate requests, concurrent drafts, source-restriction races, stale/late responses, unexpected HTML, literal tokens, nested/forwarded mail, rich/Unicode selections, mobile/keyboard/screen reader and representative recipient clients. Documentary checks and finite synthetic models cannot substitute for that proof. Record actual limits, installed versions, dataset shape, test results and remaining empirical limitations. Trace these clauses to later OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets/implementation/release only when those stages are authorized.

### REQ26-D36-R26 — D36-R26 — Scope and evidence discipline

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

This is a Support reply feature within Asym. Keep all prior accepted owner contracts. Do not add a second CRM, support-wide workflow engine, public/internal guidance feature, SLA/automation/reporting suite, AI quoting, external helpdesk integration or a product-wide clipboard policy. Commercial vendor behavior is comparative evidence, not architecture authority. The new default is founder-selected; exact UX/safety amendments are accepted product/engineering requirements. No controlled Asym ministry usability study, deployed SQL/RLS verification or provider/client deliverability proof has run for D36. Those unknowns have named release evidence, not fabricated claims that the experience is perfect or production-ready.

### REQ26-D36-C01 — C01 — One canonical reply draft.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

New ordinary external Support replies contain newly authored content and the governed signature/footer, with no automatically appended earlier body. A deliberate quote is part of that same private canonical draft, not a live reference expanded at Send, another email, a CRM note, a Saved Section or a new transcript.

### REQ26-D36-C02 — C02 — Exact original source.

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Quote insertion names an admitted external email's stable tenant/original/message identity and current canonical content revision. The source-read command derives tenant/actor from trusted context, checks current staff read/use authority and source privacy/expiry, and derives the selected content from that canonical revision. Caller HTML, DOM offsets, snippets, body strings, source URLs and search hits are not authority. Reply-target identity and quote-source identity remain distinct; selecting a quote never retargets the reply.

### REQ26-D36-C03 — C03 — Proportionate source eligibility.

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

The normal quote action uses the eligible external email already in the current source context. An explicitly chosen earlier eligible email may be quoted without synthesizing a whole merged transcript. No internal notes/revisions, staff guidance, private drafts, unrelated merged/linked histories, CRM/care/giving data or files enter this action merely because staff can see them. The command does not search a person's other records or create a new customer model.

### REQ26-D36-C04 — C04 — Disclosure is not an email recipient's staff ACL.

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Staff source-read/use authority and permission to disclose the selected content to the explicit outgoing audience are distinct checks. Ordinary permitted external correspondents do not need a staff account, CRM record or Support source-read permission. Apply the existing D2 source/recipient/classification and protected-record disclosure rules to the actual reviewed content; preserve legitimate Reply-all and deliberate recipient editing. Adding an endpoint requires requalifying existing quotes and any required concrete audience review, not a blanket denial or universal approval modal.

### REQ26-D36-C05 — C05 — Preserve exact reviewed meaning.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Keep quoted literal text inert. Do not resolve merge variables, @mentions, CRM values, protected actions or script/URI commands found in quoted content. Do not fetch remote images or attach historical files. Preserve safe line/block/Unicode order, semantic quotations and permitted visible text; disclose material omissions. Existing embedded signature/address text is content to review, not an instruction to reconstruct extra headers or silently strip signatures.

### REQ26-D36-C06 — C06 — Stable bounded provenance.

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

Bind each source-derived quote occurrence to the draft, exact source revision, selected canonical range/content descriptor, qualified rendering profile and destination/review generation. Its protected dependency follows supported draft save/restore, editor Undo and relevant derivations into preparation. Use exact owner IDs/types and same-tenant constraints, not source-email/name/text matching. Do not add original quote bodies to immutable audit logs; the governed canonical draft/preparation owns necessary content custody.

The chosen editing interaction must make provenance preservation feasible. A reviewed source excerpt or protected quote block is simpler to qualify than arbitrary HTML replay. If supported quote edits cannot retain precise mapping, conservatively keep the whole originating-source dependency for the candidate and require clean review after a source stop. Do not erase lineage by converting a block type or accepting spoofed hidden editor attributes. This is not a demand for character-level source graphs or universal clipboard detection.

### REQ26-D36-C07 — C07 — Save as one effect.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

The existing draft command atomically persists the canonical document, active quote dependencies and current draft revision; no Saved state is returned for body-only success. Conditional revisions prevent late insertion/save/remove from overwriting newer work. A replay of the same save/quote intent cannot duplicate a quote, restore a deliberately removed quote or change another draft. An identical durable outcome is distinguishable from the latest draft state.

The implementation can use existing draft CAS and local insertion transaction identities; it does not need a quote ledger per click. A unique logical source occurrence or editor transaction token should dedupe a retried insertion, while a separate deliberate action may insert another quotation as an explicit authored choice. Do not dedupe solely by equal text; two different emails may intentionally say the same thing.

### REQ26-D36-C08 — C08 — Source changes are explicit.

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

A new incoming email, source reclassification, merge/unmerge, changed Party/contact, changed response endpoint or inbox move cannot replace the chosen quote or reply target. Changed actual content/source/disclosure authority invalidates affected quoted material and preparation. Preserve separable authored text and explain a targeted repair. A late fetch cannot insert into another tenant, conversation, draft, compose mode or obsolete editor revision.

### REQ26-D36-C09 — C09 — Current privacy/retention fences.

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

D16/D17 govern known source-derived quote copies. Restriction/expiry prevents future quote reads, restored draft use, preparation and new dispatch even when worker cleanup lags. Copying material into a draft is not native publication, new purpose or a renewed source lifetime. An actual admitted reply keeps D17's qualified native-admission semantics without automatically renewing a different linked original merely because it was quoted. No snapshot/Undo/old writer recreates withdrawn material.

Preserve the distinction between tracked source-derived representations and independently authored/received quoted emails. Do not claim a D16 operation erased every occurrence everywhere or silently rewrite separately owned sent evidence. Known derived content must be enrolled in the existing finite representation/correction inventory; when admitted copies are independent evidence, the actual privacy/records owner governs their correction. Identify affected original/representation in review and preserve factual communication outcomes. Recipient mail already sent is not remotely recalled.

This is the required reconciliation with D16's scope. A global cascade deleting every matching quote would contradict accepted independent-evidence protection. Conversely, dropping all dependencies at admission would let prepared/Recent/source-backed views resurrect restricted data. The later schema must classify each actual materialization explicitly and prove its disposal/restriction owner.

### REQ26-D36-C10 — C10 — P17 prepares what staff reviewed.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Support qualifies exact source/actor/target/audience and draft generation. Email Studio/P17 validates the complete compatible structured document, source references, signature/footer, assets and subject, then freezes canonical HTML and real plain text plus exact dependency/source evidence through its existing preparation contract. No quote is added by a mutable template token, provider template, a second Support serializer or late history query. Source IDs and private admin URLs are not accidentally transmitted as attribution.

### REQ26-D36-C11 — C11 — P6 dispatch and immutable recovery.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Before P6 admits actual dispatching, current source stop/expiry and disclosure fences must still pass for the sealed material. Serialize competing stop/dispatch admission using the existing owner guard/claim protocol, not a check-then-network promise. A stop winning first blocks submission. A dispatch admitted earlier may be in flight/accepted/unknown; preserve that exact evidence and prohibit unsafe later payload-bearing retries. Never edit, split, regenerate or rekey an already sealed/possibly submitted envelope to remove a quote.

### REQ26-D36-C12 — C12 — CRM continuity.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

The same source-owned reply composer and current quote behavior work when entered from an authorized CRM Support conversation. Restore CRM/list/draft context on return. Quote addition/removal/save creates no Party/contact, relevance link, communication event, last-contact update, donor reply, giving action or work-resolution claim. A real admitted send projects through the one existing P6/Support lineage and D9 read model with its actual recipient outcomes.

### REQ26-D36-C13 — C13 — Database access closure.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Store source/draft/preparation references using tenant-aware endpoint constraints and immutable identity/actor fields. Versioned closed JSON/schema validates source node/selection/profile/state, finite size/depth and canonical body/dependency parity before persistence. Raw quote/dependency/control data is not directly editable through browser table grants. Current exact-source/privacy/disclosure checks apply in the canonical command and all views, RPCs, definer/service-role paths, exports and storage representations. No added permissive policy can preserve the old broad mutation route.

If direct reads are admitted, they must exclude private drafts and inaccessible source IDs/content/existence before pagination/counting. Updates must not change tenant, original source, author, destination owner or accepted-send identity. Both old-row and allowed-result checks must be effective, whether explicit or inherited, and qualified DB constraints must prevent invalid endpoint/state combinations. Deletion cannot cascade into original messages, CRM/giving records or required effect/replay evidence.

### REQ26-D36-C14 — C14 — Limited resource and outage scope.

Applies to **US26-D36-01**, acceptance **AC26-D36-01-01–03**.

Read/quote one explicit bounded eligible source or selection; never fetch the entire conversation merely to add context. Use existing qualified source/editor/complete-message budgets and validate decoded/serialized sizes before insertion, save and preparation; publish exact profile limits and test equality plus one-unit-over behavior. Do not silently truncate a quote and label it complete. Oversized/unavailable quote work leaves the existing draft usable and adds no quote; current source-disclosure failure must not expose a prohibited preview.

Use the qualified finite source/editor/complete-message profile and its exact boundary proof. Distinguish accepted engineering targets from actual vendor or intake/send capacities; this quote capability adds no universal byte limit. Source-conversion latency is not typing latency: ordinary typing/send-without-quote should not depend on retrieving history.

### REQ26-D36-C15 — C15 — Compatible activation.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Qualify canonical source conversion, editor round-trip, private draft CAS, source dependency inventory, complete preparation, current dispatch fences and all old writer/read paths before enabling quotes. Existing source-incompatible drafts remain readable/repairable under current permission rather than silently stripped/autosaved. Do not invent provenance on legacy body text, create mass duplicate history, or migrate by email/subject matching. Old readers must reject unsupported canonical versions. A kill switch stops new quote acquisition/preparation without altering possibly sent effects or removing existing source stops.

### REQ26-D36-EDITOR_SEAM_REVIEW-S0004 — Recommended complete journey

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

1. **Ordinary answer:** Staff open an external Reply with its current From/To/Cc and exact source target visible. The body is empty apart from its separate governed signature/required framing. No history is appended, and no quotation setting is required.
2. **Discover:** Near the existing reply-target context, provide a quiet text-labelled **Quote message** action. It means the specifically identified message; avoid the ambiguous label Original, which could mean the earliest thread email. Each eligible external message also offers **Quote message** in its ordinary message actions. Both invoke the same insertion. No bulk history picker or multi-select is added.
3. **Choose less when useful:** A valid selection within one qualified source message may offer **Quote selection** as an accelerator. It uses an exact source revision/range, not screen DOM text as authority. Whole-message Quote remains fully operable without text selection; staff can trim the inserted quote. If precise selection mapping is not qualified, do not silently quote the whole message under a Quote selection action.
4. **Insert into existing work:** Use the stable remembered draft caret at a valid block boundary. With no valid remembered caret, insert at the end of the authored body before the managed signature. Never overwrite selected authored content, place source content inside the managed signature, split required framing or insert into another draft/mode. This is one ordinary undoable edit. After insertion place the caret in an ordinary paragraph after the block so the answer can continue outside quotation; preserve prior content and expose the inserted block for inspection without a full-screen transition.
5. **Review naturally:** Show the quote expanded when added. Use a restrained logical-side border, readable body type and a compact source line. The Source/Open message and Remove quote actions are reachable by keyboard and touch. No small grey italic wall of text, hover-only controls, nested card dashboard, permanent modal or automatic collapse. Source reading Compact/Full does not alter included bytes. If the user later chooses to collapse an inserted quote, label it as included and make every byte inspectable before Send; initial implementation need not add collapsing at all.
6. **Trim/edit in place:** The quote text is editable in the same composer; no second Edit quote dialog or editor. Source identity/attribution is the narrow locked semantic unit. Any meaning-bearing canonical alteration from the inserted excerpt, including trimming, ordered/list/table structure or link destination changes, displays **Edited excerpt from …** in both the composer and delivered HTML/plain text; only qualified presentation-only formatting is exempt. This deliberately conservative marker avoids a complex deletion-versus-rewriting classifier or a false verbatim attribution. If a source-selected excerpt is inserted unchanged, it is an excerpt, not a claim to contain the whole message. Do not silently say X wrote after rewriting X's words.
7. **Remove/undo:** Remove deletes that inserted block only, with ordinary local Undo and no confirmation modal. Undo uses current source authority; a restricted quote cannot reappear. Subsequent typing, another quote and preexisting files survive. An accidental double-click/replayed insertion action adds one block; a new deliberate insertion may quote the same source again. There is no one-quote cap beyond the governed complete-document budgets.
8. **Send:** The same visible complete canonical draft, including quote bodies and permitted source attribution, is validated and compiled by the existing path. No new quote confirmation on a routine valid send. Only an actual changed audience/source/permission, unsafe content or invalidated preparation requires targeted inline repair/review. Successful quotation insertion means only the draft changed; it is not delivery, a new conversation event or a completed CRM action.

This placement is a product judgment using D18's existing grammar. Always appending to a hidden footer is the strongest simpler placement alternative, but makes useful inline question-and-answer awkward and risks another history container. A generic freeform clipboard-only answer is less work to build but fails source lineage, reliable selection and a discoverable mobile journey.

### REQ26-D36-ES01 — ES01 — One canonical quotation.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

A source-derived quote is copied once into the current canonical Reply document with a stable source identity, exact eligible source revision/excerpt and occurrence provenance qualified by Support. It is not a live source reference, provider template, raw HTML footer, duplicate conversation or newly published Saved Section. Ordinary source updates never silently rewrite a saved quote; actual source restriction/expiry still stops unsafe use.

### REQ26-D36-ES02 — ES02 — Trust and transformations.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Source, tenant, actor, source attribution and eligibility are server-derived. Caller-provided text, HTML, source IDs, selected ranges and hidden attributes are not authority. Verify source resolution before acquisition and complete source/recipient eligibility before preparation/admission. Known source-bound editor cut/copy/unwrap/Undo transformations retain the affected dependency; explicit removal releases only dependencies proven no longer represented. Do not create document-wide permanent taint, a clipboard surveillance service or a similarity/secret classifier. Independent retyping or external clipboard provenance has the limits already stated in D16; the product does not promise perfect disclosure detection.

### REQ26-D36-ES03 — ES03 — Honest editable attribution.

Applies to **US26-D36-02**, acceptance **AC26-D36-02-01–03**.

The inserted quote body supports ordinary editing within the qualified Reply profile. The source label cannot be edited into another sender/date. Compare meaning-bearing canonical content with the inserted qualified excerpt, including text/order, meaningful list/table structure and link destinations; these changes produce recipient-visible Edited excerpt attribution, while only qualified presentation-only formatting is exempt. The marker does not imply the source itself was edited. Undo back to the exact eligible semantic excerpt may clear the marker. This changes only the draft, never the source message or D35 note history.

### REQ26-D36-ES04 — ES04 — Safe conversion.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Quote acquisition derives eligible semantic text/formatting/safe links from the authorized source, not arbitrary fetched remote HTML or a browser screenshot/DOM. Script/style/tracking/remote resource loads, recipient variables, protected action nodes, macros and mentions cannot execute. Literal brace tokens remain literal. Incoming nested quoted text actually included in the selected body remains visible for review; no recursive fetching of older messages. No heuristic removal of signatures or headers may silently change meaning. Where conversion must omit unsupported formatting/content, show the omission concisely and never claim the complete original was included. Unrepresentable meaningful content offers a safe qualified excerpt/normal answer path rather than a misleading success.

### REQ26-D36-ES05 — ES05 — Assets are separate.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Quoting text never acquires, reattaches, republishes or refreshes an old file, inline image, signature logo or action link. Any actual included asset or destination requires its own admitted source/recipient/retention capability. Existing source signature/address text is not automatically a second managed signature and remains within complete-message disclosure review. Source-derived structured tokens are resolved to permitted inert content; they do not activate P17 variables or domain actions in the outgoing reply.

### REQ26-D36-ES06 — ES06 — Context change.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Quoting an earlier message does not retarget the reply, widen recipients, restore removed Cc/Bcc, change inbox/assignee or update CRM. A deliberate reply-target/From/recipient change preserves the quote and authored work but invalidates affected audience/source approval and displays the actual affected excerpt/source for targeted review. D2's exact addressing model remains authoritative. An unavailable target/source never falls back to the newest email, current CRM address, forwarded private header or another tenant's cached body.

### REQ26-D36-ES07 — ES07 — Ownership.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

Support owns source qualification, draft/quote provenance, target/audience, current permissions and atomic reply admission. P17/Email Studio owns the shared canonical profile, complete message compilation, immutable presentation dependencies and exact preparation. P6 owns the sealed envelope, dispatch/reconciliation and provider facts. Quotation is human content use, not a new template publication/review workflow. P17 and the provider cannot append mutable history after staff approval or create an independent Support mailer.

### REQ26-D36-ES08 — ES08 — Source fences and recovery.

Applies to **US26-D36-03**, acceptance **AC26-D36-03-01–03**.

D16/D17 restrictions and expiry apply to quote copies, drafts, prepared material, rendered caches, known descendants and replay. Keep unrelated safe authored work. If the affected contribution cannot be separated safely, stop affected preparation until clean review; never silently redact and send. Before dispatch admission requalify current authority. After may-have-submitted/accepted, preserve actual sealed evidence and reconcile without replacement/resend/rekey. Provider outages do not authorize a different payload or alternate sender.

### REQ26-D36-ES09 — ES09 — Shared surfaces.

Applies to **US26-D36-04**, acceptance **AC26-D36-04-01–03**.

The same source and draft capability may be entered from an authorized CRM Support record. CRM navigation preserves draft/source/selection and return context, but CRM linkage does not grant Support or file disclosure rights. Requester, participant, authenticated staff, CRM contact/organization and source author remain distinct; matching email is not permission. Internal notes, guidance, member-care/giving data and merged-view neighbors do not become eligible quote sources automatically.

### REQ26-D36-ES10 — ES10 — Scope and maintainability.

Applies to **US26-D36-01**, acceptance **AC26-D36-01-01–03**.

Qualify only the necessary Reply blockquote/source metadata in the existing code-owned shared schema and purpose validation. Do not widen signature, reusable-wording, public guidance or internal-note profiles merely because Reply supports it. No second editor, general document provenance platform, source-history synchronization, AI rewriting, history default preference or tenant quote-policy builder is introduced.

## Private Reply drafts

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — Begin in the conversation

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Maya opens a Support request from its permitted CRM context and begins an answer. Opening Reply alone creates no draft. Once she makes a meaningful author change, the same composer quietly saves the complete private candidate. A small status line below the editing area says Saving, then Saved only when her newest eligible work is acknowledged. Ordinary successful saves do not create toast noise or move focus. Save now is available for deliberate checkpointing; an actual failure exposes Retry save.

She can write incomplete text, leave a required fill-in unfinished or still be choosing recipients. Saving preserves that incomplete work safely; sending requires the full validated reply. Unknown canonical content or forbidden source material is not treated as harmless incompleteness. An unfinished file upload has its own explicit status: saved text does not imply the file bytes are saved. Before navigation would destroy those local bytes, preserve the qualified existing transfer, wait for completion, or explicitly offer Leave without this unfinished attachment. Saved text survives; the missing file remains honestly pending/failed rather than falsely restored from a manifest. Combine this consequence with any unsaved-text/unknown-save warning in the same guard. No Send, internal note, task or CRM Activity results from saving.

If Maya consults CRM context without unmounting the composer, writing stays exactly where it is. If navigation would unmount it, the owner completes current IME input and saves the latest bundle. Routine success continues without a dialog. A known failure offers Retry/Stay or explicit Leave without saving these changes; an uncertain result is checked under its original operation before the UI can claim failure. If checking cannot complete, offer Stay or explicit Leave with **The earlier save may still finish; your latest unacknowledged changes may be lost**. Preserve its minimal scoped recovery handle; do not trap the person indefinitely or claim leaving canceled the write. Browser crash/close cannot guarantee the newest unsaved keystrokes; the UI must never claim otherwise.

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — A predictable place to return

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

**My drafts** remains a visible entry in the existing Support work navigation, even when empty. No badge count, urgent colour or forced landing page is needed. The page starts with the title My drafts and a short explanation: **Your saved replies across your accessible inboxes.** Product access is private to their author; separately qualified infrastructure/privacy custody remains governed by its owner rather than becoming an admin draft browser.

A restrained conceptual layout:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> My drafts
> Your saved replies across your accessible inboxes.
> 
> [Search conversation titles…]   [Inbox: All accessible inboxes] [Refresh]
> 
> Receipt question                         Donor care
> Alex · Saved 12 minutes ago                          [More]
> 
> Travel document question                 Member services
> Original request B · Review needed · Saved yesterday [More]
> 
> [Load more]

Names and requests are illustrative, not ministry research or proof of record authority. Row identifiers come from currently permitted source metadata. There is no body snippet, quote text, recipient list or thumbnail to accidentally expose private writing or trigger asset fetches. A visible requester is conversation context, not a promise they remain the draft's exact recipient. If current target and immutable draft origin differ through deliberate merged-source work, display their distinction clearly enough to resume the intended draft.

Use regular readable type, shared spacing, semantic muted metadata and clear focus/selected state. Avoid a card wall, avatar crowd, count dashboard or custom motion. On mobile, rows stack rather than force horizontal table scrolling; the full title/context remains available through wrapping or deliberate disclosure.

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — Find without reconstructing the old work view

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

The page initially covers all currently accessible Support inboxes and ordinary D3 work statuses. A draft on a Resolved conversation still appears while its own current authority permits it. Assignment and following are not ownership. A merged handling view does not merge private drafts: one row remains one stable draft from its original working slot.

Maya can filter to one inbox or search permitted conversation titles. The search label makes its scope clear; searching a private phrase typed only inside a draft does not return it. This preserves D22's indexing boundary. Unknown/failed permission or source reads are not empty results. Existing source labels are not rebuilt from unrestricted CRM facts.

Results sort by the last accepted meaningful author edit, newest first with a stable tie-break. Merely opening, selecting text, checking permissions or saving identical content does not move a row. Pages initially load20rows, bounded to50per request, with Load more to reach all eligible work. No recent-only cutoff or misleading total. While someone uses a row/menu, background data changes cannot move another row under the pointer. A quiet Results changed/Refresh control reconciles order while preserving identity and focus.

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — Resume directly, with the correct context

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.

Selecting a row opens the same conversation and existing composer with the exact saved bundle. There is no intermediate Edit draft screen and no separate document editor. Authorize the private owner and source before returning the body; do not mount a blank/default editor that is then overwritten. The saved target, audience, signature, quotations, attachment selections and pending shortcut changes come back together.

If new input or a material source/audience change requires review, show it in the normal conversation. Opening the draft does not reopen, reassign, contact anyone or execute a staged Resolve. If two original draft slots deliberately target the same B message, keep both identities and D10's B-source reply affinity; never silently combine them. Current component-wide collision review and any merge Undo destination review still apply before Send.

On desktop, focus the resumed editing context after current loading when this follows the explicit user action. On mobile, reveal the conversation and recipients first; do not force the virtual keyboard over them. Returning to My drafts restores the same-session query/filter/scroll/selected row where available. Cross-device restoration preserves acknowledged content and context, not an exact cursor position.

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — Keep editing through failures

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

The normal save state is quiet. Not saved means the latest local work is not durably confirmed; Saved never describes just an older server snapshot while new text exists. A slow network can show Saving; a lost response can show Checking save. The original operation is recovered rather than resubmitted with a new identity.

If another tab saves first, preserve the current permitted local candidate and explain **This draft changed elsewhere**. A safe current saved version can be reviewed without replacing the local editor. Staff deliberately reload the saved version or reapply their changes against the new revision. No blind overwrite, automatic text merge or live collaboration product is introduced.

If permissions/source restrictions changed, current safety wins: clear or withhold affected content and explain only allowed facts. A stale row is not permission. The system keeps independently safe authored work only where the existing privacy/retention owner can prove separation. It must not offer copying forbidden content as recovery.

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — Discard with one clear decision

Applies to **US26-D37-05**, acceptance **AC26-D37-05-01–03**.

More → **Discard draft** opens one concise shared confirmation, identifying the conversation and stating that the saved reply and its pending draft-only changes will be removed; the conversation remains. **Keep draft** cancels, **Discard draft** confirms. No typed magic phrase, extra reason, expiring Undo toast or hidden trash product is needed.

Confirm acts on the exact reviewed revision. If another tab has changed it, do not delete the newer work; return a clear changed-draft state and require review again. A successful discard removes the row and stops old autosaves from resurrecting it. Discard failure/unknown result stays visible until the original operation is resolved. A possibly admitted Send cannot be canceled by this action; follow its existing recovery state instead.

An existing draft whose text has been cleared remains saved until an explicit lifecycle action; it may say No reply text yet. This prevents implicit deletion of its audience, files or pending work. The zero-effort open/signature baseline never creates that row in the first place.

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — Send and return to work

Applies to **US26-D37-05**, acceptance **AC26-D37-05-01–03**.

Send stays inside the existing conversation review. The complete latest candidate is validated and prepared through P17, then admitted with the permitted D4 work intent. Admission consumes that exact draft generation atomically. The draft disappears as active writing only when consumption is established, not optimistically because the button was clicked.

Queued is not Delivered. An accepted reply whose transport fails is an existing send needing owner recovery; it does not return as a fresh editable draft that can accidentally be sent again. An uncertain admission keeps an operation-recovery path under the original identity. Source constraints, signature/quote provenance and immutable prepared material cannot be reset by reopening My drafts.

Support retains source/private-draft/save/admission ownership. Email Studio provides canonical authoring/schema/presentation and prepares the complete reviewed outgoing message. P6 handles actual dispatch and reconciliation. CRM uses the same source and actual outcome, with no duplicated private draft or fabricated receipt/refund/contact action. This is one connected journey across authorized surfaces.

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — Empty and exceptional states

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State                                       | Useful response                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No saved replies                            | “No saved replies yet. Replies you start in a conversation will appear here after saving.” Link back to Support conversations; no forced setup. |
| No title matches / inbox filter empty       | State the current filter and offer Clear search/All accessible inboxes. Do not imply all personal drafts are gone.                              |
| Initial loading                             | Lightweight row skeleton without private title/body placeholders; no false zero count.                                                          |
| Read failure                                | “Couldn't load your drafts” and Retry. A prior permitted list may say Out of date only while current authorization permits it.                  |
| Save failed                                 | Keep current permitted editor work; Retry save and direct failure detail. Do not reset the editor.                                              |
| Save status unknown                         | Checking save / Save status unknown with original-operation recovery; no fabricated latest Saved state.                                         |
| Conflict                                    | Preserve local work and offer deliberate current-version review/reapply; no overwrite shortcut.                                                 |
| Source review needed                        | Resume allowed content; normal source/audience review before Send. No automatic recipient refresh.                                              |
| Source/schema no longer usable              | Qualified unavailable/read-only repair state; no stale cache, stripped-body save or empty new draft.                                            |
| Discard pending or send admission uncertain | Original operation recovery. Neither disappearance nor a new row proves no send occurred.                                                       |

### REQ26-D37-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0010 — Accessibility and validation

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Use Base UI shared menu/dialog semantics, labelled inputs/controls and actual row links/buttons. Keyboard navigation into the list never triggers Send. Discard restores focus to the originating row or a predictable next row/page heading if removed. Do not move focus from routine save/status refresh; concise material status is available to assistive technology without announcing each keystroke. Test IME, screen-reader editing, keyboard-only search/open/discard, touch menus, mobile keyboard,320CSS-pixel reflow,200% text resizing,400% zoom-equivalent layout, long names, Thai/RTL and timezone dates.

The required proof includes real intended-staff find/resume/recover tasks and actual source/database/editor/send paths. Official vendor documentation informs placement and behavior. Browser image inspection was unavailable in this turn, so no screenshot-quality or authenticated vendor walkthrough claim is made; this blueprint must still be rendered and tested during implementation.

### REQ26-D37-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O01 — Five residual controls

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** One confirmed private/cross-tenant draft or metadata disclosure, unsafe restoration or sensitive body/token in logs.

**Owner:** Support security/privacy owner with engineering on-call

**Response:** Stop affected exposure/writes, preserve body-free evidence, apply owner containment/correction and verify before re-enable. Do not revoke unrelated valid work wholesale.

### REQ26-D37-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O02 — Five residual controls

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** Technical save failures over2% in a rolling15minutes with at least100eligible attempts; exclude typed user-cancel/conflict/validation/denial from that numerator.

**Owner:** Support draft engineering on-call

**Response:** Diagnose authoritative save path; preserve candidates, expose truthful recovery, scope-disable broken autosave while qualified manual saving remains possible. Low-volume failures remain visible/reportable; aggregate alert does not claim coverage.

### REQ26-D37-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O03 — Five residual controls

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** One confirmed lost acknowledged edit, false newestSaved state, duplicate active slot, resurrected discard/consumed generation or duplicate admitted send.

**Owner:** Support draft owner; P6 owner for send

**Response:** Contain affected path and reconcile original operations; fix/add regression proof before resume. Never fix with a blind new send or direct body rewrite.

### REQ26-D37-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O04 — Five residual controls

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** Finder or save-ACK p95 exceeds its release-qualified budget for two consecutive15minute windows, each at least100eligible completed requests.

**Owner:** Support performance owner

**Response:** Inspect scope/payload/index/concurrency and shared editor rendering; repair or reduce admitted work. Do not relax privacy, skip ACK or impose hidden truncation. Actual budgets are required by P31 before activation.

### REQ26-D37-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O05 — Five residual controls

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

**Signal and exact threshold:** Three independent same-task friction reports in30days, or one reproduced keyboard/AT blocker preventing save/find/resume/discard.

**Owner:** Support product/design owner and accessibility lead

**Response:** Reproduce actual journey, correct and retest; avoid adding settings/modal steps by default. Track through existing authorized work system.

### REQ26-D37-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003 — Five residual controls

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

These initial thresholds are accepted operating judgments. Actual on-call/team assignments must replace role-only ownership before activation. Use existing observability and repair tooling; no new draft analytics product. Correctness is a release gate and incident trigger, not monitoring in place of prevention.

### REQ26-D37-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0004 — Required implementation sequence and limits

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

1. Qualify current actor/tenant/source contracts and the private canonical draft plus immutable operation/terminal evidence. Close the public-message writer/read bypasses first.
2. Implement and test atomic whole-bundle create/save/discard, current source/retention gates and consumedSend linkage, including same-op/no-op/concurrency and unknown results.
3. Qualify the shared Tiptap closure and canonical validation; add the narrow autosave/ACK/hydration/navigation controller without a collaboration platform.
4. Add metadata-only My drafts and existing-reader resume using shared Base UI/Maia; preserve CRM/list context.
5. Run P01–P32 and capture actual limits, versions, plans and role/browser/staff evidence before activation. Stage rollout by eligible cohort with owner kill switches and compatible roll-forward.

The initial20/50row query bounds and750ms/5sautosave attempt timings are exact accepted interface/engineering limits, not source-provider constraints. D23's broader numeric payload/operation profile and D17's actual retention/custody inventory remain required qualified dependencies; no invented default lifetime replaces them. No runtime task is performed by this document.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0005 — T01 — Existing owner, one coherent semantic draft

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

My drafts reads the current person's currently authorized, server-saved external Reply drafts. Each draft remains one stable Support-owned identity with original source context and owner. The saved candidate atomically includes the versioned canonical Tiptap document, explicit reply target/audience, governed signature choice/copy, quote and wording dependencies, durable attachment references, staged D4/D24 work and the revisions necessary for later current review. HTML/plain text are derived message artifacts, not independent draft authority. Save, list and resume never invoke P17 preparation or P6 delivery.

The UI returns to that same draft whether entered from My drafts, the ordinary Support reader or the authorized CRM entry. A new destination does not justify a provider draft, CRM activity, Email Studio reusable candidate or copied body table. Raw browser `File` objects, temporary blob URLs and expiring download URLs cannot serve as cross-device attachment references; unfinished transfer state must remain explicit.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0006 — T02 — Meaningful changes, not every editor event

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

Create a durable draft only after the first meaningful deliberate change; initialization, ordinary signature/default audience seeding, focus, selection and mere viewing do not create one. Changes to the authored body, deliberate audience/target/signature choice, staged files or work plan participate in the semantic candidate. Once a durable draft exists, deliberately making its body blank is a normal saved revision, not an implicit Discard.

Use canonical semantic comparison to distinguish a content change from a `setEditable` update, hydration, selection, caret movement or an unchanged normalized document. Preserve deliberate body-less work such as attachment/audience/staged intent according to the source owner; empty-body send validation is a separate decision. Do not rely only on editor `isEmpty`, a text string or a debounced keystroke callback.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0007 — T03 — A small autosave coordinator, with honest timing

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

For a valid authorized foreground draft, schedule a coalesced save after750ms of quiet and attempt a checkpoint within5seconds of continuing non-composing change when online and no earlier write outcome is unresolved. These are accepted Asym implementation tuning values, not vendor standards or durable-save guarantees. Save now flushes the latest stable candidate through the same owner command. Persist no keystroke history or server-side editor transaction log.

Keep one in-flight write per draft session and at most one latest pending candidate, coalescing obsolete intermediates. A slow write or unknown result cannot trigger concurrent speculative saves to meet5seconds. Retry a failed/ambiguous operation with its original identity; do not change the captured payload under that identity. After reconciliation, submit the newer candidate as a new conditional operation if it remains permitted. Network, server latency, invalidity and active composition suspend the attempt bound; show the truthful state instead of claiming Saved. Limits and capacity must be qualified with the final canonical document budgets before activation.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0008 — T04 — Saved belongs to an exact acknowledged candidate

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

Saving and Saved refer to the exact draft identity and acknowledged semantic revision. A response for an older local candidate may advance the known server checkpoint but cannot mark newer local work Saved, overwrite its content, move its caret or change its audience. A server refusal, timeout, offline condition or conflict remains visible with preserved currently permitted work.

The same receipt feeds the authorized My drafts metadata projection. Update its saved timestamp only for an actual semantic checkpoint; opening, hydration, focus, no-op saves and background reads do not move a draft to the top. The view must distinguish a server-saved checkpoint from newer session-only changes. Optimistic acknowledgement is inappropriate for the Saved label even when optimistic local typing is natural.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0009 — T05 — Conditional revision, not collaborative drafting

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Every save includes the expected owner revision and immutable operation identity; tenant and actor come from trusted server context. A same-person second tab/device cannot silently overwrite a newer candidate. A conflict preserves both currently permitted versions long enough for a focused choice or manual reconciliation of the same draft; do not introduce shared co-editing, Yjs, CRDT history or a team takeover mechanism.

One active draft per source/profile slot does not mean one tab lease or locked editing. Compare the complete semantic bundle, not body alone. Loading current server work is explicit when it would replace dirty local work. Keeping local work requires current validation against the newly read revision; it cannot be a blind force-write or bypass a restriction/previous send. Separate permitted side-by-side text for manual reconciliation from exposing drafts to another teammate or permanently creating a version-history product.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0010 — T06 — Restoration is gated before editor initialization

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.

Fetch and authorize the exact draft through the source owner; validate the original versioned envelope and JSON before mounting a writable editor. Hold the composer in a named loading state until a qualified baseline is available. An access error, failed read, unsupported schema or missing result is not an empty new draft.

Bind responses to tenant, principal, draft identity, source topology and local session generation. A late response for another draft is dropped. Never apply a background query refresh into a dirty active editor. Set initial content once for the accepted draft baseline, using `emitUpdate:false` for any intentional hydration and a non-user-change marker in the owner coordinator. Explicit acceptance of a replacement may reset relevant editor history; silent background restore may not.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0011 — T07 — Schema errors stop writing; original bytes remain authoritative

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.
