Unknown schema versions, keys, nodes, marks, attributes, protected/source metadata and incompatible source profiles must fail original-input validation before Tiptap normalization. Preserve the owner's original retained candidate and show a useful read-only Needs update or repair state. A contentError handler stops writable initialization, autosave and send. It cannot persist stripped or empty replacement content.

The official documentation describes permissive normalization for some ordinary editing use cases. That conflicts with Asym's D23/D36 protected semantics: attributes can carry quote/source/plan meaning that must not silently disappear. Server validation is independently required; editor parsing is not RLS, source-use authorization or a safe metadata validator. A later migration creates the qualified new candidate with explicit loss handling, rather than accepting an old client writer after a schema downgrade.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0012 — T08 — Stable identity, safe mode separation and normal Undo

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Keep the editor instance stable while editing the same qualified draft; typing, saved timestamps, list refreshes, resizing and read preference changes do not remount it. Treat tenant/principal/draft/purpose/schema-generation changes as explicit identity transitions with preserved safe working state or required clearing. Do not reuse a history stack across Reply and Note or unrelated source/draft identities.

Use the existing shared editor/context in the shared UI package. A key can express identity but is not a persistence mechanism: coordinator state must survive permitted navigation before an editor unmount. Normal Undo/Redo within the active identity remains useful and D24 body/plan Undo remains coherent. Reopening a saved candidate does not require durable ProseMirror undo history or cursor synchronization across devices. Same-session caret/scroll restoration may be retained ephemerally when the exact document revision still matches; otherwise choose a stable useful position without stealing focus from review controls.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0013 — T09 — IME and navigation flush preserve actual committed input

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Do not send, switch away destructively or programmatically replace content while input-method composition is active. Respect keyboard composition and previously handled events; use the editor's supported composition state. After composition commits, capture the resulting committed editor document before an explicit Save/Send or guarded route transition proceeds.

The inspected ProseMirror-view1.41.8 `src/the qualified source contract documents Safari's near-composition Enter behavior. Its `compositionend` handler at502–511 may flush pending DOM work in a microtask, so an immediate snapshot in a raw compositionend callback is insufficient proof. Use qualified supported integration and real Chinese/Japanese/Korean/Thai input, mobile virtual keyboards and browser tests. Do not copy private internal500ms/20ms timing constants into product behavior or create a custom IME engine. Preserve original native editor handling and add a narrow qualified primary-action guard.

Permitted in-app navigation retains and flushes safe dirty work through the same owner before calling it Saved. When only session-local unsaved work remains, provide a clear keep-editing/leave consequence rather than silently clearing it. Browser/OS termination recovery is limited to confirmed saves; visibility flush and beforeunload warnings are best-effort. No automatic offline send or persistent browser outbox is added.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0014 — T10 — Safety overrides recovery, without hidden reappearance

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Current access loss, tenant/principal/logout transition, source privacy restriction and content expiry win over autosave, Undo, browser state, caches and late responses. Stop forbidden writes and clear unavailable local representations; protect source-derived data under D16/D17/D36. A protected source or completed discard cannot reappear through an old save acknowledgement, stale draft list, browser back or replay.

Preserve independently permitted authored content where the accepted source contract can safely separate it. Do not claim arbitrary text can always be separated from restricted source-derived content. Inaccessible drafts do not reveal subject, snippet, count or identity merely because the person previously authored them. Minimal owner-authorized operation recovery may remain available as already qualified by D4/D35; that is different from retaining the private body.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0015 — T11 — Save/resume never executes staged work

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.

Restoring the draft preserves D2's exact reply target/audience, D23 signature, D36 quotation provenance and D4/D24 staged plan; it does not retarget to the newest message, refresh to latest wording/signature, change recipients from CRM, acquire files, assign staff, resolve the request, notify mentions or run the work plan. Deliberate Send performs current preparation/admission review against current actor, topology and dependencies.

Changing composition mode preserves separate working drafts and neutralizes incompatible staged actions as already defined. Q37 covers saved external Reply discovery. It creates neither durable new-note drafts by inference nor persistence for D35's local edit of an already-posted note. Notes keep their existing working-state behavior.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0016 — T12 — Submission recovery is distinct from ordinary drafts

Applies to **US26-D37-05**, acceptance **AC26-D37-05-01–03**.

An unresolved Send belongs to the original D4/P6 effect-recovery path, even if safe working content is still retained. It is not a fresh unsent draft with a new Send button. Saving or opening My drafts cannot cancel an admitted email, duplicate its action, reset dispatch identity or retry all recipients.

Definitive rejection before admission may restore ordinary editing after reconciliation. Admission closes/consumes the submitted draft revision and links the immutable operation outcome; provider delay/failure does not recreate that draft or undo its Support work. New writing after an admitted reply starts another qualified draft. My drafts may show a clearly separate owner-authorized recovery affordance where needed, but it must not become a second outbox or delivery state machine.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0017 — T13 — Metadata-only list, one editor when resumed

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.

The My drafts list uses currently authorized metadata and control facts; it mounts no live Tiptap editor for each row and does not fetch full private bodies merely to show a subject, timestamp, inbox or attachment count. D22 private-body search exclusion remains intact. Open one row to load its full qualified candidate in the existing conversation reader.

Keep the list client independent of editor transaction rendering. The active editor should have stable extensions/callback identity and small selector subscriptions; `useEditorState` is appropriate for formatting controls. Counts/list rerenders must not remount the document or interrupt input. Shared safe static rendering is for actual read-only body surfaces; a metadata list needs neither a second rich-text renderer nor a static-renderer body fetch. This reduces payload and accidental disclosure while keeping narrow/mobile navigation quick.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0018 — T14 — One modest stack and qualified dependency closure

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Use the existing Next.js client boundary, shared Tiptap3 editor, source-owned Support API, approved browser read layer and Supabase/Postgres persistence. Do not add Tiptap Cloud, paid snapshots, Yjs, a generic workflow/draft service, provider-draft synchronization, cross-user awareness payloads containing draft text or a second Email Studio draft library for this view.

The composable API may improve the shared editor at its normal qualified maintenance boundary; My drafts does not depend on a provider rewrite. Preserve `immediatelyRender:false`, original-input checks and exact base-maia. Resolve actual peer/version/schema/runtime compatibility before activating the writer. Test installed/upgraded closure in the implementation change; do not opportunistically install latest into the worktree during research.

### REQ26-D37-TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0019 — Email Studio and CRM seam in full

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Support owns the private human reply draft, source identity, current tenant/principal checks, save revision/operation, complete candidate and later human admission. P17/Email Studio owns governed content schema, wording/signature publication and the shared compiler/preparation of a complete reviewed message. P6 owns sealed transport, per-recipient evidence, provider reconciliation and actual delivery history. Tiptap is an authoring implementation, not another owner or provider integration.

My drafts has no preparation side effect. Autosave must not repeatedly compile/prepare outgoing payloads, renew human preparation custody, create a system-message key, publish a Saved Section or contact Resend. P17's source-document authoring autosave and Support's human draft checkpoint use sound shared primitives where appropriate but remain separate domain aggregates. Support owns the draft lifecycle; Email Studio's reusable library does not enumerate private human drafts.

The same authorized Support reader/composer is reachable from CRM with its return context preserved. CRM stores no copied draft body or private draft activity and gains no private draft count from an association. Requester/contact, sender endpoint, authenticated draft owner, support worker and CRM owner remain distinct. A saved draft may refer to an existing source that later merges/moves; retain its original source/target and reauthorize rather than silently reassociating it. Neither the draft nor its content proves a giving/contact/member-care action occurred.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — C01 — Finder identity and scope

Applies to **US26-D37-01**, acceptance **AC26-D37-01-01–03**.

My drafts is a built-in private Support view over the current actor's saved external Reply drafts in the currently selected tenant. It includes all currently accessible Support inboxes and all D3 work statuses by default. It is not an assignee queue, shared saved-view definition, contact history, second authoring surface, shared draft store or a new default landing page. Do not create a draft by merely opening the composer or adding its automatic baseline signature.

Use current permissions for every row and field. No other worker's draft, body, count or existence is discoverable by assignment, following, D34 awareness, inbox membership, CRM relation, ordinary admin role or a query guessed from a URL. Separately qualified infrastructure custody is not a product administrator's My drafts browsing capability.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — C02 — One source-owned draft and cardinality

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Maintain one active external Reply draft per tenant, real profile owner and original Support source. Its stable draft identity remains the same through saves, explicit D2 retargeting and cross-surface entry. A merged continuing conversation is a navigation destination, not draft identity: distinct originals may yield distinct drafts in one combined reader. Merge/Undo never merges bodies, transfers ownership or deduplicates by root, subject or email.

The logical active key includes fixed `purpose=external_reply`; do not expose a generic draft-type framework merely to store that fact. Once a draft is sent/admitted or deliberately discarded, a subsequent new reply gets a new draft identity. Persist the original identity even if the displayed conversation title/root changes. Two concurrent first saves must resolve to one active draft or a real conflict, never two rows or silent overwrite of different documents. Body equality alone does not establish same human intent.

**Explicit cross-original retargeting is reconciled with D2/D10 as follows.** “The draft's original is its immutable private working-slot origin, not an instruction to file an eventual reply under that origin. An explicit D2 target change within the currently authorized combined context preserves the same draft, owner, body and protected dependencies, rechecks the actual target/audience and reviews changed context. The selected target's original owns any admitted reply, as D10 requires. Thus a draft begun at A and deliberately targeted to a message from B is admitted once at B and handled through B's then-current qualified root. Do not rehome the private slot, combine it with another draft or rewrite original message affinity.

Different original-bound drafts may deliberately point to the same target; their separate existence is not duplicate-send authority. Each keeps its own content and identity and the existing component-wide send-collision/review guard applies. Reply navigation that requests an existing draft resumes that exact private draft; it never silently imports another draft merely because targets match. If topology changes separate the private origin and target, preserve writing but require explicit current destination/context review before resuming Send against the target's current handling component. Revalidate necessary origin, target, content and actual current component authority; never transparently act on the stale former group. D16/D17 source dependencies remain exact, and native-reply retention admission belongs to the selected target original, not the finder slot.

This is an application of D10-R07, its lifecycle example “Reply referencing an original B message while B is handled in A,” and D10-P13/P17. It avoids a new copy/transfer/replace-draft workflow. The implementation must retain two distinguishable references where they differ; a single ambiguous `conversation_id` must not silently stand for private draft origin, reply source and current root.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — C03 — Actual types and trusted actor

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Use UUID tenant/profile/auth/membership endpoints and TEXT original conversation/message/agent endpoints where those are the actual owning keys. A new draft ID may use the qualified source-owned ID convention, but changing existing Support TEXT IDs to UUID is not part of this decision. Derive tenant, real actor/profile, current selected acting scope, applicable active membership and attribution from trusted shared server context. Do not accept owner, author, role, approval, admitted-send or tenant-control fields from the caller.

The durable owner is the qualified real profile, not an email address, current assignee, CRM Party, selected directory agent or transient membership row. Current membership authorizes use; it does not transfer ownership. Tenant/profile consistency must be proven through the platform's actual membership mapping, not `profiles.tenant_id` equality that accidentally excludes legitimate multi-tenant membership. Where Support agent representation is necessary, resolve the current qualified explicit profile/auth mapping and reject ambiguous legacy mappings. Shared email or email reuse proves neither identity nor authority.

Tenant, owner profile, original source, draft ID, purpose and schema/head revision are non-null on qualified active drafts. A reply-target email reference may be null for an explicitly qualified first response to a phone/form-origin source; null is not permission to guess from current contact data. Conditional checks forbid email-reply states that lack their required target. Use positive bounded revision values and trusted UTC timestamps; terminal facts cannot revert to editable through a generic update. Deleting a profile/original/inbox must not incidentally cascade away required terminal/send/source evidence or transfer a body to a new owner. Qualified offboarding performs actual custody/cleanup before any permitted endpoint retirement.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0008 — C04 — Canonical persisted unit

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Save the draft's canonical document and compatible schema/profile version, original/target references, explicit audience and its review generation, governed signature state, attachment manifest, quote/source dependencies, staged work plan and draft revision as one atomic effect. The command never reports Saved after a body-only write. Optional local cursor, viewport and picker state are presentation aids rather than mail authority.

Source/body/preparation objects remain distinct. Derived HTML/plain text may be caches under exact canonical generation, not independently writable truth. Reference IDs must use same-tenant foreign keys to actual owning endpoints; polymorphic strings, unchecked JSON claims or cross-tenant foreign keys by ID alone do not establish relationships. Closed schema validation and size/depth/content rules protect canonical JSON. Do not put repeated full snapshots in durable audit/operation receipts.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0009 — C05 — Conditional save, no-op and unknown result

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Each accepted save conditions on the expected draft revision and binds a stable operation identity to the exact normalized semantic command. Retrying that identity returns its original outcome or conflicts if its meaning changed. An identical canonical no-op changes neither draft revision nor human-updated ordering time, but its resolved operation cannot later be reused to change content. Stale saves cannot overwrite newer work, a terminal draft or current source restrictions.

Coalesce local editor changes with one in-flight save and the latest waiting canonical state, keeping the previously confirmed revision distinct from local unsaved text. Only a confirmed server outcome earns Saved. A request timeout yields save result unknown, not certain failure or permission to insert another draft. Recover the original operation before advancing the expected revision. Minimal body-free, scope-bound operation handles survive navigation and reconnect; they are not bearer permissions and must not carry recipients/body in URL or analytics.

The UI can retain newer safe local text while reconciling an older accepted revision. A server acceptance must not overwrite the newer editor generation. Record source/draft operation results with the existing owner mechanism and a qualified finite replay horizon; do not invent a per-keystroke event store.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0010 — C06 — Resume and conflict

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.

Opening a row resolves the same canonical draft under current owner/source authority, then restores its exact saved composition context. Loading or failed fetches are not absence and must not create a new empty draft. Late load/save/refetch responses for another actor, tenant, original, draft or editor generation cannot hydrate the current editor. An older browser tab cannot autosave over a newer confirmed revision.

On conflict preserve independently safe local writing, show the latest saved state for deliberate review and use the existing revision reconciliation rather than automatic last-write-wins, collaborative merging or forced lease/takeover. Opening the same draft elsewhere is allowed; ownership is not a locking protocol. Retargeting/new input/recipient changes still use D2/D4 review. Reopening a Resolved conversation through the finder does not reopen work, reset timers, assign/follow, execute the staged plan or imply successful domain action.

A missing list row is not evidence that a save failed, a send succeeded or a discard completed. Reconcile the original operation through its current authorized typed result. Exact pending recovery may be shown separately from ordinary editable drafts using the existing recovery treatment; after known accepted admission, preserve only the permitted result/continuation needed to explain the actual state. Discovery failure cannot mint replacement send authority.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0011 — C07 — Save and Send are distinct boundaries

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

A private saved draft remains unpublished writing. Deliberate Send freezes the exact reviewed draft revision through P17 preparation, then Support atomically admits the source reply, staged local work effect and P6 dispatch intent according to D4. Accepted admission consumes that draft exactly once and removes its ordinary resumable entry; provider delivery remains a separate factual status.

Race save/discard against preparation/admission by expected generation and the shared owner fences. A stale autosave cannot recreate a consumed draft. A lost send-admission response keeps the exact operation in recovery and cannot advertise an ordinary Send again path. An admitted queued, failed, bounced, delivered or indeterminate envelope does not reappear as an editable draft merely because the provider has not confirmed delivery. A definite pre-admission rejection may leave the same draft editable; an uncertain rejection cannot. New writing after completed admission is a new draft, and never implicit retry of the consumed one.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0012 — C08 — Discard is one guarded local-source effect

Applies to **US26-D37-05**, acceptance **AC26-D37-05-01–03**.

Offer explicit Discard draft for a saved draft with one plain-language confirmation. Acceptance conditionally ends the exact current draft generation, withdraws its draft-owned body/reference grants and ends its ordinary finder entry. Retain only qualified body-free terminal/replay evidence to reject late saves and replayed creates. Do not create a trash mailbox, hidden retained body, timer-based restore service, duplicate message or normal communication event.

A newer saved revision or send admission wins a race by conflict rather than silently discarding work or canceling a submitted envelope. An unknown discard result reconciles that operation before the client retries or clears recoverable safe local work. Draft-owned staged uploads enter the existing reference-aware cleanup obligation; originals/shared authorized blobs and independent admitted-send material are not deleted by a draft cascade. Actual content destruction remains D16/D17/owner governed, so the ordinary UI does not claim it erased every backup or shared object immediately.

Use the same already-scoped operation identity for first create/save. After discard, replay of the old create is terminal even though the active uniqueness slot is free. A deliberate new composer has a new draft intent. Removing all editable text from an existing saved draft is a user change, not automatic deletion: preserve intentional audience/attachment/quote/work-plan state until explicit discard. No meaningful initial change means no durable draft.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0013 — C09 — Private read query and pagination

Applies to **US26-D37-01**, acceptance **AC26-D37-01-01–03**.

List only permitted safe metadata: stable draft/source reference, current permitted conversation title, permitted requester label if available, inbox, human saved-update time and typed actionable state. Do not fetch the draft document, private recipient list, filenames or quote bodies to render the finder. Private bodies remain excluded from D22 ordinary search and general timeline/CRM read projections.

The final finder searches only qualified current conversation titles, with a separate explicit inbox filter; permitted requester context is display-only here. Do not search private draft bodies, private recipients or restricted CRM fields. Resolve complete current authorization and effective filters before pagination; use deterministic ordering by actual accepted human draft update and stable draft ID tie-break. Do not use generic `updated_at` changed by cleanup/retry/refetch, whole-tenant message loading, pre-filter limits, recent-only cutoff or client filtering of hidden rows. Use keyset pagination and relevant `(tenant,owner,lifecycle,saved_at,id)` and tenant/source indexes qualified against actual plans. No initial sidebar count is required. Any later count must use the same authorized semantics and count drafts, not merged roots or Open work.

Refreshing results is not an instruction to move focus, selected draft, route or scroll. A visible filter/empty state must distinguish no saved drafts, no matching drafts, loading, access loss and failed loading. No phantom unavailable row should reveal a draft/source the actor is no longer allowed to discover.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0014 — C10 — Effective database and Storage closure

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Canonical draft writes remain commands in the shared API owner; thin app routes and qualified authorized read hooks reuse that boundary. No anonymous/raw authenticated DML may alter canonical private body, owner, tenant, original, lifecycle, source dependencies, revision or accepted-send evidence. Enable appropriate RLS, restrict grants and function execution, and prove private owner/current-source predicates for every exposed read.

Do not overlay private semantics on current broad `support_messages` policies without retiring the conflicting paths. A source-owned draft relation is the clean minimal direction; if physical reuse is justified later, equal isolation must be demonstrated across raw Data API, timeline, search, export, Realtime and attachment routes, with direct broad writes closed. Invoker views obey RLS; any definer/function/service role path needs explicit narrow authority, fixed trusted search_path and tested grants. Effective USING and WITH CHECK must prevent transforming allowed rows into another tenant/owner/source/published-message state. Attachments and signed delivery paths need independent current draft-owner/source authority; a private row pointing at a public URL is not private.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0015 — C11 — Privacy, source lifetime and departure

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Apply D16/D17 source restriction/expiry to draft-derived content, metadata, recipients, cached representations, editor undo/restoration and staged attachments. Draft save/open/autosave is not a native admission, real work purpose or retention renewal. Bind the draft content inventory to its original Support source generation and owner-qualified lifetime; use the existing policy and oldest-content review rather than a new indefinite private archive or a seven-day prepared-material timer.

D4's seven-day maximum human-reply preparation is not a draft lifetime. Independently safe authored work may be retained only under its own qualified draft purpose; never keep restricted copies through a generic preserve-draft promise. When separable, remove affected source-derived material and preserve safe work for current review; when mapping is uncertain, affected material remains unavailable until clean review. Do not silently rewrite and send a cleaned sealed message.

Loss of membership/source access suppresses finder rows and future reads/writes immediately at the authority boundary, even if cached lists or workers lag. Reauthorization can restore only still-retained currently lawful material to the same durable person, not resurrect erased content. Departure or email reassignment does not transfer a private draft to an administrator/assignee/replacement user. Use actual offboarding/privacy custody; no new admin-inbox exception. Restore source stops and terminal command fences before restoring data or accepting an older browser/client.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0016 — C12 — CRM and Email Studio seam

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Support and the CRM's authorized Support entry resume the same private canonical draft and original source. Preserve the caller's CRM record/list/scroll return context; the CRM record anchor cannot silently broaden because a draft list covers other inboxes. Deliberate Open in Support Hub may broaden navigation as already allowed, with the previous CRM return preserved. No draft discovery/save/discard creates a CRM note, Activity, contact, address update, ownership transfer, follow, assignment or giving/receipt/refund result.

Support owns human private draft persistence, audience/source checks and admission. Email Studio/P17 owns governed reusable content/schema/signature/presentation and complete immutable preparation; it does not own a second human draft copy. P6 owns actual sealed dispatch/reconciliation and per-recipient evidence. Listing, saving or resuming creates no P17 delivery material, calls no Resend draft/send API, publishes no template and does not turn donor correspondence into a system-message catalog entry. D35 posted-note editing and unsent new-note working state remain separate.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0017 — C13 — Outage and navigation

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Before app-controlled navigation would discard dirty writing, complete its pending qualified save or retain scoped working state and expose a recoverable failure. Do not claim server persistence from an optimistic cache, unload beacon, localStorage or closed-tab event. A browser crash or network outage before server acknowledgement can lose unconfirmed changes; Saved refers only to the confirmed canonical revision.

A status lookup that remains unknown must not trap navigation: offer Stay or explicit Leave with the earlier-save-may-finish/latest-unacknowledged-changes-may-be-lost explanation, retaining the original scoped operation handle. Leaving proves neither cancellation nor nonacceptance. Local-only unfinished upload bytes also need the shared navigation guard even when text is saved; keep a qualified transfer alive, wait or explicitly abandon that attachment without claiming the manifest can restore it. The existing automatic-save cadence may reduce exposure, but it is not an offline guarantee. No durable browser body store/offline outbox or hidden pending send is introduced. Cancel in-flight fetches and reject obsolete results on tenant/account change. Clear or make inaccessible sensitive state including caches, editor undo and mounted content when scope or authorization changes. Same-user tenant switches need explicit handling, not only logout cleanup. Ordinary drafting continues when the finder alone is down; ordinary CRM work continues when Support is unavailable.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0018 — C14 — Migration, activation and bounded proof

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Qualify owner/source/auth mapping, canonical draft transaction, compatibility profile, private read projection, source restriction/retention inventory and all old writers/readers before enabling My drafts. Never backfill owner from JSON author/email, current assignee or first agent, and never invent a missing original/audience from current CRM context. Proven legacy drafts can migrate idempotently with their original meaning; unknown authorship/source remains restricted reconciliation with an accountable owner and finite existing custody obligation.

Multiple legacy draft rows cannot be silently collapsed as if they were revisions; preserve evidence and require qualified reconciliation. Migrate while inactive; fingerprint source inputs and persist mapping exactly once, preserve queued/sent facts, make old incompatible writers fail closed and verify rollback/new-code-old-schema/old-code-new-schema behavior. A feature stop disables new finder/save behavior as appropriate without deleting drafts, reopening broad readers or disabling accepted-send recovery. After new canonical data exists, roll forward rather than roll back to a serializer that strips unknown quote/signature nodes. No unsupported source or draft is silently parsed, stripped and autosaved.

### REQ26-D37-DATA_CONTRACT-S0019 — Minimal logical data footprint

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

These are required logical constraints; physical table naming remains with the owning module. One private draft relation with typed immutable tenant/owner/original/purpose identity, mutable canonical current head, closed lifecycle and revision; the existing draft-bound file/reference/dependency records; and the existing command-result/terminal evidence mechanism. Every extra persisted projection has a declared source and cleanup owner. No dedicated draft version-history product, global workflow store, Yjs document service or recipient synchronization database is justified.

Meaningful states are: locally changed but not acknowledged; saving; confirmed saved; definite save failure; uncertain save outcome; revision conflict; awaiting exact send admission result; consumed by accepted send; deliberately discarded; restricted/expired. The first six include local transport/presentation states and need not all be SQL enum values. Source availability is an orthogonal authoritative condition; it is not encoded merely by hiding the UI. Closed server lifecycle need only represent the true durable source states and immutable operation relationships.

### REQ26-D37-R01 — D37-R01 — Scope, need and strongest alternative

Applies to **US26-D37-01**, acceptance **AC26-D37-01-01–03**.

My drafts is the primary finder for saved, unsent Support Reply drafts, with direct restoration when returning to a known conversation. The accepted new-Note extension uses the same finder with independent purpose and private identity. Posted-note correction working state remains local. No additional My draft view filter, compact parallel picker, shared drafting, approvals, scheduled sends, AI drafts, outbound prospecting or product-wide My work surface is introduced.

### REQ26-D37-R02 — D37-R02 — Stable entry and restrained information architecture

Applies to **US26-D37-01**, acceptance **AC26-D37-01-01–03**.

Place **My drafts** in Support's existing conversation/work navigation group, separate from shared/saved work views and Email Studio authoring. Keep it discoverable when empty; do not make the navigation appear/disappear as someone types or force it as the landing page. Use the same name on narrow screens. Start without a sidebar count, red urgency badge, global reminder or extra overview tile. A source-qualified personal **Draft** indicator on an already rendered conversation may link to that exact own draft; it is not a shared indicator or proof of unsaved local text. Do not add the unchosen global filter/picker product merely to provide this modest inline continuity.

### REQ26-D37-R03 — D37-R03 — Complete personal population, not work status

Applies to **US26-D37-01**, acceptance **AC26-D37-01-01–03**.

The default scope is the current actor in the current tenant and all currently accessible Support inboxes. Include every eligible active saved Reply draft regardless of Open, Waiting, Resolved, assignment or current ordinary view. Source access/privacy/retention and actual draft lifecycle still decide eligibility. One row represents one canonical draft, not one merged handling root or one CRM person. Merged original conversations may therefore have separate own drafts; preserve original source identity and enough permitted context to distinguish them. Do not hide unfinished writing merely because a colleague resolved, moved or reassigned the conversation. Opening a draft never changes that work state.

### REQ26-D37-R04 — D37-R04 — Readable rows, minimal controls

Applies to **US26-D37-01**, acceptance **AC26-D37-01-01–03**.

Use compact responsive rows with permitted conversation title, current qualified source/inbox identification, authoritative **Saved [time]**, and a concise existing-state label only when it changes the next action. Use an admitted conversation/requester display projection, never the draft body's first line or an unrestricted CRM lookup. Missing/permitted redacted titles use the owner's neutral label, not stale cached content. Each row opens directly; no separate Edit or Load screen. A separate accessible action menu offers **Discard draft**. Do not place Send, Send all, bulk discard, new compose, rich-text previews or mounted editors in the list. Long titles wrap appropriately, and a saved time exposes localized absolute time and zone without requiring hover.

### REQ26-D37-R05 — D37-R05 — Scoped search, filtering, ordering and pagination

Applies to **US26-D37-01**, acceptance **AC26-D37-01-01–03**.

Provide **Inbox: All accessible inboxes / one authorized inbox**, **Search conversation titles**, and Refresh. Search uses the existing qualified title/source search semantics and index eligibility; it does not search draft prose, private recipients, quote bodies or restricted CRM fields. Do not introduce a new draft-body corpus, direct-scan bypass or arbitrary saved-view grammar. Blank search returns the scoped personal list. Default ordering is last accepted meaningful author edit descending, then stable draft ID; reads, same-content saves, safety checks and worker callbacks do not make a draft recent. Use server keyset pagination, initially20rows, maximum50 per request, no truncation of the overall population. Those are accepted UI/query bounds, not a total draft limit. No exact total count is required. Show honest loaded-result information and Load more; preserve focused row/scroll and expose Refresh/Results changed rather than reorder under a pointer. Existing D22 200ms debounce/IME/explicit Enter behavior may be reused for this title query.

### REQ26-D37-R06 — D37-R06 — Trusted owner and stable cardinality

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

A saved Reply draft has one immutable original source, tenant and real staff owner plus a stable identity and current revision. Enforce at most one active external Reply draft per tenant, trusted owner and original conversation. Explicit D2 retarget changes the current target inside that same draft under review; it does not silently create a second draft. Merge/unmerge uses original identities and never collapses private drafts by continuing root, email or CRM Party. A deliberate new draft after accepted send/discard uses a new lifecycle identity/generation; old writers cannot recreate a terminal one. Preserve actual TEXT source IDs and UUID tenant/profile/auth relationships rather than assuming they are interchangeable.

The immutable draft origin is its private working-slot anchor, not published reply source affinity. D10 permits explicitly targeting a B message while working in merged A: preserve the draft's stable origin, content and identity, show the distinct current target/source, and revalidate both required source dependencies. The actual target B determines reply admission/source affinity under D10, never the draft anchor A. Two independently anchored drafts may deliberately target B; existing component-wide collision review still prevents stale double handling. Merge Undo/current access may invalidate this cross-source target and require review, without silently rehoming the draft, copying it into another active slot or publishing the reply under A.

### REQ26-D37-R07 — D37-R07 — Meaningful creation without phantom drafts

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

Opening Reply, focusing/selecting text, reading a source, hydration, loading a preference or seeding the normal signature creates no persistent draft and no My drafts row. First deliberate meaningful author change to the draft bundle may create it: prose/formatting, quote/wording insertion, intentional audience/target/subject/signature omission, admitted attachment selection or staged shortcut work. Preserve incomplete work rather than requiring send-ready content. Once a draft exists, clearing its body does not silently discard it, erase the audience/plan or reset its lifecycle; it remains with an honest **No reply text yet** state if needed until Send or explicit Discard. A default signature alone in a newly opened empty composer remains non-draft baseline. Exact canonical equivalence and creation intent are server-validated, not a browser text-length guess.

### REQ26-D37-R08 — D37-R08 — Quiet bounded autosave

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

Save eligible user changes automatically after750ms of quiet, with an attempt by5seconds after the first unsaved eligible change during continuous input. These are accepted engineering scheduling targets in a foreground, online, authorized, valid-schema, non-IME-composing editor—not durable-save latency promises. Coalesce to the latest coherent bundle, with at most one in-flight save per active draft controller. Do not start a competing save while the previous result is unresolved. A delayed, offline, background-throttled or blocked editor shows truthful status and saves when eligible again; elapsed time does not manufacture Saved. Selection/focus/toolbar inspection/hydration/no-op transactions are not saves. **Save now** flushes deliberately when changes exist, and **Retry save** repairs an eligible failure; neither sends or resets the editor. Reuse one shared private-draft controller, not a timer on every list row.

### REQ26-D37-R09 — D37-R09 — Draft-safe content is not send-ready content

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

The save command admits a structurally valid, purpose-qualified incomplete draft, including absent audience, incomplete authored text and explicit unresolved typed fill-ins. It does not require a final email address, complete message or executable work-plan eligibility merely to preserve writing. Conversely, arbitrary/unknown canonical nodes, invalid protected source metadata, unsafe links/assets or expired/restricted material are not harmless incompleteness. Prevalidate the full document and closed metadata schema before Tiptap normalization; retain an explicitly typed missing/invalid-for-send state where appropriate. Do not accept arbitrary raw recipient blobs or HTML as a back door. Real address, content, source/disclosure, attachment and staged-action requirements still block preparation/admission at Send. Saving never executes variables, mentions, shortcuts or source actions.

### REQ26-D37-R10 — D37-R10 — One atomic bundle and exact acknowledgment

Applies to **US26-D37-02**, acceptance **AC26-D37-02-01–03**.

Persist canonical structured document, explicit target/audience and action provenance, managed signature/wording/quotation references, attachment-selection manifest, staged shortcut plan, owner/schema/source generations and draft revision atomically. A body-only save cannot report Saved. Server context derives tenant/real actor and validates every reference. The browser binds an acknowledgment to the exact submitted operation and client draft generation. **Saved** means the newest eligible local bundle is durably acknowledged; an older successful acknowledgment may advance the known base but never marks later typing Saved or overwrites it. A canonical no-op produces no new content revision or recency time, while its operation/result identity still remains unambiguous.

### REQ26-D37-R11 — D37-R11 — Concurrency without collaborative editing

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Save uses expected revision and current owner/source/privacy/lifecycle guards. Two devices or tabs starting from the same base cannot silently overwrite each other; one wins and the other receives a conflict with its own permitted candidate retained. Show **This draft changed elsewhere**, the currently permitted saved version and local unsaved work through the existing qualified editor/review pattern. Let staff deliberately reload current saved content or reapply their changes against the new base. Do not offer a blind overwrite, automatic merge, CRDT/Yjs service, shared editing lock or cross-user takeover. An inactive clean editor may refresh current authorized state; a dirty editor never replaces its document from a list refresh, ACK or setContent callback. D34 awareness remains neutral and is not a lock or draft authority.

### REQ26-D37-R12 — D37-R12 — Unknown results and durable effect identity

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Bind each admitted create/save/discard operation to exact tenant/owner/source/draft generation, expected revision and semantic command hash. Reusing the same operation with different input conflicts. Unknown response means **Checking save** or **Save status unknown**, not success/failure or permission to create another draft. Recover the original operation under current access; an empty lookup is not proof of nonacceptance while an old request can still commit. The owner protocol must fence late admission before proving definite nonacceptance. Keep a minimal body-free operation handle/result through supported navigation; no second private content ledger. Replay returns original result separately from the current draft snapshot. Canceling HTTP or unmounting a component does not roll back an accepted write.

### REQ26-D37-R13 — D37-R13 — Navigation, IME and browser lifecycle

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Navigation that keeps the composer mounted, including eligible CRM side context, does not disturb it. Before supported navigation would unmount a dirty composer, finish IME composition and flush the latest committed bundle through the draft owner. On routine confirmed save, continue without a modal. While unresolved show Saving/Checking save and preserve work. On known failure offer Retry/Stay or an explicit **Leave without saving these changes** choice; do not silently drop the candidate. The latter abandons only the local delta and cannot undo an already accepted server operation. If an outcome remains unknown, do not trap the person until reconciliation succeeds: offer the same explicit Stay or Leave choice, stating **The earlier save may still finish; your latest unacknowledged changes may be lost**. Keep the scoped original-operation handle for later recovery; leaving does not prove cancellation or nonacceptance and cannot authorize a new Send. Do not repeatedly block the choice behind a failing status lookup. Browser close/crash warnings are best-effort; no new offline outbox or guaranteed last-keystroke recovery is promised. Source/privacy loss and real account/tenant changes clear forbidden bodies/Undo regardless of navigation guards. No unbounded collection of hidden mounted editors or localStorage/IndexedDB body archive is introduced.

A navigation guard also accounts for local-only pending attachment bytes even when text is acknowledged. If leaving would destroy the current upload/controller, keep its existing qualified transfer alive, wait for completion, or offer explicit **Leave without this unfinished attachment** while preserving saved text and truthful pending/failed file state. Do not claim a saved manifest can recover a browser File. Combine text/unknown-save/file consequences in one focused navigation guard rather than stacking dialogs. No new offline attachment store is required; owner cleanup handles abandoned upload occurrences.

Keyboard Send must respect IME/composition, near-composition Enter, defaultPrevented, key repeats and active popup/editor handling. Do not snapshot/send on a raw compositionend callback before the editor's pending DOM transaction has settled. Qualify the actual installed editor/browser commit path, including microtask ordering, rather than copy a browser-specific500ms heuristic as product timing. Programmatic setEditable/setContent events are not proof of human document edits. The current hotkey path without these guards must be replaced before activation.

### REQ26-D37-R14 — D37-R14 — Resume the exact saved draft

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.

Selecting a row performs current owner/source authorization and restores the exact saved bundle into the existing Support conversation composer. Do not first flash defaults, newest-message target, current CRM email or a blank editor and then overwrite it. Load one draft body only when opened; no body prefetch for the list. Preserve D24 pending work, D23 signature pins and D36 quotations/semantic attribution. Changes requiring review stay visible and cannot readdress or repersonalize content automatically. On desktop focus the resumed editing context deliberately after current loading; on mobile show source/recipients before user-directed keyboard focus. Same-session return restores list search/filter/scroll/selected row where available; cross-device persistence guarantees content/context, not an exact caret coordinate. A failed open leaves a truthful retry/unavailable state, not a blank new draft.

### REQ26-D37-R15 — D37-R15 — Actual source changes and incomplete eligibility

Applies to **US26-D37-03**, acceptance **AC26-D37-03-01–03**.

New relevant input, changed participants, relinking, inbox movement, merge/unmerge, source restriction/expiry, role changes and tenant policy changes requalify the exact retained draft under prior contracts. Metadata-only changes do not cause a gratuitous content conflict. A readable draft whose send context needs review remains resumable with **Review needed**, without pretending the source can be reconstructed from CRM. Source/privacy loss may require withholding the affected content or row; never expose forbidden existence/counts through a disabled item. Do not call all unresolved provider outcomes Review needed drafts; they use the existing operation-recovery status. Saving, viewing or drafting does not reopen a conversation, renew its retention anchor or satisfy a reply target.

### REQ26-D37-R16 — D37-R16 — Deliberate discard, no hidden trash product

Applies to **US26-D37-05**, acceptance **AC26-D37-05-01–03**.

Offer **Discard draft** in the row/composer's existing actions, with one concise confirmation identifying the draft and explaining that saved reply content and pending draft-only changes will be removed, while conversation/messages remain. Cancel does nothing. Confirm uses current ownership and the exact reviewed revision/lifecycle; if another tab saved newer work, show the conflict and require renewed review rather than discard it unseen. Commit terminal discard and cleanup obligations atomically. Retain only the body-free retirement/operation evidence needed to reject late writes/replays; no normal Restore, timed Undo promise, second trash inbox or bulk discard is added. Pending/possibly accepted Send cannot be canceled by discarding a draft. Ordinary editing Undo before discard remains separate. File cleanup affects only eligible draft-owned occurrences; it never deletes independently owned source files.

### REQ26-D37-R17 — D37-R17 — Send consumes the draft through existing admission

Applies to **US26-D37-05**, acceptance **AC26-D37-05-01–03**.

Deliberate Send uses the newest exact reviewed draft bundle with current revision, target/audience, source/quote/privacy and staged-work guards, ready P17 preparation and D4 atomic local admission. In that admission, mark the exact draft generation consumed and link the admitted intent so concurrent autosave, discard or Send cannot create divergent effects. A validation/pre-admission rejection preserves the active draft. If local admission is uncertain, reconcile its original operation; do not leave a fresh editable resend in My drafts. A confirmed admitted reply is no longer an active draft even if transport is queued, failed or unknown; delivery recovery stays in the conversation/P6 owner. Later failure does not automatically resurrect its old draft. Any genuinely new reply is explicitly new work with a new draft/intent identity after required review.

### REQ26-D37-R18 — D37-R18 — Privacy, retention and attachment custody

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Apply D16/D17 and each owner deadline to canonical drafts, dependencies, attachment occurrences, controlled cached/derived representations and temporary server material. Draft creation/editing/reads/autosave are not native content admission or renewal of a linked source's lifetime. No new24-hour/30-day draft rule is copied from vendors, and no indefinite private body custody is promised. The release retention inventory must name actual draft/body/attachment/control-receipt horizons and restore barriers before activation. A source stop invalidates unsafe quote/wording/file material even if a worker is late; preserve independently safe author text only when qualified separation is proven. Upload-in-progress local selections are not completed server-saved bytes; indicate separately that the file has not finished uploading. Discard/consumption removes only this draft's custody through owners, preserving immutable sent and independent original evidence.

### REQ26-D37-R19 — D37-R19 — Enforce the private database boundary

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Qualify one private Support draft store and authorized finder projection. Do not expose current support_messages draft-delivery rows and merely filter their UI. Tenant-aware primary/foreign relationships must bind original source, real owner, draft, dependencies, assets and operation receipts; non-null identity/purpose, revision checks, active uniqueness and terminal-state constraints prevent invalid combinations. No generic staff CRUD or caller author field can mutate private owner/source/approval/admission identity. Actual service-role paths repeat current actor/tenant/source checks. Use least grants, RLS on exposed data, effective SELECT/USING/WITH CHECK, safe views, RPC EXECUTE/search_path/definer closure and constrained immutable columns. Check permissive-policy combinations and all old writer routes; FORCE RLS is not protection from every bypass role. Deletion does not cascade into conversations, CRM/giving records or required intent evidence. There are no new money fields.

### REQ26-D37-R20 — D37-R20 — Tiptap is the editor, not draft authority

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Reuse the shared Tiptap3 Reply profile and code-owned schema/static renderer; apps consume shared Base UI/base-maia components. SSR-safe initialization remains immediatelyRender:false. Gate every restoration before setContent and suppress synthetic update emission deliberately; emitUpdate:false alone cannot stop stale overwrite or schema loss. Isolate the active editor from list refreshes and subscribe toolbar state narrowly; selection-only transactions do not dirty the draft. Hydration runs after exact current document/source validation and cannot fire autosave, template expansion, mention callbacks or user-edit recency. Unsupported saved structure produces an explicit read-only migration/repair state, never a successfully saved stripped/empty document. No read-only editor per row, document history SaaS, Tiptap Cloud/Yjs/AI or provider draft sync is required. Package/version closure is qualified as a shared upgrade decision, never an automatic dependency change in grooming.

### REQ26-D37-R21 — D37-R21 — Source ownership and authoritative projections

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Support owns the private human draft, its source/actor, revision, save/discard/consume operations and finder. PostgreSQL holds authoritative draft state; the list and caches are expendable current-authorized projections. P17 owns reusable content/schema/presentation and complete-message preparation; D18/D23 sources are pinned copies with retained adverse fences, not live mutable links. P6 owns intent/delivery recovery and actual communication evidence. My drafts is not Email Studio's Draft publications, a shared saved view, CRM activity, scheduled mail or an SLA queue. Neither the list nor draft-body HTML is a write authority; one canonical structured bundle remains authoritative.

### REQ26-D37-R22 — D37-R22 — CRM and identity continuity

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

A draft begun through authorized CRM Support context is the same private draft found in My drafts. Opening it preserves a qualified return route without duplicating CRM bodies or permitting restricted related-record reads. An authenticated principal, Support draft owner, assignee, requester, participant, CRM person, represented organization and record owner remain distinct. Matching email, reassignment, membership in a conversation or an administrative role does not grant another worker's drafts. A departed person's draft is not silently handed over; qualified staff continue the actual Support obligation with their own authorized writing. Viewing/saving/discarding creates no Party/contact, relationship, Activity, finance mutation or business-completion claim. CRM remains usable independently of Support.

### REQ26-D37-R23 — D37-R23 — Email Studio preparation and publication seam

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

My drafts discovery, restoration and ordinary save invoke the qualified editor/document validation capability but create no delivery preparation, message intent, template publication or email. Human reply content remains Support-owned and outside the finite system-message catalog. At actual Send, P17 prepares the whole reviewed canonical body, audience context, signature/footer, quote attribution and authorized assets through the existing compatible contract. It does not reinterpret literal source tokens, append history or refresh mutable signatures/CRM values. P6 seals exact material and reconciles the immutable envelope under ADR0032. Opening a draft cannot trigger D29 confirmation, D15 attention, D28 feedback or a shortcut plan; those owners retain their existing real triggers. Source/reference safety may be checked without creating a new outgoing message.

### REQ26-D37-R24 — D37-R24 — Responsive, accessible and stable interaction

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Use restrained semantic rows and existing shared inputs/menu/dialog, not a card dashboard or new visual system. Heading/entry remain My drafts; helper copy explains Only you can see these saved replies without implying no exceptional records/privacy custody exists. Keyboard Enter on a row opens, never sends; menu/discard focus returns predictably. Maintain logical reading order, visible focus, touch hit areas and contrast; default no automatically raised mobile keyboard obscuring context. Qualify320CSS-pixel reflow,200% text resize,400% zoom-equivalent reflow, long international names, Thai/RTL, timezones, IME and reduced motion. 44CSS-pixel touch hit area is an Asym product target, not a claim that WCAG's24CSS-pixel minimum/exceptions require44. Save/error/result messages are accessible but do not announce each keystroke or every successful autosave.

### REQ26-D37-R25 — D37-R25 — Failure, freshness and bounded performance

Applies to **US26-D37-04**, acceptance **AC26-D37-04-01–03**.

Read the finder on entry, applied query/scope change, explicit Refresh and relevant foreground reconnect/invalidation. Coalesce requests and bind them to tenant/actor/scope generation; a stale response cannot replace a newer list. No per-keystroke list polling or perpetual full-tenant subscription. When refresh fails, label results out of date only while current authorization/privacy permits retaining them; otherwise clear affected metadata. No permission/missing/incomplete/error result becomes zero drafts. Body fetches occur only for an opened draft and use current checks. Index owner/tenant/lifecycle/meaningful-edit sort and source dependency lookup before pagination; enforce shared document/node/depth/asset/operation/query limits before expensive processing. Publish actual numeric profile and measured workload/latency before activation. The20/50row page bounds and750ms/5s scheduling targets do not prove server performance or total capacity.

### REQ26-D37-R26 — D37-R26 — Migration, activation and rollback

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Inventory current drafts and alternate writers before enabling the finder. Current caller-author/isPrivate:false message rows cannot be relabelled private without positive trusted provenance; ambiguous legacy rows stay in owner-qualified restricted migration/repair custody, never assigned by email/text resemblance or silently destroyed. Deploy compatible private schema, grants, source checks, operation handlers and readers before new writes; then qualified Tiptap restoration/autosave and finally My drafts. Old readers/writers must fail closed on unsupported schema/generations and cannot strip unknown nodes or recreate discarded/consumed data. Backfills are idempotent with explicit source/owner evidence and preserve D16/D17 history. Kill switches stop affected new writes/finder exposure while keeping authorized safe reading and accepted-send reconciliation. After new data exists, use compatible roll-forward; rollback cannot restore the broad old writer or replay mail.

### REQ26-D37-R27 — D37-R27 — Observability, audit and residual operations

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Use body-free draft/operation/version correlation, typed save/discard/admission outcomes and bounded latency/conflict metrics through existing observability. No editor JSON, source body, recipient addresses, filenames, signed URLs or raw exceptions in logs. Saving every few seconds is not a CRM Activity or employee productivity trail. Ordinary revisions provide concurrency, not a new user-facing version-history product; retain only actual owner-governed recovery evidence. Source privacy/retention operations retain their separate durable audit. O01–O05 in the proof record name residual signals/thresholds/owners/responses. Disclosure, lost text, duplicate effect, silent schema loss and unsafe send are release blockers and containment triggers, not monitor-only accepted risks.

### REQ26-D37-R28 — D37-R28 — Proof and stage discipline

Applies to **US26-D37-06**, acceptance **AC26-D37-06-01–03**.

Require the32release groups in the proof record on actual qualified UI/editor/API/database/role/consumer paths. Prove list completeness/privacy, meaningful creation/no-op, whole-bundle save, multiple-tab/IME/navigation/lost-response behavior, source stops, conditional discard, atomic send consumption, migration, accessibility, performance and CRM/P17/P6 continuity. Record actual dependency versions, resource limits, environment and production-shaped data. Static/source/helper probes and document checks remain explicitly limited; no live database, browser/AT, provider or staff-study result is fabricated. Trace to formal OpenSpec/design/tasks/issues/implementation/release only after those stages are authorized. The complete design resolves this decision without expanding into an enterprise helpdesk or another Asym product.

## Private new Internal-note drafts

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — The simple experience

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

Maya writes an internal note in a Support conversation. Before she is ready to share it, another request interrupts her. Her writing saves quietly. Later, **My drafts → Internal note → continue → Add note** brings her back to the same work. No save ritual, separate notebook, reconstruction of a CRM record or extra publication screen is needed.

The private draft and the posted note are different facts. The draft is her unfinished work. **Add note** deliberately publishes the currently reviewed content to authorized internal readers. Saving, mentioning someone in the draft or switching modes does not perform that publication or notify anyone.

The strongest alternative is explicit Save note draft; it gives deliberate retention control but creates a recurring step and a different habit from accepted Reply autosave. Local-only notes keep less durable content but cannot offer this return journey. A is selected. This blueprint makes A dependable without adding the unchosen modes as settings.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — UX01 — One existing destination, with clear kinds

Applies to **US26-D38-01**, acceptance **AC26-D38-01-01–03**.

Keep **My drafts** in D37's existing Support navigation, visible when empty and without a count, urgency badge or forced landing page. Update its helper to:

> Your private reply and note drafts across accessible inboxes.

Keep the same title search, Inbox filter, Refresh and Load more. Extend each row with a readable **Reply** or **Internal note** label. When both kinds exist for the same conversation, show two independently identified rows, each with its own accepted meaningful-save time and exact activation target. Repeated conversation titles are valid; the kind resolves their purpose without inventing private draft titles or using body snippets.

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> My drafts
> Your private reply and note drafts across accessible inboxes.
> 
> [Search conversation titles…]   [Inbox: All accessible inboxes] [Refresh]
> 
> Account question                                      Donor care
> Internal note · Saved 4 minutes ago                         [More]
> 
> Account question                                      Donor care
> Reply · Saved 12 minutes ago                                [More]
> 
> [Load more]

This fixture is illustrative. All title/inbox/source metadata must come from currently permitted projections. The kind marker describes the draft's purpose, not its audience authority. There are no note-body previews, mention names, file thumbnails, rich-text row editors, extra Note tab, new kind filter, avatar crowd or new reminders. One row remains one exact draft; merge grouping does not collapse different original sources or purposes.

Retain D37's actual 20-row initial page, maximum 50 per request, stable ordering and current title-search semantics. Those are query/page bounds, not a total draft cap. No recent-only cutoff. Adding a Note kind must not reset a user's current search/filter/scroll or make background autosaves reorder rows under a pointer.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — UX02 — Enter Internal note without creating phantom work

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

The existing Reply/Internal note control stays text-labelled and purpose-specific. Selecting **Internal note**, focusing it, moving the caret, opening formatting controls or restoring an empty baseline creates no durable draft. First meaningful permitted author work—text, supported formatting/content insertion, a qualified file selection or a deliberate note reference—creates the new private Note draft. Tiptap update events caused by hydration/selection/editability are not evidence of author work.

The ordinary composer shows:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Internal note
> Private until you select Add note.
> 
> [Existing qualified formatting / insertion controls]
> [Write the note…                                      ]
> 
> [File state when relevant]
> Saved                                      [Add note] [More]

Explain the qualified internal audience through the existing note-mode help, for example **Added notes are visible to staff with access to this conversation.** Do not claim all tenant staff can see them, describe a private draft as already shared, or hide the difference behind color. Technical privacy/security custody remains governed without adding implementation jargon to the composer.

The note has no To/Cc/Bcc, From, external signature, email footer, Reply-all preference or outbound email preview. D24 reply-and-work shortcuts and their staged actions never enter Note mode. Existing qualified Saved notes/mention/file tools keep their current Note purpose; this feature adds no new content family or automatic source import.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — UX03 — Quiet saving reuses the accepted contract

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

Reuse D37's accepted shared draft coordinator semantics for the Note purpose: after 750ms quiet, with a checkpoint attempt within five seconds of eligible continued editing, subject to foreground/online/authorized/schema-valid/non-IME conditions and no unresolved prior operation. These are scheduling targets, not guarantees that a five-second-old keystroke is saved. Keep one unresolved write per draft controller and coalesce newer work; do not create a new autosave engine or configurable timer.

**Saved** means the complete newest eligible Note candidate is acknowledged, including actual source/kind, typed mentions, source dependencies and file-selection state. A body-only save cannot describe the complete note as Saved. An older acknowledgment may establish a checkpoint but cannot erase later typing, move its caret or mark that later candidate Saved.

Keep one small status region: **Saving**, **Saved**, **Not saved**, **Checking save**, or an actionable failure. Ordinary successful checkpoints do not produce toasts, notification entries, timeline events or focus movement. **Save now** and **Retry save** reuse the existing deliberate-checkpoint/recovery path; no separate primary Save note draft button is needed for the selected automatic policy.

An incomplete but structurally safe note may be saved. No recipient, signature, complete email fill-in or external provider readiness is required. Unknown/unsafe nodes, forbidden source content or invalid protected metadata are not harmless incompleteness. Preserve the qualified original and show the existing safe repair state rather than silently stripping the document.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — UX04 — Files and mentions have truthful pending state

Applies to **US26-D38-02**, acceptance **AC26-D38-02-01–03**.

File selection may create meaningful draft work before a note has prose. Persist qualified occurrence identity and display Uploading, Ready, Failed or another truthful owner state. Never imply that a saved manifest can reconstruct a lost browser File. A restored note may keep its acknowledged text while an unavailable attachment requires re-selection or deliberate removal. No automatic removal of required content or retry of an expired source is hidden behind a successful text save.

A selected @mention is private draft content until actual Add note admission. Saving, restoring and re-rendering the token must not notify, follow, add recipients or confer source access. Changed staff eligibility is rechecked at posting and shown with a precise repair choice under the existing note/mention rules; do not silently notify a replacement person inferred from a matching name or address. Plain unselected @text remains ordinary text.

Draft completeness and publication eligibility differ. **Add note permits a meaningful canonical body or at least one ready, clean, currently authorized selected attachment.** Do not require dummy “see attached” prose. Zero meaningful body and zero ready files cannot post. A selected pending/failed/unqualified attachment blocks publication until it is ready or deliberately removed; existing body text does not authorize silently dropping that file. Incomplete and file-only unfinished drafts still save privately. D23's purpose profile and D32's current file custody/readiness remain mandatory.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — UX05 — Switch purpose without converting content

Applies to **US26-D38-04**, acceptance **AC26-D38-04-01–03**.

Reply and Note are separate candidates, persisted identities and Undo histories. A mode switch retains the first candidate under its own identity before activating the other; it never moves text, recipients, files, D36 quotes or D24 staged actions into the other purpose. The same shared editor can render the selected candidate without retaining a collection of hidden mounted editors.

A normal switch that preserves both qualified controllers/work states adds no confirmation. If an identity transition would destroy unsaved text, pending local attachment bytes or an unresolved result, use the single existing navigation guard rather than losing work or stacking dialogs. Complete IME input before taking the relevant checkpoint; don't treat raw keydown or compositionend alone as the final canonical document.

Returning to a known conversation honors the user's explicit mode action and restores that purpose's own saved work. It does not choose a mode by inspecting whether the latest timeline item happens to be a note. My drafts activation explicitly selects the exact stored Note or Reply; no ambiguous generic Open draft action can pick one by last-updated time.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — UX06 — Leave and resume without needless interruption

Applies to **US26-D38-04**, acceptance **AC26-D38-04-01–03**.

CRM context that leaves the composer mounted preserves it. When leaving would unmount it, perform D37's qualified save/flush and continue normally on confirmed success. Saved Note work needs no Are you sure dialog. Keep accepted content/context across devices; do not promise an identical cursor coordinate or crash-proof last keystrokes.

Use D37's one focused guard for an actual problem. Known failed save offers Retry/Stay or **Leave without saving these changes**. Unknown save offers an honest Stay/Leave path with **The earlier save may still finish; your latest unacknowledged changes may be lost** and retains the original scoped operation handle. Do not trap staff indefinitely in a failed status check or claim leaving canceled an accepted save.

An unfinished attachment shares that guard when leaving would destroy local bytes. Preserve the existing qualified transfer where possible, wait, or offer **Leave without this unfinished attachment**. Keep acknowledged text and honest file state. While the Reply controller and its permitted working state remain safely retained, an unrelated Reply save need not block resuming a safe Note. If navigation would destroy either purpose's dirty work or local files, include every affected purpose in the same save/leave guard, including the inactive one. A successful Note save never marks the Reply saved.

Select an **Internal note** row to authorize and load the exact candidate, source and Note schema before mounting a writable editor. No intermediate editor, default Reply flash or blank editor followed by replacement. Loading or access failure is not an empty new note. On desktop, focus the resumed editing context after deliberate activation; on mobile, show conversation/source and internal mode before user-directed keyboard focus. Returning to My drafts restores same-session list context where available.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — UX07 — Known source changes get targeted review

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

Ordinary status, assignment and same-source metadata changes do not erase a draft. A Note on Resolved work remains discoverable while its actual draft/source authority permits; opening it does not reopen the conversation. Assignment never transfers another worker's private note.

If a source merge/unmerge or other material change affects the note's actual destination or current internal audience, keep permitted work and explain that specific change before Add note. Follow D10's general-note continuing-origin rule and any already-qualified explicit source action. Do not use a private draft anchor as silent publication authority, invent a new source chooser for every note, or attach by typed names. The reviewed publication destination must be visible and exact.

When only permission to post has changed but current private read/custody remains valid, allow the eligible private candidate to be inspected and keep posting unavailable with truthful explanation. If read/source/privacy authority is lost, withhold or clear affected bodies, Undo and forbidden metadata immediately; do not expose a stale disabled row as a count/existence leak. Retain independently safe authored work only when the existing owner can prove that separation. Do not offer Copy as a bypass for forbidden content.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0010 — UX08 — Add note is the deliberate publication boundary

Applies to **US26-D38-03**, acceptance **AC26-D38-03-01–03**.

**Add note** acts on the exact current reviewed Note bundle, owner, source destination and revision. It preserves existing note admission/content rules together with the explicit file-only clarification in UX04. No extra generic confirmation is needed for an ordinary unchanged valid note. Current source/audience/mention/file problems require focused review or repair; they are not hidden auto-corrections.

While actual publication admission is pending, identify **Adding note** or **Checking whether your note was added** and prevent a competing new publication/discard of that same candidate. Keep permitted content visible; the separate Reply can remain intact and usable under its own state. HTTP cancellation or leaving the view is not proof of non-admission.

Confirmed publication consumes only that exact Note draft generation and shows one posted note at its actual source/history position. Remove its active My drafts row; leave any separate Reply row and D24 plan unchanged. Avoid optimistic duplicate note bubbles. A later callback for the consumed Note cannot clear a newly created Note or resurrect the old one. Preserve existing post-action navigation rather than forcing a detour back to My drafts.

**Note added** means the actual internal note was admitted. It does not mean a colleague read it, a notification email was delivered, a response target was satisfied, or a giving/care/CRM action completed. Existing D15 optional following and independently qualified direct attention follow the actual published event. Retry/reconciliation cannot mint a second publication or repeat notifications as new source events.

### REQ26-D38-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0011 — UX09 — Discard affects only the identified draft

Applies to **US26-D38-04**, acceptance **AC26-D38-04-01–03**.

Use the existing More → **Discard draft** action from the row or composer. One concise confirmation identifies both kind and conversation, for example:

> Discard this internal-note draft?
>
> This discards your unfinished note and its selected attachments. The conversation and your reply draft remain.
>
> Keep draft / Discard draft

The file statement means only eligible draft-owned occurrences are released; independently owned source files are not deleted. Where a release cannot occur immediately under current custody, the UI must not imply physical disposal already completed. No typed phrase, mandatory reason, bulk discard, hidden trash or expiring recovery promise is added.

Confirm uses the reviewed version. A newer save in another tab requires renewed review rather than deleting unseen work.
