### REQ26-D38-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O01 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed unauthorized/private/cross-tenant draft or metadata exposure, unsafe restoration, forbidden asset access or sensitive draft data/token in logs.

**Owner:** Support security/privacy owner and engineering on-call

**Response:** Contain the affected read/write/access path, preserve body-free evidence, correct owner-controlled data and verify before re-enable. Keep unrelated authorized work available.

### REQ26-D38-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O02 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Technical save failures exceed 2% in a rolling 15-minute window with at least 100 eligible attempts, per affected purpose/path. Exclude typed user cancellation, conflict, validation and authorization denial from the failure numerator.

**Owner:** Support draft engineering on-call

**Response:** Diagnose the durable save path, retain permitted local candidates and truthful recovery; disable broken automatic attempts where needed while qualified manual saving remains available. Individual low-volume failures remain visible, not hidden by the alert minimum.

### REQ26-D38-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O03 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed premature note/attention from drafting, lost acknowledged content, false newest-Saved status, cross-purpose overwrite, duplicate active slot, terminal resurrection or duplicate admitted note/attention occurrence.

**Owner:** Support draft/note admission owner; attention/P6 owner for downstream effects

**Response:** Stop the affected producer/command, reconcile original durable operations and obligations, fix and add regression proof before resuming. Never repair with a new Post or by deleting legitimate independent notes.

### REQ26-D38-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O04 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Finder, save acknowledgment or Add note admission p95 exceeds its qualified P28 budget for two consecutive 15-minute windows, each with at least 100 eligible completed requests.

**Owner:** Support performance owner

**Response:** Investigate actual payload/scope/index/policy/controller/transaction contention. Repair or reduce admitted work, without relaxing privacy, dropping files, claiming premature success or hiding drafts.

### REQ26-D38-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O05 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Three independent reports of the same continuation task friction within 30 days, or one reproduced keyboard/AT blocker preventing writing/save/find/resume/post/discard.

**Owner:** Support product/design owner and accessibility lead

**Response:** Reproduce the exact journey, correct and retest through the existing authorized work process. Prefer clearer behavior and defaults over more settings or routine dialogs.

### REQ26-D38-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D38-05**, acceptance **AC26-D38-05-01–03**.

Reuse the five D37 control families, including their thresholds, with explicit Note purpose and publication outcomes. The following extension is binding for new Internal-note drafts. Actual accountable teams/people and P28 latency budgets must be assigned before activation. These signals monitor residual failures; correctness/privacy remains a release gate.

## Personal read/unread

### REQ26-D39-READER_TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0002 — One quiet cue, in the existing journey

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**UX01 — Presentation and placement.** “Display personal Unread using a restrained dot and modest title emphasis in the existing Support conversation list/card. Include the accessible meaning **Unread for you**; color or font weight alone is insufficient. Keep shared work state, priority, assignment and mandatory recovery visibly distinct. Reuse the existing row and reader **Conversation actions** menu for one state-appropriate **Mark read** or **Mark unread** action. The dot is decorative, not a tiny hidden toggle. No new unread count, filter, timer setting, bulk command, reading dashboard or shortcut family is required.

The new action belongs with ordinary conversation utilities, separated from consequential shared actions by the existing menu grouping. It does not go inside **Reading: Compact/Full**, which is already D33's personal content-presentation setting. Use a quiet helper, where clarification is needed: **Only changes your reading status.** Do not display a toast on every automatic read. A deliberate action has a brief accessible success acknowledgment after confirmation. No confirmation dialog is needed for these reversible self-only actions.

Base UI controls and the exact **base-maia** preset remain required. Shared foreground, muted, border and focus-ring tokens carry the design; no hardcoded red unread badge, dashboard chrome or reduced type size is introduced. Current the shared UI package and the installed shadcn `info --json` report base-maia/Base UI; that proves configuration only, not a completed visual implementation.

**UX02 — Honest initial meaning.** “A currently permitted source with eligible other-authored content and no recorded personal coverage is Unread for you, including old or newly accessible history. This does not mean received today, urgent or owed. No unread marker is fabricated for an empty or excluded-only source, and own-authored content alone does not automatically make a source unread. There is no activation-wide mark-read baseline or per-person history fanout.

Show original content times accurately. Do not rewrite dates, replay historic notifications or sort old material as a new arrival merely because it is newly accessible. A staff member may deliberately mark eligible own-authored content unread to revisit it; this is a personal intent, not a new deadline or shared reminder. A source that no longer has applicable permitted content must not retain an unexplained dot that reveals removed material.

### REQ26-D39-READER_TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0003 — Ordinary opening, viewing and returning

Applies to **US26-D39-02**, acceptance **AC26-D39-02-01–03**.

**UX03 — Qualified open.** “Automatic personal acknowledgment requires a deliberate opening of the actual selected conversation reader in the foreground, a visible and active reading surface, current source-qualified snapshot coverage, and successful safe presentation of its current latest eligible content region. A table focus movement, preview, prefetched request, automatically selected row, hidden mobile/desktop duplicate, background tab, loading skeleton, failed fetch or mounted empty component does not qualify.

Opening the same authorized Support reader from a CRM link has the same effect. Merely visiting a CRM Party record or expanding a summary card does not. Pointer, keyboard and assistive-technology opening use the same meaning; no mouse-only gate or editor focus is required. Window/document activity, app-selected reader and actual presented region are complementary local signals. None is a server authorization boundary or proof of human attention.

There is no dwell timer. The user should not wait to earn a read state, scroll every old message, or put an entire tall card on screen. Only the qualified current orientation event is acknowledged. Expanding a repeated signature, changing Compact/Full, resizing, hydrating or moving focus between controls does not become a separate open or clear a newer manual-unread intent.

**UX04 — Usable content before automatic success.** “The read integration must distinguish successful current content presentation, legitimately bodyless eligible content, loading, authorization failure, unsupported/invalid document content, and rendering failure. A valid attachment-only contribution can qualify when its authorized message and attachment metadata are presented; downloading or opening every attachment is not required. An error placeholder or silently blank failed current body cannot automatically acknowledge that content.

Qualified safe-text fallback may represent the same authorized current body when allowed by the owning content profile. Arbitrary raw HTML, guessed JSON parsing, stale text from a different revision, or a generic error label cannot be relabeled successful content. D33's already-qualified older repeated-history folds remain compatible; unique current content cannot be hidden just to obtain readiness. All-full-archive loading is unnecessary.

**UX05 — Exact represented coverage.** “Bind an automatic acknowledgment to the exact server-qualified content/source cutoff vector represented by the opened reader. Never substitute the server's newest head when the acknowledgment arrives. A newer contribution after that snapshot remains unread until a subsequent qualified presentation or deliberate Mark read covering it.

The cutoff is a durable content-order boundary, not a client wall-clock timestamp or mutable `updated_at`. The browser reports a qualified local view, while the owning server independently validates actor, tenant, current source permissions, topology, expected personal intent and represented cutoff. Rendering or observing content never grants permission. Root's D39 data/lifecycle contract supplies that single authoritative mutation boundary.

### REQ26-D39-READER_TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0004 — Mark read and mark unread without fighting the interface

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

**UX06 — Deliberate actions remain deliberate.** “**Mark unread** records a personal revisit intent for the currently qualified applicable content. It stays unread throughout the current reader activation, including rerenders, new fetches, ordinary focus/visibility changes and already-open tabs. A new deliberate open after that intent, or an explicit **Mark read**, may clear it with current qualified coverage. Delayed automatic acknowledgments from older activations cannot undo it.

The usual action in an unread row is Mark read; in a read row it is Mark unread. Both desktop and mobile have a labelled menu path. Do not add an obligatory second confirmation, force a close, navigate away automatically, or save a reminder time. **Mark read** acknowledges only the exact qualified scope shown to the person; it does not certify inspection of every body/file. The action may intentionally clear a cue without visiting all old content, while a source/head lookup failure must not fabricate its scope.

After selecting Mark unread in the reader, keep the reader open, preserve focus and quietly confirm the personal change. Returning from a tab switch does not count as a new deliberate opening. Leaving this conversation and deliberately reopening it does. A known command conflict or uncertain outcome retains truthful pending/unconfirmed state and cannot silently override a later deliberate intent from another device.

### REQ26-D39-READER_TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0005 — New content while already working

Applies to **US26-D39-02**, acceptance **AC26-D39-02-01–03**.

**UX07 — Stable reading.** “A new eligible contribution arriving while the person is looking at older history, viewing a file, composing, in another tab or behind another surface stays unread until qualified current presentation or Mark read. Show a quiet **New activity** action in the existing reader when useful. Preserve the visible message anchor, selection, draft, focus and list position. Do not auto-scroll or move a row under the pointer.

Selecting New activity deliberately returns to the current latest readable region and preserves the composer. It does not send, readdress, resolve, subscribe or mark P17 notifications read. A new contribution arriving while the Reply or Note editor is actively being used for writing or IME composition remains unread even when the latest message region is visible. It can qualify when the person deliberately returns to current reading, including New activity, or explicitly uses Mark read. Merely retaining an inactive draft does not block normal qualified viewing. Returning from the composer does not mint a new deliberate-open epoch that overrides a prior Mark unread; UX06 still applies.

If already at the current region and actually reading it, new successfully rendered material may qualify through the same rules; a stale render, hidden pane or later arrival beyond the acknowledged snapshot cannot be swept into a previous acknowledgment. A floating action must not obscure content, the editor or mobile controls.

Do not announce every streaming/backend event or flip a live region for every message. Announce the meaningful appearance of new activity politely, without stealing focus; the visible action remains available. Repeated events are coalesced by the actual UI state. W3C status-message guidance supports presenting status without an unexpected focus move; it does not require a success toast for every passive cue change.

**UX08 — Drafts and preparation remain untouched.** “A read-state update, content invalidation, newer conversation message or list refresh must never call Tiptap `setContent`, replace a Reply/Note draft, reset its selection, change its recipient/source, post it, discard it, prepare email or imply current Send coverage. D37/D38 private draft custody and D36 quote provenance remain authoritative.

The user can read a newly arrived message while preserving both Reply and Note working states. A genuine source or recipient change still invokes the already accepted review rules; a read marker is not a substitute for those checks. The writer and reader have independent state lifecycles even when they share a visual pane.

### REQ26-D39-READER_TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0006 — Merges, CRM and permission changes

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**UX09 — One grouped reading journey, qualified originals.** “A qualified combined conversation open may acknowledge its exact represented authorized original-source cutoff vector when the combined current latest eligible region successfully renders. Older bodies may remain folded or paginated; there is no requirement to bring every original source head into the viewport. Sources absent from the authorized snapshot, unknown or incompatible coverage, and later topology/content are not covered. Merge/Undo preserves personal coverage on the original sources rather than inventing a shared root flag.

This refines an initially overstrict review suggestion. Requiring a separate scroll/open for each old merged original would leave a normal reader perpetually unread and confuse orientation with body-by-body attestation. Ordinary old-body pagination is not missing source coverage when the snapshot explicitly and correctly represents that original's cutoff. Conversely, seeing source A alone does not authorize a server to guess B's existence or frontier. A server-complete component vector and current authorization are essential; a root maximum or current list counter is not sufficient.

Changing a Party link, requester identity, assignment or CRM owner cannot transfer one person's state to another or grant access to a source. Narrower CRM access and Support permissions are both respected. Return to the same CRM record/list position. No separate CRM read field, conversation copy, interaction-history entry or broad CRM write is created.

### REQ26-D39-READER_TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0007 — Failure, mobile and accessibility

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

**UX10 — Readable and operable under ordinary constraints.** “Keep the same cue meaning and menu actions on desktop and mobile. Provide accessible textual state, native/established Base UI menu semantics, visible focus, predictable Escape/focus return, Core touch targets of at least 44 CSS px, and no hover-only or gesture-only controls. Keep language understandable at 320 CSS px, 400% zoom, large text and mixed LTR/RTL content. Reading mode does not shrink message type.

New activity must be reachable by keyboard and AT without tabbing through every historical control. Do not trap the reader in a mandatory scroll sequence to clear a cue. The reader's legitimate scroll and source-window navigation remain; D39 does not introduce page-wide horizontal scrolling or animate history heights. Use existing reduced-motion behavior. No read pulse, blinking indicator, sound or celebratory motion is warranted.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State | User-facing behavior | Truthful persistence behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Messages load but personal status is pending | Content remains usable; retain a valid scoped last-confirmed cue only if labelled stale when necessary. | Do not invent a confirmed Read state or acknowledge a guessed version. |
| Message request fails | Existing source/content error with Retry, not an empty conversation. | No automatic acknowledgment of unavailable current content. |
| Current body has unsupported format | Safe qualified fallback or **Message content could not be displayed.** | Failure is not successful rendering. Manual read remains an explicit orientation command only when its authorized scope is known. |
| Automatic read update cannot be confirmed | Quiet, deduplicated **Could not update your reading status.** with appropriate Retry/reconcile path. No repeated toast loop. | Do not claim confirmed success; server cutoff/intent checks prevent stale replay. Reading and typing continue. |
| Manual command definitely fails | Keep/recover the confirmed prior state and show a nearby clear error. | Never report a saved personal intent or retry with a newly broadened scope. |
| Manual command response is lost | Show unconfirmed outcome; reconcile the same logical command and current personal revision. | Do not confuse ambiguous success with rejection, fabricate a second intent or override a newer device action. |
| Another personal device changes state | Update the same owner's current cue through qualified synchronization. Preserve the reader/draft position. | Already-open view epochs do not cancel a newer manual unread intent. |
| Access is lost or source expires | Remove unavailable body/cue/context under current source policy. Do not reveal hidden counts or names. | No restored draft, cached marker or old attachment URL can bypass revocation. |

Read status never blocks a legitimate reply or note merely because orientation synchronization is unavailable. Actual send/post authorization, content validation, draft custody and D14 coverage remain independent requirements. Recovery should be economical: one honest state and action, not a new operational inbox for read markers.

### REQ26-D39-READER_TIPTAP_CONTRACT-S0008 — Tiptap's exact role

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**UX11 — Shared static rendering.** “Reuse the qualified shared rich-text reader and document profiles. Read-only Support content uses `@tiptap/static-renderer`; D39 does not mount a `useEditor` per message, introduce Tiptap collaboration/presence, add Pro/AI services, or migrate the existing editor API. Compact and Full are presentation over the same permitted message content, not separate read-state owners.

Tiptap static-renderer documentation describes rendering JSON into HTML/React without a browser or editor instance and exposes explicit handling for unknown nodes/marks. Core's canonical Tiptap skill independently prefers static rendering for feeds. These support the existing architecture. They do not prove arbitrary JSON is valid or that rendered content was seen.

**UX12 — Events are not reading evidence.** “Do not use Tiptap editor creation, focus, update, selectionUpdate, transaction, setContent or hydration as a read acknowledgment. Keep personal marker data out of canonical message/draft JSON and all email serialization. Expose current safe-render readiness at the reader adapter boundary, with message/source/content identity; a component mount alone is insufficient.

Tiptap events describe editor and document activity. They do not supply a conversation-reading contract. The documented `contentError` is an editor/schema event, not a replacement for validating the read-only path. Preserve the existing `immediatelyRender:false` editor configuration. The official Composable API guide still identifies `useEditor` as appropriate for simpler direct-control cases; this narrow reading feature is not a reason for an unrelated migration.

**UX13 — Visibility is a local hint, not attention surveillance.** “Use current app selection, document activity/visibility and bounded local current-region presentation signals to determine whether an already-authorized snapshot is actually shown. Do not collect per-message viewing histories, dwell measurements, screenshots, read-duration analytics or teammate receipts. Invalidate queued local acknowledgment intent when its source, actor, topology or activation no longer applies.

The Page Visibility API distinguishes visible/background documents; document visibility alone does not establish that a particular pane is visible, and focus alone does not establish visibility. Intersection Observer reports geometry asynchronously, can fire on initial observation and is not proof of perception. Avoid a 100%-of-card threshold for tall content, observer-per-history-node tracking, or a zero-area sentinel that marks content read before presentation. An app-hidden/inert reader and known covering dialog must be excluded by app state. No browser API provides a comprehension guarantee.

**UX14 — Email Studio and domain boundaries.** “Support owns the current person's qualified source-reading marker. CRM supplies only permitted shared context through its own authority. P17 owns notification engagement; D15 owns Following; D14/D31 own response/reminder obligations. Email Studio owns its already accepted templates/content tools and P6 owns delivery. Reading, Mark read, Mark unread, New activity and Compact/Full do not prepare, send, record a delivery, enroll a campaign or change any of those domains.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0005 — C01 — Personal meaning and source ownership

Applies to **US26-D39-01**, acceptance **AC26-D39-01-01–03**.

Support owns a self-only reading aid over original conversation sources. One person's view or explicit personal action changes only that person's markers. It never changes shared Open/Waiting/Resolved work, assignment, reminders, reply targets, due timers, native-content clocks, notification engagement, delivery evidence or CRM business truth. No reader roster, named last-seen time, analytics or requester receipt is exposed.

Store state by trusted tenant, real staff owner and immutable original source; do not key by current merged root, email, assignee or Party. The combined conversation cue is a current-authorized projection of its relevant originals, not a second mutable counter. Markers are inexpensive personal UI state, not P6 semantic delivery intents.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0006 — C02 — Eligible content and the honest absent-state baseline

Applies to **US26-D39-01**, acceptance **AC26-D39-01-01–03**.

Derive automatic unread from currently readable, first-qualified human content authored by somebody else: admitted human requester input, qualified recorded initial request content, published native-human internal notes and other staff's admitted human replies. A locally admitted human reply may be queued; its content is new while delivery is separately truthful. Do not wait for the optional-follow acceptance event merely because D15 has its own timing.

Exclude private drafts, generated/system rows, unqualified/quarantined bodies, source edits, redaction/expiry, assignment/status changes, timers, attachment progress, automatic confirmations and later provider callbacks. Count a genuine source contribution once at first reading eligibility; late provider dates and imports of duplicates do not rewrite that clock. Prove native provenance rather than trusting `type:note` or caller author JSON. Trusted same-person authorship can suppress self-generated automatic unread; matching email cannot.

No personal marker means unvisited/unacknowledged: show Unread only if currently permitted eligible other-authored content exists. Empty/self-only sources have no automatic unread cue. Existing and newly accessible unfamiliar history is not fabricated as already viewed. There is no enrollment cutoff, read-all migration, per-member source backfill, aggregate unread burden or requirement to visit every historical source. A separate deliberate manual marker has the meaning specified in C07, not a claim of new external input.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0007 — C03 — A compact state model, not a readership ledger

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Use one personal original-source state with a stable incarnation/current manual-intent epoch, optional manual-unread override and a source-qualified covered frontier. The common homogeneous-access source needs one cutoff. Where actual source visibility is heterogeneous, retain the smallest bounded coverage representation that distinguishes already covered authority from newly admitted coverage; never silently reduce it to an uncomparable hash.

The minimum authoritative facts are tenant/owner/original, current state incarnation/intent epoch, covered source/visibility basis and cutoff, and the manual override. Operational updated time is not shown as a reader surveillance record. No per-message-per-person receipt table, every-keystroke event, global reader roster, per-arrival personal fanout, notification intent or durable prepared-read artifact is required. State is created lazily by a qualified view/manual command, not by merely listing an unread source.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0008 — C04 — Commit-ordered source content frontiers

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Every first-qualified eligible contribution receives an original-source reading ordinal under the same locked source transaction that admits its actual content/eligibility. The normal source-row counter and content row commit together. A later ordinal cannot become visible while an earlier allocated eligible contribution in that original can still commit behind the reader's cutoff. No counter advance on reads, ordinary edits, redaction, arrival retries or provider callbacks.

Reuse an existing qualified source-admission ordinal only if its eligible classes, timing and commit discipline actually satisfy this rule. Do not reuse D15 optional-follow acceptance ordering blindly, a PostgreSQL sequence, auto-increment/UUID sort, transaction ID, client clock, email Date, created_at or generic updated_at as commit order. Sequence gaps are not the only problem: later commit is the counterexample. Per-original locking avoids one tenant/global serial counter and uses the already-required source admission transaction. Any source-import/backfill must preserve first qualification and cannot insert newly eligible content invisibly below a previously acknowledged live cutoff.

Read snapshot body/projection and its offered cutoff must come from one coherent committed snapshot or equivalent proved source protocol. Fetching an old body and then the latest head in a later statement is unsafe. PostgreSQL isolation choice must be tested with the actual query/lock protocol; merely declaring Repeatable Read or Serializable without handling conflicts/retries does not prove the application behavior.

For existing content that predates this control ordinal, establish a **source-local migration baseline before any personal marker can be admitted for that source**. Gate all relevant source-eligibility writers and marker commands, capture the complete already-committed qualified eligible content under the source protocol, assign stable internal reading-control ordinals, and serialize every later eligible admission above that boundary. Preserve original content IDs, native admission times and provenance. This does not reconstruct or claim actual historic COMMIT order, create a native content/D15/D17 event, or mark any person's history Read. It is not the rejected per-user enrollment cutoff. An incomplete/unproved baseline cannot activate personal acknowledgments; later first-eligible material never slips behind live cuts because it has an old email/content date.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0009 — C05 — Server-bound snapshots and acknowledgment

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

A reader or explicit manual action uses a bounded server-issued snapshot token binding tenant, real owner, exact original set, source cutoff(s), current visibility coverage, topology/context generation and personal state/view-intent epoch. The client cannot claim an arbitrary future cutoff or another source/member. Revalidate current source access at acknowledgment; a token is context, not a grant.

The UI sends a qualified automatic acknowledgment only for the actual deliberate visible conversation reader under the selected UX rules. Prefetch, hidden panes, API fetch, CRM-profile loading, Tiptap mounting/focus, composing awareness and programmatic background refresh cannot themselves mint a new deliberate-view activation. A read acknowledgment is a product cue, not attestation of comprehension, all historical paragraphs or file inspection. Server validation does not pretend it can prove human attention.

Active composition is not qualified viewing of a newly arrived contribution even when the latest message region happens to remain visible beside the editor. Keep the new content unread and offer the established intentional return-to-current-content path without interrupting the draft or IME. A merely saved/inactive draft does not block ordinary reader qualification. Intentional return still uses the valid original view-activation/manual epoch; it cannot silently defeat a later Mark unread that requires a new conversation opening or explicit Mark read.

Keep raw source ordinals, hidden coverage entries and prior forbidden authority references server-side. The browser receives an opaque, integrity-protected bounded context token or equivalent owner reference plus only current-authorized display state; a merely base64-encoded signed object can still disclose its contents. Do not expose raw ordinal gaps as an accidental hidden-message count through the token, direct state relation, URL, analytics or error detail. Use existing scoped context mechanisms rather than a new per-view durable material store.

Apply only the token's offered cutoff, never “whatever is latest when ACK arrives.” If H+1 commits while H is being viewed/acknowledged, H+1 remains unread until separately included in qualified current viewing. The ordinary combined reader can acknowledge its complete currently authorized original/visibility snapshot vector after the latest eligible combined region is rendered. Older bodies may remain folded, paginated or offscreen; no per-original reading chore or all-history inspection is implied. Missing/unproved/truncated/inaccessible coverage or failure of the required current reader load cannot be included by guessing. Slow/out-of-order responses bind their original owner/source/session; they cannot clear a later source or account's marker.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0010 — C06 — Authorization coverage: preserve contractions, expose expansions

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

The source authorization owner supplies a bounded, control-only coverage basis and a sound comparison: current eligible coverage is unchanged/contained in acknowledged coverage, or it contains newly admitted coverage. The representation references existing source visibility/grant episodes, not new permission groups created by this feature. A hash/version mismatch alone cannot determine which case occurred.

Retain acknowledged cutoffs for proven retained coverage. Redaction, expiry, hiding or loss of access removes eligible contributors; it does not reset the remaining already-covered source to unread. Newly readable coverage that was previously hidden has no acknowledged cutoff, even when its content ordinal is below another scope's old cutoff. A regrant starts a newly qualified access episode unless the owner can prove the prior retained coverage is still valid under its actual rules. Neither a grant expansion nor merge can inherit a hidden source's Read state from unrelated content.

A compact vector of cutoff plus existing visibility/grant-episode basis is the narrow implementation direction for actual heterogeneous sources; the ordinary source remains one entry. It must be bounded by a measured source contract, with subset/added-scope checks provided by the actual authorization owner. Where no such owner contract exists yet, implementing and qualifying this narrow coverage contract is a prerequisite, not permission to ship a hash-only approximation. Do not create a message-reader ledger, user fanout on publication, arbitrary ACL language or new policy-history platform to obtain this proof. Where coverage cannot currently be established, return a truthful unknown/needs-current-view state and deny automatic catch-up; do not claim Read or reset all remaining material merely because an opaque epoch changed. Activation must qualify the supported policies and expansion/contraction cases, rather than monitor an unproved implementation.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0011 — C07 — Manual Read/Unread is a small conditional personal command

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

Explicit Mark unread changes only the caller's personal override and advances the current intent epoch with an expected-epoch comparison. Mark read advances that epoch and covers only the exact offered source snapshot. Repeating an old command cannot reverse a later manual choice. Automatic ACKs never advance the manual-intent epoch; they only monotonically extend the currently valid covered cutoffs when their deliberate-view activation epoch still matches.

A manual Unread while a source is already open must survive that view's later effects, rerenders and background refetches. Existing views/tokens remain tied to their earlier activation epoch; only a fresh deliberate opening or explicit Mark read after that choice can clear it according to the selected UX. New content never clears the manual override. A user's self-authored contribution never silently marks older other-authored content Read. The manual flag is not an unread-message count or workload obligation. An explicit revisit marker can apply to a readable source containing qualified human content, including self-only content; an empty/inaccessible/excluded-only source supplies no content to mark. The main decision may narrow that action without changing automatic baseline rules.

Use self-only CAS and max operations, not one forever receipt per click. Unknown response refetches the currently authorized state and reports that state; never blindly retry the old intention under a newly fetched epoch. A stale comparison may be a conflict/no-op even if the desired boolean happens to match; do not infer the exact earlier outcome from today's value. No outbox, email preparation or business audit event is created by these personal commands.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0012 — C08 — Bounded identities and anti-replay through cleanup

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Snapshot/view activations and manual requests are scoped to current source/access and personal-state incarnation with a bounded admission validity. Current state and minimum rejection fences live long enough that an issued old request cannot match an erased-and-recreated epoch-zero row. Regrant/retirement/restore must invalidate old access/view generations before accepting new personal state.

Reuse existing bounded authenticated command/context primitives. This does not require durable body snapshots, per-click result history or permanent reading receipts. Server-side expiry/generation checks, conditional creation and current self/source authority fence delayed duplicates; cancellation of HTTP is not server rollback. Clearing UI storage is not this fence. The exact token/recovery window and state/control retention belong to the qualified release contract and actual privacy owner, not a new guessed forever/30-day rule.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0013 — C09 — Merged conversation projection and commands

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

A merged UI cue is computed from currently admitted visible original-source reading states. Read/unread belongs to each original and is not copied into the current root. Undo preserves each original's own state, and a source newly combined with read work cannot become read just because the root was read.

Automatic acknowledgment covers the complete authorized original/visibility cutoff vector represented in the qualified combined reader snapshot when its latest eligible combined region is presented. Representation does not require every original's head/body to be separately mounted or visible: A+B may be covered while B's older body is folded or on another history page. An A-only or incomplete/unproved snapshot cannot acknowledge B. Explicit Mark read can cover the displayed authorized component snapshot, including its precisely offered original/cutoff/coverage vector; it cannot claim later membership. Apply the reviewed personal updates atomically across that bounded set with deterministic row-lock ordering, or reject the changed scope and refresh; never sweep in newly merged/hidden members at commit. A narrower authorized view acknowledges only its actual admitted source scope, not missing or inaccessible data. Current source authority is checked before exposing even aggregate boolean/count metadata. There is no cross-tenant command and no all-inbox bulk Mark read introduced by this model.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0014 — C10 — Database relationships, types and mutation limits

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Use actual UUID tenant/auth/profile relationships and TEXT Support original IDs. Derive the real owner/profile and active selected tenant from Core context; membership authorizes use but is not the durable owner. A tenant-aware unique original/owner key prevents duplicates. Same-tenant relationships bind coverage/source references and state; wrong owner/original/tenant/incarnation cannot be changed by a generic update.

Use bounded nonnegative/positive integer revisions and cutoffs, preserving exact values through the API rather than unsafe JavaScript Number conversion of unbounded bigint. Cutoffs cannot exceed server-offered admitted frontiers. Closed coverage schema and valid override/epoch combinations are checked; caller timestamps never establish ordering. A manual command needs current self/source-read capability, not another domain's write/refund/note-publication permission. No client-supplied reader identity is accepted. Deleting a personal marker cannot cascade into messages, source history, CRM or notification state. This feature adds no money field or financial arithmetic.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0015 — C11 — Grants, RLS and current acting context

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Personal-state reads/mutations use the shared API owner commands and the approved authorized read projections. Apply least grants and RLS/self-owner/current-source predicates on all exposed relations. Check effective SELECT/USING/resulting-row WITH CHECK, column immutability, permissive-policy unions, function EXECUTE/search_path/owner, invoker views and every privileged service path. A normal admin or broad tenant staff policy cannot enumerate others' reading state.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0016 — C12 — Privacy, restriction and retention

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Treat personal markers, covered source/grant references and operational times as potentially identifying metadata under an actual owner purpose and finite retention/cleanup policy. Exclude them from ordinary CRM Activity, staff productivity reports, viewer rosters, public APIs, donor/missionary portals, search bodies and generic exports. No read-time history is needed.

Ordinary successful view/ACK/manual-state operations must not create durable actor-plus-original-source-plus-time activity or diagnostic history. Use aggregate latency/error/conflict counts with bounded non-identifying dimensions; do not log success request bodies, coverage/view tokens or resource-identifying paths correlated with a principal. Qualify application, gateway and tracing configuration, not only one logger. Keep current self-state and necessary bounded command fences, not a succession of every previous reading state. Narrow security/incident events may retain minimum actor/resource facts under the existing restricted audit purpose and actual retention; this exclusion does not delete required security evidence or authorize general reading analytics.

D16/D17 restrictions govern ordinary source visibility and must invalidate forbidden cached metadata/contexts before use even when physical cleanup lags. Source contraction/redaction cannot manufacture new unread for retained covered content; a marked-unread source that becomes wholly unavailable shows no forbidden dot or existence. Independently valid metadata survives only under its declared purpose, not because it once identified a read note. Regrant restores no erased content. Privacy/offboarding cleanup handles self-state without transferring it to a replacement user, assignee, CRM owner or reused email. Source data restoration must restore its current source/privacy/access and personal-state invalidation barriers before old requests are accepted.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0017 — C13 — Failure, efficient queries and optional Realtime

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

Compute the personal boolean from bounded existing conversation rows, self-state and an indexed existence/frontier query over currently eligible source contributions. Do not scan whole histories into the browser or return raw global unread_count. Index current owner/original state lookup and original/eligible ordinal/visibility predicates; authorize before LIMIT/pagination. Sparse markers grow with actual personal interactions, not every message times every staff member.

No per-keystroke polling, per-row editor or eager body/attachment load is needed. Coalesce same-view acknowledgments; a stable covered cutoff requires no duplicate write. Realtime may carry minimal private invalidation to refetch through current authority, but it is optional and neither ACK transport truth nor a complete permission guarantee. Do not broadcast another person's reading state or enroll the relation into public table streams. Connection-time channel policies and cached JWT authority must not leak forbidden source activity after revocation. Current API/database checks remain authoritative.

On failure, retain only currently lawful existing state with an explicit stale/unknown cue; never fabricate zero unread or Read. Personal-state failure does not stop independent authorized drafting, posting, CRM inspection or actual work handling. Measure actual row/source volume, visibility-scope bounds, page size, concurrency, lock duration and p50/p95 before activation. No benchmark multiplier, instant-sync guarantee or new numeric unread count is inferred from vendors.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0018 — C14 — Email Studio, P17 notification engagement and CRM

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Reading-state changes never publish/prepare/send/rerender email, alter P6 delivery evidence, read/archive P17 notification groups, change Follow membership or acknowledge mandatory source review. P17's notification engagement is a separate capability; D34 composing presence does not attest to reading. A qualified Support reader reached from CRM updates the same self/source reading state without CRM copies or an Activity.

CRM-only profile loading, list prefetch or a hidden Support panel cannot count as the selected reading action. Actual source content remains owned by Support and adjacent business facts stay with CRM/giving/care owners. External tracking pixels, requester receipts, shared-team read switches, read analytics, document/attachment acknowledgment and generic workflow triggers are not added. Reading says nothing about responsibility, comprehension or business completion.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0019 — C15 — Migration, source qualification and safe rollout

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Do not import the old shared unread_count as every staff member's marker, divide it among agents, backfill fake read times or mark all old history read. Qualify source-first-human-content provenance and commit-ordered reading ordinals before activating personal cues. Retain accepted original source identities; unsupported legacy/generated content gets the owner's honest qualification treatment rather than guessed author/eligibility.

Deploy source ordering/coverage and private-state commands/readers first, then current UI semantics; retire old global marker reads/writes for the new cue. Old clients cannot submit unbounded future cuts, set another owner, drop coverage proof or restore stale epochs after schema changes. Initial enabling is on-demand absence semantics, not a global personal-state fanout. Scope kill switches disable the affected optional cue/state commands without changing real work, destroying personal intent or rolling back into shared-read semantics. Compatible roll-forward retains source/epoch/privacy fences. Source ordinals and exported control metadata must preserve semantic identity across safe migration; no provider-mailbox read synchronization is introduced.

Existing qualified legacy content uses C04's gated source-only ordinal baseline before personal state is enabled, rather than invented historical commit order. The boundary must cover all relevant writers and a complete committed source population; future/live eligibility then serializes above it. Real content/provenance/time and existing D15/D17 activity remain unchanged, and every unvisited person's content still follows C02's ordinary Unread baseline. Test interrupted/repeated migration, late old writers, incomplete qualification and activation ordering; do not generate a reader-by-source backfill or fake read audit.

### REQ26-D39-SUPABASE_CONTRACT-S0020 — C16 — Required falsifiable proof

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Prove the actual API/database/client protocol for: two people independent; same person across tenants/devices; absent/self-only/old newly accessible sources; own new content versus earlier other-authored unread; queued human reply versus later delivery; lower allocated sequence committing late; source lock/snapshot correctness; H view versus H+1 arrival; delayed acknowledgments; manual-Unread versus already-open tabs; new deliberate opening; explicit Read against a changed personal epoch; token expiry/cleanup/regrant; merge/Undo with exact original set; hidden old content expansion behind H; contraction/redaction of only an unread contributor; expired-source visibility; all source access roles and service routes; unavailable coverage and honest unknown state; cache/realtime invalidation; complete indexed pagination and rollback/restore.

Concurrency tests must exercise separate database sessions and actual isolation/row locks, not just a JavaScript arithmetic model. Include reverse commit order and grant/visibility transitions while a view token is outstanding. No logs or tests should expose real private bodies or reading rosters. Static source facts and the reasoned counterexamples here remain limited evidence; no database, provider, live UI/AT or production role tests were executed. The root's complete proof matrix should incorporate these outcomes without turning the small personal cue into an enterprise tracking system.

### REQ26-D39-R01 — R01 — Personal meaning

Applies to **US26-D39-01**, acceptance **AC26-D39-01-01–03**.

Support SHALL expose read/unread as the current staff member's personal orientation state over currently permitted conversation content. One person's action SHALL NOT change another person's cue. Read does not mean understood, handled, delivered, inspected in full, approved for sending, or completed in CRM/giving/care. No colleague names, reader roster, last-seen timestamp, requester receipt or employee reading report is added.

### REQ26-D39-R02 — R02 — Honest initial state

Applies to **US26-D39-01**, acceptance **AC26-D39-01-01–03**.

When no personal coverage exists, a source with currently eligible other-authored content SHALL be Unread on demand, including retained history and newly permitted history. An empty or self-only source SHALL have no automatic unread cue. Do not invent historical reads, introduce an enrollment cutoff, create staff-by-conversation state on arrival, send retrospective alerts, or turn unfamiliar history into a work obligation. No aggregate unread count/badge is added.

### REQ26-D39-R03 — R03 — Eligible contributions

Applies to **US26-D39-01**, acceptance **AC26-D39-01-01–03**.

First-qualified requester input, an admitted human staff context brief, a published native human Internal note, and another staff member's locally admitted external Reply SHALL qualify once under the owning source's provenance and safe-read rules. An already admitted Reply can be new content while its delivery remains Queued, failed or unknown. Later acceptance/delivery does not make it new a second time. Native trusted actor attribution alone identifies self-authorship; email resemblance, CRM relationship, assignment or caller JSON cannot establish it. This requires no speculative detector of whether every inbound sentence was typed by a human: use the existing qualified requester/contribution class and distinguish system-generated events by trusted provenance.

### REQ26-D39-R04 — R04 — Excluded events

Applies to **US26-D39-01**, acceptance **AC26-D39-01-01–03**.

Draft saves, composing presence, generated system notes, automatic confirmations, upload/scan progress, assignment/work changes, reminders, optional Following, note edits, redaction/expiry, merges and provider callbacks SHALL NOT create ordinary unread contributions. Existing direct attention and work obligations remain independently governed. Own posting SHALL NOT advance coverage over unseen contributions by others. No source body or attachment is admitted merely to make an unread cue possible.

### REQ26-D39-R05 — R05 — Source ordering and coherent snapshots

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

The source owner SHALL allocate a committed per-original reading order atomically with first content eligibility, using a source-local serialized admission protocol. A bare sequence, timestamp, email Date, generic updated_at or UUID order is insufficient. Content represented by the snapshot and its offered cutoff SHALL come from one coherent committed view. An acknowledgment of H SHALL never cover a newly committed H+1. A previously reserved lower ordinal SHALL NOT commit later behind an acknowledged cutoff. Source locks must follow a documented deterministic order and bounded transaction protocol, with retry behavior qualified on the actual database. Existing already-committed content may receive stable read-control ordering through R23's gated source baseline before any personal coverage; this neither reconstructs historical commit order nor creates new source content.

### REQ26-D39-R06 — R06 — Authorization coverage without a new permission system

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Personal coverage SHALL distinguish acknowledged permitted content from newly admitted visibility, even when newly visible content has an older ordinal. Preserve cuts for proven retained coverage on contraction; do not reset the whole source on every permission hash change. Reference existing source visibility/grant episodes, using one cutoff in the ordinary homogeneous case and the smallest bounded vector only where actual visibility requires it. The source authorization owner must prove containment/expansion. An uncomparable hash or missing coverage produces a truthful unavailable/needs-current-view result, not fabricated Read or a blanket Unread reset. Implementing this narrow owner contract is a preactivation prerequisite; do not create new ACL groups, a policy-history platform or per-message readership ledger.

### REQ26-D39-R07 — R07 — What automatically marks read

Applies to **US26-D39-02**, acceptance **AC26-D39-02-01–03**.

Automatic acknowledgment SHALL follow a deliberate opening of the actual selected, visible foreground conversation reader, after successful current-authorized data qualification and safe rendering of its latest eligible combined region. Fetch success, prefetch, list preview, default selection, roving focus, hidden pane, background refresh, notification receipt or editor focus cannot qualify. No dwell timer, percentage-read calculation or all-paragraph inspection is required. The product claim is orientation to the current conversation, not human comprehension or attachment inspection.

### REQ26-D39-R08 — R08 — Combined conversations and historical reading

Applies to **US26-D39-02**, acceptance **AC26-D39-02-01–03**.

A normal combined reader MAY acknowledge its exact complete authorized original/visibility cutoff vector after the latest eligible combined region renders successfully. Older bodies may stay folded, paginated or offscreen; users need not visit every original's head separately. Missing, unproved, inaccessible or incompatible scope cannot be guessed into that vector. A narrower original/search reader acknowledges only its represented scope. State stays attached to original sources across merge and Undo; a new original added after the snapshot never inherits Read. Multi-original commands apply the bounded exact set atomically or refresh on conflict.

### REQ26-D39-R09 — R09 — New activity while working

Applies to **US26-D39-02**, acceptance **AC26-D39-02-01–03**.

When someone is reading older history, following a search match or actively composing, newly arrived content SHALL remain unread until qualified viewing or explicit Mark read covers it. Active composition suppresses automatic catch-up even when new content renders nearby in the visible latest region. A deliberate return to current reading or **New activity** may qualify its presented snapshot under the still-valid activation; it cannot mint a fresh epoch merely to bypass a newer manual-unread choice. The mere presence of an inactive saved draft does not prevent normal reading. Preserve scroll anchor, keyboard focus, text selection, IME composition, recipients and both Reply/Note drafts. Do not reorder rows merely because a personal cue changes. Ordinary new content at the already selected latest region may qualify only after that new snapshot is safely presented under the still-valid view activation and the user is not actively composing.

### REQ26-D39-R10 — R10 — Simple manual actions

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

Use the existing conversation/row **More actions** menu for the state-appropriate **Mark read** or **Mark unread** command; retain text labels on touch and keyboard access. No routine confirmation or separate reading settings are needed. Mark read covers only the server-offered authorized displayed snapshot, not future content or a whole inbox. Mark unread is a personal revisit marker over current eligible readable human content, including one's own content when deliberately chosen. Empty, wholly expired, inaccessible or excluded-only sources provide nothing to mark and do not create phantom personal rows. No new bulk action, filter or unread folder is selected.

### REQ26-D39-R11 — R11 — Respect deliberate Mark unread

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

Manual commands SHALL compare and advance a personal intent epoch. Automatic acknowledgments only extend valid cuts under their original deliberate-view activation epoch. Mark unread made while the conversation is open SHALL survive that view's later rendering, old tabs, refreshes and ordinary focus changes. Only a new deliberate conversation opening after that choice, or a current explicit Mark read, may clear it. New arrivals and the user's own posting do not clear the override. This needs no editor lock, colleague roster or presence lease.

### REQ26-D39-R12 — R12 — Minimal conditional state and recovery

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

Use sparse current personal state and bounded context/generation fences, not a permanent receipt per reading click. A stale manual command cannot reverse newer intent; a lost response requires a current-authorized refresh, not blind reapplication under a freshly fetched epoch. Automatic retries remain bound to the original owner/source/cut/intent. Cleanup/regrant/restore SHALL fence old generations before state can be recreated, preventing epoch-zero ABA. No deferred offline queue may silently replay old reading intent later. Canceling an HTTP request is not database rollback.

### REQ26-D39-R13 — R13 — Trusted identifiers and database invariants

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Derive actual UUID tenant/auth/profile identity from trusted Core context; preserve TEXT original Support IDs. A same-tenant unique owner/original identity SHALL prevent duplicate active states. Tenant, owner, original, incarnation and author attribution are immutable through generic updates. Use constrained cutoffs/epochs and a closed coverage representation; preserve exact large integers across serialization. A client cannot choose a future cutoff or another owner. Personal cleanup cannot cascade into source content, CRM, P17 notifications or delivery evidence. No money field or arithmetic is introduced.

### REQ26-D39-R14 — R14 — Grants, RLS and opaque contexts

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

Route personal commands through the shared API owner and the approved authorized read-projection boundary. Current self ownership AND source read authority SHALL protect the relation, projections, result lookups and all privileged paths. Check grants, SELECT, USING, resulting-row WITH CHECK, column immutability, permissive-policy unions, RPC EXECUTE/search_path/actual owner, invoker views, Storage references and service-role paths. Ordinary staff/admin rights do not grant others' personal state. Tokens bind the exact owner/source/coverage/topology/epoch and remain bounded, opaque and integrity protected; a signed but merely base64-readable payload must not reveal hidden source IDs, ordinals or coverage. Tokens are context, not access grants.

### REQ26-D39-R15 — R15 — Reader and Tiptap boundary

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

The canonical safe reader SHALL distinguish successful nonempty body, valid empty/file-only content, restricted/unavailable content and invalid rendering. The current empty-wrapper-on-error behavior cannot trigger automatic Read. Validate source documents before lossy normalization; use the existing qualified canonical document and viewer profiles. Reading state SHALL NOT be a Tiptap document field, `onUpdate`/`onFocus` side effect, editor extension, autosave write or collaboration document. Do not remount/rewrite the editor when a cue changes. File-only content may qualify through permitted ready metadata without opening file bytes; failure of required current presentation remains truthful.

### REQ26-D39-R16 — R16 — Visual and accessible experience

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Use Core's Base UI and exact base-maia theme, semantic tokens, existing row/menu patterns and restrained emphasis. An unread dot plus appropriate subject weight may aid scanning, but expose **Unread for you** or equivalent accessible text; color and a hover tooltip cannot be the only meaning. Keep reading emphasis distinct from status/urgency and leave typography readable in Compact and Full. Menus must be keyboard/touch accessible with reliable focus return; no attention-grabbing animation or announcement on every background acknowledgment. Qualify reflow, zoom, contrast, reduced motion, Thai/RTL/international text, low bandwidth and assistive technology through the actual journey.

### REQ26-D39-R17 — R17 — Truthful failure and cross-device refresh

Applies to **US26-D39-03**, acceptance **AC26-D39-03-01–03**.

Reading-state failure SHALL NOT block otherwise authorized writing, posting, sending, CRM navigation or work handling. A pending/failed state must not settle into false Read; retain only currently lawful confirmed state and offer a small Retry where useful. Coalesce updates and refetch current authority on appropriate view/foreground navigation. Cross-device state converges through qualified refresh; no unsupported instantaneous-sync promise. Optional Realtime may carry minimal private invalidation, never bodies, a colleague read roster or read authority. Its join/JWT policy cache is not a per-message authorization check.

### REQ26-D39-R18 — R18 — One Support source across CRM

Applies to **US26-D39-04**, acceptance **AC26-D39-04-01–03**.

A genuinely authorized Support reader opened from CRM SHALL use the same real person's original-source state and preserve return context. CRM record/list opening alone does not mark Support read. Requester, participant, authenticated staff owner, CRM Party/contact, represented organization, assignee and CRM owner remain different concepts. Shared email, linking, unlinking, Party merge, assignment or conversation membership grants no additional Support/CRM/giving/care access and does not transfer reading state. No duplicate CRM body, Party, Activity, synchronization or business mutation is created by viewing/marking.

### REQ26-D39-R19 — R19 — Email Studio, P17 and P6 seam

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Support owns eligible source content and personal orientation. P17/Email Studio continues to own its governed reusable authoring, whole-message preparation and notification presentation/engagement; P6 owns actual communication/delivery and reconciliation. Viewing or marking SHALL create no Email Studio draft/publication/prepared material, dispatch, tracking pixel, provider read synchronization or recipient read receipt. It SHALL NOT read/archive related P17 notifications, change Follow membership or satisfy source-result/response/Send review. A real typed notification-click engagement remains with its existing owner; subsequent qualified Support presentation may separately update D39. D35 posted-note history, D36 quotations and D37/D38 drafts remain unchanged.

### REQ26-D39-R20 — R20 — Privacy, retention and departures

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Markers, cutoffs, hidden coverage references and operational times are potentially sensitive personal metadata. Inventory their purpose, retention and cleanup before activation. Ordinary user/admin exports, CRM history, public/missionary/donor APIs, global search and employee reports SHALL exclude them. Restriction/expiry removes ineligible contributors without fabricating new activity or renewing native source clocks. Offboarding never transfers markers to a new worker or a reused address. Minimum rejection fences may outlive active UI state only for a declared bounded purpose; restore must reinstate source/privacy/control barriers before serving old data. Previously disclosed bytes cannot be recalled by changing a dot.

### REQ26-D39-R21 — R21 — Query and workload discipline

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Compute one private boolean/known-state projection using bounded conversation rows, sparse owner/original cuts and indexed authorized eligible-content existence checks. No bodies, editor instances, staff-by-message fanout or whole-tenant scan solely to decorate a row. Authorization and eligibility precede pagination/aggregate conclusions. Coalesce identical acknowledgments and avoid writes when coverage is already sufficient. Record actual source/page/visibility cardinalities, active staff, concurrency, query plans, lock durations and p50/p95 under the existing qualified list contract before release; no invented scale or latency claim and no arbitrary new limit frozen by this decision.

### REQ26-D39-R22 — R22 — Minimal useful observability

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Measure aggregate technical read/command failures, latency and typed conflicts with body-free protected correlation. Normal successful view/acknowledgment/manual-state operations SHALL NOT generate a durable actor-plus-source-plus-timestamp activity stream that reconstructs employee viewing. This applies to application logs, gateway paths and traces, not just product analytics: avoid principal-correlated resource paths, view tokens and success payloads. Current state is not a public history journal. Narrow existing security events may retain necessary attribution under their own controls. No bodies, filenames, addresses, tokens or raw hidden ordinals in telemetry. O01–O05 define residual signals/thresholds/owners/responses; authorization or false-read correctness is a release gate, not merely a monitor.

### REQ26-D39-R23 — R23 — Source-first rollout and compatibility

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Qualify source provenance/order/visibility before private-state commands and their UI. Existing qualified content predating reading ordinals SHALL be captured as a complete already-committed source baseline under a gated source generation before personal markers/acknowledgments are enabled. Assign stable control ordinals without claiming to recover historical commit order, changing original content IDs/times/provenance, or emitting new content, D15 attention or D17 clock events. Serialize all subsequent first eligibility above that baseline; prove live publication cannot slip behind it. This is a one-time source-order initialization, not a per-user enrollment cutoff or fabricated read history. Do not backfill per-person state from shared `unread_count`, assignee, email, last-update time or provider status. Existing history uses R02 on demand. Retire the old shared-dot dependency for this cue; preserve any separately justified existing data under its actual owner. Mixed versions cannot bypass epochs, offer future cuts, strip coverage or revive retired state. A kill switch may stop the optional cue/commands while retaining current intent/fences and independent work. Roll-forward and restore preserve restrictions and exact original identity; do not roll back to misleading shared-read semantics after new personal state exists.

### REQ26-D39-R24 — R24 — Deliberate scope limits

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

This decision adds a personal cue and two contextual actions, not a new help desk, CRM, workflow engine, knowledge base, AI feature, tracking system, count/filter catalogue, offline vault or editor platform. It does not authorize new message intake, external attachments, refunds, receipt reissues, contact changes or disclosure. Reuse existing capabilities only where their semantics and authority actually fit. Do not preserve the current weak global count merely for visual consistency.

### REQ26-D39-R26 — R26 — Completion and release proof

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

P01–P30 SHALL be satisfied on the actual selected API/database/browser stack before activation, with real authorization, concurrent-session, migration, accessibility and production-shaped evidence. The owner coverage contract, numerical budgets, retention inventory and accountable operating assignments are prerequisites, not unknowns silently deferred to production. All 30 runtime groups remain required and unexecuted in this grooming session. Documentary checks and the four source-backed renderer fixtures are reported at their actual evidence level. No claim of perfect UX is made without intended-staff journey validation and correction.

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P01 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Two authorized staff open/mark the same conversation independently. Ben's actions never clear Ava's cue, reveal her read state or change work/assignment/reminder/response-review state. Current self state follows the same real person across authorized devices and remains tenant-separated.

**D39 clauses:** R01/R13/R18

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P02 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** No marker with retained/newly accessible other-authored eligible content returns Unread on demand; empty/self-only/excluded-only sources do not. Listing does not fan out rows, alerts or work. Explicit Mark unread can flag readable own human content; empty/expired/inaccessible sources produce no phantom marker.

**D39 clauses:** R02–R04/R10

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P03 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Exercise every qualified content class, queued/failed/unknown colleague Reply, duplicate inbound and later provider acceptance/delivery. Each eligible contribution enters once. Self attribution uses real source identity, not matching email; own posting does not cover older others' content. Edits/system events/drafts produce none.

**D39 clauses:** R03–R05/R19

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P04 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Explicit keyboard/touch/pointer conversation opening, visible focused reader and successful latest-region rendering acknowledge its exact snapshot. Prefetch/default selection/roving focus/hidden pane/API success/background tab/list preview/notification receipt do not. No timer or per-word inspection is required.

**D39 clauses:** R07/R15–R16

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P05 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Ordinary combined A+B snapshot after latest eligible region render catches up both offered authorized original cuts while old bodies remain folded/paginated/offscreen. Partial A-only/search/unknown coverage cannot acknowledge B. New C merged later and H+1 arriving after snapshot remain unaffected/unread.

**D39 clauses:** R06–R09

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P06 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Read older history/search results or actively compose a Reply/Note and receive new activity, including new content visible beside the editor. It stays unread while composing. Deliberate return/New activity navigates without automatic jump, caret loss, IME interference or row resorting due solely to the cue, and cannot bypass a newer manual-unread epoch. Inactive saved drafts do not prevent ordinary reading. At-latest noncomposing snapshots acknowledge only after successful presentation under a valid activation.

**D39 clauses:** R07–R09/R15–R16

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P07 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Real separate DB sessions reverse transaction timing: one eligible contribution begins before another and pauses before commit. Qualified source locking prevents the lower-behind-ack failure. Test deadlock/order/retry and coherent content+cut snapshot; a sequential JS arithmetic mock is insufficient.

**D39 clauses:** R05/R21

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P08 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Display H; admit H+1; then automatic ACK H or explicit Mark read H commits. H+1 stays unread. Old responses cannot substitute newest head or switch actor/source. Fault-inject between snapshot body and cut acquisition to prove coherence.

**D39 clauses:** R05/R07–R08/R14

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P09 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Validate complete visibility coverage at read/ACK, including heterogeneous original sources. Same/contained coverage preserves old cuts; permission hash mismatch alone cannot choose Read/Unread. Unknown comparison returns honest unavailable/needs-current-view without disclosure or silent reset.

**D39 clauses:** R06/R08/R14

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P10 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Grant access to an old note below a previous scalar head: its new scope is unread. Contract/restrict/redact/expire only unread or already-read contributors: retained acknowledged content does not reset. Wholly forbidden source gives no dot/metadata; regrant uses qualified episodes and cannot revive erased content.

**D39 clauses:** R02/R06/R20

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P11 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Mark unread while view epoch4 is open creates later intent. Old ACKs from that view or another already-open tab, rerenders, refetch and ordinary focus return cannot clear it. A newly deliberate qualified opening or explicit current Mark read can. Own posting and new arrivals do not clear override.

**D39 clauses:** R11–R12

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P12 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Concurrent manual commands with equal expected epoch cannot overwrite each other silently. Old opposite commands cannot win after newer intent. Valid auto ACKs merge nondecreasing cuts without advancing manual epoch or erasing a newer manual override. Multi-original writes apply exact reviewed scope atomically with deterministic locks.

**D39 clauses:** R08/R11–R14

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P13 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Drop response before/after mark commit, retry old request, cancel transport and refetch. Current authorized state reconciles; UI does not infer noncommit or reapply old intent under a new epoch. Pending/failed state never falsely confirms Read; no offline queue reverses later intent.

**D39 clauses:** R12/R17

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P14 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Retire/delete/recreate state, expire token, revoke/regrant membership/source and restore from backup with stale commands outstanding. Incarnation/control fences reject old generations; no epoch-zero ABA or generic update-as-create. Minimal retention ends only after old contexts cannot be admitted.

**D39 clauses:** R12–R14/R20/R23

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P15 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.
