Caller-forged tenant/owner/source/cut/epoch and allowed-row-to-forbidden-state transformations fail without existence leaks.

**D39 clauses:** R13–R14

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P16 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Inspect actual tokens, API payloads, direct relation visibility, errors, URLs, caches and telemetry. Another person's state, raw hidden original IDs, ordinal gaps and prior forbidden coverage are not disclosed, even inside merely encoded signed context. Current source and self checks apply on result lookup.

**D39 clauses:** R14/R20/R22

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P17 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Revoke access while list/reader/request/channel is active. New commands and result projections deny forbidden state; application cache clears appropriately. Optional Realtime join/JWT caching never broadcasts forbidden body/activity after revocation; fallback uses current API authority. Personal-state table is not a public stream.

**D39 clauses:** R14/R17/R20

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P18 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** A read/B unread → merge → qualified combined catch-up → Undo preserves each actual original cut. Partial source readers, changed topology mid-command, link/unlink/CRM merge, archived work and return navigation neither duplicate nor transfer coverage. A later new original remains uncovered.

**D39 clauses:** R06/R08/R18

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P19 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** On actual reader, valid text, valid empty/file-only, malformed document, unknown extension, restricted source, failed HTML/safe rendering and pending attachment profile yield distinct truthful outcomes. The current silent empty wrapper never triggers Read. File metadata orientation never claims downloaded-file inspection.

**D39 clauses:** R07/R15/R17

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P20 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** D35 note edits/history/redaction, D34 composing cues, D36 quote insertion, D37 Reply drafts and D38 Note drafts remain unchanged. Tiptap selection/onUpdate/onFocus/hydration and save/restore do not write read state; read feedback cannot rewrite/remount editor or clear either draft.

**D39 clauses:** R04/R09/R15/R19

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P21 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** From an authorized CRM record open its actual Support reader, return and reopen without losing context; same personal source state is used. CRM-only load causes no ACK; Party/contact/shared-email/organization/assignee associations grant nothing. No duplicate Party/body/Activity or financial/care mutation occurs.

**D39 clauses:** R18

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P22 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** P17 notification engagement, D15 Following, actual source-result/response/Send review and P6 delivery stay independent. A notification click follows its own existing typed rule; only subsequent qualified reader updates D39. View/mark creates no email preparation/publication/provider call/pixel/read receipt.

**D39 clauses:** R01/R03–R04/R19

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P23 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Disable/fail personal-state read/write/refresh while independently valid Reply/Note save/post, Send review and work/CRM commands run. Those owners still enforce their own guards and are not blocked by the cue. Failure is quiet/actionable, not a pagewide false-read/error cascade.

**D39 clauses:** R12/R15/R17

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P24 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Current restriction/expiry/departure/cleanup/export/backups follow declared purpose and finite retention. No ordinary manager/user export or report lists read times/people; departed owner's state is not reassigned. Source clocks and independent audit/communication evidence are neither reset nor cascaded away.

**D39 clauses:** R13/R20/R22

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P25 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Disposable qualified DB migration exercises old code/new schema, new code/old schema, restarted backfill, source-order qualification, legacy shared-dot retirement, optional-cue stop and roll-forward/restore. Existing eligible committed content receives a complete gated source-order baseline before personal ACKs; concurrent live publication cannot slip behind it. Preserve real IDs/times/provenance and create no new content/D15/D17 event or historical commit-order claim. No fake per-person historical Read or staff fanout; old clients cannot ignore coverage/epochs.

**D39 clauses:** R05/R12/R23

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P26 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Keyboard/screen reader/touch/IME tasks identify Unread for you separately from work status and operate More actions/New activity with reliable focus. Test Compact/Full, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, 200% text resize, 400% zoom-equivalent reflow, Core contrast/target requirements, reduced motion, Thai/RTL and long international names. No hover/color-only dependency or per-ACK announcement noise.

**D39 clauses:** R09–R10/R15–R16

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P27 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Actual representative tenant/staff/original/message/visibility/cardinality and concurrent-view/admission workloads record exact units, versions, limits, query plans, p50/p95 and lock duration. List projection remains bounded metadata-only; no per-row body/editor load, full-tenant scan, per-keystroke polling or staff×message state. Test boundary sizes and stale/missing coverage honestly.

**D39 clauses:** R05–R06/R21

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P28 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Formative intended-staff validation includes routine and occasional users: unfamiliar message, merged catch-up, deliberate Mark unread while open, older-history new arrival, failed reader/cue, mobile and CRM return. Use at least five participants as a study floor, not statistical proof; correct/retest any critical false-read/privacy/lost-work error and require core tasks without facilitator rescue. Do not invent study results.

**D39 clauses:** R01/R07–R10/R16/R26

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P29 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Trigger each O01–O05 signal; verify actionable ownership and response using synthetic minimized data. Normal successful automatic ACKs leave no durable actor/source/time reading stream; aggregate failure/latency metrics and narrow security attribution remain useful. Tokens/bodies/filenames/addresses are absent from logs.

**D39 clauses:** R20/R22/R26

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0002-P30 — Required actual release groups

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Falsifiable user/domain outcome and boundary:** Trace all R01–R26 and companion requirements into required glossary/ADR/OpenSpec/design/tasks/issues/implementation/release records. Reconcile stale Twenty prose to ADR0001; retain the accepted D1–D38 invariants. Record actual coverage owner, retention, budget and accountable assignments before activation; verify every evidence claim's limits.

**D39 clauses:** R24–R26

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O01 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed cross-tenant/cross-person/forbidden-source reading metadata exposure, unauthorized mutation, raw hidden coverage/token disclosure, or employee-view history leak.

**Owner:** Support security/privacy owner plus engineering on-call

**Response:** Contain affected projection/command/channel, preserve minimized security evidence, correct owner-controlled data and prove current access before re-enable. Keep independent authorized work available.

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O02 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Technical reading projection/command failures exceed 2% in a rolling 15-minute window with at least 100 eligible attempts per affected path. Exclude typed authorization denial, user cancellation, validation and expected CAS conflict from the failure numerator. Individual failures remain visible below the alert minimum.

**Owner:** Support reading-state engineering on-call

**Response:** Diagnose API/DB/renderer-specific path; preserve truthful state, bound retries and disable broken optional cue path if necessary. Do not block independent work or repeatedly replay stale intent.

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O03 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed false Read caused by skipped content/permission scope, a lost deliberate Mark unread, or a stale command that reverses newer intent.

**Owner:** Support source/data engineering owner

**Response:** Treat as correctness incident: stop affected auto-ACK/command path, retain minimal evidence, repair source/control cause and add actual concurrency/visibility regression proof before re-enable. Never mass-mark everyone read as repair.

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O04 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** p95 for an affected qualified reading projection/command exceeds twice its P27 release budget for 15 minutes with at least 100 samples; any unbounded scan/fanout regression triggers review immediately.

**Owner:** Support performance owner and database on-call

**Response:** Inspect plans/locks/coalescing/coverage size, mitigate optional cue load and roll forward qualified fix. Measure aggregates, not named employee reading speed.

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O05 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Three substantiated reports of the same reading-cue friction within 30 days, or one keyboard/assistive-technology task blocker or critical loss/privacy misunderstanding.

**Owner:** Support product/design owner with accessibility owner

**Response:** Reproduce the complete journey, correct the relevant cue/control/copy and retest intended-user tasks. Critical safety/accessibility failures are addressed immediately; do not wait for three reports.

### REQ26-D39-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003 — Residual operating controls

Applies to **US26-D39-05**, acceptance **AC26-D39-05-01–03**.

Reuse existing Support engineering/security/design responsibilities. Actual accountable people/teams and P27 workload/latency budgets must be assigned before activation. These numerical alert policies are **accepted operating judgments**, not vendor best-practice constants or performance promises. Safety/correctness defects below block release and trigger containment after release; they are never excused by low event counts.

No monitoring requirement creates a per-user reading analytics program. Needed diagnostic attribution is minimized and protected by its actual security/operational purpose. Coverage/authorization correctness, numeric release budgets and retention/owner assignments remain preactivation gates.

## Unwanted correspondence and future-mail holds

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0002 — UX01 — Four verbs with distinct consequences

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Use **Mark unwanted**, **Restore**, **Hold future email…** and **Stop holding** as distinct labelled actions. Mark unwanted and Restore apply to the current qualified admitted conversation disposition. Hold future email and Stop holding apply to a reviewed exact receiving-inbox/mailbox policy. Neither pair silently performs the other. D19's separate Release to inbox, Dismiss and Return to review continue to govern individual held inputs.

Do not use Block person, Ban contact, Unsubscribe, Clear spam, Trust sender or Delete as synonyms. A policy hold means review before admission; it does not establish malicious identity. A legitimate complaint or difficult request cannot be marked unwanted to remove real obligations. The same meaning and controls apply in the authorized Support reader reached through CRM.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| User intention | Correct action | What must remain independent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stop treating this qualified non-support conversation as ordinary work | Mark unwanted | Future-mail policy, CRM identity, subscriptions, delivery evidence and lawful source history |
| Correct that current disposition | Restore | Existing sender holds and already-held inputs |
| Hold new email from a reviewed exact address in one receiving inbox | Hold future email… | Current conversation disposition and each existing input's recorded intake decision |
| Stop that policy for newly received email | Stop holding | Already-held inputs, other gates, current unwanted conversation and prior decisions |
| Admit one held input after qualified review | D19 Release to inbox | Future sender policy and other input decisions; remaining safety gates still apply |

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0003 — UX02 — Current action in the existing conversation menu

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Place **Mark unwanted…** in the existing conversation More actions menu, distinct from the ordinary work-state picker and visually separate from permanent disposal/security actions. It opens one compact reviewed effect summary for the exact current qualified source/work scope. Never add Unwanted as a fifth everyday work status, a freeform label convention or an action on a CRM person.

This current Mark capability applies to qualified ordinary email-origin conversations, including their later notes and replies. It does not replace D26 staff-recorded/created-in-error correction, D12 related-work correction or D29 web/form safety and their own current source rules. Existing source kind/provenance remains intact; merely having an address or quoted email does not qualify another source as email-origin.

The summary identifies the current permitted conversation and receiving/handling context only where it affects the action. It explains:

> This correspondence will move out of ordinary Support work. Later email still follows normal intake. This action sends no email.

The primary action is **Mark unwanted**; secondary is **Cancel**. No mandatory essay, typed phrase or second generic confirmation is added. Show the actual retention consequence: **Recoverable until [current deadline]** only when that is true. If source content is already due to expire or the resulting action makes expiry immediately applicable under D17, say so before admission; there is no invented new recovery grace period. Restriction, holds and independent lawful metadata custody retain their actual meanings.

The server-qualified action must establish that real remaining work, owed correspondence, owner assistance and actionable recovery are not being buried. If that is not true, show a specific permitted explanation such as **This conversation still has work to review**, with the existing relevant review path. A checkbox saying the user accepts the risk is not a bypass. Mixed legitimate/unwanted content or originals cannot be hidden wholesale; use the data/lifecycle contract's exact eligibility and already accepted source-correction paths.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0004 — UX03 — A calm result and persistent recovery

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

After confirmed current disposition, show a quiet persistent **Unwanted** banner in the same reader with a visible **Restore** action wherever the actor has current restore authority. Keep the authorized source, notes and history readable under their existing rules. Preserve the selected record, position and drafts rather than immediately closing the pane or selecting a different conversation.

When the entire qualified component is set aside, show the Unwanted designation in place of a misleading active Open/Waiting presentation. Preserve actual work/source history; a dormant stored work value is not a current obligation. A component containing ordinary legitimate work remains visible under the main decision's exact original-source projection.

Show **Marked unwanted. This action sends no email.** as the brief confirmed result. A toast may supplement it but cannot be the only evidence or recovery route. This wording describes the Mark action; it does not deny or recall any earlier or possibly submitted communication. Marking does not imply deletion, successful support, requester awareness or a future sender hold.

The banner's current-policy line is independently qualified. Where the applicable policy is known and visible, it says either **Future email follows normal intake** or **Future email from [address] in [receiving inbox] is held for review** with the qualified management action. Do not assert that no hold exists when that lookup failed or the actor cannot inspect that policy. A neutral **Future-mail settings unavailable** is preferable to a false assurance or hidden-scope disclosure.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0005 — UX04 — Unwanted discovery without another work queue

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Add one built-in **Unwanted** inbox view over the same canonical admitted conversations, containing only currently all-Unwanted components with no genuine ordinary work to hide. The normal D20 work views exclude only those qualified components through an explicit projection amendment. If a component contains an ordinary original or actual owed work, it stays in ordinary work and is not presented as wholly Unwanted. Its other originals' unwanted designation/history remains accessible in the authorized combined reader and D22 search. Do not create another content store or search index.

Ordinary authorized D22 search includes admitted unwanted source matches and labels that matching original **Unwanted**, opening the same source/current reader and applicable Restore path. It must not label the entire mixed component unwanted when another original is ordinary. This preserves accurate source and current-work meaning without requiring a separate original-management dashboard.

The view uses the existing bounded list controls and current tenant/inbox scope. Default ordering follows the latest current unwanted designation, with a stable tie-breaker; do not rewrite source message times. Show permitted subject, actual source sender, marked time and current availability where useful. Reuse existing complete server pagination and its approved 25/50 list facilities; no numerical badge, all-matches selection, new bulk effect, advanced filter builder or folder hierarchy is needed.

An authorized complete empty result says **No unwanted conversations in this inbox**. Loading, inaccessible scope, partial result and failed lookup are not that empty state. A search with no match says **No matching conversations** while retaining the query. Unknown/expired content is never represented as a fully restorable record merely because metadata remains; current source/custody determines what can be listed.

Held inputs remain in D19 **Needs review**, not Unwanted. One is admitted correspondence disposition; the other is input awaiting admission. The UI need not teach internal architecture, but its labels and navigation must preserve that distinction.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0006 — UX05 — Restore is a current correction

Applies to **US26-D40-02**, acceptance **AC26-D40-02-01–03**.

Restore uses the exact current unwanted episode and current source/work authority. It removes the applicable current designation and returns the conversation to **Open for review** under qualified current handling/coverage. It does not rewind old status, old assignments, expired reminders, source dates, original message IDs or independently admitted effects.

Keep the visible Restore control in the banner, Unwanted view's contextual actions and the same qualified search/CRM reader. Where current preflight permits a simple restore, one explicit action is enough; the banner/action summary already explains its effect. A changed or ambiguous work plan requires the current existing review, not a blind historical replay. Confirm **Restored to Support work** only after the actual owner result; preserve the reader context.

If an applicable hold remains active, explain before/at Restore: **This restores the conversation. It does not stop holding future email.** Offer the separately authorized management path. If source bytes are expired or restricted, never promise restoration of them; show the actual permissible correction, metadata availability and reason. A missing old source cannot be replaced by a copied transcript or recreated CRM record.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0007 — UX06 — Notes and drafts remain useful

Applies to **US26-D40-03**, acceptance **AC26-D40-03-01–03**.

Current authorized Internal note creation and original-author posted-note correction remain available on an unwanted conversation for explanation and accountability, without requiring Restore. D35/D38 and current source lifetime still apply. External Reply or new Support work requires the current Restore/review path first; it cannot silently restore by sending.

Keep the accepted private Reply and Note working states, save truth, files and revision guards intact. The Reply area says **Restore this conversation to reply**, with the qualified Restore action. Do not erase an existing Reply draft or switch its mode/recipient to make the disabled action look simple. Notes retain their clear Internal label; publishing one is not an email and does not invent completed work or renew an expired source clock.

Current Mark unwanted, Restore and policy operations preserve both dirty drafts, selection and IME. If a real navigation would destroy work, apply the existing D37/D38 leave protections to all affected working states. A draft alone is not proof of an actual Support obligation; a possibly admitted send/post requires its existing recovery and cannot be dismissed through this UI. Do not mutate Tiptap document content to store the designation or policy.

If a genuinely new actionable owner result or delivery-recovery obligation arises after a valid Mark, its qualified original/current work home returns to visible **Open for review**, ending only the now-inapplicable current exclusion. Show the actual recovery need; do not fabricate an incoming human message or erase prior classification history. Duplicate or already-reviewed results do not repeatedly reopen work. The sender-hold policy remains unchanged, and a provider-status event alone does not become a D39 human-content unread contribution.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0008 — UX07 — Start a hold from exact existing evidence

Applies to **US26-D40-04**, acceptance **AC26-D40-04-01–03**.

Offer **Hold future email…** contextually from an actual admitted inbound message's More actions or from the trusted action area of a currently authorized qualified D19-held input. Both use the same canonical input owner and independently proved single From mailbox, actual receiving inbox and current hold-management authority. A conversation-level convenience may prefill only when there is one unambiguous eligible pair; otherwise select the actual source message explicitly. Do not infer the pair from a CRM card, display name, Reply-To, quoted forward, CC/BCC list, current assignee or current handling inbox.

A held input need not be released into ordinary Support merely to create a future hold. Starting the policy changes neither that input's existing gate/decision nor its safety, classification, availability or Release requirements. Review access alone does not grant policy authority. Keep the trusted action outside untrusted message content; it grants no new right to preview an unsafe body or attachment. A manual/web-only record, arbitrary entered address or quoted message is not a qualified canonical incoming-email occurrence.

The future action does not require misclassifying all current work as unwanted. A mixed conversation may retain genuine work while a separately authorized exact future policy is reviewed from an eligible source; ordinary policy eligibility still applies. Mark unwanted never launches or checks the hold automatically.

A move matters. If input reached receiving inbox A and the conversation is now handled in B, the hold review names A and checks A's current authority. It cannot silently act on B or all inboxes. Merged originals with different sender/inbox pairs need one exact source selection. Missing, ambiguous or unsupported sender/receiver evidence leaves this action unavailable with a useful explanation, rather than a guessed address or arbitrary input form.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0009 — UX08 — One small, explicit future-policy review

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

The hold review presents an immutable exact address/inbox pair and current receiver/review readiness. It uses one primary **Start holding** action and Cancel. No preselected block checkbox, domain/IP matching, alias expansion, multi-inbox scope, freeform rule builder or combined Mark-and-hold command is introduced.

Suggested compact content:

Illustrative control arrangement (labels and effects govern, not fixed pixels):

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
> Hold future email
> 
> From                 offers@example.org
> Receiving inbox      Donor care
> 
> New email from this address to this inbox will wait in Needs review.
> This does not block a person or change this conversation.
> This does not change email already in Asym.
> 
> Cancel                                      Start holding

The address/inbox above are synthetic copy examples. Use the real currently authorized pair; never use a fallback inbox name. Match policy is the source owner's exact canonical mailbox semantics. Do not collapse plus aliases or broaden to a domain merely to increase hit rate. Clearly state that a mailbox can carry legitimate email and that held messages use the inbox's existing review team. This is a fixed hold policy, not a trust-verification claim.

Hold readiness requires the qualified receiving owner and viable D19 review coverage. If it is unavailable, retain current work and explain **Future-mail holding is not ready for this inbox** with the existing permitted setup/repair path. Do not expose hidden team names or use a saved-rule row as proof the receiver enforces it. The action becomes **Starting…** while pending and **Holding future email** only after the owner confirms effective admission. Original received timestamps never decide a retroactive batch sweep.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0010 — UX09 — Explain what happens to future input

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

A matching input is held under the policy snapshot established by the receiving owner at its first accepted intake boundary. It joins the existing D19 Needs review journey with the additional plain reason **Sender hold** and the currently permitted exact address/inbox explanation. No second review queue, new Support conversation, automatic deletion or hidden auto-release is created.

An input first accepted before a hold became effective keeps its recorded decision even if downstream processing is delayed. Stopping later likewise does not rewrite already accepted input. User-facing copy refers to newly received email in Asym after activation; the technical contract binds the actual trusted first intake boundary, never the provider's earlier receipt time, sender's Date header or an arbitrary worker execution time.

D19 reviewers still see all relevant gates and source availability. **Release to [inbox]** decides that one input under current authority; it does not stop the hold. **Dismiss** does not strengthen it. Technical Retry is not Release. Any ordinary automatic confirmation after release still requires D13's existing eligibility and deadline; neither this policy nor this UI invents an email notice.

If held material reveals a false positive, the reviewer can make the appropriate one-item decision and, if separately authorized, navigate to the hold's management. A qualified held input may also launch the independent exact future-hold review without first being released, as UX07 specifies. Stopping or starting future holding is not bundled with Release. Staff without future-policy authority retain the existing qualified escalation path; they do not need a new omnipotent reviewer role.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0011 — UX10 — A durable, small management location

Applies to **US26-D40-05**, acceptance **AC26-D40-05-01–03**.

Manage existing holds in **Support settings → [receiving inbox] → Sender holds**, within the qualified inbox receiving settings. The inbox context is always explicit. Default to **Active**, with a second **Stopped** view for retained policy history/correction. Exact sender/inbox pairs are read-only; change of target is a new reviewed policy operation from qualified input, not editing an existing identity.

Each row shows the full mailbox, current policy state, relevant created/stopped time and permitted attribution. Do not show message bodies, sensitive source titles, live private content, noisy hit counters or a staff productivity score. Provide exact-mailbox search and the existing bounded server pagination, without advanced filters, aggregate badges, imports, arbitrary Add-rule forms or a global contact blocklist. An original conversation need not remain readable or retained to stop a currently authorized policy: policy control has its own declared minimal custody and capability.

Active rows offer **Stop holding**. Stopped rows may offer **Hold again…**, which reviews the same pair under current source/policy capability, route readiness and review coverage. It creates/admits the current qualified generation; it does not resurrect an old token or repeat a previously stopped command. If current required proof is no longer available, explain the necessary current qualification rather than blindly activating an old row. Stopping remains independently usable where authorized.

Empty copy: **No active sender holds in this inbox** after complete successful Active loading; **No stopped sender holds** for Stopped. Keep inbox context and help visible. A failure says **Could not load sender holds** with Retry, not a reassuring empty list. Existing stop/history data is limited by its actual finite control-purpose retention, not an indefinite promise to display every previous policy.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0012 — UX11 — Stop holding is easy and does one thing

Applies to **US26-D40-05**, acceptance **AC26-D40-05-01–03**.

Stop holding is a contextual conditional action for the exact active policy generation shown. Its visible helper says **New email received by Asym will follow normal intake. Messages already held still need review.** No second generic confirmation is necessary when the exact current pair and effect are already presented. Never combine Stop with Release all, Restore conversation, trust/allowlist, or a provider change.

Show **Stopping…** while pending. Only confirmed success shows **Stopped holding [address] in [inbox]**. In Active view, remove/move the row after the actual result while preserving selection and keyboard focus predictably; it remains discoverable in Stopped while retained. A supplemental result may link to Needs review, under current permission, but does not imply a visible pending count if that population is unknown.

There is no blind Undo that reactivates a stopped policy. **Hold again…** remains the clear requalification path. If another authorized operator changed the policy, show **This hold changed. Review its current state**, preserving the intended action without overwriting it under a new revision. Ordinary safety/review gates may still hold future email after this particular rule stops; the UI says normal intake, not guaranteed delivery to work.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0013 — UX12 — Role and capability clarity

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Current disposition, restore, source read, D19 review, hold management and control-history read are separately authorized operations under existing Core owners. One person's assignment, generic staff status, reviewer membership, CRM relation or permission to read the old message does not automatically grant future-policy control.

A qualified ordinary worker may mark/restore current unwanted correspondence while lacking hold controls. The page stays useful; do not make future-policy setup a condition of current cleanup. Where revealing the action's existence is permitted, a disabled control can explain **You don’t have permission to change this inbox’s sender holds** and retain the established authorized help/request path. Do not imply that a generic administrator label grants the capability or expose hidden inbox/team/actor names through denial messages.

The sender itself receives no notice, account ban or subscription change. Managers see only authorized policy/source data, not private drafts or another person's read history. Holding an address does not grant visibility into all CRM people who use it or all other inboxes receiving from it.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0014 — UX13 — Truthful pending, failure and changing context

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Situation | Visible behavior | Required boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Known current action success | Confirm its exact current/policy effect and retain the persistent inverse control where valid. | Never infer success from a clicked button or an optimistic moved row. |
| Definite rejection | Retain the applicable confirmed state and useful error/retry path. | No partial fake current disposition or effective-policy promise. |
| Lost response/unknown outcome | **Could not confirm the change. Checking current state…** then truthful resolved/unconfirmed state. | Reconcile the original operation under current authority; no fresh key or blind new-revision replay. |
| New message/work/topology during current review | **Conversation changed. Review the latest activity.** | No burying newly legitimate work or extending a prior review to new originals. |
| Sender/receiving route/current policy changes during hold review | Recheck and show the actual current pair/effect before a new deliberate admission. | No default-inbox fallback, scope expansion or expired generation replay. |
| Coverage disappears | Existing D19 coverage exception/repair is visible to its owner; stop control remains independently qualified. | Offboarding/security revocation is never blocked, and intake is not silently dropped. |
| Source content expires | Source displays the true current availability and permitted correction; policy management remains accessible under its own authority. | No new recovery grace, body recreation or resetting D17 clocks. |
| Hold cannot be loaded/enforced | Show unavailable/unknown readiness and qualified repair. | A stored policy is not proof the intake receiver is enforcing it; no silent passthrough assurance. |

Keep ordinary authorized reading, note work, CRM navigation and independently valid owner operations useful during a policy lookup outage. Actual current-disposition/send/hold commands still require their own guards. Error repair cannot stop all source privacy/retention enforcement or bypass a held-input safety gate. No setting refresh replaces a draft or discards changes to unrelated inbox settings.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0015 — UX14 — Coherent, accessible and restrained visual design

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Use the existing shared Base UI menus, dialogs, tabs, buttons and form relationships with exact **base-maia** tokens. Keep the message content and exact address/inbox identity visually primary. Use a quiet Unwanted banner and clearly labelled policy status; no red person badge, alarm animation, unread count, dense admin dashboard or custom control toolkit.

Current action and future hold previews are short: readable title, exact scope, concrete consequence, primary action, Cancel. Long addresses and international inbox names wrap or expose their full accessible value; do not truncate away the part that distinguishes the target. Use direction-isolated mailbox text where needed and preserve Unicode/IDN source semantics without pretending visual similarity proves equality.

Menus/actions are reachable by keyboard and touch, have descriptive accessible names, visible focus, proper Escape and predictable focus return. Use Core's touch targets of at least 44 CSS px, readable type at 320 CSS px/400% zoom and no hover-only action. Pending/confirmed/error messages are visible and politely announced without repeating on every background event. Keep the same route and essential actions usable on mobile; avoid horizontal page scrolling or controls hidden behind the keyboard.

Do not animate list reordering or auto-scroll to a different record after an action. When a row legitimately leaves the current view, keep its reader/result accessible until the user navigates, with predictable focus to the retained result or nearest stable control. Existing reduced-motion behavior remains. No browser prototype or automated check alone establishes this quality; actual intended-staff and AT journeys are required.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0016 — UX15 — CRM, Email Studio and reporting stay coherent

Applies to **US26-D40-07**, acceptance **AC26-D40-07-01–03**.

The same authorized Support source and disposition appear when reached through CRM, with return navigation preserved. No CRM Party, organization, relationship, contactability, donation, receipt, consent, login or care record is deleted, blocked, copied or updated through these controls. The mailbox/inbox policy belongs to receiving, not to CRM identity.

Current action, Restore, Start/Stop holding and management create no Email Studio draft/template/prepared message, P6 dispatch/provider spam report, tracking pixel, automatic response, unsubscribe or survey purpose. They do not read/archive P17 notifications or claim D39 viewing. Actual note posting, legitimate newly admitted input and allowed typed attention retain their already accepted effects. D28 spam/auto-only exclusions and genuine handling facts remain: a mark/restore cycle cannot fabricate a successful resolution, reroll feedback, erase past delivery or improve historical metrics.

An active sender hold is an inbound per-occurrence gate, not a global outbound or contactability suppression. A valid D19 release returns that specific admitted input to its normal purpose rules without stopping the policy or creating a fresh deadline/opportunity. D13 still requires its original confirmation qualification; D28 still requires actual eligible completed work, and Release itself is no feedback trigger. Other legitimate conversations keep their independently authorized communication behavior. Current Unwanted designation still disqualifies its own definitely-unsubmitted optional effects through their actual source/P17/P6 fences; already or possibly submitted evidence remains immutable.

### REQ26-D40-UX_BLUEPRINT-S0017 — Required complete journeys and acceptance evidence

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

These are future runtime/participant proofs for root's consolidated matrix, not tests claimed run now.

1. An eligible single unwanted conversation can be marked in one compact review, remains identifiable/readable under current source rules, leaves default work views, appears in Unwanted and authorized ordinary search, and can be restored from the persistent same-source path. Only all-Unwanted components enter the Unwanted view; a mixed component remains ordinary while its matching unwanted original is accurately labelled in authorized search/history. No hold or email occurs.
2. Restore changes only the qualified current episode; an active applicable policy stays active and the UI explains this. Old expiry, assignments, reminders, P6 evidence and CRM facts are not replayed.
3. Both draft modes survive all current/policy commands. Internal note and original-author correction remain usable when allowed; external Reply/new work follows explicit Restore/current review. Pending admitted operations cannot be discarded as drafts.
4. Hold creation starts from one actual admitted inbound message or currently authorized qualified D19-held input, with independent exact From/receiving-inbox and policy rights. A held input is not first released merely to expose the action and all its current gates remain unchanged. A moved A→B conversation reviews receiving A; merged/multiple sender pairs cannot silently pick a latest/default/CRM-derived target. Ambiguous/missing input evidence and manual/web/quoted substitutes fail honestly.
5. Mark unwanted never enables a hold. Start holding has one exact address/inbox review, current policy authority, viable existing review coverage and no domain/alias/all-inbox broadening.
6. Inputs first accepted before versus after start/stop retain the correct intake policy snapshot despite delayed processing, retries or stale email Date headers. No retroactive batch changes occur.
7. Future matches use D19 Needs review with Sender hold plus other actual gates. One Release does not stop the policy; Stop does not release or undismiss the backlog. Other safety gates still govern.
8. Sender holds management works independently of reading/retaining the original conversation. Active/Stopped, full mailbox, existing search/pagination, Stop and requalified Hold again have truthful empty/error/unknown states and no private-content or hidden-count leak.
9. Stale concurrent Start/Stop/Restore/disposition responses cannot reverse newer decisions, expand source scope or create duplicates. Pending/unknown outcomes reconcile the original effect; requalification never silently reapplies an old intent.
10. Incoming legitimate work, mixed originals, existing assistance, owed replies and delivery recovery cannot be buried by current disposition. Qualified later admitted input returns appropriate current handling without requiring requester resubmission or inventing another original message. In A+B, newly ordinary B makes the component ordinary and removes it from the all-Unwanted view; A's remaining classification/history is preserved and labelled at original scope. Newly actionable owner/delivery recovery after Mark similarly exposes the affected current work, without a fake incoming message, changed future hold or provider-status-generated D39 unread.
11. Permission changes, receiving-route changes, reviewer offboarding, source expiry, holds and old-generation replay preserve current authority and useful recovery. No fallback Donor Care name or saved default is treated as target authority.
12. Current/held/policy/reporting views remain source-authorized and coherent through CRM; no Party/account block, unsubscribe, P17 engagement sweep, provider spam feedback or D28 eligibility invention occurs. With an active sender hold, a legitimately released input and a separate existing legitimate conversation retain their normal independently qualified communication eligibility; no mailbox-wide outbound suppression is inferred.
13. Real keyboard, touch, screen-reader, IME, mobile, zoom/reflow, long-address and mixed-script tasks complete with clear scope, focus and result states. Low-bandwidth failures preserve drafts and never falsely show an effective hold or restored content.
14. Intended staff distinguish the four verbs and D19 Release without coaching: set aside one item, optionally hold future mail, correct each independently, and recover a legitimate held input. Test ordinary workers and appropriately authorized policy/review staff rather than assuming everyone has the same permissions.

The resulting journey is complete but small: one current classification with a persistent Restore path, one optional exact future hold with independent Stop management, and the existing review queue.

### REQ26-D40-R01 — R01 — Two independent capabilities

Applies to **US26-D40-01**, acceptance **AC26-D40-01-01–03**.

Support SHALL provide recoverable current unwanted handling and an optional separately chosen future-mail hold. Mark unwanted does not create a rule; Hold does not require marking the current conversation. Restore does not stop a rule; Stop holding does not release existing held inputs. No command deletes a CRM Party, changes consent/login, sends mail or grants new source access.

### REQ26-D40-R02 — R02 — A classification outside ordinary work

Applies to **US26-D40-01**, acceptance **AC26-D40-01-01–03**.

Unwanted SHALL be an original-source designation, not a fifth D3 work status, deleted message, successful resolution or requester reputation. Preserve prior source/work events. An all-Unwanted component presents an Unwanted banner instead of a misleading active Open/Waiting badge. A component with any ordinary original or genuine owed work stays visible in ordinary work; retained unwanted originals remain available as authorized history rather than disappearing from the combined reader. Historical outcomes are not rewritten. The projection has one canonical source, not a copied spam conversation.

### REQ26-D40-R03 — R03 — Exact eligible current scope

Applies to **US26-D40-01**, acceptance **AC26-D40-01-01–03**.

Mark unwanted applies to ordinary admitted email-origin sources in this selected journey, including their legitimate source history of notes and replies. It SHALL require an authorized explicit review that the bounded current source/component has no legitimate Support obligation to hide. It does not replace D26's staff-recorded created-in-error correction or D29 form-safety owners. Outstanding promises, assistance, actionable owner results or actual delivery recovery cannot be erased. A difficult complaint or donor problem is not unwanted. A mixed legitimate/unwanted conversation cannot be sidelined wholesale. Use existing exact-input No reply needed or legitimate D10/D12 corrections where applicable; do not invent message reparenting, duplicate records or an AI legitimacy scorer.

### REQ26-D40-R04 — R04 — One authoritative Mark command

Applies to **US26-D40-01**, acceptance **AC26-D40-01-01–03**.

The command SHALL bind exact originals, current topology/content/work revisions and actor authority. Atomically record the designation, immutable decision/result and qualified changes to current work projections. It may apply D14's exact reviewed No reply needed disposition to truly unowed contributions and retire only their inapplicable deferral/review effects; preserve genuine obligations, original ages and known misses. No redundant second click is required merely to perform those same reviewed effects. Do not append a successful resolution, fabricated reply, feedback trigger or new human-content event.

### REQ26-D40-R05 — R05 — Restore means current review

Applies to **US26-D40-02**, acceptance **AC26-D40-02-01–03**.

Restore SHALL remove only the applicable current mistaken designation and return the permitted source to **Open for review** under current handling/coverage authority. It is a new correction, not rollback to stale Waiting, assignment or reminder snapshots. Reverse only still-current mistaken D14 no-reply dispositions under that owner's existing correction rules; accepted-covered inputs, independent Off decisions, newer content and historical deadlines remain intact. A newly admitted relevant human input also returns its valid source to review; held-before-admission mail does not do so until genuine release/admission. Restore alone creates no incoming message, feedback opportunity or new retention lifetime.

### REQ26-D40-R06 — R06 — Originals, merges and topology

Applies to **US26-D40-02**, acceptance **AC26-D40-02-01–03**.

Persist designation and correction on actual original sources. A component-wide action requires exact permitted scope and eligibility for every affected original, with atomic application or conflict—not hidden partial success. A new merge involving Unwanted work requires lawful Restore first; D10 Undo remains available when otherwise permitted and preserves each original's actual designation/history. An all-Unwanted resulting component does not automatically become Open or acquire retention activity merely because ordinary D10 detachment normally creates review. A new relevant contribution changes its own valid original and current work-home projection atomically, making actual work visible without erasing the other originals' classification history. A later unrelated or newly merged original never inherits an old action. Future holding may be initiated from one qualified inbound message in mixed work without misclassifying the whole conversation.

### REQ26-D40-R07 — R07 — Drafts, notes and pending sends

Applies to **US26-D40-03**, acceptance **AC26-D40-03-01–03**.

Private Reply/Note drafts remain private and may save/discard while their actual custody allows. They neither block Mark by mere existence nor disappear with it. Public Reply or creating new actual Support/owner work requires Restore and normal current review first. An authorized Internal note or own-note correction may document the decision without auto-restoring work; D38 admission/mentions and D17 native-note clocks still apply. Mark SHALL NOT silently cancel or hide admitted human mail. Outstanding submission/dispatch/unknown actionable effects require their existing reconciliation or explicit permitted cancellation first; a reviewed historical uncertainty with no remaining effect must not become an eternal blocker. A newly actionable owner result or delivery failure after a valid Mark makes its valid current original/work home visible for Open review, ending only the now-inapplicable current exclusion while preserving designation history. Duplicate or already-reviewed evidence cannot repeatedly reopen work. This source-owned transition creates no fabricated human-content admission or D39 unread event.

### REQ26-D40-R08 — R08 — Current-action UX and recovery location

Applies to **US26-D40-01**, acceptance **AC26-D40-01-01–03**.

Offer Mark unwanted in existing conversation actions with one concise review of scope, effects and actual recoverability; future holding is a separate optional action, never a prechecked add-on. Keep a built-in **Unwanted** inbox view and a persistent **Restore** action on the same authorized conversation. Reuse the list/reader and Base UI/base-maia shell. Preserve position, focus, dirty drafts and mobile navigation; show meaningful pending/error outcomes rather than vanishing a row before durable acceptance. No permanent-delete button or new trash timer is added.

### REQ26-D40-R09 — R09 — Exact receiving inbox and observed mailbox

Applies to **US26-D40-04**, acceptance **AC26-D40-04-01–03**.

A hold SHALL target one tenant, one immutable qualified **receiving inbox** and one exact qualified observed sender-mailbox key. Current handling inbox, a hardcoded default, Reply-To, envelope return path, CRM preferred email, display name or quoted forward is not a substitute. Contextual creation may start from an actual admitted inbound message or a currently authorized qualified D19-held input, always with independent policy authority and the same proven receiving/mailbox pair. Staff must not release an input merely to configure a future hold; creating the rule changes neither that existing input's recorded decision nor its gates. A conversation shortcut may prefill only an unambiguous eligible pair. Show the actual sender address and receiving inbox explicitly. Ambiguous/unsupported evidence withholds the shortcut rather than guessing. Manual/web-only context cannot fabricate email evidence. No domain wildcard, plus/dot alias collapse, all-inbox scope or arbitrary sender registry is selected.

### REQ26-D40-R10 — R10 — Straightforward hold management

Applies to **US26-D40-05**, acceptance **AC26-D40-05-01–03**.

Use **Hold future email for review** as the deliberate command and **Sender holds** within the actual receiving inbox's existing settings for management. Show Active/Stopped, exact address/inbox, actor/start or stop evidence and a source-authorized route to related held work. Policy permission does not grant message-body/held-count access. Start/Stop are explicit actions; immutable scope is not silently edited. Restarting a stopped pair is a fresh qualified activation, not resurrected approval. No rule builder, administrator approval queue, second settings hierarchy or compulsory expiry picker is added.

### REQ26-D40-R11 — R11 — Canonical intake policy owns holding

Applies to **US26-D40-06**, acceptance **AC26-D40-06-01–03**.

Implement the bounded sender-hold predicate in the canonical intake owner and shared the shared API owner boundary, with one authoritative policy store/read model. This is new typed capability qualification, not a claim that current recipient-route CRUD already implements it. No Support-local matcher, second sender identity system or configurable automation engine is authorized. Phase34 retains general rule vocabulary; the narrow owner integration must be captured and proved before activation. Runtime unavailability is an owned pending/processing condition, never permission to silently ignore the hold.

### REQ26-D40-R12 — R12 — Define future by durable acceptance

Applies to **US26-D40-06**, acceptance **AC26-D40-06-01–03**.

Enable/Stop SHALL serialize with the canonical first durable accepted input/policy decision, not email Date, retry time or delayed Support admission. Record the effective policy revision/decision on the original receiving occurrence. Inputs accepted before Enable are not retrospectively captured; later matching inputs are held. Stop changes later first-accepted input only. Deferred hydration, repeated webhooks and routing recovery reuse the original effective decision. Initially unresolved receiving scope must be evaluated from retained original acceptance/policy evidence when resolved, not whatever policy a worker happens to see later. Current non-overridable safety and source authority are rechecked independently.

### REQ26-D40-R13 — R13 — Qualified parsing and limited trust

Applies to **US26-D40-04**, acceptance **AC26-D40-04-01–03**.

The intake owner SHALL parse and validate the actual supported single From mailbox and define versioned exact equality before rule creation/matching. Preserve local-part distinctions unless its qualified protocol explicitly proves equivalence; normalize domain semantics under that same supported contract. Preserve plus tags and do not infer aliases or CRM personhood. Multiple/malformed/unsupported From evidence is not reduced to the first convenient string. A valid signed provider event or domain check proves only its actual technical evidence; it does not certify the person's identity or authorize disclosure. Reject self/receiving infrastructure loop targets under existing owner rules, not a broad ban on legitimate role-based ministry addresses.

### REQ26-D40-R14 — R14 — Reuse Needs review and single-input Release

Applies to **US26-D40-06**, acceptance **AC26-D40-06-01–03**.

Matching future inputs SHALL remain in the canonical D19 held-intake/review lifecycle with a clear **Sender hold** reason and the actual inbox's qualified coverage, safety gates, content schedule and age. No ordinary message, acknowledgment, reply target, D39 unread contribution or CSAT opportunity is created by holding. D19 **Release** is a one-input decision/override for that exact applicable hold gate; it neither disables the policy nor licenses other held mail. Preserve all other gates and generation/actor checks, and prevent retries from reholding or duplicating an already qualified release. Dismiss retains its existing one-input meaning.

### REQ26-D40-R15 — R15 — Stop holding without a backlog surprise

Applies to **US26-D40-05**, acceptance **AC26-D40-05-01–03**.

Stop holding SHALL affect only the exact currently reviewed policy activation under expected revision/current authority. It does not restore the old unwanted conversation, release/dismiss/delete held messages, change other inboxes or allowlist the sender. Show **Existing held messages still need review** with an authorized link. Releasing an item does not stop the hold; restoring the conversation does not stop it either. Avoid a combined stop-and-release or bulk recovery product. A stale stop cannot disable a later restarted activation.

### REQ26-D40-R16 — R16 — Honest failures and separate operation results

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Mark, Restore, Start hold and Stop hold SHALL have separate durable outcomes and retry identity. If Mark succeeds and optional hold creation fails, show both facts; never imply a combined rollback or success. Lost responses reconcile the same operation and currently permitted result before admitting a conflicting retry. Preserve work and clear errors without repeated modal/toast loops. A processing failure holds unresolved input visibly for qualified operators; it is not “not matched,” released, dropped or safe. Independent ordinary work remains available where its owners permit it.

### REQ26-D40-R17 — R17 — Database shape and invariants

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Use actual UUID tenant/auth/profile relationships and TEXT Support original/inbox IDs as qualified by current schema. Same-tenant keys bind originals, receiving occurrences, policies and decisions; one active hold per exact tenant/receiving-inbox/mailbox key. Scope, actor, source and generations are trusted/immutable, with closed typed states, nonnegative exact revisions and uniqueness for durable business effects. No caller-selected audit time, author, owner or future epoch. Disposition/hold history is append-only under its declared custody; deleting a policy/state cannot cascade into source content, held evidence, CRM or communication. No money field is introduced.

### REQ26-D40-R18 — R18 — Operation-specific authorization and RLS

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Separate current conversation handling, Restore, hold management and D19 review/release authority within Core's actual permission system. Assignment, generic staff/admin status or a CRM link grants none by implication. Derive actor/tenant/current membership server-side and recheck source/action authority at commit and replay/result access. Qualify grants, SELECT, USING, resulting-row WITH CHECK, immutable columns, policy unions, views, RPC EXECUTE/search_path/actual owner and every privileged service/Storage/cache/export/Realtime route. RLS enabled with broad grants alone is not this boundary; no ordinary contact operation edits intake policy.

### REQ26-D40-R19 — R19 — Atomicity, replay and concurrency

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Mark/Restore and hold Enable/Stop require current source/policy generation checks, deterministic lock order and one committed decision/result with required owner obligations. Input acceptance, hold effectiveness, release exceptions and canonical admission share an actual serialized/fenced protocol. Duplicates cannot create multiple policies, notes, target changes, admissions or notices; distinct legitimate operations are not deduplicated by similar text. Revoke/move/expiry/merge and pending command races must fail or reconcile safely. Current-generation barriers survive cleanup/restore; absence of a result or canceled HTTP is not proof of noncommit.

### REQ26-D40-R20 — R20 — Inbox changes, coverage and departed staff

Applies to **US26-D40-05**, acceptance **AC26-D40-05-01–03**.

The hold follows its immutable receiving-inbox identity, not a moved conversation's handler or a renamed address label. A recreated inbox has a new identity and inherits nothing. Before Start/restart, require current eligible review coverage and finite custody for matched inputs; no unsupported active hold is advertised. Security revocation/offboarding always proceeds and raises D19's owned coverage exception rather than granting access or blocking revocation. Holds are tenant policy, not transferred personal drafts; the departed creator is retained only under permitted audit purpose. Rebinding receiving routes must show/requalify affected policy scope, never silently broaden it.

### REQ26-D40-R21 — R21 — CRM integration and real identity

Applies to **US26-D40-07**, acceptance **AC26-D40-07-01–03**.

CRM-hosted Support uses the same authorized originals, designation and intake policy references with preserved return context. A requester, message participant, authenticated worker, CRM Party, represented organization, assignee and record owner remain distinct. Linking/unlinking, shared email, Party merge/deletion or contact changes do not retarget rules, reclassify other conversations, duplicate Activity, suspend login, unsubscribe or alter giving/member-care authority. CRM context reads and any independently requested owner action keep their actual permissions/validation/history. A source address is an operational match, not a second CRM identity.

### REQ26-D40-R22 — R22 — Email Studio, P17, P6 and current communication

Applies to **US26-D40-07**, acceptance **AC26-D40-07-01–03**.

Support owns current handling and source eligibility; canonical intake owns holds; P17/Email Studio owns governed content/preparation and separate notification engagement; P6 owns admitted delivery/recovery. Mark/Restore/hold changes send no requester notice, publish no template and create no provider spam training, mailbox-state sync or read receipt. Current Unwanted designation removes new submission authority for its own ineligible optional confirmation/feedback material. A future-mail hold is an inbound per-occurrence gate, not an outbound or consent block on every conversation with that address: held-before-admission input creates no mail, and a qualified D19 release may regain only its normal D13 purpose eligibility within the original fifteen-minute window and other rules. Independently valid ordinary outbound work is unaffected by an active sender hold. Already or possibly submitted P6 evidence remains truthful and cannot be recalled/rekeyed. Human pending sends use R07's owner recovery. D38 notes/mentions and D15 optional Following remain separate; no cleanup action mass-reads notifications or fabricates communication completion.

### REQ26-D40-R23 — R23 — Retention and honest Restore availability

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

D16/D17 and D19 remain the source/held-content custody owners. Mark records a genuine purpose ending only when actually proved; correcting falsely active work or mark/restore cycling cannot create a new lifetime. Show the owner's actual recoverability/deadline before consequential action, including content already due for expiry; never promise Restore for expired/restricted bytes or invent a trash grace period. New genuine Internal notes retain their existing D17 native-content rule. Active hold policy metadata has its own operational purpose/finite post-stop history; it does not retain the triggering body forever. Restore obeys current restriction/expiry/holds, and backups cannot revive negative controls or deleted evidence.

### REQ26-D40-R24 — R24 — Reporting and attention preserve facts

Applies to **US26-D40-07**, acceptance **AC26-D40-07-01–03**.

Keep current unwanted population, review decisions, input holds/releases, real resolutions, missed targets and feedback eligibility distinct. Designating unwanted is not successful service or a new D28 opportunity; a correction cannot erase valid historic misses, invitations or denominator evidence to improve scores. D14's independently proved mistaken-eligibility/time correction remains available with its own audit; this designation is not that proof. D19 held backlog retains original receipt age and existing 24-hour routine-review/48-hour expiry attention; policy changes/retries do not reset it. Use existing grouped source-actionable attention with current authorization, not per-message emails or staff rankings. Retain lawful D15 Follow intent; Mark/Restore are housekeeping corrections, not E4 successful-end notices or new follow enrollment. Actual E1/E2/E3 content and direct mentions retain their separate producers. Mark/Restore alone does not create D39 unread activity; an actual qualified new human contribution does.

### REQ26-D40-R25 — R25 — Lists, search and recoverability

Applies to **US26-D40-02**, acceptance **AC26-D40-02-01–03**.

Amend D20 ordinary work views explicitly to exclude currently Unwanted material while its dedicated view remains discoverable under current access. Do not silently change the meaning of work-status predicates or treat an ordinary label as policy. The built-in Unwanted view lists only current all-Unwanted components. Mixed components remain in ordinary work and retain each original designation in their authorized history. D22 admitted-content search can still find unwanted original matches, with that original clearly labelled and the current component work state accurate; open the same source and applicable Restore path, not a duplicated unwanted component. No new body store or search engine. Held inputs remain outside ordinary conversation search under D19. Source privacy/expiry precedes hits, counts, pagination and snippets. Keep missing/partial results distinct from an empty list.

### REQ26-D40-R26 — R26 — Bounded efficient implementation

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Reuse existing paged metadata lists; for the new Unwanted and Sender holds management projections use 25 initial rows and at most 50 per request, with stable cursors and no total-population truncation. These are chosen consistent UI bounds, not measured capacity. Index exact active policy lookup, receiving occurrence/effective decision, original designation and authorized review queries. No scan of all senders, bodies or CRM records on every arrival. Record actual burst/skew, tenant/inbox sizes, policy counts, lock/query p50/p95 and backlog capacity before activation. No promised instant processing or universal sender-rate budget is copied from vendors.

### REQ26-D40-R27 — R27 — Useful audit and manageable operations

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Keep immutable business/security attribution for Mark/Restore/Enable/Stop/Release, exact scope/generation/result and required current owner actions, separate from technical traces. Record aggregate technical failures, conflicts and latency without bodies, full addresses in ordinary logs, tokens, filenames or hidden-source metadata. Policy managers may see authorized operational address data without message-body authority; aggregate held counts still need their own current source permission. O01–O06 provide named residual signals, thresholds, responsible roles and responses. No manual DB repair, tribal-knowledge cleanup or hidden unowned review queue is an acceptable normal operating path.

### REQ26-D40-R28 — R28 — Source-first migration and safe rollout

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Add qualified canonical control identities/constraints/decision history and retire conflicting route/review writers before enabling commands or UI. Do not reinterpret old recipient routes, spam-like labels, requester addresses, shared counters or current status as approved holds/designations. Unknown legacy provenance stays owned and restricted for reconciliation, not silently blocked or deleted. Mixed versions cannot bypass current generation/policy snapshots or revive stopped rules. Separate optional UI/policy-write stops from required intake safety, held recovery and P6 reconciliation; rollback must honor accepted effects and negative controls. Qualify disposable database migrations and live-path compatibility before activation.

### REQ26-D40-R29 — R29 — Prove the complete journey

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

P01–P40 SHALL verify actual DB/RLS/current roles, multi-session races, parser/matching, source policy timing, pending sends, drafts/notes, restore/expiry, receiving-route changes, CRM and reporting outcomes. Real keyboard/touch/AT/IME, Compact/Full, low-bandwidth, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, text zoom, Thai/RTL, reduced motion and Core target/contrast requirements apply to the same Base UI/base-maia journey. Intended-staff formative testing and corrections are required; a source helper probe is not UI or production proof. Numerical capacity budgets, actual custody inventory and accountable operating assignments are preactivation gates. All 40 runtime groups remain required and unexecuted here.

### REQ26-D40-R30 — R30 — Traceability and disciplined scope

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Trace each clause into authorized OpenSpec/design/tasks/issues/tests/release evidence and reconcile stale Twenty/synchronization prose against ADR0001's native CRM authority. No new provider, AI classifier, global blocklist, generic rules/approval engine, bulk block/release, arbitrary contact search, separate CRM or privacy-export product is selected. The complete correction is B with bounded explicit actions, not a return to A disguised as a missing implementation dependency.
