### REQ26-D40-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O01 — Residual controls after qualification

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed cross-tenant/forbidden-source exposure, unauthorized policy/work mutation, scope broadening, privacy control failure or secret/body/token leak.

**Owner:** Support security/privacy owner and intake engineering on-call

**Response:** Contain affected command/projection; preserve minimized evidence; keep retained input recoverable; correct and requalify before re-enable. Do not disable independent source restrictions.

### REQ26-D40-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O02 — Residual controls after qualification

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Technical Mark/Restore/hold command failures above 2% over 15 minutes with at least 100 eligible attempts per path. Exclude typed validation, expected conflict, authorization denial and user cancellation. Individual low-volume failures remain visible.

**Owner:** Support/intake engineering on-call

**Response:** Diagnose actual durable owner/result path, reconcile ambiguous outcomes and bound retries. Disable broken optional action if needed; retain truthful state and independent valid work.

### REQ26-D40-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O03 — Residual controls after qualification

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed wrong-inbox/sender hold, admitted-input decision changing with retry, duplicate/lost Release, stale policy resurrection or concealed legitimate obligation.

**Owner:** Canonical intake owner and Support source owner

**Response:** Treat as correctness incident; stop affected new policy/actions or route uncertain input to owned retained recovery, repair the root boundary and add actual concurrent regression proof. Never mass-release/mark-read/resolve as repair.

### REQ26-D40-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O04 — Residual controls after qualification

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** p95 for a qualified input-policy lookup or command exceeds twice its P36 release budget for 15 minutes with at least 100 samples; any unbounded scan/fanout or backlog exceeding tested recovery capacity triggers review immediately.

**Owner:** Intake/database performance owner

**Response:** Inspect plans, locks, effective-history lookup, duplicate work and tenant skew; mitigate and roll forward with current-policy truth. No implicit policy bypass for speed.

### REQ26-D40-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O05 — Residual controls after qualification

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** Three substantiated same-journey friction reports in 30 days, or one critical keyboard/AT blocker, wrong-scope choice, hidden legitimate work or lost draft.

**Owner:** Support product/design and accessibility owner

**Response:** Reproduce complete journey, correct scope/copy/control and retest intended-user tasks; critical errors are immediate, without waiting for three reports.

### REQ26-D40-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003-O06 — Residual controls after qualification

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

**Signal and threshold:** D19 coverage unavailable at Start/restart; any qualified reviewable input reaches the existing 24 elapsed-hour review threshold or has 48 elapsed hours or less until expiry. Older/shorter cases surface immediately under D19.

**Owner:** Responsible inbox's designated intake reviewers, backup and tenant oversight

**Response:** Refuse unsupported new activation, preserve current security revocation and retained inputs, raise the existing grouped in-product coverage/aging condition, assign lawful review and qualify capacity. No per-message mail or new review queue; Stop alone does not clear backlog.

### REQ26-D40-PROOF_AND_OPERATIONS-S0003 — Residual controls after qualification

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

These operating controls are binding for unwanted handling and future-mail holds. Assign actual accountable teams/people before activation. O02/O04/O05 numerical alert policies are engineering/product judgments, not vendor constants. Coverage, authorization, exact input timing, custody and correctness are release gates; monitoring is not their substitute.

Source holds here are future-mail policies, not legal preservation holds. Existing preservation and expiry rules remain with their owners. No runtime group, participant study, deployed role test, benchmark or actual provider operation was executed by this document.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0005 — C01 — Two owners, two independent actions

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Support owns Mark unwanted and Restore for exact admitted original conversations. The canonical incoming-email policy owner owns a fixed exact observed-mailbox hold within one qualified receiving inbox. D40 adds the narrow policy predicate and management use case to that boundary, not an independent Support rule registry, arbitrary filter builder, domain policy or CRM-person status. Marking unwanted does not enable the future hold; enabling/stopping a hold does not mark, restore, dismiss or release existing correspondence.

Use existing the shared API owner command ownership and shared projected reads. A new physical table, if needed by the qualified owner, remains an implementation choice; naming an unimplemented owner contract is not evidence that it currently exists. Do not append sender types to the recipient-route enum and inherit its destination-changing/auto-resume behavior.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0006 — C02 — Exact original disposition and valid topology

Applies to **US26-D40-02**, acceptance **AC26-D40-02-01–03**.

Mark unwanted qualifies the complete current reviewed email-origin component and every included original under current tenant/source/action authority. It is allowed only for non-support correspondence with no legitimate Support work or retained genuine commitments that the action would conceal. One nuisance message, shared email, an optional label or AI classification cannot authorize hiding a mixed component. Bind accepted contributors to immutable original IDs, exact topology and source/work versions; preserve D10 provenance and Undo. D26 manual creation and D29 public-form decisions are not replaced or broadened by this email-origin action.

Use one current source disposition plus append-only decisions; do not copy or delete message bodies and do not add a fifth D3 work status. A component is absent from ordinary work only when the source projection proves every included original is unwanted and no independently owed work is hidden. New legitimate admitted input for B makes B ordinary and the A/B component visible for current review; it does not silently restore A's unrelated original or erase A's history. A new Merge involving unwanted material requires the accepted Restore path first. D10 Undo reprojects the surviving original designations; no new per-message classifier or generic split editor follows.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0007 — C03 — Operation-specific authority and trusted attribution

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Viewing set-aside material, marking it, restoring it, inspecting active hold policy, enabling/stopping that policy and deciding a held input each require their own existing qualified source/inbox capability. Staff assignment, review designation, policy authorship, shared email, CRM relationship or tenant-admin label alone is not blanket body access or policy authority. Derive tenant, auth user, actual profile/membership, current capability and decision time from trusted server context.

A policy manager may Stop an independently retained active rule without revealing an expired original body. A reviewer can Release one permitted input without authority to alter future policy. Do not require the original creator to remain employed to manage an active rule, and do not block actual security revocation to preserve reviewer coverage. Follow D19's coverage/oversight exception handling rather than grant emergency access.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0008 — C04 — Exact observed address is not sender identity

Applies to **US26-D40-04**, acceptance **AC26-D40-04-01–03**.

Enable future holding only from one currently permitted, canonical accepted input with an unambiguous source mailbox qualified by the intake owner's versioned parser and equality contract. Show that exact address as observed, plus the receiving inbox. A display name, Reply-To, Return-Path, CRM contact field, forwarded body, embedded original header, shared-address relationship or synthetic missing-address fallback is not a substitute.

Preserve the exact parsed local part under qualified syntax; normalize domain comparison under the owner's DNS/IDNA rules. Do not generically lowercase local parts, strip dots or plus tags, equate aliases, expand to a domain, or infer all mailboxes of a person. Multiple From mailboxes, malformed/unsupported syntax and uncertain forwarded origin make this shortcut unavailable with a plain explanation; they do not pick the first address or invite arbitrary unreviewed text entry. Existing broader mail parsing/routing behavior must not be silently changed for unrelated features; qualify the canonical predicate required here and its normalization version.

A verified provider webhook establishes an integration event, not the human sender's identity. Authentication evidence, if used, comes only from its trusted receiving boundary; user-supplied Authentication-Results or quoted headers cannot elevate trust. This is a review hold on observed mail, not identity verification. Shared/forwarding addresses can carry legitimate mail: preserve one-input Release and simple Stop, and never label a CRM person blocked.

The qualifying canonical source may be an already admitted inbound message or a currently authorized D19 held input with the same proved exact mailbox/receiving pair and independent hold-management permission. Enabling future holding never requires releasing unwanted current mail first, and it does not change that held input's own review gates or historical acceptance decision. Review-body access is not granted merely by policy-management permission.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0009 — C05 — Receiving inbox remains distinct from current handling

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

The hold key is the actual tenant-qualified receiving inbox and exact observed source mailbox. Bind that inbox through D1's canonical receiving/recipient occurrence and qualified connection/routing evidence, not the conversation's current handling inbox, a mutable merged root, a visible To string alone, or a guessed domain. Transfers, aliases, rename, Merge/Undo and forwarding do not silently expand or move the rule.

A receiving-inbox alias already owned by that same qualified inbox follows its actual owner mapping; this does not grant domain-wide matching or a new alias management feature. Multiple recipient occurrences retain their D1 independent scope. A rule for inbox A cannot hold delivery to B solely because A's conversation was moved to B. When the one receiving scope is not provable, keep existing safe intake review and withhold policy activation. A retired/replaced inbox must not transfer a rule to a newly created inbox with a reused name/address.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0010 — C06 — Future means first canonical intake acceptance

Applies to **US26-D40-06**, acceptance **AC26-D40-06-01–03**.

Hold Enable/Stop and the first durable accepted canonical input/receiving occurrence use one qualified intake-owner ordering boundary. The input retains the applicable policy revision/decision once. If first acceptance wins before Enable, that Enable does not retroactively hold the input. If Enable wins first, a later matching first acceptance records the hold gate. Stop affects later first acceptances; it does not release or reinterpret previously held input.

Use durable acceptance and immutable policy revisions, not sender Date, received-at guesses, webhook redelivery, worker execution time or a global message counter. Capture a coherent policy checkpoint with first accepted input; where receiving scope is initially unresolved, the intake owner must later resolve the applicable retained version for that original acceptance rather than read worker-time policy. Missing evidence remains pending/restricted recovery, not an invented pass. This versioned boundary is an explicit preactivation gap in current source, not an existing deployed mechanism.

Serialize empty-rule insertion, Enable/Stop and first decision too: locking only a row that does not yet exist leaves a race. A short owner-scoped policy-head/shared-admission versus exclusive-change lock protocol is one viable design; choose and prove the actual protocol with deterministic lock order and bounded retries. Do not hold DB transactions across provider fetch, scan, network dispatch or user interaction. Current independent security, tenant/source restrictions and expiry are rechecked at final admission even though the ordinary hold decision is historically fixed.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0011 — C07 — Minimal relational facts and constraints

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Store only facts needed for current disposition, exact policy and once-only review/admission. Tenant-owned references must agree structurally or through an equivalently constrained authoritative boundary. Caller data cannot transform a permitted row into a different tenant, receiving inbox, original, match address, actor, decision or authorized effect.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact                              | Required relationship/invariant                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Original unwanted disposition     | Same-tenant immutable original reference; constrained current disposition; exact nonnegative current revisions and strictly advancing accepted decision versions; source-owned decision reference. Component state is derived, never a second write authority.                 |
| Disposition decision              | Append-only actor/profile attribution, exact original/topology/work revisions, operation/effect key, server accepted time and permitted reason/outcome. No transcript copy or mutable before-state rollback authority.                                                         |
| Exact hold policy                 | Same-tenant receiving-inbox reference; fixed matcher kind; qualified parser/equality version and canonical mailbox key; stable rule identity and current version; independently governed active/stopped state and history. No CRM FK that turns into sender truth.             |
| Active uniqueness                 | At most one effective identical mailbox hold per receiving inbox, including across normalization migrations. A partial active-rule unique index is useful, but uniqueness must follow semantic scope rather than allow duplicates by changing parser-version text.             |
| First-acceptance decision         | Immutable canonical input and D1 recipient occurrence; applicable intake-policy checkpoint, matched gate occurrence or qualified no-match, and original first-acceptance evidence. Unknown tenant/scope cannot be represented as a normal tenant row with broad null fallback. |
| One-input release                 | Exact input/recipient admission effect; accepted decision/review generation; exact ordinary hold-gate occurrence exemption; independently current authority and all remaining source gates.                                                                                    |
| Required work/dispatch obligation | Existing owner occurrence and source generation, atomically accepted with its producer decision; no second Support job queue or generic workflow plan.                                                                                                                         |

Use actual UUID identities and TEXT Support IDs without coercing one into the other. Nullability must distinguish an unknown/not-applicable reference from a fabricated profile, inbox or address. Constrain enumerated kinds/states, monotonic versions and valid combinations; serialize large integer control values exactly. Enforce actual tenant-aware FKs and unique durable effects, index FK/filter predicates, and prevent cascading deletion that erases independently required decision/admission evidence. D40 adds no money fields, floating amounts or copied CRM data.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0012 — C08 — Enable, Stop and duplicate requests

Applies to **US26-D40-06**, acceptance **AC26-D40-06-01–03**.

Enabling a hold reviews and commits one exact scope under current policy authority and expected version. Concurrent identical requests resolve to the same effective rule or a truthful Already holding result; they do not redirect an existing rule, create stacked holds, broaden scope or replay a second notification. Stop ends that rule's future applicability and records its own authorized correction history.

Policy commands and disposition commands keep separate results. If one succeeds and the other fails, preserve and show the actual success rather than a false all-or-nothing toast or compensating action. Changing address/inbox scope is not an unrestricted UPDATE: stop the old scope and explicitly enable a new independently qualified one. Hold again is a fresh activation of the retained exact pair, requalifying current policy authority, receiving scope, review coverage and custody; it never resurrects old approval or requires recovering an expired triggering body. Lost command responses reconcile the durable same operation/effect; retries cannot re-enable a newer stopped generation or undo a later Restore. A Stop can be idempotently repeated but cannot erase matched historical gates.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0013 — C09 — Held input and the exact Release exception

Applies to **US26-D40-06**, acceptance **AC26-D40-06-01–03**.

A D40 match enters D19's existing retained Needs review path before ordinary Support admission. It carries an explicit future-mail-hold reason alongside other independently current gates. Reviewers may Release that one qualified input, Dismiss it, or return a dismissed input to review under D19. Release neither disables the rule nor grants sender trust; Stop neither releases this input nor dismisses it.

The durable release exception targets the exact canonical input/recipient occurrence and the hold-gate occurrence matched from first-acceptance evidence, not the mutable current active-rule head. Same-effect valid retries recognize that exception and cannot loop the released input back into the same hold. Later Stop/re-enable does not attach a new ordinary hold to old input. Release still cannot bypass malware, missing body, classification, unknown binding, expiry, changed reviewer authority or other source gates. An exemption is not reusable for another email from the same address.

Before admission, an authorized D19 cancellation can invalidate that attempt; a new release uses a new decision generation but the same single admission effect. After admission, cancellation reports actual Already released and correction uses the current source owner. Held messages retain original receipt/custody deadlines; policy activation, viewing, Stop, Return and retries do not renew them. No body/file preview or external confirmation is implied by matching a rule.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0014 — C10 — Atomic admission and unknown success

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Canonical input/D1 recipient occurrence has at most one actual Support admission effect. The input-to-Support linkage, source message/conversation contribution, current disposition reactivation where applicable, custody receipt and required owner obligations commit under one qualified authoritative admission boundary. A read-before-write, temporary worker claim, workflow event ID or repair-to-first-duplicate lookup alone does not provide this invariant.

D19 decision/audit/continuation commits atomically; downstream admission checks the still-valid decision and all current gates. If source admission committed but the response or secondary delivery is lost, reconcile the same effect and required outbox obligation. Do not manufacture a new input, message, release, CRM occurrence or preparation to retry. Current source's separate routing and bridge writes are a verified gap to close, not a model to endorse. Preserve already admitted evidence on replay; a new hold policy cannot pull admitted content backward into intake.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0015 — C11 — Database grants, RLS and privileged paths

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Keep raw input, sensitive policy mutation, review, disposition mutation and durable history server-command owned. Existing RLS-enabled/no-browser-grants raw intake tables are an appropriate posture. Approved browser read projections expose only current permitted source/policy metadata; they do not grant raw rule or history mutation. Inspect actual table/schema/column grants, effective SELECT/USING/WITH CHECK policies, views, RPC EXECUTE and every service-role path.

USING qualifies the old row; WITH CHECK and immutable-field/command constraints qualify the resulting row. Broad same-tenant predicates are insufficient for current inbox/source capability, trusted actor or valid state transitions. An omitted WITH CHECK can inherit USING, and SECURITY DEFINER uses its actual owner's rights; neither shorthand substitutes for testing effective authority. Fix search_path and qualify objects for justified definer functions, revoke ambient execution, and test owner/BYPASSRLS roles, policy unions and invoker/definer views. A direct update must not transfer scope, clear a hold, forge admission or change audit attribution.

Services derive their input from authenticated canonical source/operation context and recheck tenant, actor delegation, receiving/source scope and current restrictions. A valid signed webhook is not permission to accept caller-selected tenants or spoofed sender identity. No service credential enters a browser, message body, log, output artifact or client token. An API pre-request check does not replace Storage/Realtime policies. Expected hidden-row denial must not reveal policy existence through raw uniqueness/FK errors or counts.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0016 — C12 — Files, caches, privacy and recovery views

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Set aside and held-review views reuse current authorized source representations; do not create a second transcript store, public bucket or revealable privacy archive. D16 restrictions and D17/D19 custody still apply to bodies, previews, derivatives, signed URLs, search, exports, notifications and restored data. Restore cannot bypass a restriction or bring expired bytes back.

Plain filenames, snippets, counts, matched addresses and rule history can be sensitive; authorize before pagination, aggregation or presentation. Signed URL issuance uses the current source permission and approved short-lived delivery boundary; old URLs/cache/provider copies require the already accepted owner inventory and restriction handling. A nuisance hold is not a legal preservation hold and grants no malware override. No automatic link fetching, remote images, file execution, public lookup or private-message extraction follows from marking or reviewing.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0017 — C13 — Existing work, drafts, reading and CRM

Applies to **US26-D40-03**, acceptance **AC26-D40-03-01–03**.

Mark/Restore and admission serialize with the exact source/work/topology boundary and relevant accepted send/result guards. A stale tab cannot hide new genuine work, erase a pending obligation, manufacture resolution or submit from a no-longer-valid source. Never reset recipients/drafts, post a note, clear D39 reading state, acknowledge P17 notifications, stop required direct attention, or mutate CRM/consent to make the action succeed.

Manual Restore re-establishes current ordinary review under current authority; it does not replay a saved old assignment/status/reminder snapshot. A newly admitted relevant B contribution restores B's participation in ordinary work without clearing unrelated A provenance. D28 sampling, invitations and truthful reporting cannot interpret non-support disposition as a successful resolution or improve denominators secretly. Definitely unsubmitted obsolete optional material uses its existing cancellation owner; a may-have-begun P6 effect keeps immutable reconciliation rather than a fake recall or fresh dispatch. Existing dirty drafts remain private and subject to their own live source guards; no default external response is created.

A genuinely new actionable P6/owner recovery after an otherwise valid Mark makes the affected original and its current work home visible for review, ending only the now-inapplicable unwanted exclusion. Its actual owner records the obligation and any real purpose change; do not manufacture a new human message, source-content timestamp, D39 unread event, reply fulfillment or duplicate notification. Duplicate or already-reviewed outcomes do not repeatedly reopen work. Other originals and historical designation evidence remain intact.

CRM Parties, represented organizations, requesters, participants, real actors and mailbox claims remain distinct. Marking/holding changes no Party/relationship, registration, consent, contactability, suppression, login, giving or care fact. Existing admitted correspondence history remains honest and permission-aware; held input stays outside ordinary CRM correspondence history under D19. Source navigation through CRM reuses the authorized Support record rather than duplicating it.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0018 — C14 — Email Studio and communication seam

Applies to **US26-D40-07**, acceptance **AC26-D40-07-01–03**.

Support owns current unwanted disposition and recovery; canonical intake owns the optional future hold and its historical input decision. P17/Email Studio retains governed content, whole-message preparation and separately owned notification engagement; P6 retains communication/delivery and reconciliation. Mark, Restore, Enable hold, Stop holding and review inspection send no sender notice, auto-reply, complaint, unsubscribe, campaign or provider-mailbox update and create no prepared email.

D19 source-owned attention continues through its already accepted role-safe P17 presentation and P6 local `in_product`/`available` occurrence, using the no-artifact contract; do not add a raw notification writer. This ownership is explicit in governing ADR0032:19–22 and the fully ratified D19 Email Studio integration, not inferred from notification UI. It creates no provider preparation, provider state or Resend traffic. One-input admission preserves D13's original fifteen-minute confirmation opportunity/suppression and D14's actual readiness/time facts; review does not create a fresh window. D35 note history, D36 quotes and D37/D38 private drafts retain their owners. Shared authoring does not make Internal-note Post an email preparation; separately governed post-derived notices and required direct mentions remain distinct from D15 optional Following.

An active future intake hold is not a global outbound suppression or contactability decision. Its held inputs have not yet earned admission-dependent confirmation/feedback authority; a qualified one-input Release may establish normal source eligibility within D13's original window. Independently authorized outbound communication about other legitimate work remains governed by its own source and P17/P6/contactability rules.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0019 — C15 — Finite custody and independent policy life

Applies to **US26-D40-05**, acceptance **AC26-D40-05-01–03**.

An active future hold has its own current inbox-policy purpose and may outlive the original correspondence that motivated it, within the owner's qualified policy/evidence retention inventory. It does not retain the original body forever. Stopping a hold ends future matching while retaining only necessary bounded configuration/admission/correction evidence and replay fences. No arbitrary new D40 deletion period is introduced.

D19 ordinary held payload remains under its accepted fourteen-elapsed-day original-receipt ceiling and existing earlier restrictions/unknown-receipt recovery rules; policy unavailability does not extend it. Already admitted set-aside content remains under D17 purpose/expiry decisions rather than borrowing intake's fourteen days or P6 Recent settings. Policy versions must remain available long enough to classify retained accepted inputs honestly; expiry/cleanup cannot destroy a needed decision fence before pending authority ends. Restore after authority expired reports unavailability, and restoring old backups reinstates current restriction, policy, admission and operation-generation barriers before service resumes. Inbox deletion/offboarding cannot accidentally release mail or reassign policy ownership to reused identities.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0020 — C16 — Query discipline, business evidence and operations

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Use indexed equality lookup within one receiving inbox and sparse source disposition; no full message-body scan, per-person fanout, global domain registry or new AI classifier. Index canonical input/effect/review keys and current permitted recovery-list predicates. Measure actual inbox/rule/input/original cardinality, policy-lock contention, list/query plans, retained version growth and provider/retry load before activation.

Bound/coalesce retries through existing intake/work ownership. Policy lookup/first-decision failure retains input in a truthful processing/recovery state and raises qualified operational attention; it never treats a failed check as no rule or success. D19 review coverage, aged unresolved input, expiry and stuck admission already have owners and thresholds; extend those signals to this reason rather than create a second operations queue. Configuration, disposition and review decisions need durable body-free actor/scope/revision/effect history because they affect shared work/intake. Technical diagnostics are separate and exclude raw bodies, addresses, sensitive subjects, tokens and unnecessary payloads; normal D39 reading remains excluded from a staff-viewing journal.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0021 — C17 — Migration and activation sequencing

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Qualify the canonical observed-mailbox parser, immutable receiving occurrence, first-acceptance policy checkpoint/history, D19 review/admission, guarded original disposition and current action authority before enabling D40 controls. Add narrow constraints and projected reads, retire unsafe bypass writers, then activate the UI with actual evidence. Do not infer unwanted history from Resolved/labels or seed future holds from old messages, CRM consent or provider complaints.

Pending legacy input without trustworthy first-acceptance/policy/receiving provenance stays in qualified review/recovery with explicit limits; no worker-time guess silently releases it or invents a past hold. Existing unrelated destination routing remains its own fact. Mixed versions cannot admit through the old unguarded path, drop matched gates, overwrite receipt/actor identity or duplicate Support admission. A stop/kill switch can disable a broken optional command/UI path while retaining matched gates, backlog and independent work; it must not fail open by ignoring an active hold. Roll forward or qualify an explicit owner policy change. No fallback to provider blocking, manual SQL repair or Support-local rules is a permanent solution.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0022 — C18 — Falsifiable implementation proof

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Before activation prove the real selected API/PostgreSQL roles, isolation, indexes, service/Storage and browser workflows. Documentary reasoning and the six actual helper calls below do not prove those paths.

Required cases include: two tenants/inboxes with the same mailbox; true auth/profile separation; sender spoof/Reply-To divergence/shared/forwarded/multi-From/malformed/SMTPUTF8 and normalization-version cases; receiving A moved to handling B; multiple D1 recipient occurrences; concurrent identical Enable; Enable versus first durable acceptance in both orders; Stop versus acceptance; deferred routing/body retrieval under old policy checkpoint; policy-unavailable retained recovery; exact gate exception with same-input retries, Cancel/re-release and Stop/re-enable; security gate arriving after Release; expired content; replay after actual admission; source/bridge/outbox partial success; Mark versus new real work or Send; all-original versus mixed topology; Merge/Undo and B-only new input; unchanged drafts/reading/CRM/P17/P6; all grants/RLS/old-row/new-row/view/RPC/service/Storage paths; permission loss and restore; mixed-version rollback and actual performance limits. Require negative proofs that no held input becomes a new CRM person, ordinary support message, sender communication or duplicate admission prematurely.

### REQ26-D40-DATA_CONTRACT-S0023 — Bounded source probe and disposition

Applies to **US26-D40-08**, acceptance **AC26-D40-08-01–03**.

Six unchanged-source helper calls produced: `User@Example.ORG` lowercased completely; plus tag preserved; two mailbox input reduced to the first; an unquoted local-part space accepted; a non-address rejected; and a quoted local part containing `@` rejected. These expose why the current convenience helper cannot establish D40's sole exact observed-mailbox match. They do not test all RFC forms or demonstrate deployed exploitation. No production data or external request was used in the probe.

**Data-boundary disposition: Accept with required amendments.** B remains viable with C01–C18. The main necessary changes are qualified first-acceptance policy evidence, per-inbox exact observed-source semantics, independent current versus future actions, all-original source eligibility, one-input gate exemption and once-only admission, and complete current authorization/custody. The narrow interaction does not justify a new CRM, spam engine, workflow builder or indiscriminate provider block. Current source gaps become explicit implementation release gates; no database or role behavior has been declared tested here.
